Final Assignment

Made by: Mario Markovic

Learning Launch

Challenge:   I am working I data analytic company as product manager. Due to the fact that we are  monetizing datasets we are always trying to find new ways of monetizing existing assets.  However, the main plan is to develop something that can be scalable internally as a products/  service but also a solution that can be scalable externally. One of our services is lead list/ b2b  selection services that provide our clients an exact list of potential clients to contact. In a  default way these lists are provided as hard copy lists in excel or some other legacy format.   We wanted to make one step further in our offer and provide to our clients not only list of  potential clients but also offer them a full-service product with capabilities to contact their  potential clients, online, contact them at social networks such as Facebook and LinkedIn.     Selections:  We decided to focus on that project for 4 weeks. We gathered a small team of people coming  from different departments (sales, IT, tech, product, customer care finance). We decided to  go with learning launch in order to get quick responses from the market/ clients. We wanted  to ran this project as agile process knowing that our main hypothesis -“Clients want to have  capability for micro targeting of their niche potential clients at social networks“ need to be  verified. We wanted to prove each step in our product delivery process in order to spent time  and resources in a good and meaningful way. My Assignment - Reflection – Visualization

Name : Shirley Medina

Company: Applied Materials Inc.

Challenge & Selection:

As soon as I receive a client request, I start thinking how to approach it. I ask questions over the  telephonic discussion or mail to the client to help me visualize exactly what is required.

Then I sit down to understand the requirement and identify possible solutions to the requirement of the  stakeholder. The challenge is to understand and give them what they want, keeping aside what we  know. My stakeholders are mostly automobile dealers and sales promoters for their product. I help them  build a marketing creative. I interpret their words and thoughts into illustrations and images to help in  their services which will be later delivered to their customer. I also suggest them opportunities for  improvements or solutions. This project was about Customer journey through a supermarket. How he  can use a single Contactless credit card for charging his car when parked at the parking lot, at the  supermarket premise  and how he can use the same card to do his shopping all at the same time, easily  cutting downtime. Earlier which was 10 steps process and by using 2 separate cards can now be  transformed to a single card and 4 easy steps process with the new customer card.

To avoid any communication gaps and understanding  gaps which possibly can rise due to inter-cultural upbringings, can be sorted by using sketching the  prototypes. Prototypes are an effective way to make our ideas flexible and ensuring the idea is  communicated effectively.

text:
Craig Gonzalez  Design Thinking for Innovation

Mind Mapping for Product Planning

Challenge & Selection

As part of my role, I am a business analyst who works very closely with the Product Owners in my organisation and  our customers are large corporates or big banks from across the world. A large part of product lines which our  customers consume will have 80% core product features which are globally common and 20% is either  customisation per geography or any other specific regional compliance obligations. Other than rolling out new  features into our core product globally, we keep on updating the customisation layer also. Whenever we get into  discussions with our customers, there are variety of issues which are brought on to the table by them which could  be either in the core product or the customised layer and we will have to collate all of those and analyse the  commonality between them and pick the items which qualify for enhancements, bug fixing and new features on  the core product and how it will impact the global customer base, which in fact is the trickiest part. Now, it is not  always the same problem which the customers bring forward and the result of fixing for one could result in  creating a new problem for another customer who was unaffected earlier. Therefore, in order to resolve this  efficiently and effectively I have been making use of mind mapping concept with the help of some real-life tools  e.g. XMind. I find mind mapping as very powerful as it looks for patterns and insights which comes really handy  when there is variety of data and stakeholders in the mix. It becomes very handy from my job perspective as if I  relay it back to the course would be the ‘What If’ phase. It helps me a lot in getting the stakeholders engaged and  also help them understanding my process with respect to other customers who are contesting to get a change  agreed and get rolled into the product roadmap.

PEER-GRADED ASSIGNMENT: REFLECTION

DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION.  BY: Shailesh Jain

1.  Challenge:

I am the general manager of a Music Record Label in Colombia. Our company has one  of the largest independent music catalogs in Latin America. Technological and cultural  changes have made people consume music digitally through mobile applications such  as Spotify, Deezer, Apple Music, etc. The sale of physical formats such as vinyl records  and compact discs has fallen to almost nothing. However, there is a musical product  that we want to keep as tangible, it is the "14 Dancing Cannon shots". This is a  compilation of the best musical themes during the year. This music compilation is highly  expected in the December season because they represent the arrival of the end of the  year holidays.  The challenge then is: Can the product be released in a different physical format from  CDs and vinyl records and at the same time incorporating a technological development  that also induces consumption on digital music platforms?

2. Selection:

The chosen tool was Visualization. Since it was about making a creative proposal of a  musical format different from the traditional ones, it was important for the  communication that there be a non-verbal description of what the people involved in the  process   wanted    to    express.    As    Lorena Hidalgo    explains    in    the    video.   it tries to awaken parts of our mind in which We relate the images with our ideas, the  creative part and artistic talent to improve, not only the generation of new own  perspectives, but also facilitate communication with peers. Allow me as a banker being a member of one of the most successful operational teams  in the banking sector, to share my own digital initiative idea "Adventure project".  My journey in the bank, as a head teller and a front liner enabled me for better  understanding of the customer journey, giving me the opportunity to come up with digital  innovative solutions.    Starting in 2017 after leading a team consisting of 7 employees in Sanstefano Br. one of  the most crowded branches and being one of the top three branches specified for tuition  fees payment for educational entities and universities and other schools in Alexandria  region.     Despite, the huge stress we have been through and the large number of operational  transaction that had been executed on daily basis all over the year. Behind every  obstacle lies a hidden opportunity.  The huge number of transactions executed to serve Non-bank customers specially  youth segment had negatively affect the AVG “Average waiting time” and may cause  customer dissatisfaction for banked and unbanked customers.     Therefore, I decided to take the advantage of such challenge and to go digital by  coming up with new innovative idea to migrate the traditional payments & fees to be  done through our digital channels, offering an exceptional digital experience " being  more efficient, quicker and cheaper" through our digital channels such as "Wallet,  Internet banking, ATM as well as the Mob App” offered to our bank customer and non-  bank customers, hence gaining their satisfaction and grabbing new to bank customers.     This will identify addition more opportunities for new products launch such as  educational loan and new type of accounts & services specifically tailored for the Youth  segment being the main source of NTB and Big Data. Design Thinking Course

Challenge and Selection      I selected Mind Mapping (Module 3) to develop a strategic vision, stimulate ideas, track  socio-cultural patterns and invisible connections, gain deep human centered insight and  detect the emotional needs of our audience to find a common thread between all the  different elements and activities proposed during the event, through mind mapping we  are looking to find solutions to enhance the atmosphere, the culinary experience and the  workshops proposed through out the event compared to the last 2 editions that took  place in Casablanca, Morocco during late fall season of 2014 and 2015.   Our challenge is to integrate a healthy vegetarian lifestyle in the community, build  bridges between our audience and the local organic farmers, yoga and music instructors  around a healthy meal with special flavors and recipes, while keeping in mind that  Moroccans used to eat very little meat and had a wider choice of vegetarian dishes  today eating meat is a lifestyle that leads to many diseases and environmental issues  but has increased significantly in the last 50 years, due to fear of malnutrition,  desertification of the land (Desert), the need for survival, however today, it is a sign of  wealth, power and belonging to a higher social class.         Application       Along with other stakeholders, we each drew a mind map based on the 4 main elements  (Music/ Vegetarian cuisine/ Workshops/ Cultural Exchange) while relying on existing  data, resources and feedback from our audience to guide us through out the process.  After brainstorming comparing and the results, i clustered similar ideas and emotions to  one large mind map (Attached below) keeping in mind the challenge that we are facing,  to help us generate a storyboard with keywords, shuffling them together, combining  ideas, gave us a deeper perspective and seeing the big picture and the connection or  common thread between the different 4 poles

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation  Learning Launch Reflection  Ravneet Williams  May 5, 2018

Challenge

I have worked as a Senior Project Manager in the engineering and construction industry for over fifteen  years. Most recently, my work has been managing large scale façade projects for skyscrapers and large- scale medical or commercial campuses. A typical project budget would average around $40M with a  project duration of roughly eighteen months. The three key phases of a project would, in order, include  1) design engineering (where our engineers would turn the architect’s vision into hundreds of detail  drawings), 2) production (where the detail drawings would be converted so the product could be  fabricated and assembled at one of our production facilities), and 3) field installation (where the  assembled product would be installed onto the building). A near constant that occurs once a project team  has been assembled is that many of the team members across departments have not worked together  before. Also, the mindset of individuals from each department is different simply because their job duties  are vastly diverse. The monetary scale of a given project, the risk that comes with such a long project  duration, and the possible issues within the project team makes, among many other things, the challenge  of fostering and constantly improving efficient communication of the utmost importance. For this  assignment, I am going to reflect on such a design thinking challenge I encountered while managing a 4- building biotech campus south of San Francisco, California.

Selection

After taking this course, I realized that I was using the “learning launch” tool on a regular basis. For the  reflection I am going to describe a situation where I encountered an appreciable communication challenge  at the forefront of a project. - Pushpalatha Bisht,

Co-Founder &

Lead, Business Operations

Legal Design Arc

Visualization Challenge & Selection

Being a legal designer, we understand that law is complex and this slices it away from its effective application.  As a legal designer I decided to use visualization as a tool to develop legal courses for the acts to help students  better understand these concepts. I decided to use a storyboard to explain the Right to Information Act in  India. This will help the students achieve a practical understanding of the concepts and help their future clients  effectively.

Application

The following steps were taken by me to develop this storyboard: -

1. Deciding on the key elements required to make someone understand the Right to Education Act. This

required consideration of the frequently asked questions regarding this act.

2. Then I started deciding on the best manner of describing these elements, experimented with

characters, objects, icons, personifications to develop the flow.

3. Developed the elements like a woman who needed information regarding one of her job applications

with a government department.

4. I then went on to decide the flow of the story and the application of the elements.   5. There were three things that had to be kept in mind while developing it first, the conceptual

explanation of the Act; Second, the procedural understanding of the Act; Third the cases that are key  to the Act.

6. Then I went on to develop a storyline to explain all the three things to students.   7. After I had the narration and the storyline with me I started to develop the visual depiction of the

story.

Desing Thinking  Vizualitation  Olga Alvarez

Challenge:

When I was in college finishing a technical course, I remember very well the  exhibitions in which we had to present some information about, the teaching material  that the teacher gave us. Many of those times we had to express our thoughts through  speech with voice. Many were bored and they did not understand what we wanted to  express.   Expressing our ideas, became detestable and no one wanted to come forward to  expose any kind of information. After a little stress on the part of the students, it was  decided to change the way we worked.

We decided to investigate what were the methods in which you can get attention  without having to talk too much. We did not find studies that explained that words  could get attention for only 15 minutes, after it became monotonous but incredible  because between a word and an image, the image would be more attention or  between a video and an image, the video would win and position as number 1 for  catch the attention of participants.    Another thing that we developed was the games. Everyone decided to make people  laugh while they were learning as there was more chance to remember a specific  topic. If they were willing. Here we include materials that express drawings as the  game of guessing what I express in the drawing. Game finds the couple of words and  colors, among others.

Selection:

A way to express when your mind creates based on experiences to the literal sense.   I want to say, what you imagine, you think and you get to express others through  phases of creation. The moment you think how to do something with materials that  show others classmates what you have in mind. That's why we apply visualization.

Maicol Sanchez

January 2017

Design Thinking for Innovation

University of Virginia  Final Course Assignment

Reflection: Learning Launch

Challenge

I have offered support to a start-up company in the food business to take their venture to the next  level. Among all the areas that need to be covered in this process, we have decided to leverage  Design Thinking to take a step back and think again about the overall customer experience when  consuming the company products. The portfolio of products is composed of a set of high-quality  snacks based on Japanese cuisine that is intended to be consumed as quick meals mostly for  people who prioritizes a healthy and lean lifestyle. The challenge we have identified was that some  consumers were not figuring out how to open the meal package correctly, what was creating an  issue on the overall experience to consume the product. This fact would represent a problem in the  growth of the business as they plan the expansion to a more diverse audience for those snacks,

Selection

I have selected Learning Launch for this assignment because it brings a new perspective about how  important it is to avoid confirmation bias of project team members when trying to build real impactful  innovation to the business. Also, to test the concept of learning cycles to test assumptions in fast  and cheap ways, understanding that failures are also opportunities to get insights for the business.

I have been working for the last 15 years in leadership roles in the IT industry, and I have used  different methodologies to keep evolving my operation, most of them associated on shaping  behaviors of internal teams during innovation and planning cycles, using tools like Six Thinking Hats,  Instinctive Drives System and Future Based Planning. It was interesting to realize that most of these  tools have a strong focus on the ways internal teams build plans. Reflection Design Thinking

Challenge & Selection    The challenge is to identify the problem of a process that has been carried out in the same way in  a company in different places and in which different departments are involved.    I selected the visualization tool, before defining and solving the problem, since it provides a shared  vision of the project and by using elements such as photographs, symbols and colors, they help to  have a single perspective of what is happening.    In this way we will seek to unify concepts and make evident the problems that have the greatest  impact to prioritize.    Using this technique in an all-day workshop helps people from different departments see the  problem also from the perspective of the other, thus finding a shared vision to define the impact,  scope, limits, actors and key elements .    In this case, the way of doing things has been the same for a long time and surprisingly we believe  that it is different in each city where the company operates and in many cases the reason why it is  done that way is not known. Using the visualization tool will add impressive value to the process  as it will allow us to understand the different realities and highlight the easily solvable problems  that exist today. For this diagram, symbols are  used that identify the action that is happening, who performs it, whether it is an operation, a record, or a  decision.  For this, apart from the usual identifiers, we use photographs of the people who do it.  As there are 5 different departments in 3 cities, we made 3 groups of 5 people randomly, to reach a general  consensus faster. Peer-graded Assignment: Refection

Asif Khan

Design Thinking for Innovation

January 16, 2021

Challenge

We all love to eat good food. Cooking good food at home is not always feasible.  Sometimes we want to taste diferent good food from diferent sources. We visit our  nearest restaurants, food shops, travel to diferent regions, and taste diferent cuisine.  We also love to have good food delivered to their homes.

In the COVID-19 pandemic, the situation is changed. The demand for food delivery  services is geting higher. we use the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to  understand and know the users' pain points, come up with user-friendly and  functional solutions.

Selection

Visualization is one of the very important tools. It is a core component of the way to  communicate. It allows us to think in a nonverbal way. Designing a food delivery service  involves diferent groups of people. Food makers, delivery persons, and users of the  service are the indispensable parts of the service.

We will focus on trying to uncover what they think, speak and do. And also use  technology to ensure seamless food delivery service and experience. We take  inspiration from diferent resources. "The Good Kitchen" story mentioned at the very  beginning of the course is one of them.   (http://jacobs-fisher.com/listpost.html)

Application

Before diving down to the core we tried to understand the current scenario frst. We  identifed the targeted users and the stakeholders to fnd answers to some very  important questions.

Who they are? Where they live? What are the problems and how they face them now?  How they address and communicate? What solutions they currently have and how  they use them? What are the pain points and experiences? What are their  expectations?

Designing for Innovation Loredana Abidin

Reﬂection: Visualization Tool

Challenge + Selection

My challenge was how to create a year long content calendar for a wellness blog that I’m  launching. I needed to come up with interesting blog post titles for weekly posts and create a  content calendar that would help me plan content for the year.

I chose the visualization tool to help me get a big picture view of what I would be writing about  and to help me ensure that the content ﬂowed well together.

Application

I ﬁrst sketched out the 4 main topics that I would be writing about. These I called Life Wellbeing  areas. I also created symbols and colors for each area.

Next I created two customer personas for my target audience. I drew landscapes of their daily  life and what their problems and needs were. I created 4 life boards for the 4 main wellness  areas and I added stickies with ideas, problems, solutions, and inspiration. I shared with a  family member and gathered additional stickies of ideas.

I wrote list of books and research that I would be writing about and I drew where they  connected to the persona’s life.

I drew symbols for holidays, seasonal milestones and other important events throughout the  year. I sketched out where content ﬁt in throughout the year and where psychological shifts  would be for the customer.

I drew a visual calendar with weekly topic ideas and where it ﬁt in my customer persona’s life.

Insight + Approach

Using the visualization tool helped me get a better sense of my customer persona by visually  mapping out their life and how they transition throughout the year with seasons.

What I learned is that by laying out the four main topics that I will be writing about over a visual  map of the customer persona’s life and seasonal milestones, I was able to see better where  content would be most impactful. text:
Guayaquil, September 24, 2020.  Name: Adam Filip  Project: “Mirror Lake Laundry and Press Solutions”

Challenge:

My challenge was more complicated than what I thought at the beginning, to be honest I  believed that my group of problem solvers would finish this job in 1 or 2 weeks. However,  it was not. The problem we were assigned was a question from our employer: How can  he get more contracts and success in his micro-business with our help?

The person who hired us for this university problem solving project is called Saman Mojica, he is an excellent mechanical engineer. He has studied at recognized  universities in the United States and Argentina. Saman is dedicated to advising and  auditing metallic and mechanical structures and civil works in the national environment  (Ecuador) and abroad. Their main problem was not the quality of their work or the lack  of funding, their biggest problem is that not many people knew the usefulness of their  work and who could offer that service, that is, lack of advertising or marketing and  ignorance of the possible clients regarding the work offered by Saman Jaramillo and his  micro-company called “Bachpan NGO”.

Selection:

It is for this reason that we lean towards “Storytelling”, although we also use other tools  many times, such as: “Visualization” or “Learning Launch”. These additional tools and  steps were very helpful as we uncovered hidden issues that neither Hector nor we had  seen in the beginning. But we all create the same hypothesis. Our hypothesis was that, if  we were able to obtain the most efficient solution for all the problems that slowly came  to light, we could achieve our main objective, which was for Saman's micro-business to  expand. For this and many other reasons, it was very important that we integrate all these  tools and apply them in different processes, at different times, in order to obtain what we  wanted as a group.

Challenge

My name is Sunny, I am a civil engineering student and the challenge I was presented with  was given in the intrapreneurship course I was taking at the university which was about  how to inspire CORE@HTU's clients to use technological tools to optimize time in  transactions. In a group of 6 people we had to identify what were the key reasons why the  client did not access the digital platforms. The team focused on finding the main reasons  why the client did not use the digital platforms, and instead preferred to go to the  establishments in person. The deadline for the development of the pilot project was two  months and the solution had to present something innovative.

Selection and Application

The team focused on using the visualization tool as well as secondary tools such as the  customer journey or the empathy map. The main tool of visualization allowed us to the  main reason from the application of the 4 key questions: What is?, What if?, What wow?  and What work?  As it is mentioned in the first weeks of the course, it is from this tool  that the group can acquire a great number of perspectives since being 6 people,  considering that we were from different careers we could get the most out of the tool.

We also conducted research by acquiring first-hand information from customer  interviews, asking them basically what were the reasons why they did not perform  transactions using digital applications, and in the What is? stage, we were surprised that  one of the main reasons was that they felt insecure and untrained in the use of mobile  applications.

NAME: Susan Pritchard

PEER-GRADED ASSIGNMENT

TITLE: “MY LEARNING, MY PRIDE”

“My Learning, My Pride”

Challenge: As a Lecturer from Faculty of Business and Globalization from Vlisco,

since 2007 up to 2013 our students used to be so vibrant, so full of energy and always eager to

come to school. This created a very conducive environment for both students and staff

members. For the past three years (2014-2016) our Faculty has been experiencing a challenge

of students’ poor attendance (lectures and tutorials) and lack of interest in their learning.  This

has even affected lecturers’ performance in classes as well. As one of the experienced lecturers

in the faculty, I always reported this challenge in my weekly report. In one of the faculty

meeting I tabled the discussion about this challenge; it became evident that every lecturer was

facing the same problem. I therefore volunteered to lead a team that was to find solutions to

this challenge.

Selection: I chose the storytelling design thinking tool to address this challenge. Storytelling is

an “essential human activity” for sharing experiences, explaining values, and deciding on

solutions through vivid verbal and visual accounts. Stories take on a variety of forms :  visual

storytelling, storyboards, scenario generation, storytelling through videos, animation or talk. I

did use talk form of storytelling so as to be able to narrate the challenge as well as listen to the

students’ concerns. This will also give me the opportunity to discuss with the students the

negative impact of this current challenge on their academic work and why there is a need to

find solutions to resolve the challenge.  Listening engages people and empathy is an essential

and fundamental component in the process of solving the challenge.

Course Assignment - Mind Mapping – Integrating Solutions

Note:  The following is a true story with many of the details made generic in order to preserve privacy.

Challenge

Our firm recently acquired a technology company (TC) that built a suite of tools and services that serves  a niche market, opening up a new market for our firm.  Within that market, our firm has another  business unit (BU) that serves a segment of that niche market with a set of tools and services (some  similar and some exclusive), but within a smaller segmentation of that market.  I was selected to be part  of a team of 6 to evaluate the newly acquired TC to determine if there were tools and/or services that  could be integrated into the BU offering.  Goals include:

1. Keeping the various systems nimble.   2. Proving the efficacy of the front-end data reporting for existing business.  3. Exploring the feasibility of pursuing a larger segment of the market.

Selection

We conducted a dozen interviews with various stakeholders across both business units and other  technology experts.  We collected a large amount of data from those interviews, and chose as our  primary tool Mind Mapping to help aggregate and identify themes in the data.

Application

Each team member individually took notes from those interviews.  We then identified key terms and  themes from each interview and wrote them on sticky notes.  The team reconvened in a room with a  large white board and we drew a grid with 4 quadrants.  The top two quadrants were goals which were  separated by quotes/defining words and thoughts/beliefs.  The bottom two quadrants were pain points  separated by actions/behaviors and feelings/emotions.

Challenge

I work for a non-profit organization that provides quality education to under-privileged children.  My company adopts under-performing public schools in low-income communities. After adopting  those schools, we implement reforms that lead to positive student learning outcomes and increased  student enrollment.

In order to raise funds for our initiatives, we organize fundraising dinners. Guests pay an entry fee  to attend a musical performance followed by dinner. During the event, my company’s Fundraising  department used to highlight important facts about the shortcomings in the public school system  by displaying shocking facts about the low student enrollment, high drop-out rate, and abysmal  student achievement. The Fundraising Department personnel would then distribute donation forms  among the guests and ask them to make donation commitments to address the problems that they  were highlighting. At the end of the event, we would collect these firms. Very few people would  make any commitments and those who did, would not follow though by actually sending a  donation check. We were unable to identify why our guests were not making any donation  commitments when they clearly cared enough about the cause to attend our event.

Selection and Application

Last year, we all sat down to discuss ways to collect more donor commitments during our  fundraising dinner scheduled for December. We decided to interview guests and tried to place  ourselves in the shoes of our donors. We realized from our discussions that our fundraising pitches  during the events did not draw any interest from the guests. They would mostly tune out or start  talking among themselves when our Fundraising Manager would come on stage. The Fundraising  Manager would list out a number of facts and figures about the abysmal state of public schools but  it did not resonate with the guests.

Reflection — Learning Launch  Guiding a Digital-First Mindset Shift in an  Online Enterprise SaaS Business

By Santosh Kumar

Challenge    Enterprise businesses offering digital SaaS (Software-as-a-Service) products often rely heavily  on traditional Sales workflows. This means, the selling process is entirely manually driven with  individuals, or even whole teams of Sales and Pre-Sales professionals being involved in  helping a customer make a purchase decision and closing a deal. While this has worked  traditionally because of such digital products usually being expensive, high dollar-value items;  it comes at a great cost to the scalability of a business, especially when entering and capturing  newer or larger markets.    As a member of my organization’s marketing leadership, my team of cross-functional experts  and I were faced with the challenge of proving the market demand for a scalable, fully digital,  “try-before-you-buy” business model to our Executive leadership who had grown accustomed  to the traditional methods of doing business and reflected a fixed mindset1, convinced that  the market, or the customers, didn’t voice such a need for change.

Selection    My team and I have decided to employ the Learning Launch tool as we have already gone  through several Design Thinking activities and tools such as co-creating a Journey Map2 of  “What Is” our customers’ current state of engagement with our product’s website to  understand what is or isn’t working in helping them express interest in buying our product  and starting a purchase-conversation with us.    We have also engaged in mind-mapping3 activities building alignment on the “What If”  scenario of our proposed solutions and we feel that a Learning Launch, being an  experimentation tool, will help us quickly gather valuable data4 in testing our hypotheses  and validating market-demand for a fully digital, instant “try-before-you-buy” experience of  our product as outlined in the “Challenge” section abov

Mind Mapping

Challenge:

Managing the starting up and opening of a restaurant business, all by myself.   (An appropriate title would be: ‘Project manager without a project team’)   Three years ago, I was hired as a project manager by a small businessman  to manage sales and inventory of a restaurant. Turns out, construction of the  restaurant has just begun. It was a long way from its first opening. Since, it was  a small business restaurant, I found it intriguing to see the whole process of the  start-up. So, I proposed to help manage the start-up by negotiating with the  business owner. The owner counted on me and handed over the entire project  for me handle. From exterior & interior designing to managing sales and  stocking kitchen & food supplies, I had to manage everything and time was  running out. I had been informed that only 8 months had been remaining in the  first opening. Knowing it was not a one-man job, I decided to take on the  challenge to gain experience.

Name: Bilal Sajid

The visualization aspect of mind-mapping helps to keep  track of tasks/activities and the order of completion for each of them.  (Mind mapping) I initiate by placing the main task in center and then divide it  into sub-tasks. Sub-tasks are ordered in hierarchically. I start working on the  lowest order activities and work my way up from there. Reflection – Stakeholder Mind Mapping

By Melvin Lu

Challenge

As a Senior Manager of a Shared Service Center(SSC) I work with multiple stakeholders for multiple  countries across Asia Pacific region for an FMCG company. Challenge on hand was the Quality of  operations that I run. Stakeholder including business in the country were really not happy with the  Finance Services delivered and constantly saw SSC as a task oriented team which really impacted the  morale of the employees who felt too disengaged with what they did. With the dissatisfaction of the  business it really impacted future projects which had a lot of dependency on upstream processes to  achieve the larger Finance Strategies. Missing deadlines on implementing/executing Finance Strategies  was not an option and we as a team were given 2 Quarters only to turn it around. Hence it was decided  to come up with a Design Thinking strategy which is scientific and can provide results too.

Selection

With several tools at our disposal, we as a team felt Mind Mapping for our stakeholders would be the  key tool to understand the AS IS situation and current minds of our stakeholders. We also understood it  was a ‘what is’ phase and not a ‘what if’. And since we had multiple stakeholders it was important for us  as a team to look for patterns through this tool.

Application

I invited all of my Direct Reports who are SSC country managers and managed these stakeholders  directly day in day out. Since we were 16 of us so we formed 4 groups of 4 each. I took my team through  the broad Design Thinking process for the first 1 hour and then discussed the tool we specifically chose  for the same. We assigned a white board to each group and gave 45 minutes for them to list out what  feedback we received from our stakeholders in terms of what they think, what they feel, what they say  and what they do. Another 15 minutes for the group to summarize and structure their exercise for a  teach back to the other 3 groups.

Design Thinking Assignment - Reflection

Dieter Berger

Challenge

My challenge is to convince people to reduce their organic waste in their houses

by descomposting it. We are developing an electrical domestic composter which is able

to reduce the organic waste, generated in the kitchen, in between 60% and 80% and it

takes no more than 72 hours. The compost generated by our device has got a lot of

nutrients and can be used for growing plants and trees. Our challenge is to create the

habit of decomposting organic waste in every house we can, and show that it can be

extremely important for our planet and vey handful to use on gardens and organic food

growers.

Selection

Storytelling is the chosen tool. It is able to cause a really good impact on the

people, helping them to visualize the importance and benefits of decomposting their

organic waste at home. By adressing them individually they will be able to feel that they

are really important in this process and they are trully a part of it. We want every

individual to be inspired through the current scenario, making them feel that they are

contributing for the environment’s future by reducing their waste, and in exchange they

can get the best nutrients for their plants and maybe grow their own food. The chosen

tool can help to make everyone feel and understand the purpose of the product.

Application

By using the storytelling tool we were able to tell our customers what is the real

impact of organic waste to our planet. Showing the percentages of organic waste

generated in the last decade by humans caused a huge impact and could make them

feel responsible for it too. Bringing this responsability to them and making them to feel

as part of it gave us a big chance to introduce our product and consequently the habit

of decomposting their organic waste at home. Some of them got really excited to be

parto f something with a bigger purpose, other enjoyed a lot the idea of producing their

text:
John Estrada

December 6, 2021

Design Thinking Reflection

Mind Mapping

Challenge:  Creating a comprehensive multi-year strategic plan that captures new value- driven company goals and objectives that allow for business growth and  innovation is a difficult task. The level of complexity increases when prioritizing  which objectives offer the most value while minimizing risk; based on stakeholder  input, market data, employee feedback, and past lessons learned.

Selection:  To better understand the individual business components (gaps, past targets, key  performance indicators, etc) and align them with the collective stakeholder input  (data, key lessons etc) I selected mind mapping as my preferred tool.

Application:  Mind mapping was instrumental in my ideation sessions held over several days  with stakeholders across my company. Each session was 2 hrs long (3 sessions  total) with key stakeholders participating in all 3 sessions. The goal of my  ideation exercises was to:   1. Level 0: Start with the organization’s mission, vision, value at the center circle

2. Level 1: Itemize the various departments/business units that are parts of the  organization as a whole

3. Level 2: Create the following groups for each department: 1. Staff 2.  Technology 3. Process

4. Level 3: Create the following categories: 1. Challenges 2. Successes 3.  Future Goals then place stakeholder input, data, insight within each bucket

5. Draw connector lines for all dependencies and/or similarities between  departments

Insight:  Having the ability to visualize the various components of my organization and  showing how each department and their challenges, successes, and goals were  directly connected gave all stakeholders that participated in the exercise much  more clarity on the current-state as well as where they needed to be for the  future-state. Challenge and Selection

A key area of my job scope is to develop step-by-step digitalization guides for the  small and medium enterprises (SMEs) of various industries and sectors. The SMEs  are important to Singapore, collectively employing 70% of Singapore’s workforce and  account for almost half of Singapore’s GDP. Hence, digitalisation of SMEs can have  a profound impact on Singapore’s economy.

However, SMEs generally lack the technical know-how and find it difficult to divert  resources to digital transformation. Hence, it is important to develop a guide to make  going digital simple for the SMEs.

To develop a guide that is most suitable to the needs of the SMEs, I plan to conduct  a series of workshops with various SMEs, and use the Mind Mapping tool to  generate insights, collect information and create design criteria.

Application

In the first workshop that I conduct, I will gather information from the SMEs to  understand their experiences in digitalization. I will get each SME to fill up a form to  provide me with information regarding their digital transformation journey, such as:

-  Current mode business operations (manual vs digital)

-  Areas of improvement for business operations

-  Challenges that SMEs when digitalizing

-  Obstacles that are stopping them from digitalizing

In the second workshop, with the information consolidated, I will set up a room with  walls filled with the common problems faced by the SMEs in the industry and the  SMEs can go around the room to understand the problems and think about how  digitalization can come in to help solve the problems.

Reflection on Learning Launch

Jorge Bernardo, 18.05.2021

Challenge

As a head of remote entry agency for clients using wallets for a popular Moroccan bank, my main  goal is to ensure that the services ordered by a client are successfully activated. However, successful  integration is only guaranteed if the customer carries out certain steps himself.

These steps are emailed to the customer after placing the order. Although these emails are very  personal and detailed, we noticed that customers often did not complete the steps and as a result  the onboarding did not always go as smoothly which also resulted in a drop in the customer  satisfaction.

Selection

Due to several possibilities to solve this problem, we decided to launch a learning launch. The  learning launch tool allowed us to test very quickly and at minimal cost if we were on the right track  or if we needed to completely change our thinking. Even if the result is not what you want, the loss is  minimal because the investment is low. A learning launch is indeed always beneficial: you quickly  know if you are on the right track with something or if you need to go back to the drawing board and  formulate a new or refined hypothesis based on the information gathered.

Application

Our guess was that the text of the mail might have been too long and people hadn't bothered to read  it. Based on this hypothesis, we decided to create a digital milestone plan. We were very excited  about the launch as we were hoping to see a lot of people click on the stage map. We did notice,  however, that the click-through rate was very low.

Despite the fact that all team members have the same academic background, we all have  different interests in different areas of our major and therefore different approaches to  solving problems: a part of the team is more focused on software development, while the  rest is more interested on hardware development. This was a great area of opportunity for  our project, as it gave us the possibility of having a broader repertoire of possible solutions.

The limitations of our project were based on time: 9 months to complete the project and a  maximum budget of $ 500 usd.

Name:

Carolina Finetti

Date:

February 15th, 2021

Challenge

My name is Carolina Gomez, I am currently studying Engineering in Development and

Innovation, where the application of design thinking is crucial for my career to know

how to create a new product idea or even optimizing one that already exists. The

reason why I started this course is because one of our final projects on the subject of

“Innovation and experimentation of creative processes” is to design furniture made

out of cardboard. This sustainable furniture must help the elderly to carry out

different activities, such as putting on shoes, cutting their toenails, moving around,

doing flexibility exercises, and other simple activities that may be difficult for them

due to their age. Thanks to the different steps of the design thinking process, I will be

able to successfully create these innovative cardboard furniture and empathize with

the user in the best possible way.

Selection

I believe that using the visualization tool allowed me to get to the main purpose of

the project, to empathize with the user through innovation. As Angela Weyes said in

NAME: Ignacia Hernandez   Roll No. : 932353568953  Product : Hair Dresser

Questionnaire

(INPUT REQUIRED)  ❖ Electricity

➢ Does it work at home based output voltage?

■ Yes, it works on normal input current present at home.

➢ Would it also work on a dc input current?

■ No, as we have given the option of working on chargable batteries, dc

input current wont work.

❖ Battery

➢ Is it rechargeable or one time battery ?

■ We have given the option of rechargeable batteries.

(DRYING MODES)

❖ Hot

➢ Is the hot mode safe?

■ Yes, we have taken into consideration of the damage, thereby giving a

lower temperature .

➢ What is hot mode for?

■ It is for fast drying.

❖ Cold

➢ What is cold mode for?

■ It is to set your hair in the style you wanted it to be.

➢ Can it dry my hair?

■ The main purpose is sor styling and not for drying.

(PERFORMANCE)

❖ Fast dry

➢ What is exactly fast dry?

■ This feature is mainly for the people with long hair , for whom drying the

hair takes alot of time.

➢ How is that carried out?

■ There is a separate clip available to ensure more air outlet.

❖ Styling

➢ Why is there a separate feature for styling?

■ We wanted to give a wide range of styling features for different kinds of

hair styles.

➢ How is this carried out?

■ For different kinds of hair we have given hair clips to style accordingly.

(VARIANTS)

❖ Colour

➢ How many colors are available?

■ There are a total of 5 available right now.

➢ Are there different models for men and women?

■ Yes, according to their needs we have.

❖ Price

➢ What is the price range?

■ Price varies from 3Thousand to 8Thousand rupees.

➢ Y the difference in the price ?

■ Different models have different output power levels, accordingly the

variations have been given.

Using Storytelling Tool for Student Counseling

 Challenge:

I am a faculty of a university and I have to deal with many types of psycho-social problems of the  students. Though my job is mostly academic, still being a mentor and adviser, I need to address  these issues. Students often do not open up at their first interaction. Their symptoms of disturbance  are usually expressed through their attitude in the classroom and other interactions. Some students  are irregular and remain unmindful in the class, others are ill mannered or rough in conduct. Some  students seems stressful and tired and even suffer from psychosomatic physical sickness. The  university has appointed a full time psychologist, with a separate office and facilities, who provides  Psycho-Social Counseling services for the students. But the students have some stigma regarding  communicating the psychologist as they think it will isolate them from others and they will be  considered mentally ill. Hence they sometimes share their problems with teachers and course  advisers. But the problem is teachers can listen to them with empathy and suggest some general  solutions, but they are not expert person for professional counseling. So, the challenge for the  teachers are to detect the students who need help and convince them to communicate the psycho  social counselor.

 Selection:

Just as this course resources mentioned, - through a good story, we could simply convey a message  that has logic. And also that a good story creates a cause and it ignites and unites people to solve  a bigger problem. Keeping the same spirit in mind, I have chosen storytelling as a tool to convince  the students to open up and address their need of counselling and eventually communicate the  Psycho-Social Counselor of the university for better solution of their mental anxiety.

Done by Ahmed Figo

Tool that applied : Storytelling

▪  Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a powerful tool that are applicable in various situation of our daily life,  ergo it is the tool that I applied all the times. As Team leader in Media Player of Digital Dialogues, I sometimes face some obstacles in how to deliver the training to the  whole team because of the 24hours shifts that won’t allow me to meet all of them in the  same time. Besides, I also faced challenges of how to align all these messages and  make sure that all updates are well received and applied on our daily work.

I choose to apply storytelling as it can get insight into users, build empathy and reach  them effectively. I often create personas to represent target users and add conflict to  stories that reflect their user journeys and problems.

One of the reasons is through crafting stories, we can better understand what users  want from a solution. Good stories always captivate the team. In user experience   design, if all management team use storytelling throughout the design process to  ensure that all work focuses on the teams’ needs and the value that company want to  give those users. After completing design research to understand your users’ needs and  desires, you use your insights to tell a story about who your users are, what they need  and how you’ll provide that. This story makes it easy for everyone involved in the project  to empathize with the users and ensure that their work matches the story. Having a story  throughout your project means visualizing the design at the end of the launching  process is also straightforward, as you already know exactly which story to tell to show  how your training and updates provides value.

My storytelling will involve all my team in my section and my mission is to reach all of  them and deliver the same message to all my team.

Guddu Singh Reflection of Design Tool Application

Challenge and Selection:

I was working on a project and needed to communicate the magnitude of the discrepancy  between men and women in consulting. I needed to show how gender representation numbers  change over time as you progress into the higher levels of consulting. This was going to do into a  powerpoint deck that later made the case for offering unique networking opportunities for  women. I knew that, in order for the Ask later to be strongest, the audience really needed to feel  the disparity that exists at the highest levels of consulting.

I was deciding between using visualization and story-telling as a means of really connecting with  the audience and making this part of the presentation impactful. Ultimately, I decided to focus on  the Visualization tool. I chose this for a couple reasons: firstly, I thought of the saying “a picture  speaks a thousand words.” I knew that if people saw not just the numbers but the numbers  reflected in visual form, that would be more impactful. Secondly, I this tools is one I am less  comfortable with, so this also felt like a prime opportunity or practice.

Application and Approach

I ended up taking the data in Microsoft excel and spent time thinking about different ways to  visualize the data. I ended up deciding to start with showing a pie that starts out showing 50%  men and 50% women at entry level roles. I then removed respective parts of the pie as we moved  up the ranks to finally leave just 17% of the Partners were women. At the same time, the portion  of the pie that represented men keeps growing at each level up the ranks. So we start out with  parity and end up showing how the disparity looks by the end.

Design Thinking for Innovation Final Project 1/26/2017

Fabio Sameh

Challenge and Selection: The challenge I would like to review has to do with recruiting potential students to a graduate  advertising program where I work.  We are a small program, only 200 students, and we have a  different way of funding as compared to most graduate programs at public institutions.  Our  operating funds are directly related to the students we can recruit to our program, meaning if we  don’t get 100 students each year, we might not be able to make certain purchases, hold events  or hire new staff or faculty.  Interestingly enough, while our students are highly successful after  graduation (we have a 99% placement rate after 6 months and hold a recruiter fair where almost  300 recruiters come to interview and hire 100 students) we always had a difﬁcult time getting  enough qualiﬁed recruits each year to ﬁll the tracks.  Many times we would only get 190  completed applications where our goal was at least 300.

Clearly there was a disconnect and we were certainly missing something important.  In this  case, we used a form of visualization to try and ﬁgure out what was going on.  We needed a  global view of our data and see the “what is” before we moved to the next steps (of course I did  not know these steps in the names that this course has given them at the time).

Application: As mentioned above, we can get plenty of data from our application process and qualitative  data from our current students as well.  We pulled data from the start of the application  download process where students tell us about themselves, how they heard about us, where  they lived, etc.

We also did a poll of our current students gathering other data that included questions of the  application and acceptance process and their impression of the number of students that apply  versus the 100 that get in. Storytelling is an important design thinking tool. I use it to work with youth in difficulty in a suburben  area of Tunis. Those teenagers have communication difficulties, are aggressive, some of them live in  very difficult situations in families with alcohoolic or unemployed fathers that are violent with them  by assault or rape. Some of them quit their schools and become drug dealers or thieves. These  teenagers need to be empowered by culture, education and art . They need to be more confident in  their future and welth. I spend a lot of time finding ways to improve their circumstances and help  them become good and happy citizens. I work with them helped by some students from different  profiles : art students, ingeneers… We share with those youth stories about our lives to give them  more confidence and help them change ideas about life. We use stories to better understand their  fears, needs and interests.  Those stories help me convince local responsables in the community to  give those youth some facilities to do activities helping them well being.

Course: Design Thinking for Innovation

Student: Randy Sanz

I.  Challenge

I was part of the A.T. Kearney account team for a Consumer Packaged Goods (CPG) customer in Lima, Perú. The  customer needed to implement a process to accelerate the time to market for new products. In order to do so  they needed to include all the steps required, from idea generation, through launch.

The customer had already selected the software they wanted to use which handled the core Product Lifecycle  Management (PLM) and engineering functions.  They wanted us to implement it for them.

As A.T. Kearney, we wanted to provide the customer additional value by proposing a more complete solution and  while doing so, include additional A.T. Kearney products. We needed to include these products in order get internal  approval since we were not allowed to sell and implement a non-A.T. Kearney product in isolation.

Our challenge was to design a solution that brought value to the customer by integrating a specific, third party  software with A.T. Kearney products. This software had never been integrated with the A.T. Kearney platform before.

II.  Selection

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

In my spare time I help the coach of a local Rugby club to improve the game of their youngsters’ team.  The target group consists of 25 kids in an age between 12 and 14 years of age. During last season this  team won only 1 game in a tournament (out of 20 games played) and this clearly brought frustration  and dissatisfaction in the young players. The team coach was worried that many kids would drop out  from the team and look for a different sport. The local club isn’t a very wealthy one, and their success  is founded on building senior players from within the club. Losing young players today has a high  impact on the future of the club and their senior team. Our challenge was to design a new way of  training kids, aimed to improve their game and make them stay with our club for long time.

Selection

In the What is? phase, we looked at the current reality and collected some statistics around errors  occurred during games (like ball handling, missed tackles, missed catches etc.). We also focused on  the errors occurred during the training sessions, and collected interviews with different kids (across  different clusters, like as an example: by position, by maturity level, by fitness level, …). These  interviews were aimed to highlight problems of the kids with different fundamentals of the game.  Along with a colleague, we then selected Mind Mapping tool in order to explore the data we collected  and to identify common threads. Through Mind Mapping we were able to identify some common  patterns in how kids learn sports (observation, listening to, emulation, …) and translate them into  design criteria for the future training sessions.

Reflection -  Learning Launch

By Joe Ferrara

Challenge

As a member of a team who manage a large portfolio of critical IT projects for a big national company, I’m  invited regularly to collect the needs from my clients, launch and manage new projects, and especially to  meet the deadlines, the budget and requirements. It’s such as successive challenges I faced in my business  life, especially when client’s requirements and needs changes continuously. This is the reason why I was  always wondering the following: When I have a challenge, how do I approach it? In reality, even in our  personal life, we face many problems and we go through different challenges every day. We solve most  of them every day too.  The most important thing I learned from this “Design Thinking” course is that we  should resist the temptation to jump directly to a solution and that the value is in realizing that we can  create something that can help people make their lives easier.

Selection

There are several tools and techniques of understanding the needs of a user, client or a customer, but in  my point of view, Learning Launch is the most effective way. To rephrase “Learning Launch”, it is a manner  of creating a minimum viable product that let customers or users test their key assumptions and get an  answer to the big question “What if?”. The point is to start creating a minimum and test it, then we quickly  get more feedbacks and clearer ideas that led us to a prototype. We could also iterate this operation as  much as we need until we get sufficient prototypes, and finally choose the appropriate prototype for our  project or product.

DESIGN THINKING COURSE  Suman Salim – Universidad San Francisco de Quito Honduras  Reflection Asignment

1. Tool: MIND MAPPING

2. Challenge:

Implementatio of biosefaty measures for the new incoporation to face-to-face  academic activity.

3. Selection:

It will allow to clarify ideas in a simple way, organize and connect ideas visually.   I can include a brainstorming with my team and discuss the ideas in a group, so I can  organize the information.

4. Application:

  We identify the needs

  Each member of the team made contributions to each need

  We locate the ideas of the contributions according to each need

  We made the connections to identify priorities

  We define the actions according to the prioritized needs

  We prepare a work plan for implementation

5. Insight:

  We were able to represent the ideas, concepts and tasks, linking it to our main  project.

  We link the different elements contributed by each team member, using them as  key points to address specific ideas.

  We develop the ideas starting from the important project point, according to the  objective of defining the main actions to be implemented for the implementation  of the necessary measures for the incorporation of face-to-face academic activity  on campus and headquarters.

  We achieve greater clarity in the identification of needs and actions relevant to the  project.

  We organize information in a better way.

  It allowed us to better plan the activities to be implemented in a work plan.

6. Approach:

Define more clearly the scope of the project in stages, to identify the needs and  required actions.

text:
Cynthia Chatel

Example Reflection – Visualization

Challenge and Selection

Visualization is used in my daily work life to communicate and organize thought  in different ways. Using visual thinking enhances the way we see things. Since  working at a publishing company, I use this approach with workers and clients.

During a project at work a client wanted to rearrange his entire branding  strategy one week before his launch, a project we were working on for almost  five weeks. We delivered the first draft of the project which he approved and  then a few weeks after he was unhappy, so we were tasked in redoing the  entire project over in less than a week.

Application

I began the entire process by first doodling his new changes, then we  compared it with other successful designs from this and other clients, comparing  feedback and feedforwards. Then we put all our ideas together on the drawing  board.

With this strategy the client was ultimately thrilled with the new plan, including  the new ideas that were included.

Insight and Approach

I believe we became overconfident with our first ideas on the project at the  time, and that I did not check in with the client until almost the last week. I have  now learned to always check in with clients on a weekly basis.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation – Karim Elnazer

Challenge:

During Coronavirus time here in Dubai March 2020, am a father of a family of 4 with my wife and 2  children (13 and 10). As a family we used to go out a lot and we also had very active night life  without the kids. With almost everything closed in the city, as a family we had many ideas on what  we can do during this time we have remote schooling and working from home. All ideas had some  levels of risks (e.g. going out with bicycles or inviting neighbors so increase the possibility of virus  exposure) or investments (e.g. paying for more subscribed TV channels) so needed to prioritize.

Selection:

The tool I selected was Learning Launch to filter and prioritize each idea.

Please watch the video lecture of Bernd Kersten (week 4) for best explanation for the tool.

Application:

I made a family time where I explained to my wife and kids the process. I focused on Data and our  assumptions and confirmation biases. I focused on finding out under what circumstances a certain  idea could be a bad one, and looking for discomforting fact. My son (10y.o.) played a great role in  this being the most skeptic of the family 😊

Insight:

One great insight when we look at the facts that “must be true” was discussing some assumptions  that we will be in this lockdown for only 2 or 3 weeks. Some more pessimistic scenarios can take  more time, so the ideas have to be sustainable.

Approach:

One of things that I could have done differently is to decide to do this regularly, or invite more  friends/neighbors/family via video conference to participate.

Visualisation tool for drone development

For our ﬁst visualisation tool we started with everyone in the team putting up their ideas on a  board in picture, word and design form. This lead to lots of discussions about diﬀerent types of  idea and brought up new ideas which we also added to the board. Our  challenge was to pick out which to leave out and focus on whats important and doing so in a  group, everyone is diﬀerent and cant agree on everything.

One of the most important tool and the relevant tool I learnt is  the visualization tool (i.e. the visual thinking) to manage my  stakeholders to understand the extend and depth of the pain  points we are trying to eliminate in our project. It allows us to think in a non – verbal way and  access parts of the brain, our creativity. Most design thinkers call  visualization as “mother of all design tools”, because they are  used in every stage of the design thinking process.  Visualization  is equal part listening, thinking and drawing. Listening is the  input, thinking is the processing and drawing is the output. These  three skills work together equally in understanding complexity,  visualization outcomes to create new possibilities

The previous process was fraught with  high turn around time, decreased customer satisfaction.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Diana Vazquez

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling in my field is a tool often used to connect with people all around the world who often  share an idealization of a dream or a story itself. Everyone has a dream, many people dream about  opening their own business themselves.

I have came across a lot of small business who were opened to the public with the main goal of  connecting with people and share their story (aside the obvious side of making a business). I find  these kind of processes very noticeable among the new trend of opening Little cafés or food  service places, people frequently visit these places no just because of the producto (food and  drinks), but because of the differential experience each of these business can give them.

Application

Nowadays people use social media to reach out to a broader public. It’s a very effective tool to  continue the path of storytelling itself. For example, i like to “hunt” for new places to visit every  time on social media, watching their Instagram feed can tell me so much more about the place  before i even get the opportunity to visit it, but it also makes my curiosity grow.

There’s a little patisserie that opened 3 months ago in the city, the owner used to make bread and  cakes for other cafés, quite famous around “the scene”, but she never got to open her own  business until recently. Al lof this was discovered by a simple approach and conversation, so I  wondered, how many people could feel motivated by her story and will her story make her own  brand seem more approachable and not just a single new business in town?

Insight

Using social media as a tool for storytelling can tell me so much not only about the place or their  producto, but their story itself. Has anyone tried to interview these entrepeneurs about the  challenges and dreams they had in order to get to that place were they finally were able to open  their business to public? Challenge

I was in mixed feelings when I was offered to lead a Non-profit organization. First and foremost, I did not  have previous experience with non-profits, second the whole management team members were looking  forward to transition their responsibilities using this leadership change as an opportunity. Not to  mention, all management roles were voluntary and last three years membership was declining 20%  consistently and fundraiser programs were not attracting new donors. I was really called to turn around  this failing organization by the Chairman and Founder who had emotional ties with this organization.  The challenge in day one was to recruit new management team members, understand the cause of  member reduction and lack of attracting donors to the fundraiser programs.

Covid 19 was in the news and spreading. The mission of the organization was so relevant to create  impact in multiple countries if we could use this as an opportunity to energize this sleepy yet promising  organization.

Selection, Application and Insight

While I was recruiting my management team, I must confess that my first selection was this course. I  thought, design thinking methods and the tools will help. I decided to join this class as the rest of the  team members had day jobs. They were okay for me to share with them weekly class learnings. This  turned into kind of fun way of working and started to create bonding and motivated everyone to focus  on problems at hand.

Once the management team were fully in-place, it was my second week in the course. It was also our  second zoom meeting with management team where we started to use visualization tool to draw  pictures of stake holders and identify questions which will highlight their unmet needs. text:
FINAL ASSIGMENT IN DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION.

I am Muhammad Shafiq and I joined healthcare industry in 2001.

I am going to discuss and share my experience in this assignment.

Challenge:

In one hospital we have introduced 4D ultrasound specifically for ANC patients.  Unfortunately we were failing to boost it as per our expectations and there was  no progression. Management decided to review the activities and planning to  redesign the marketing plan to attract target customers.

Tool selection:

(Referrence video : WEEK 4 Rossi)

We discover through survey that people are not aware about the benefits of what  we are delivering to them .So, we decided to create awareness workshop and  showing live images to them that they could understand.

For this activity we planned to use LEARNING LAUNCH Tool to achieve the goals.

We allocate one area near gynaecology department and giving handouts, lectures  and also first session of ULTRASOUND free of cost to show the difference  between traditional and 4Dultrasound. Also announced discounts on subsequent  visit in order to bring patients back to clinic.

Insights:

In this learning launch where we deliver ideal environment and deliver service to  customer results into tremendous increase in the number of patients and success  comes where patients visit in subsequent visit that could help in rating the  success rate.It also results in the morbidity rate of infants because of timely  treatment during pregnancy.  We got success and implement the same activity to help in promoting other  departments.

Aproach:(Visualiztion)

In future I would prefer to select Visualization tool because it is the best tool to  transform idea from mind to real world and the easiest and comprehensive way  to communicate whatever comes to your mind.

Design Thinking: Final Assignment    Rhiannon Karim

Katia Rania

Design Thinking

Peer Reviewed Final Assignment

Submitted by: Rhiannon Karim

Challenge

I have recently completed a move, and the week-long process still haunts me. After

completing the modules of this course, it became apparent to me that design thinking can be

applied to all aspects of my life. My first chance to apply my knowledge occurred during my

move. Let me take you back to three years ago, when I was purchasing my stereo system. I had

met a young salesman; whose passion was sound systems. I believe he has four personally built

systems in his home to date. After two hours, I left the store with a completely personalized

package, a small map of connections he drew up for me, and an increasing sense of dread

growing in my stomach. I have never built a stereo system on my own and here I was walking

away with 40 ft. of copper wiring that I needed to personally splice and use to create connectors.

Fast forward five hours. I am sitting on the floor in front of my television completely distraught

and defeated: I could not get my system to work. I had to phone an expert the next day to

complete the installation for a fee.

During my present day move, I was determined to complete the re-installation of my

system independently. I wish I could say I had the foresight to create my own mind map of the

connections I had made, but who thinks of that before learning about Design Thinking? Not me.

My boyfriend connected the wires to my speakers, turned on the receiver, double checked the

cables, and waited for sound. None came. As he headed back to work from lunch, I set to work

on conquering my system. I did not want to experience the failure I did three years ago, and I

was determined to be successful. Before immediately jumping to frustration, I decided to try the

design thinking approach because I needed a creative, systematic approach to a challenging

problem that I was facing.

Peer-graded Assignment : Storytelling

By Shivam Giri

Challenge and Selection:

Storytelling is the perfect tool for my work, which helps me share and link my lived experience with my work. Here is tory of my work.

There is a saying, ‘go where the problems are’ which tells people from outside to come and work for the development of locals. But we stand to be different by saying ‘build the leaders where the problems are.’ Because we believe in local leaders to address local

problems not outsiders. It only will lead to the goal of what we say sustainable

development. Hence we aim to build development leadership among youth from

grassroots to help them become actors of their own development. We recognize that

higher education as a crucial tool to cultivate leadership among them. At MAYA firm we support them to pursue higher education in premier institutes of higher education,

especially in the field of humanities and social sciences which would help them to realize their potentials and build their capacities to start a career in the development sector and eventually become development leaders. Our target group is those who are largely underrepresented in higher education which are the first generation learners,

attended schools in Marathi or vernacular medium, rural youth coming from

educationally and socially underprivileged families including dalit, adivasis and nomadic tribes. Due to lack of awareness, aspiration, reference, mentorship and guidance they remained underrepresented in higher education. Their representation is even worse in premier institutes like IITs, IIMs, TISS and Central Universities etc. We want to send more and more underprivileged students to premier institutes of higher education and enable them to address their own problems.

Example reﬂection - storytelling by Sara Perez

Challenge & Selection

I use the design tool storytelling because I feel it can connect business with people. Not only

is it useful for making new strategies and brand positioning, but also to create trust and

loyalty with our customers. In my process, ﬁrst, I deﬁne the business story in three parts:

introduction, confrontation, and resolution. Second, investigate who the audience is, where

they come from and what they need, so I can conceptualize brand values and improve its

communication channels. If I don’t have tools like that, I only create empty stories without

purpose.

Application

I use storytelling to create content for a brand on Instagram. First, I have to do research and

meet the client because I need to ask a lot about new ideas and know what needs to be done

to conceptualize its brand values. I seek to develop content that highlights human factors

and the brand's tone of voice. It has to be sincere and short copy as my aim is to connect

emotionally with customers and not bore them into the process. It has to contain the

inspirational idea that there is a person with a difﬁculty and tell how they overcame it. Once

the writing is ﬁnished, I read it out loud to hear how it sounds; I also ask my friends how it

sounds and what resonates with them. After making the necessary corrections, I publish it

and measure how the audience responds to see the impact it created.

Insight & Approach

Texts created from storytelling improve the communication of brands because they make a

more natural and empathetic relationship with the audience. Society is looking for this type

of connection in a globalised world full of companies looking to sell their services or

products. The important thing is to stand out from the rest and create a brand tone of voice

Reflection – Storytelling

By: Fabian Jones

Challenge:

As part of my role as facilitator and team coach, I had the opportunity to work with people in  charge of customer service at the cable transport company “ZOlie” in Bolivia.

The challenge it was based in developing new behaviors that generate greater quality in customer  service for this transport service. The managers identified the need to give a magical touch to the  perspective of such a unique form of transport. Users travel through the sky, suspended by air,  with the most spectacular view of the city, however, the routine of the care process they receive  and the lack of attitude they experience, take away the importance of the service and, in many  cases, it was identified that the flow of use of the means of transport suffered a considerable  decrease.

Selection:

One tool that was very useful in the process was Storytelling, since it was perfectly suited to the  logic of highlighting film-worthy situations. Reinforce the way of telling magnificent and unusual  experiences. Share experiences from a different perspective, highlighting situations that go  unnoticed and subtract magic from the adventure of touring the city from the sky.

“I think the narrative helps leaders in terms of strategy because it makes it simple, it can be  counted, it gives color, life, character and plot to the strategy and allows the production line  worker to the vice president of marketing to understand equally. What we are trying to do.”  (Fabian Jones)

Application:

The tool was applied from two perspectives. The first had to do with a message to open the  sessions by the company's top manager, who, through video, told the story of flying over the city  from a creative perspective.
