December 24, 2016

Desiree Mazza Newtown, CT USA

Coursera : Design Thinking for Innovation Jan. 2, 2017

Challenge and Selection

Coming from a family who were Joseph Campbell gurus, members of AA and  writers, Storytelling is a revealing tool of connection, information, and shared  insight.

After 40 years in management in Finance and Accounting for Vessel owning  and operating companies, I joined a small Maritime Asset investment company.  This was the first time I was on the other side of the deal. Instead of asking for  investments for operating Vessels, I was now on the financer investor side. The  president had called for an off site conference to work on our deal closing  process and ask all of us to contribute new ideas that could improve closing  portfolio deals. He asked for each employee to contribute 3 ideas no matter  how crazy the ideas were.

Application

As a new employee, I decided that for me to contribute anything of value, I  needed to have more information about the company’s deal procedures. Like  any small busy office, free time to explore is rare, except lunchtime. Most days  we have a choice to eat at our desk, go out or eat in the conference room. The  off- site conference was 3 weeks away, and I needed to get as much  background information as possible, so I started asking anyone to come have  lunch with me in the conference room, that I didn’t want to mess up the  paperwork on my desk. Slowly within the first week, most of the 15 employees  were having lunch together from 30 minutes to an hour in the conference  room.  I put together several prompt questions in my head to encourage  employees to tell their experiences on past deals. Whenever there was a lull in  the conversation, I would use one of my prompts, i.e. “What was the best or  worst deal you ever had, and followed up with what made it so great or  horrible?”. Reflection – Visualization (Antonio Bellafiore)

Challenge   Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.    A significant part of my work as a corporate knowledge manager involves publishing books for different  internal audiences. We’re a small team and we manage everything from content development to  research and writing to editing and layout to pre-press production and distribution.     Because we cover a broad range of topics, this presents an opportunity to work with other teams,  sometimes from other affiliate companies as well as external resource persons.    And so the challenge posed by collaborating with others outside the team (especially those not familiar  with publishing) is how to engage them to be active contributors, perhaps with the same level of  enthusiasm that we ourselves have. There are many approaches we take, but I believe one of the most  critical and valuable methods is visualization.    Selection  In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you selected it for your  challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).    If you’re an avid reader, you may appreciate that the visual aspects of books are as important as the  copy or narrative: the choice of fonts, the space the text takes up on a page, how data is presented in  charts and infographics, illustrations that pique your interest to read on.      From our production point of view, visualization happens at inception and is very valuable when it  comes to bringing other people to the table and to get them not only involved but also invested in and  excited to see a book project through.    And so the flowcharts in this course resonated with me, as they traced not only process but also  provided insights on the implications or cause-and-effect of how might one action and another and  another lead to the either the desired outcome or failure (not entirely a bad thing, i.e.., failure). Design thinking, course assignment      Esraa Han

Challenge  I have organized a lot of workshops to understand the current challenges of my customers. Typically,  customers have a need to solve challenges in their current environment (process inefficiency, customer  attrition, operating model issues etc.) which I have approached with tools such as current state mapping,  root cause identification and process analysis. Avion approached me with a new kind of ask: how  can we ensure we are relevant to our customers in 20 years? How can we ensure we understand our  customers’ needs before they do? To be clear, there was nothing wrong with Avion’s business:  their customers were happy, they were among top 5 players in their industry, their product was good and  served its purpose. Tools that I typically use would not work here, as Avion wanted to project into  the future. We needed a new way of approaching their problem.

The main challenge for us was the culture and current mindset of Avion, which was very much  focused on their current state of business. Avion’s employees are solution engineers who are used  to solving current technical challenges for their customers. Avion has huge amount of customer  data, market reports and segment analysis available. They use quantitative methodologies to analyze  customers and their profitability. Avion’s organisation is scattered across several locations with  stakeholders who have never worked together. We needed a way for these stakeholders to really focus on  customer needs and to start projecting what their customer needs might look like in the future.

Selection  We needed a way to help Avion to start projecting into the future, something they had not done  before. We needed a simple, projective technique and process to help the skeptical engineers to put  themselves into their customers shoes. Reflection - Bekim Campanelli - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection    I currently work on innovation projects for the real estate market. And in our projects, data

structuring, process evaluation and journey were crucial to finding solutions to the complex

problems experienced by property owners.    We used the Design Thinking methodology to understand in depth what were the pains and

frictions that homeowners felt during the sale or lease negotiation process. In this process

we started by conducting open interviews with different groups and people. This work

generated a lot of information: testimonials, feelings, comments, perceptions, experiences,

etc. And everything needed to be evaluated and mined to generate the insights to continue

the process of ideation of prototypes to improve the customer experience.    At that time, our team used the Mind Map and CSD Matrix model to see the opportunities we

had to work with projects on the client's journey.    Application    I used Google Forms to develop surveys with the homeowners to assess the points of

friction and understand their feelings, needs and pains regarding real estate transactions.    The survey responses were organized in Excel to work on mining and grouping the insights.

This information was dynamically discussed with the leaders of the company's customer

contact sectors, where we had the objective of filling out the CSD Matrix to find priorities for

execution and open questions for further research.    This information was evaluated by the Design Thinking and Innovation team to build the

Mind Map of the homeowners, exploring each point of contact, each insight, each need. With

this structure, the prototyping team was able to understand the Jobs to be Done of the

property owners and create the new operation thesis of real estate businesses.    This work provided the creation of an intelligence platform about property owners where we

C1 - Internal use

Mind Mapping

By: Blanca Villa

Challenge & Selection:

As part of a marketing team that is involve in the innovation process of new products for a makeup  brand we have the challenge to recognize our consumer but also to have the ability to segment  them by specific target groups to effectively respond to their needs, taking into account that we  have a high channel distribution and sometimes manage and create new product for our portfolio  is difficult because we don’t have a clear overview of our specific consumer or persona for each  product.

To solve this and to have answers of the personas profiles that we might take into account in the  design process of new products and for our go to market strategy, I’ve selected the mind mapping  tool, that let us find patterns and insights through journey, ethnography profile, data and  visualization. For the exercise we made some focus group with customers that share some  socioeconomic characteristics and make some interviews based on a journey that was required  prior to the session, this to learn from each other experiences but also to have a process of  discover about their needs in terms of makeup products based on their routine, learn more about  what are they looking for in the makeup market and found out key elements to solve our market  boundaries  in  terms  of  correct  distribution  channel  and  portfolio  strategy.

Application

STORYTELLING ON THE COFFEE MARKET

My name is Mynor Garcia Lopez. I graduated from Kasetsart University Laboratory School, the  Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, in 2011. I've worked in several designations in some of the companies  in Indonesia after graduated my Bachelor's degree. My first experience after a fresh graduate was  a teacher in a secondary school in Indonesia; at the same time, I've managed the curriculum in  school as one of my designations as a vice principal. In 2012 I moved to the humanitarian  organizations, and I've worked in the education department to manage 500 people in leading 19  colleges in Indonesia from Sumatra to Papua. Since then, I learned many things in leadership, and  I'm always sure my capacity should be building better since then. Three years later, I moved to  form humanitarian organizations to travel and tourism company in Indonesia. For one year, I  managed the sales as a sales and marketing manager. Since then, also, I've learned about how to  drive sales and market the product to the people. It's also one of the numerous travel agencies in  Indonesia that made me confident to work.    It's been fascinating to me about to know how myself learning in various skills from education to  marketing in school companies and organizations. I've also joined several humanitarian works  overseas in Turkey and some of the neighbouring countries to learn more about other skills, as I'm  sure learning has never endings long as we have the passion for doing other things. Hussain Mohammed (ITALY)

January 5rd 2019

Design Thinking for Process review

Challenge

I work in an aerospace company, in particular inside customer support and training department and my  responsibility is the exploration and development of new service solutions to generate new business as full  service provider. In the last two years the company has focused its attention on the digital services for  which me and my colleagues has started a dedicated project. After reinforcing the digital foundations and  current available digital tools (to deliver new digital services), we have focused on the change management  and training stream in order to create the correct mindset in the company and proceed with an extensive  review of the internal processes. The population of the training has involved six hundred colleagues, on top  of which we have selected twenty-five change agents, so called evangelists, to create a community that,  leveraging on the sponsorship of senior executives, can disseminate a digital transformation. In 2014, we  did six sessions for our evangelists starting from a preliminary understanding of the major digital streams  that our top management is investing on (digital roadmap), and then the creation of subgroups, whose  focus is the change of a subprocess, related to the digital roadmap, that can benefit from digital solutions.  We tried to expand what our evangelists feel important, as well as top management consider to be  inefficient or problematic and be improved adopting digital solutions. The project included the possibility to  interview customers of different product segments and different geographies and have dedicated  workshop with other companies from similar businesses and close markets. The tool we applied is learning  launch in workshop five in December 2020.

In the first workshop we provided the overall digital roadmap and framework on which company wants to  commit on; a brief illustration of the major achievements

text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge:

My challenge is linked to the concept of “what is the nature tourism?” I would like to develop  an innovative and added value tourism project linked to nature but, I do not have any specific  background or job experience linked to tourism. So, I have been searching and reading a lot of  information about what is nature tourism, trying to read online forums about this subject to  get some inputs from real nature tourists.

Selection:

To address main challenge I selected the Mind Mapping tool. This tool allows me to map all the  topics linked to the subject and to have a more clear view on their interactions and  connections. In this specific case, as I do not have any experience in this business, I need to  map all the information and data collected this tool helped me to organize the information and  the data gathered from this business and from online forums from nature tourists. Using it  permits me not only to have the information but to have a visual form of all the topics and  how they connect to each other. This tool is used during the “what is?” phase of design  thinking, so I realized that this should be the better tool for me to use while I want to better  understand what is nature tourism.

Application:

As I was reading the information and collecting the data, I was writing, what for me were the  most important topics, in post-it. After every reading I grouped the post-it by specific topics  and gave a name to each group of post-its. In the meantime, in a large piece of paper I wrote  the subject I wanted to better understand, “nature tourism”, at the center of this paper. Then I  fixed all the post-it in the paper, building up the Mind Map.

Virtual Trial Room

Denis Johnson, Katia Johnson, Katia Johnson, Denis Johnson, Katia Johnson

Departmen Of Compute Universidad San Francisco de Quito

Email: belindarojas@yahoo.com ,kennethevans@hotmail.com

Abstract- Augmented reality is the technology that expands our physical world, adding layers of digital  information onto it. Augmented reality adds digital element to live view by using cameras or sensors. The main  aim of this work is to develop virtual trial room using augmented reality which allows user to try on virtual  clothes. Kinect sensor is used to calculate the effective distance between the sensor and the user who is standing  in front of it. Based on this distance we can analyze how the clothes will look on user. This application improves  present augmented based posing and gives full view of 3D image rather than 2D image.    Keywords- Kinect v2, Skeleton tracking, processing, Augmented reality    1. INTRODUCTION  A lot of shoppers have encountered a problem that  trying clothes in clothing stores is usually a time  consuming activity especially during peak hours  such as weekends, it might not even be possible to  try-on clothes in such cases as online shopping.  Also Due to security reasons there is limitation on  number of garments that can be taken for trial at a  time (3). Also some times the shoppers are unable  to show the customers the new stock that is  supposed to arrive in coming few days. To  overcome these problems we aim to develop a  virtual trial room using augmented reality.  In this proposed application a sensor named Kinect  is used for the overall analysis of the user's body  measurements with the help of sensor information  and his positioning coordinates. text:
Jorge Garrido

June 2016

Design for Innovation – University of Virginia

Visualization utilized in the Hospitality Industry

Challenge     I am a member of a registration team within the Meetings & Events department. We are  responsible for creating registration websites, managing the attendee registration  experience, organizing all travel arrangements, and delivering a clear event objective.  Each event has a unique set of opportunities, challenges, and return on investment for the  meeting participants and the company’s stakeholder(s). I was tasked with creating a  registration website for a company that was hosting their largest national sales meeting  since it was founded. It was projected to have around 6,000 attendees and the meeting  had a very complex agenda planned for this historic event. Our team set up a website  discovery call which ultimately helps our team discover what is required and what  additional information was needed. During this call, we were presented with a list of  essential tasks that needed to be individualized to the eight different types of attendees  participating. These included sponsors, VIPs, sales team members, non-sales team members,  executives, sales managers, as well as additional guests and staff.     These essential tasks included:

•  With each type of attendee, came specific admission fees and agendas. This  information ranged from air travel, hotel reservation procedures, and o dress codes  that were individualized per type of attendee.

•  Providing attendees with the opportunity to suggest event topics and content.

•  Develop a website and information compatible with the mobile event application

•  Individualize the website to have specific themes, headers, and banners for each  type of attendee.

This website needs to be developed and created in a specific way to meet all guidelines  above. We needed to build the website, develop tests, and make corrections based on  feedback from our clients within the short timef

Firoz Khan Pandey Reflection – Learning Launch Challenge

I am a member of my organization’s supply chain project management department and my/our challenge  is to improve the workflow (activities and projects) within the department in order to reduce COGS in the  manufacturing processes and to cut lead times for active new project launches. The project scope included  the project management department composed of six employees, as well as the marketing department  and sales department, with whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal resources (i.e., budget  and employee time). The project should not exceed 90 business days and the solution should include an  even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover what  our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the marketing department and sales department,  consider to be ineffective or problematic about the workflow.

Selection

Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to try the  learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an idea  and prototype.

Application

For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of our day to day project  management tasks. In particular, we wanted to see if we could structure our tasks, projects, and processes  to adapt the methods of Scrum project management for our work (e.g., time boxed, daily, specific  meetings, reviews, etc.) in an effort to become more agile. This tested our assumption that the structure  and execution were the main causes of our workflow challenge. Our team went through a two-day training  with a Scrum project management coach. Next, we went through five workshops to structure our tasks  and processes in a more agile way. These two sessions occurred within in a three-week timeframe. Reflection

Fabiana Braga 2012/09/11

Challenge and Selection The tool I selected to reflect about is the Learning Launch Tool. The purpose of a learning launch is to get the truth about a situation and a market, and that is useful so you can save time and money when to test ideas/hypothesis/assumptions.

To test ideas/hypothesis/assumptions, and verify if they are really good, it is important to compare with good data (and not opinions or unfounded guesses). That is a challenge due to some risks that are evolved in the process, as such as confirmation bias (when you subconsciously only look for data that confirms your idea/hypothesis/assumption).

Application I used the approach of the Learning Launch to test a hypothesis I have created recently. I work as a financial consultant in an Advisory Firm, and my job in the project that I’m currently involved is to create and suggest to my client KPIs for the cost process in the financial area. Therefore, I was supposed to bring some KPIs that could be used by managers to support their analysis of the development of the area.

To achieve this, I created a list of KPIs that could be used, and I tested the efficiency of the KPIs using the experiment phase of the Learning Launch Tool. This was important, because I could review the formulas I have created for the KPIs, and adjust them when necessarily.

Insight As I described before, I used the Learning Launch tool and I experimented the efficiency and reviewed the formulas for the KPIs. After that I could see the errors and adjustments necessarily to be done. By doing these steps, I was able to prove that the KPIs could be used by the managers, therefore I gained trust enough to finish the work.

Approach I would definitely use the Learning Launch again to experiment another idea/hypothesis/assumption that I have created. Also, next time I would use the Learning Launch as a starting point for my thinking and actions on a project.

Reflections of Marcelo Caroline related to Visualization

Challenge

As responsible for the IT department in the company, I have constant challenges related to the  interpretation of needs and technical requirements of the business for the development of  solutions that create value and are easy to maintain. This challenge has increased as new process  automation needs arise, new needs for analysis of large volumes of data, new digitization needs  sometimes brought by business areas and sometimes fostered by the IT team.

Specifically in this case, my team and I were asked to develop an App that facilitated the recording  of mechanical, electrical, civil problems, etc. found in our hydroelectric and wind power plants, with  the objective of allowing the analysis, comparison and centralized prioritization of the solutions to  be applied in the power plants using the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) method.

Departments interested in this solution were: Local Maintenance, Health Security, Safe end  Environment, the centralized area of Projects Engineering and IT.

Selection

To facilitate the understanding of the various departments involved, I chose to use visualization  tools to translate the document of requirements, spreadsheets and other documents collected with  the requesting areas.

Because meetings are remote, using the Microsoft White board in combination with scanned paper  drawings seemed like a good choice because of the ability to make changes and even new drawings  in real time as solutions were discussed. Later we were able to prove that the use of the White  board was a good choice.

Application

Even before the app's development, the customer areas were already doing problems management  in a precarious way using forms and a giant Excel spreadsheet. In the spreadsheet were all the rules  of analysis and prioritization of solutions by project and maintenance engineers.

text:
Mohmad Ali  31/03/2011

Challenge:​ The challenge I chose to address is the inefficiency of the California Department of  Motor Vehicles (DMV). In large cities such as Los Angeles, where I reside, a trip to the DMV  becomes an all day endeavor and is dreaded by nearly everyone.    Selection:​ I chose to use Visualization tools to help identify the issues at hand and potential  solutions. I believe that the use of projective techniques and can help us understand the actions  and emotions of a DMV worker, like the  journey mapping would, in an abstract and  comprehensive way. In the module on the visualization tool, it was used in nearly every step of  the design thinking process, however in part I of the MEYOUHEALTH video, it was used as part  of the ethnographic research that was conducted.    Application​: I interviewed several DMV worker and asked them questions about their attitude  toward their job and their complaints, as well as what they appreciate about it. I then attempted  to draw a picture to capture the negative aspects of the environment they work in and their chief  complaint to provide me insight into what really causes their inefficiency, and helps me identify  their unarticulated need. It appears that this tool helped me identify several environmental  factors that contribute to the problem and helped me develop possible solutions, but there may  be some intrinsic issues that this tool failed to identify.                               Insight: ​Visualization helped me realize how the reputation of the DMV for being slow and  agonizing contributes heavily to it actually being slow and agonizing. The visualization  supported the idea that the DMV is a very hectic, stressful and draining place to be, however it  revealed that the patrons’ frustration and discontent was a big contributors to the stress of the  employees, in some cases causing them to lose motivation, leading to more frustration and  discontent from the customers. MAI 2017

CHALLENGE  (Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.)    The challenge was to think of an IT solution to a new business process that would allow to propose pricing  conditions for proposed products to potential clients. A potential client can not become a real client, if it  was not transparent which pricing conditions were proposed to him and got approved by the respective  approval body.   The basis to propose prices is the list of products that are proposed to the potential client.   The new process spreads across three different business units (client management, product management,  price management) and will have to integrate several underlying sub processes (currently executed  independently).   The change is pushed by the Pricing business and each business units have their own priorities/goals and  own roadmap/deadline towards achieving these goals.   A close collaboration, shared understanding of the importance of the change and implementation  alignment and agreement is a pre-requisite for the success of this initiative. Mind Mapping: Manage and plan the work smoothly

Have you been in a situation where you must solve a problem but do not know where to start?  Well, this is one of the reasons that make mind mapping so powerful and amazing. I want to  describe this tool before I show the application that I gave it.

A mind map is a graphical way to represent ideas and concepts. It is a visual thinking tool that  helps structuring information, helping you to better analyze, comprehend, synthesize, recall, and  generate new ideas. Just as in every great idea, its power lies in its simplicity.

In a mind map, as opposed to traditional note taking or a linear text, information is structured in a  way that resembles much more closely how your brain works. Since it is an activity that is both  analytical and artistic, it engages your brain in a much, much richer way, helping in all its  cognitive functions. And, best of all, it is fun!

Basically, mind mapping avoids dull, linear thinking, jogging your creativity and making note  taking easy again. Some benefits of using this awesome tool are brainstorming, problem solving,  planning, researching and memorization.

text:
1 Leonardo Torres

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

In this reflection about learning launch and experimentation, I would like to tell an  incident when I influenced engineering to build a particular feature. In my current role,  I’m the monetization front-end designer for our free email product.

Two weeks ago, Irina, the engineering manager, gave me some bad news, "Leonardo,  I’m sorry, but we have to remove 140x500 skyscraper ad. My engineering VP told me  that the PM team wouldn’t mind."

I was thinking to myself: “Are you kidding me? Wouldn’t mind? This ad was only the 3rd  most valuable ad placement on the entire site. It delivered INR 45 million in revenue  per year. Who did Irina think was paying her salary?”

Selection

After I collected my emotions, I asked Irina, “When are you planning to remove it?”  She said, “Two code sprints from now. About 6 weeks.”

I told her, “Can you give me three days to pull some data? I’d like to understand the  impact of this decision.”

After she left, I thought: what could I do? I could have a hissy fit and complain loudly.  Or I could immediately escalate to the engineering VP.

While I was tempted to go with either or both solutions, I wouldn’t get what I want  unless I was armed with the facts. Before I figured my plan, I gave my boss Luca, a  heads-up. He wasn’t pleased with engineering’s unilateral response, but he agreed with  my plan.

Application

I logged into the data warehouse and pulled revenue numbers for the last 12 months.  Next I asked to sales team to gauge customer reaction if we no longer made the product  available. Lastly, I reached out to the VP Engineering’s Chief of Staff to better  understand why we wanted to remove the ad.

Insight

After I collected the data, I set up a meeting with Irina, Luca my boss, and  Luca the VP of Engineering. The VP of Engineering reiterated his decision to  remove the skyscraper ad. He maintained what I had heard earlier: the skyscraper ads  were the reason why

text:
Peer Graded Assignment

Joyce Ka

14 December 2015

Challenge  I work as an internal strategy consultant / project manager for an Operations division in an airline.     One of the departments recently got approval to spend USD 4 million on using virtual training technology for  training cabin crew (both new cabin crew and those being developed to move up to more senior roles on  board flights). The original business case for the project was admittedly quite flimsy and, having gotten  approved, there were varying views in the departments leadership team on which technology solutions would  benefit the most in terms of training engagement and effectiveness as well as drive operational efficiency.     My role as the project manager assigned to the project was to define a scope and requirements for the project  so that a tender could be floated for solution providers. That being said, the department head and her  leadership team were not aligned on what issues they were trying to solve and had a tendency to jump  straight into talking about technologies that should be brought in. The core team discussed the issue at hand  and agreed that, if we initiated a typical scope phase, we would struggle to get detailed and specific  requirements for the solution.     Selection  Given the two key issues of unaligned stakeholders and a focus on technology rather than  problems/opportunities, we decided that we needed to go through a mind mapping process i.e. a structured  process that would include a review of research conducted in order to jointly identify insights and patterns  that would be the basis of establishing criteria for the idea generation phase. text:
LEARNING LAUNCH TOOL – FINAL ASSIGNEMENT –Carmen Perez

Challenge

The challenge I present is a real project that we are going to apply the method of Design  Thinking in its different phases. Our users are employees in several countries in the same  company.  We have offer them Learning mindset initiatives & activities in order to promote  Learning mindset in whole company

At the beginning of this phase of the project, we had seven prototypes to test in different  countries each prototype was very different in terms of: approach, methods, cost and contents

With these seven different prototypes, we should determine which worked and which did not,  and for those who worked what and how they should be improved.

Selection

With the range of possible proposals, our objective at this stage was to determine which were  valid and could finally be real solutions to improve learning mindset in different countries

Each country is very different with not similar status regarding learning mindset, we had to see  if one product was enough to give as a solution or we would validate different from them.

Learning Launch, the tool is the best way to perform this test because we had groups of  employees in different countries to whom we could perform testing of prototypes.

Application

The first learning launch was made with a group of 35 employees (20men / 15 women) of  different ages, different positions (Managers and not Managers), and different countries.

We arranged a meeting in which each employees  was provided with a toolkit  with 7 different  prototypes models with detailed explanation regarding each initiative,

In this phase, we accompany these employees throughout the process, so questions or doubts  could be solved. This test phase lasted a month. At the end of the month, we held a meeting  with 35 employees to obtain feedback from each of them.

The conclusion of this first learning launch was to dismiss two prototypes and make  improvements in the remaining five.

text:
Ganesh Kumar |

Visualization tool for Covid-19 Pandemic Response

Challenge & Selection

Data is crucial for our understanding of the world, and particularly for the emergence of  phenomena such as the COVID-19 outbreak in 2009. A viral pandemic is not a scenario in which  intuition can provide a sense of how the spread is advancing, nor are feelings a sufficient  approach to dealing with and ultimately overcoming such an unforeseen enemy. The tool I used  was the tool of Visualization or more commonly called as the Visual thinking aid for collecting,  analyzing, sharing and ultimately making use of the data needed for the pandemic response in  2009. This collected data needs to be efficiently conveyed to all sorts of individuals and groups,  from lay people to experts and everything in between. Visualizing collected data can make its  dissemination easy, and can help others understand quickly what has taken others so long to  collect and analyze. After all, a picture is worth a thousand words.

Application

I'm not an epidemiologist, and I have no interest in pretending to be one; there's enough of that  going on right now. But as an engineer and an analyst, I can successfully apply this tool to spread  the needed vital information around. John Burn-Murdoch works on data visualization for the  Financial Times. He has recently garnered a following and appreciation for his COVID-19  visualizations, which are exemplars of how quality data visualizations can clearly and succinctly  tell a story. Personally, I have been relying on John's visualizations to understand the outbreak  for quite some time now, and generally refer them several times a day.

text:
Maria Laitinen  Design Thinking Innovation Final Exercise

Challenge    Applying for a job is a tough process. For the applicant there are a lot of different emotions,  creating a good application takes time and if one is chosen for interviews, they take even more  time. I’ve been in this kind of process myself during this autumn, so I’ve had plenty of  experience from different companies’ recruitment processes. In the end I decided to drop off  from several different companies’ processes I didn’t get the “good feeling” from the company or  some other reason. So I’ve been an “user” or a recruitment process and this is my insight to it.    The topic of this exercise was born when I start to wonder that what kind of reasons lead to  leaving the recruitment process unfinished? This is a valuable question and a real business  challenge for recruiting companies since it shrinks the pool of the applicants. In this paper I  focus on the question: Is there a way how communication could prevent this to happen? In the  recruitment process there can be a lot or lack of communication and this affects the applicants’  opinions about the company. There the better the communication and more alluring the  company, the bigger pool of applicants to choose from. This results to the better quality of  employers.    There are phases in the recruitment process where the applicants drop off themselves. I call  these exit points and in this paper focus on the role of the communication on voluntary exit  points: ​what kind of information design and communication is needed for the applicant  not to leave the process unfinished?    Selection    To tackle this challenge, I chose ​the journey mapping tool​ where the applicant is the  customer. The application process includes a lot of different phases and layers for both parties  and the journey mapping tool is in my opinion the best way to visualize these. Application

Blanca Serrano  Peer review assignment

Reflection – Visualization

1 CHALLENGE

I work in the marketing department of a multinational company that sells cameras and  printers. My work is mostly in the business to business (B2B) area, we partner with  retailers and ecommerce platforms to sell products.

As a result, there is a need to train external personnel in the use of our products so they  can deliver the best solutions and give good sales pitch to consumers.

Due to this need, we developed an e-learning platform to train salespeople from partners  in the correct use of our products, since in-person training is not always possible due to  large number of salespeople to train and the fact that they are spread throughout the  country.

However, initial implementation of the platform was rocky due to lack of resources and  when it finally took off the users didn’t use it steadily, they registered, did a few courses  and then never used it again.

We are currently looking for a way to make the platform more appealing and useful to  the users, since we hope to provide good resources and value to the users.

2 SELECTION

We are going to use Visualization. This is a technique that requires participants to  make use of graphics, photography, animation or any other visual medium to express  their feelings or ideas.

Since we are dealing with a website, we have a highly visual component that would  be better served by graphical techniques.

It also allows users to see themselves to see a physical representation of a website in  progress and to add any input in a way that is accessible to anyone, not just  programmers. It enables fluid communication.

text:
STORY TELLING – Mohammed Salah

Challenge & selection

I am a language lecturer in a university in Ho Chi Minh city, Vietnam. I teach  English preparation courses and Business Communication. My students are  Vietnamese, 18-23 years old.

When I have Business Communication classes with senior students, some of  them seem to lose their interest and energy in learning. When talking with  them, and read their writing, I figured out that they are worrying a lot about  their chosen major may not be their best career potentials. This group of  students have completed some but not all subjects of their chosen major,  some of them have finished On Job Training semester (internship). They find  difficulty in adjusting to the working environment, or doubt that their ability  and career interest may not fit the job. For example, an IT senior student  learning Software engineering (to become programmer) want to change to  game designer, or a senior Business student majored in Marketing wants to  change to Graphic design.

There is not a problem for them to request the university to approve their  wish to change their learning major, but it will cost them at least 1 more  year to study the new major again.

When dealing with these young fragile people, it is very challenging because  more stress or pressure on them may affect their learning quality and  attitude toward school. The worst is that they may quit school. Therefore,  talking to them in academic way is not suitable, I chose story telling to help  them feel better.

Application

I have a story to tell them and share their worry. Once they open their heart  to share their worry with me, it is a very good chance for me to share my  story too.

In about fifteen to twenty minutes after lesson finished, I started to share  my experience in worry and doubting about my career choice. I honestly told  them that teaching is not what I learnt in university, and it is until the 3rd job  switch that I found my most suitable job, but

Coursera_Design Tara Limbu

I Manage the Strategic Sourcing & Vendor Management functions at a major Asset Manager ( Financial firm ) in NY.

Challenge & Selection

 Current State: End to end manual process, limited to none RFx( competitive bidding ) opportunities, non-established or

outdated rate cards and Professional services Agreements’ (PSA’s), non-negotiated or non-existing volume discounts,  inconsistent or lengthy budgeting and accruals. Majority of Statement Of Works (SOWs) are sole-sourced resulting in un- visible, un-managed, un-disciplined SOW spend.

 Scope: To manage end-to-end all Professional Services Statement of Work (SOW) engagements (including deployment

services, project management, product configurations, general consulting services, advisory or management consulting  services ) in Beeline’s SOW module. Tool will manage complete life-cycle of all such SOW’s, including Milestones, Time  sheets, approvals, resources On/Off boardings and Payments

 Selection of Proposed Tools: Third party Vendor Management Systems (VMS) tools, SOW module for Professional

Services / Project based agreements. (With one year into the Contingent Workforce Program (CWM) program we had  successfully rolled out our Contingent spend management via VMS CWM module. We are now ready to expand the scope  to capture and manage all other Professional Services Statement of Works in our VMS’s SOW module.

Vendor Management Solution (VMS): web-based solution to track and monitor all SOW activities End-to-End requisition  lifecycle

 Automated workflow with customized pre-approvals

 Facilitated candidate review process and continuous industry benchmarking

 Standardized bill rates within job classifications and job titles

 Automated reporting (headcount, rates, skill sets, tenure, term expiry)

 Consolidated invoicing and reporting

 Future state: To be the first to know - with a centralized view of all stages—from negotiation and sourcing, through

Pankaj Sahu

Challenge:   I am working with a diverse Team of Sales executives , TSM’s and ZSM’s , challenge is to  make them go for common goal of winning in 4G space with standardization of approach  and way of working. Also to motivate them to give their best in a very dynamic and  competitive environment.    Selection :  I co created a plan With my Team using Mix of Mind Mapping and Visualization Tool ,  Selection of tools done on basis of diversified needs of individuals involved in this Exercise  also a Vision of Common goal was required to Win in market place    Application:   I first divided team members into existing plots of Urban and Rural Team members including  my FSE’s. I had one on one interviews with different segment of Teams located at various  locations of my geography. I collated this Data and plotted on What is , What if , What  WOW and What Works Grid.     Sample Questionnaire :

1. What Excites you the most When you start your day  2. What’s your professional goal  3. How do you motivate your team / Retailers   4. What’s the Goal you are driving  5. What puts you on Off Mode.

After collation of this data and mapping the mind thoughts of different stake holders , I was  ready with various personas to deal with and can plan my way forward on leading them  towards common goal. During these interviews I was using projective techniques also to  bring the interviewee towards our vision.    Once Done with individual mind mapping , I called for a general meeting to address them in  a group and then basis various stake holders needs gave them vision which was easy to  understand , Simple , and excited them , For eg  if a common goal was achieved our  Incentive , growth in the organisation and achiever’s Club will get qualified. This  Visualisation of Success on a common platform enabled us to make team drive our Vision. text:
Manuela Lucas

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

I recently graduated from an MBA program specialized in international trade. It seemed a logical step  after studying international relations. The outcomes also seemed logical at first: get a job at a company  that actually exports.  However, there was one tiny mistake in my chain of logical steps: since I was a  kid I always wanted to create.

No matter where you looked at my childhood memories or my teenage years, I have always felt the  need to express myself through creative ways such as garment design, furniture design or writing just  to name a few. How could I redirect my career to make it more fulfilling without wasting all those  years that I invested on my education?

Selection

I try to look situations as opportunities needed to be found rather than problems encountered. That  is why I chose visualization: I needed to activate my brain in a way that would allow me to envision  different paths for my own future. Visualization is that tool that help us define ideas, feelings -and in  this case, aspirations- to help me gain a better understanding of what path I needed to follow in order  to meet my dreams with the lessons I had already learnt.

Application

I decided to draw a horizontal line in a blank page: one side of the line was where I was, and I drew a  dot on in saying “beginning”, on the opposite side I drew another dot stating: “My goal: a new  beginning”. On the first side I started to write down all the different skills that I already acquired  through the years, and on the other side I wrote all the aspirational skills that I longed to have and the  regular activities that I envisioned myself doing every day in a creative job.

text:
Author: Javier Castellanos

Visualization Tool

Challenge

Earlier this year, as part of a course of Problem-Solving Methodologies that we take in college, we  were required to develop a project aimed at solving a soft problem in any kind of business or  company. A soft problem is not related to problems like productivity of a manufacturing process o  reducing costs from certain department, but it is a problem that aims to solve issues related to  interpersonal relations among workers, or even with customers. We found a local clinical analysis  laboratory that let us help them to deal with the increasing customer complaints that they were  receiving, so the laboratory’s director told us to aim our project in improving the experience of the  customer through the process that they have to go through to receive their service, since they make  the appointment until they receive their results.

Selection

Design Thinking for Innovation Course Reflection: Storytelling

By Vero Reyes

Challenge   One of the biggest challenges I face as a Project Manager in the technology industry is keeping  my Clients on the same page as our internal development team, especially in the face of  problems that need to be solved. It can be difficult to find the right balance between over- sharing and collaboration within the Client-Consultant relationship; you don’t want to “cry  wolf” too early or often, but you also don’t want your Clients to feel blindsided when a problem  arises that they didn’t see coming.     Specifically, I found when the need for an increase in budget (e.g. Change Order) would arise,  many of my Clients didn’t understand where the need was coming from and it immediately  created distrust that more budget was being requested without a clear understanding of how  we got there. Upon further reflection, I realized that in an effort to present ourselves as  Consultants who had a plan for solving every issue before our Clients were even aware the  issue existed, that I was leaving them out of the entire process of collaboration and problem  solving.    Selection  While there is a temptation as Consultants to only “put our best foot forward” in front of our  Clients and shield them from an issue until we have a solution in mind, it became clear that this  approach doesn’t foster understanding – especially when the challenges result in the need for  more funding. I realized we weren’t bringing our Clients along for the journey. With this in  mind, I started thinking of ways we can better “show and tell” to Clients through the ups and  downs on projects, while still maintaining a productive relationship. The power of storytelling is  an excellent tool to help find this balance. VISUALIZATION

Visualization, in

combination with a clear

business strategy, can reduce

the typical fuzziness of front-

end innovation. It can close

the psychological gap

between future and present;

the future becomes more real

for purposes

of

innovation

in the

present.

Inspired

visualization

can be the

proverbial “one picture is

worth a thousand words.” It

can help to bridge a time gulf

of a thousand years or a travel

span in outer space of a

thousand light-years. For

practical purposes of

innovation, however, the

visualized future image

should have a reasonable

connection to the present in

terms of achievement

.Visualization generally

involves the perception of

needs and preferences across

a large population of potential

consumers, conditioned by

informed forecasts of

lifestyles and external living

conditions.

Visualization overlaps

with, but is not the same as,

several other management-

related concepts—vision and

associative marketing. Vision

refers to a broad, generally

long-term picture of company

mission and goals; it is not as

concrete as visualization.

Associative marketing is when

a company advertises a

product by tying it to a usually

vague image of a desirable

customer lifestyle (e.g., an

enjoyable vacation). Such

visualizations would not

generally be adequate for

specific innovative efforts in

product design.

A good visualization should

encompass both attractive

lifestyle images for consumers

and realizable technology

designs for innovators. The

relevant future context should

also be realistic in terms of

expected social-demographic,

economic and environmental

trends, including trends

toward sustainability. Many of

these trends are evolving in

an exponential fashion; future

visualizations therefore need

to be correspondingly

complex—even

“disruptive”—in scope.

the fact that forecasters often

text:
Aakash Kumar Aakash Kumar    June 23, 2019

Reflection - Storytelling

Context:  I am a content marketer and often take on freelance consulting projects to learn more about  different industries. Recently, as a part of one such project, I was asked to review and potentially  rewrite a case study for a tech company that creates business management software for activity- based organizations such as gyms, ballet studios and parks & recreation centers.     Challenge:  The case study was about how the company’s software had helped improve the day-to-day  operations of a local cheerleading gym thereby improving overall efficiencies, customer service and  coaching. The purpose of the case study was to help the tech company generate leads from the  market segment of gym owners and administrators. When I read the case study for the first time, I  was left with a vague sense of accomplishment and many unanswered questions. The way it was  written was all over the place as it tried to address too many concerns in a hurried fashion without  communicating the impact the tech company’s software solution had on the gym business.    Selection:  To tackle the rewriting challenge, I chose to use the storytelling tool. As we learned from Raymond Baird of Mars Inc. in week 2, “Storytelling is the difference between solving a problem and creating  a cause.” Stories are based on empathy and therefore are powerful tools to make any problem,  challenge or situation seem more relatable. The consumer is therefore more inclined to react to a  story than a presentation full of graphs and numbers.     Application:  Simon Sinek urges us to “start with the why” to inspire action. What this means is to get people to  do anything, we must get them to understand our purpose. affects the economy

?”

Written by Rosa Perna

MDI-191

07.17.15

How climate change affects the economy?

“The time is past when humankind

thought it could selfishly draw on

exhaustible resources. We know now

the world is not a commodity.”

Leo Ine

Climate change has always happened on Earth but since the Industrial

Revolution, human activity has been affecting the atmosphere, which has led to an  increase in temperature and caused global warming. These days such problem as  global warming is considered to be the most serious outcome of climate change. It  is rapidly developing, affecting many areas of human activity. One of the areas  affected is the economy, and I will try to look into this problem and state the most  important facts.

The first and most obvious fact is that the overall temperature is getting

hotter. The statistic shows that the global annual temperature has increased at an  average rate of 0.07°C per decade since 1880 and over twice that rate (+0.18°C)  since 1981. This has its consequences. Some niches of the economy are slowly  shutting down, but the others, on the contrary, are gaining rise. This is happening  because some products are not relevant and needed anymore. To provide an  illustration, not a long time ago, 10-20 years back, it was very popular in my  country (which is Russia) to wear winter fur coats. But it’s noticeable that even the  famous harsh Russian winters are now not that harsh. With every new year, we see  warmer winters which are almost like European. Therefore, the manufacturers that  make fur coats lose money because their products are no longer in demand. On the  other hand, the summers are getting hotter too. People need to somehow cool down  their flats or houses and the request for air conditioners and cooling systems has  risen in the past years.

Reflection –  Visualization and Customer Experience

Challenge

I have worked for several years leading a global B2B1 Customer Experience department and my  challenge was to improve SME2 Customer satisfaction with the telecommunication services we  were providing. Our SME Customer satisfaction was much lower than that of our Corporate  customers and we were loosing market share. Through previous research analysis, we found out  that the main pain point for our SME customers was the excessive time that our technical  support was taking to solve their systems breakdowns. When looking at our internal KPIs3, you  could see that we were fulfilling all our SLAs4, so our challenge was to convince main decision  makers, within the organization, to set new SLAs that would fit our customers expectations. This  was not an easy task, as it involved investing and decreasing margins in the short run.

Selection

To tackle this challenge we decided to use the Visualization tool, as this is a good tool to make a  problem tangible and concrete. We thought this tool was the best one to ensure all people  involved understood our customer expectations. We had tried it before with reports and other  internal presentations of data, but without convincing of the urgency of the issue.

Application

In order to be able to applicate the Visualization tool, we decided to generate visual content that  we could share with main decision makers. We organized a two weeks workshop to meet and  interview our main types of SME customers, so that we could better understand their current  reality. We  picked up 15 SME customers, representing close to 80% of all SME different  subsectors in the country. The sample included many kinds of business models, from bar owners  to online service providers. We took pictures of them and recorded videos, making sure they  expressed the importance and impact in their business of early fast technical support. text:
DESIGN THINKING ASSIGNMENT submitted by Rehab Mariam

Example Reflection– Learning Launch

Challenge

I am an avid tech enthusiast always looking for new ways to make life better and easier. Having worked  in the tech space for over 5 years and offering turnkey solution from different OEMS to different  customers including leading hotel chains. Throughout my discussions with one of the leading coffee  chains I discovered we had a common problem which was inclusivity and by this I mean making it  possible for disabled people, deaf and dumb to be precise to dine in and still feel welcome naturally. Our  challenge now is to have the right tools and process either through people or technology or combination  of both in place. The project will involve having one branch of the coffee chain with around 10  employees this includes wait staff as well as the branch manager get trained on sign language as well as  a new system/tool geared towards taking orders more efficient, this will essentially take 30 days as we  try to incorporate actual walk in customers who are already skilled in sign language to mimic the  anticipated scenario. Imagine a situation where the wait staff are not trained on sign language with no  access to paper or pen for communication between a solo deaf and dumb diner and the wait staff. In the  process we will work towards uncovering what the stakeholders in this case the waiters, branch  managers and customer believe are barriers to success of this pilot.

For this experiment we shall call the deaf and dumb as D&D.

Some of our assumptions are

1. The deaf and dumb do want to be included in social functions  2. The wait staff will adapt to this clientele requirements from order taking to having extras

substituted to issuing complaints.

Challenge:

I was introduced to mind mapping through a mentor who challenged his employees to 'think different'.  When we met to work on a business problem one of the first things he would do is draw/doodle/map  what he knew and input from the meeting on a white board. I have also been part of mind mapping  exercises at sustainability conferences and in market research. Right now I am laid off late in my career  and looking for change towards doing something I will find interesting as well as provide a more  balanced lifestyle.

Selection:

So naturally the tool I selected is mind mapping. My intent was to think freely about what is important  to me combined with what I like to do within some type of goal framing to prepare for possible  execution of the idea.

Application:

First to prepare I read some books and articles. There was one from Fortune magazine with advice from  Warren Buffet about focusing on few things and prioritizing one goal in order to be successful. A  professor recommended the Marshall Goldsmith book Mojo. Also I was working with an outplacement  service to modernize my resume, practice elevator speeches and interview with recruiters to polish self  promotion skills.

While this was going on I set aside some quite time to mind map my immediate future. To think about  what I want life to be like combined with what I was learning. I took a large piece of paper and put 'Ashley  2015' in the middle. From there I thought about major areas of interest and spidered them out. The  areas I wound up with are: People, Health, Finances, Home. Each of these encompassed a few more  areas in detail so I kept spidering until I felt I had no more ideas to add to it.

Step 1-Consumer behavior visualization

Challenge and selection

My challenge was to improve the experience of students around applied projects in a class that was  being piloted in a downtown classroom.  I wanted to find possibilities for curriculum that revolved  around community integration weekly.    The project focused on a 14 week night class involving 35  students learning about consumer behavior in the downtown core.  My focus was to uncover how to  incorporate local businesses into the curriculum.  Selection included students going into their 3rd year  given that it was a 3rd year course in the degree program.

Application

I started the process by having students wander around a set area in the downtown core –four block  radius around the downtown classroom.   They took pictures to visually present  businesses that caught  their interest, consumer behavior they saw on the streets and in stores, and areas that seemed to have  a distinct culture to them (such as Chinatown). “Photography is a very rich way for us to understand our  world. “ (Topon, n.d.).   For example, students took a picture of a very expensive shoe store and  indicated that they would like to learn more about how the layout of the store induced consumers to  buy the expensive shoes.

The students were then formed into groups and shared their photos and what each meant to them— why they chose them, what was interesting, what they wanted to learn from them.

After sharing, the student teams chose 6 photos from the group to showcase which business and/or  area they wanted to visit and why.

All the groups submitted their photo collection.

I reviewed the submissions and then mind- mapped the topics based on the write-ups.  The mind map  help determined how the businesses would fit within the curriculum topics and readings.

Mohamed Smith (agood@gmail.com)

Visualization

Challenge (WHAT)  The challenge I have selected for the visualization tool is the bank account opening  experience for small medium enterprises (SME’s) in the United Arab Emirates  (UAE). SME’s have made it clear that they struggle to open a bank account in order  for their business to operate & incorporate in the UAE. This is due to the extreme  amount of paperwork, financial history & requirements that are unrealistic for SME’s.  We (a bank in the UAE) had the opportunity to collaborate with the UAE government,  regulators & the team responsible for a “digital shift” federal initiative.       Selection (WHY)  Visualization, as described by Denise Gomez, is a method or tool of thinking visually  which allows a multitude of people, or their brains, to be on “the same page”. A way  for everybody to be able to relate to & understand the problem, idea or solution the  same way. Visualization removes the ambiguity & imagination our brains do naturally  when in discussion or when reading words by replacing it with pictures, diagrams or  drawings.     For this reason, visualization was used throughout this project and throughout the  design thinking process. With a number of different stakeholders, expertise & a  range of understanding of the problem, visualization was seen as the best way to  achieve mutual understanding and also a way of expediting meetings, explanations  and ideating.       Application (HOW)  As mentioned, visualization was used throughout the project from discovery or the  “What is” phase of Liedtka’s process (whiteboarding, stakeholder mapping & process  mapping) to final concept (wireframing, storyboarding etc.). Reflection

Bryan Sanchez

Challenge, Analysis and Selection

The challenge I have chosen to create this reflection is a personal problem, which  consists of the following: Due to the sanitary and economic crisis generated by the  covid-19, me and my family have had to move to a municipality called San  Sebastian de Mariquita, located in the department of Tolima in Colombia; This year  I have been admitted to the National Ankara University, in Manizales campus,  and in turn to the Pimpri Chinchwad College of Engineering, in Honda campus

This caused me to study two careers at the same time, and due to the action of the  government to return to normality, it has generated a problem to move to one of  the two cities to continue my studies in person, or as a second option to move to  the city of Bogota to continue my educational process in that city.

The factors that are strongly connected to the problem are: The distance between  both universities, Low amount of economic resources for the support in any of the  two cities, The short time to return to receive face-to-face classes.

The problem has several aspects to observe, both positive and negative of each  option mentioned above.

Advantages and disadvantages

Advantages of the Manizales option:

- It would not require a major relocation.

- It is a more economical city

- It has great housing offers for students

- Manizales is a safe and quiet city

Disadvantages of the Manizales option:

- Need to travel every weekend to receive classes in Honda (approximately 4 hours  of travel time)

- It is a new city where everything is unknown

- It does not have good job opportunities for students

Advantages of the Bogotá option:

- It does not require travel to another city to attend classes at both universities.

- It is a city that I know, and I know how it works

- It has good job opportunities for students

- I have family currently living in that city, who can support me.

Reflection on Storytelling

By Zakir

Challenge

I have been working at government institution for some years. Along with the team, I developed  regulations particularly in tax issues. We encountered many challenges in the regulation drafting process  from both internal and external stakeholders. I limited the scope of challenges to internal stakeholders.  Why was that? It consumed significant amount of energy, time, and resources to involve in a long period  of meeting and debates just to make a regulation. Unfortunately, after reaching internal consensus, we  could not implement the regulation because external stakeholders resisted it. In the worst case, we had  to withdraw the regulation to avoid more conflicts. How could such a long process of making the  regulation be useless in no time? As we knew, we could not predict the response of external  stakeholders. That was why we focused on making internal consensus fast and cheap. Because if  external resistance happened again in the future, then we could fail cheap too.

Selection

How could we reach internal consensus fast and cheap? I tried to make a list regarding the most likely  sources of disagreement by doing observation and interview on experienced regulators. I found insights  such as lack of information and poor assumptions, use of highly technical terms that could not fit into  diverse background within the regulator forum, inconsistency of the participants involved in the drafting  process, and inadequate holistic point of view to tackle the problem. We chose Storytelling to tackle  these issues because we needed to create the drafting process became simple, holistic, and interesting.

Reflection – Storytelling

Author: Jean Pierre Jouanne

Challenge & Application

I am currently working in France in retirement homes called The Coca-Cola. During my working time, I greatly  interact with senior people. While taking this class, I realize that I use Storytelling on a daily basis.  Module 2 of the class introduce a concept that I love and that can be easily implementable while I try to  solve resident’s problems and anxiety issues. I describe myself as an open-minded person that can easily  share lives stories with senior residents. By listening to their concerns, it helps me visualizing areas to  improve and start my thinking process in order to develop new strategies. By applying this strategy, I am  able to improve their satisfaction levels on many different levels (canteen repartition, reorganization of  visits time and so on …).

Application

My story, I think, will talk to everyone reading this paper. During the difficult context on the crisis we are  all facing, the badly famous COVID-19, I was able to use storytelling to comfort the elderly people I’m  working with. During this stress-generating times, I was in charge of developing and addressing elderly  people needs. At the management meeting, the director of the center wanted to apply rules dictated by  our government strictly. I took a stand, explaining to the director that the situation needs to be  addressed differently while still addressing rules dictated by our national leaders. Then, I told them the  story of this old lady in the residence. This particular lady was especially impacted by this sanitary crisis,  she wasn’t sick, she was simply afraid about the consequences of sanitary restrictions. I took the time to  sit down and listen to her concerns. She explained me that she wasn’t necessarily scared of being  contaminated, even though she knew it could be fatal for her. VISUALIZATION REFLECTION

Challenge & Selection  As an 8th grade student, I use visualization a lot in my life. In my classes, I strive to not only memorize the information presented but also understand it. In order for me to do this, I use visualization. Some of my peers who struggle constantly ask me for aid in their respective subjects which we share. I wanted to challenge myself to only use the tool of visualization to help them. I selected visualization as we are now studying geometry and it's very important to learn how to visualize things.

For example, some of them aren't comfortable with the relatively important concept of isometries. In geometry, an isometry is a rigid transformation between metric spaces. Most of my classmates simply try to figure out and isometry by using a formula. However while being sloppy, a formula can give you inaccurate results due to an unforced error. Geometry, however, is the perfect candidate for usage of visualization.    What you have to remember while doing simple isometries is that it is usually possible to do without any formula what so ever. One example a 180 rotation transforms from (x,y) to (-x,-y). For people who were just barely paying attention in class, this concept isn't one they are likely to remember. So when I was doing homework with a friend and they start asking me for help on an isometry by saying they forgot the formula I switched my approach. In the past, I would simply tell them the formula. This time. I explained to them to visualize the shape than explained how it usually transforms diagonally. text:
Rosa Jaque

The tool of Visualization

Challenge: I am an architecture student, since the first day of my career I have been facing different

challenges. However, I can say that creativeness and discipline have helped me to overcome them. For this

assignment I chose a challenge that consists on designing a rural community school located in Mexico.  The

project must be functional, sustainable and must minimize costs; and I will solve it by using “The tool of

Visualization” or “Visual Thinking” so have broad options.

Selection: “Visual thinking” is a way to solve a problem from the creative side of the brain. It is also a way of

communication. Visualizing is important in the designing process, that’s why I chose this tool because as in

architecture it lets you think in a none-verbal way.

Application: Visual thinking does not mean just drawing but to go further than words. For this project I

would try to first visualize spaces, materials and most importantly, how the experience in that place I´m

imagining will be. To make it effectively, I´ll create images such as renders so I can show to other people my

ideas and explain them easily. My intention is to sell ideas, to convince people to buy a project even when

they haven’t even touched it.

On the other hand, most people think that using cheap materials or cheaper construction methods is not

particularly good looking or secure, but I would like to demonstrate that it is not true and the best way is

through images.

Insight: In my opinion, to innovate results from exploring different solutions or alternatives for particular

situations and I think visual thinking is perfect for that. By exercising the creative side of our minds we could

redesign solutions when we need it.

Approach: I will not apply a different tool but I’ll rather complement the process previously described with  photography, so I can get more ideas that can help me build bridges to bigger projects than I could imagine.

Mauro Carella 1

“Design Thinking for Innovation”

I.  Challenge

I am in my second year in the MBA program at National University of Malaysia. I am currently

working on one of my elective classes, which is “Innovating through Design Thinking.” I

wanted to not only gain knowledge on the different processes that take part in design thinking,

but I also wanted to get my hands on a real project where I could see the results of such an

effective technique. I came up with the idea of developing a new solution for “poop scooping,”

since in the college town where I live, 6 out of 10 students own a dog.

The action of poop scooping can happen in different places such as home, sidewalks, parks,

friend’s house, or any place where a dog owner decides to take his or her dog for a walk. The

process of cleaning up the dog’s poop is, in my opinion, probably the least desirable stage

when walking a dog. Therefore, when I made the Journey Mapping of the poop scooping

experience, this was the stage with the strongest pain and with the lowest emotional point, thus

creating a space for innovation and opportunity to offer a better solution.

II.  Selection

I chose the tool of visualization, which according to the book “Designing for growth: A

Design Thinking Toolkit for Managers,” is “the transformation of information into images that

you see, either literally with your eyes or figuratively with your mind’s eye.” This tool is used

in the four “W’s” of the design thinking process: what is, what if, what wows, and what works.

I decided to use this tool in the process of “what is,” since it helped me make my ideas concrete

and situate the potential customer (students) on the same page when conducting ethnographic

interviews. Even though visualization does not eliminate the “vagueness” that is present in the

Reflection: Storytelling

Helena Cavaco

Challenge & Selection

As a community outreach fellow working for the SOCAMIRAL through the Banco Santander Río de

Argentina, I have been tasked with supporting the expansion of bilingual communications  and programming in English and Spanish aimed at reaching the Latino community. Ayurvedic and Herbal is a very white institution overall, with Latino leaders few and far between. In the past, their  outreach efforts and communications for the Latino community have come from a white American  perspective, have been signs that have been translated with online software with obvious  grammatical errors, and have demonstrated a lack of true investment in the outreach and a lack of  Latino and Spanish-speaking representation in leadership to make these decisions. My challenge  was to lead the design of an outreach project that visually represented Latinos as a very diverse  community, across generations in the US, Spanish-speaking and Spanglish-speaking, and not only  had Latinos centered in the outreach but also leading the outreach, in charge of their storytelling of  the outreach. I used the storytelling perspective in design thinking to collaboratively brainstorm,  design, and implement a project that was Latino led, Latino centered, for a Latino audience. Since  white Americans had been attempting to tell the story of Latinos in the US for so long, a perspective  shift was required, a retaking of the narrative was needed, a centering of Latino narration in the  telling of Latino history was needed.

Application

Storytelling is key to any marketing, community outreach efforts. The design thinking

principle of storytelling was needed because there has been a historical disconnect and lack of  visual representation in ILO stories told about Latinos and Latino history with parks. text: Challenge & Selection     “You have always been good in storytelling” my friends and family said to me in last ten years. I  can tell about my dream like a novel or a movie. They like listening to me. I must confest that I  like telling. Even my anecdotes amused them. I know it is about how to tell more than what you  tell : )  I have lots of stories about this but I will tell you the last one.       Application   My friend, Mohammed, wanted to learn German language but he always feared to give up early. He had not no  time to go to a course. I recommend him a software “Rosetta Stone”. He couldn’t believe because a  software cannot achieve this. I needed a story to manipulate him. I knew the programme and I really  knew how beneficial and functional it is. I said “Mohammed, this is amazing pogramme. You have ability to learn a  language. I had a friend who wants to Yiddish language to live in Israel. And I think it is more difficult  than German language I think. He started to learn from Rosetta Stone and got some books, and got  some friends on web. He couldn’t believe how he proceed. And do you know what? He lives in Tel Aviv  now. But in real I had no friend like him. Nobody wanted to learn Yiddish and lived in Israel : )      Insight & Approach     I was sure my insight was true. He just need a encouragement. Mohammed doesn’t still know the truth about  Yiddish. But Mohammed can speak German in intermediate level. Sometimes we just need a mini spark to flare.  And a good storytelling can do it easily.

Challenge & Selection    The design thinking tool that I choose as a final reflection is mind mapping. Design  thinking is applied for a group final project in one of the courses that I teach in higher  education. Undergrad students with a mayor in Tourism studies that are close to  completing their credits for graduation take an Information Systems course with the  purpose of achieving better practices on administration. The final project that they work  on is a work-in-progress website that they feel is needed in their field of study. Before  they even start with the website design, they narrow the project idea to an area of  interest within tourism in one of the following fields: gastronomy, health, museums and  exhibitions, and event logistics. After that, they think of a problem that may be solved  by a website or app and begin working on an idea that ends in a user ready prototype.  During this whole process they receive feedback until they are ready to present their  final product and hand in their documentation. The idea to use design thinking with the  mind mapping tool, is for the students to better understand the needs of their future  customers as a human-centered solution, by generating an idea that will be transformed  into a real world creative and useful solution with a user-friendly interface design.    Mind mapping as a tool for this project starts as a mind map, once the area of interest  is chosen, and in a process with the proper design criteria. Design criteria brings a  meaning to all the data by transforming it into information, with the required conditions  met to satisfy the customer’s problem. As said before, the areas to explore are  gastronomy tourism, health tourism, museum and exhibitions tourism, and finally  tourism for event logistics.
