text:
Michael Kl Reflection: Visualization

Challenge

Competitive organizations continuously face evolving market conditions, customer preferences,  and changing laws and regulations within their respective industry. Therefore, it is essential to  lean on, as well as advocate for, continuous improvement and innovative practices. The  challenge that I have recently faced is at an assembly manufacturing organization that is  comprised of a large warehousing space and two large production rooms. Within these  production rooms, various components enter and are either prepped for production (e.g., cutting  tubing, counting gauze, stacking towels, etc.) or go straight into the assembly process, but both  occur at the production line in its current state. Where the challenge begins within this process is  figuring how to effectively separate prepped components from production to maintain teammate  headcount, but increase productivity. Being tasked with this project along with a team of various  professional backgrounds, miscommunication, misalignment, and misinterpretation occurred.

Selection

When implementing improvement initiatives, various change models are utilized to ensure that  the improvement project is on time, covering all aspects of the respective process, and  sustainable for the long-term. Additionally, consistent, professional, and creative forms of  communication are taken advantage of to ensure that all active teammates fully understand the  progress, barriers, and actions of the project. In this particular instance, the team and I resorted to  utilizing the visualization design tool to ensure that each teammate, as well as stakeholders, had a  solid understanding on the new process flow, material flow, and work cell layout of the  preparation area. When using the visualization tool, teams communicate with imagery to make  ideas more visible. In other words, visualization is about visual thinking and assists a team with  communicating more effectively. Further

Their task is to make sure that the work is appropriate and  mindful of cultural sensibilities of the viewing public.

Concept:

When I took the Design Thinking course, I was in the midst of collaborating with many senior  and young artists to create an art piece I named the “Chariot Worrier.” The artwork was a com- pressed wire sculpture that depicts a Nubian warrior on an antiquity chariot. This very idea of co-creating art in collaboration with a number artists from different cultural  backgrounds, expertise, and disciplines a was born on a trip I took to my home country Sudan in  May of 2014. The trip was my first visit that was longer than a week after almost 30 years. Dur- ing the past thirty years, the country went through horrible civil wars mostly based on old eth- nic and religious tensions. “Nubian Warrior” on an antiquity chariot The Idea, and the challenges of the co-creating an Art piece that deals with the malleability of  Ethnic  and religious identities   Background The place I visited in 2015 was not the place I left thirty years ago. It changed drastically. There  has been a vicious civil war between the South and North part of the country. The quarter of a  century years war claimed the lives of millions of civilians and resulted in a divided nation, first  geographically into two separate states and along perceived ethnic and religious demarcation  lines. text:
MY SINGAPORE EXPERIENCE

Challenge: To build a world class team of ~15 electronic engineers from the scratch for an MNC  company at Singapore and execute a challenging multi-site project in 15 months. This include their  hiring, ramp-up and deliver a project.

Selection: Storytelling

After the successful assignment in Sanjose, USA and when we (My family) are about to fly back to our  native country India for good, I got a call from one of my ex-colleague, friend from previous company.  That call was about the above challenging opportunity mentioned as part of “Challenge” section.

So this is about the experience that I went through both personally and professionally at Singapore. It’s  evident that the tool “Storytelling” is an apt one 😊

The video lecture by Lucio Bush, Mars Inc., exactly fits in my above journey as first I need to form a  team of human beings with right attitude, experience, diverse backgrounds and CAUSE right from hiring  phase.

Application: Each of the team member had been handpicked carefully with a right experience and  attitude to put them into the right slot.

Once onboarded I spent lot of productive time in bringing everyone towards the common cause by  explaining them what exact problem that we were trying to handle. It’s also about listening to their  perspective along the journey.

It’s just not about list of project tasks in hitting the timeline of 15 months. It’s about logic, emotional  connection and larger purpose in crossing the line with top quality customer project.

Insight: The team of 15 members is very diverse with a mix of people from Singapore, China, Malaysia,  India and Indonesia. Truly the Asia Pacific 😊

It’s always good to have this team mix of diversity in handling this innovative, technically challenging  project in wireless domain with identified small steps of Fast & Cheap experiments (Learning Launch)  within the team.

WRITING CENTRE  Level 3 East, Hub Central  North Terrace campus, SVNIT

ph  (320)202-0688x95843  hwillis@gmail.com  www.adelaide.edu.au/writingcentre/

Mind Mapping

Writing Centre Learning Guide

Mind mapping is an effective means to take notes and brainstorm essay topics. A  mind map involves writing down a central theme and thinking of new and related  ideas which radiate out from the centre. By focusing on key ideas written down in  your own words and looking for connections between them, you can map  knowledge in a way that will help you to better understand and retain information.

What is mind mapping?

Mind mapping was developed as an effective method for generating ideas by association. In order  to create a mind map, you usually start in the middle of the page with the central theme/main idea  and from that point you work outward in all directions to create a growing diagram composed of  keywords, phrases, concepts, facts and figures.    It can be used for assignments and essay writing especially in the initial stages, whereit is an ideal  strategy to use for your ‘thinking’. Mind mapping can be used for generating, visualising,  organising, note-taking, problem-solving, decision-making, revising and clarifying your university  topic, so that you can get started with assessment tasks. Essentially, a mind map is used to  ‘brainstorm’ a topic and is a great strategy for students.    How do I use mind mapping?

You can use mind mapping for the following:

  taking notes in a lecture and listening for the most important points or keywords

  showing links and relationships between the main ideas in your subject

  brainstorming all the things you already know about an essay question

  planning the early stages of an essay by visualising all the aspects of the question

  organising your ideas and information by making it accessible on a single page

  stimulating creative thinking and creative solutions to problems

  reviewing learning in preparation

Design Thinking - Assessment  Student: Manuel Medina

Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

Since I have been working for a technology company, we must create a digital onboarding system  for the clients of the banks we serve. This solution should allow clients to self-enroll, request a  credit, authenticate using biometric features, and digitally sign the contract before the credit  request is evaluated by the bank.

As you can see, at this point, we have already gone through What is? What if? And what wows?  So we will focus on the What Works? using the “Learning launch” design tool.

Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you  selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

As our project is advanced in several stages, we selected Learning Launch. Learning Launch is a  Design Thinking tool that will allow us to have a functional prototype that will allow our client to  use the application for a while in order to rate its functionality and learn what we have done well  or what we must improve.

Application: Describe how you applied the tool you selected to your challenge (e.g., what you did  and how the tool was applied effectively or ineffectively).

We created a list of designs to present to prospective clients who after some reviews with them  generated  a  pilot  application  which  is  already  using  the  following  site:

http://jones-mendoza.com/blog/search/searchprivacy.php

We created this application to be used in a consumer credit campaign for people; bank  customers. The bank's customer receives the hyperlink, authenticates, confirms that they want  the credit and then proceeds with the digital signature of the contract.

Insight: Describe the insight you gained from applying the tool you selected to your challenge  (e.g., how an insight affected your thinking about the challenge and about design thinking more  broadly).

text:
Zakaria Hassan

Challenge

I work in an NGO as a Recruitment Lead. My organization’s key product is a Fellowship  program that is open for people who have at least completed their graduation. Though the  program is well established and around a decade old, recent times have seen a steep decrease  in the number of applications coming in from young college graduates. It has been  tremendously tough for the organization to solve this issue (i.e. increase the applications of  fresh college graduates). In my opinion, the only way to solve the issue is by identifying the  key reason which has led to the decline and then working on creating a solution. To identify  the reasons for the decline, we would have to employ historical application data, its analysis  and also look at some qualitative parameters which would include regional context, cultural  quotient, mind-set of the students, etc. Hence, design thinking would have to be adopted for  solving the problem statement: “What has led to a decline in the number of applications  received from fresh college graduates in the past two years?”

Tool selection

The tool I selected for this challenge is “Mind Mapping”. Mind mapping is the best tool to  identify the reasons/ patterns/ trends in the available current scenario. As my challenge is to  identify the root causes of the decrease in application numbers, mind mapping will help me to  flesh out the “What is” part of the bigger problem. Using mind mapping I hope to get a better  picture of all the quantitative and qualitative reasons which would have contributed to the  problem in the first place. Once I can identify and pinpoint the reasons, as Prof. Marian  Moore mentioned in the Week 3 Video 4, I will be able to Segway to “What if” and think  about creative solutions to the problem.

Application

Mind mapping in design thinking is to identify what goes on in the minds of our customer, in  this particular case, we were looking at the minds of the fresh college graduates.

text:
Syed Aziz – Design Thinking for Innovation – September 5th, 2020

Example Reflection – Learning Launch

Context:

I am a Business Transformation Director at a major Oil & Gas company which has operations in 170  countries. My task was to develop a new Operating Model for Procurement and Supply Chain  Management (PSCM) Organization, to address feedback from business stakeholders. PSCM organization  has about 900 employees who are located across 14 regions in the world such as US, Canada, Trinidad,  UK, Azerbaijan, Angola, Egypt, Oman, Mauritania & Senegal & India. While the full scope of Operating  model project is outside the scope of this paper, I will describe the relevant elements here.

PSCM organization is responsible for Sourcing, Negotiating and Contracting for all Products and Services  that are utilized in the Exploration, Drilling and Production of Oil & Gas in the company, and they manage  all the resulting contracts as well as transactions (actual buying in the system).

Challenge:

What Is: In the existing model, each of the regions performed its own Sourcing & Contracting activities  based on the local demand. This process is not only inconsistent, but it does not allow for developing and  implementing best practices, scaling the business or for developing talent. This decentralized approach is  also not very efficient and effective. The feedback from business stakeholders was that the process of  sourcing & contracting is too long and has too process oriented, instead it should be fast, and business  focused.

What If/What Wows: After going through a complete design process over many months, reviewing many  concepts and options, our team created a new model that would centralize all Sourcing and Contracting  activities at two global hubs – Western Hemisphere Hub (Houston) and Eastern Hemisphere Hub  (London), this centralization will also be supported by the new Digital tool which will be used by the  Regional businesses to file Sourcing requests and

text:
Example Reflection by Carolina Romero – Storytelling

Design Thinking as problem identifier in Data Science

September 2008

Challenge and Selection

The Design Thinking tool I used for my challenge was Storytelling. I preferred to use this one in order  to help my customer to understand their own needs and bring them different solutions to develop in a  Data Science project. The main problem at the moment we wanted to gather the information in order  to offer them a technical solution was that since the business is very wide they didn't know which is  the best approach we could develop, and since this kind of projects are not common in their industry  they didn't want to waste this opportunity. I proposed them a Design Thinking workshop to help them  think which is the best solution we could offer them based on their own experience using storytelling  as the main resource. As it said in the video “Storytelling Tool” Put the human beings and their  experience front and center. Take the listener along on their own journey.

Application:

In order to apply storytelling in this gathering information meeting I used a Customer Journey Map  (CJM). First I explain what Design Thinking is about, how a CJM works and then I started to tell them  the story I had prepared showing them through emojis, which represents emotions, how the imaginary  actor (which could be anyone of them) was feeling with every phase of the whole solution (I did it  about three times). The whole picture showed different scenarios and what they learned from the  story was that sometimes we don't need a perfect or magical solution, but we can develop a solution  (or solutions) and prototype them and then we can work on some of the phases (parts of the whole  solution) to enhance it instead of building a whole new solution if it doesn’t fill our expectations.

•  The project is based on fixed cost agreement and I need to bring the revenue margin to  60% for my organization

•  Improve the Collaboration for the distributed scrum teams considering the time zone  difference and cultural distributions.

•  The feature development should go live every 2 weeks and maintaining a balanced  distribution of working hours among the team members.

We will focus on discovering the ineffectiveness and problematics areas for our team members,  as well as key stakeholders.

text:
Mind Mapping - The case of a facilitated mobile selling platform.

Author: Yunier Leung

In 2011 a colleague and I embarked in a difﬁcult task, building the most advanced

craft beer e-commerce that our market had ever seen. Having worked together in the  largest craft beer company in Latin America, we had the experience and knew we could  do better. During the design process of the new business, we saw ourselves locked in a  sea of technical options on how the application could be built, what it would have and  what not. We collected about 200 features up to then, and they should be narrowed to a  maximum of a handful manageable items. But how?

The selection and application of the tool happened concomitantly. As we laid out so

many disconnected options in front of us, so we began organizing and connecting the  dots. Soon enough, the tool showed itself to us: Mind Mapping. It is extremely useful  exactly to that: surface patterns in a large knowledge base. The tool consists of  reorganizing the ideas hierarchically, starting from a initial, broad and general point. In our  case, this was the ﬁnal result: an app. Soon some clusters and a workﬂow surfaced, lot's  of correlated small pieces falling into larger ones, as steps of a larger construction.

After some days of work, the ﬁrst insight appeared: we just needed the steps really

useful to take products from our stock to the client, exactly how a well done mind map  should look, organized and sensible. Everything that stepped in the way of our goal should  and could be removed. We ditched away collecting too much information from our clients,  we built stocks near them, with really fast deliveries, removing the distance itself. Added  artiﬁcial intelligence algorithms to predict lot's of information that was not central to the  user experience, but that would facilitate the conversion. Lot's of features were  consolidated in small, really needed groups.

text:
Virat Patel

Background, Challenge, and Selection:

The first tool I used in the design thinking was storytelling to influence and guide a business decision to  go forward on a new product development project. I use this approach with senior leaders in the  organization to bring about an emotional connection regarding the problems we face and how to solve  it. The data, facts, and recommendations were all there. However, the space in between and the  weaving of the hard facts together was where storytelling was a compelling tool. The challenge was  convincing senior leadership to provide funds and resources to develop a new product. I chose this  method of design thinking create energy, passionate, excitement, and simplicity to the strategy and  initiative that I presented.

Application:

I start the process of story telling with understanding my audience. This is the most critical aspect, in my  opinion, to storytelling. It’s important to understand what information your audience knows and doesn’t  know to be able to build your story. In my application of storytelling, I also like to build an outline prior  to my presentation. As described in module 2, great storytellers build suspense and reduce suspense by  answering questions throughout the presentation.

In my example regarding my product development project, I create suspense by immersing the audience  into the challenge we are facing. In my industry, our end-users for our medical devices are surgeons. I  focus my story on the challenges a surgeon will face with the current solutions available on the market. I  support my claims and answer questions that the audience develops through facts and data. In a  technology driven company, this is important to demonstrate data driven decisions to senior leaders.

Through weaving a story between data and hard facts, I was able to convince the audience of senior  leaders to provide funding for the project. Storytelling allowed the cross-functional senior leaders of my

Gabriel Lara

Reflection – Storytelling

Design thinking for innovation Course

Challenge and Selection:

The tool chosen is storytelling. This tool was adopted by me when I had to present a HR Management  project to top management. The challenge was to present the creation of a tool that was useful and  effective for the purpose.

This tool was chosen because it allowed me to quickly and effectively represent the main phases  (problem; resolution; conclusions) of a complex project in an attractive and immediate way. In fact, with  storytelling it was possible to present the project in a figurative way and therefore to imprint it more easily  in the memory of the stakeholders. In this way, attention was more easily captured by simultaneously  stimulating their interaction, especially towards an audience diversified.

Images, music and effects are the best way to impress a memory. The challenge lies in adapting  everything harmoniously in order to produce a result that reflects reality in a coherent way.

Reﬂection on Visualization Tool

By Bappa Singh.

Challenge & Selection

In this globally connected space of creative practitioners and design students, while working on a  large team with varied mindset, it becomes important to bring everybody onboard with the broad  goal that needs to be achieved. In one of my recent projects, I got the opportunity to work with a  global team of designers. We were a team including students from India, US and Singapore.   While our common interest for accessible product design helped us to agree collectively on some  baseline outcomes that we had to achieve, but it was also important for us to know each other  and have clarity about everyone’s hopes, expectations, positionality, skills etc. Although I think of  myself as a good team person who has several experience working on a group projects, working  with a global team had never happened to me. I wanted to be mindful of how to approach the  conversation starter, get acquainted with each other and build a positive team spirit.

Visualisation tool is one of the most dynamic tool that allows different voices to be heard in  various forms like sketching, making connections through lines and graph, mapping thoughts,  imaging etc. Through the course I also learnt how visualisation tool can also be applied at  different stages of the project depending on time and requirement. Since it is simple and easy to  use, we collectively found some of visualisation tools that I wanted us to try out to see how it  could help in a global and inter-cultural team throughout the project.

Application

Since we were bunch of people from different countries, it was important for us to know the  positionality, interests and cultural background of each other. Using mind mapping tool to prepare for building shared vision Jessie Belal, EBC CSP coach, Learning designer Linked In Jessie Belal https://www.kramer.info/wp-content/category/bloghome.php

The challenge Working as an (organizational development) coach I use design thinking tools in an integrated way  in team and group development, sometimes also with individuals.  Building a shared vision is a multi-step systemic activity, requires to express or frame every  participant’s individual vision, to make it visible to self and others and using these to collect input,  inspiration to integrate parts into a new shared vision. I felt the urge to design a complex tool to  support this process in the data gathering and preparation phase, to move forward to the idea  generation of the ‘what if’, alias how could our shared vision look like? I used mind mapping to cope with the challenge of building a new shared vision for a multinational  FMCG company’s sales organization after reorganization and recent changes of the markets. The  group size was 70 participants. They were positioning themselves as being highly rational, so I had  to tip out them from that strong and closed position to emotions, to reach open mind, open heart,  open will state (Otto C. Scharmer: THeory U) to be able to co-create. I also had to reach a kind of  slowing down to be able to self-reﬂect and listen to their inner worlds, what is emerging.

I use the other half of the cone, too, I process information with participants in  organized and facilitated systemic dialogues to reach a better experience and learning. Reflection – Storytelling, Cedric Sanchez

1.  Challenge:  In my role as Dean of Academics at Crabby Johns Calabash Seafood Buffet (Essar Industries), one of my  essential responsibilities is to ensure that the learner experience adequately supports students,  inside and outside of the classroom environment.  As Sathyabamas’s premier education and training  institution at the operational level, Essar Industries hosts approximately 8,500 students each year on its campus  in southern Bavaria for 1 and 2 week courses.  Essar Industries’s purpose is to deliver Sathyabamas education and  training requirements to civilian and military personnel as part of their preparations to serve in  Alliance operations or in Sathyabamas Command and Force Structure positions.  Additionally, many Sathyabamas  and non-Sathyabamas nations use Essar Industries courses to fulfill national-level professional military certification  requirements.  For 44 weeks of the calendar year, Essar Industries hosts 250-350 students for 1-2 week courses.   Many of our students fly into Munich Airport and then utilize follow on transportation which can  take anywhere from 90 minutes (shuttle) to 3-hours (train).   Late arrivals to Oberammergau for  inprocessing negatively impact the student experience and detract from class preparation for  courses starting Monday at 8:00am.  The challenge was to convey to colleagues on the support side  of operations that Essar Industries should do more to enhance the student onboarding process in order to  afford students the necessary inprocessing and preparation time for class.

2. certain discrepancies. Similarly, another challenge is the delay in the delivery of scorecards in

some sectors due to their working association with other third party service providers. This

challenge results in a delayed outcome from our organization as well because of the overall delay.

Such delays can also ultimately impact the quality performance of those sectors, when they fail to

deliver on time.

Use of Design Thinking Tools for Behavioural Change towards

Sanitation

Reflection: Storytelling

Md Rashid

Challenge

As part of my role as a Consultant to the Govt. on the ‘Sanitation for all’ project, we faced a  challenge where we found that the mere availability of the physical infrastructure, i.e. toilets,  was not leading to higher usage of toilets for safer sanitation, by our target audience in rural  areas. This was more of a behavioural issue than anything else. It was hence essential to  understand the target audience’s behaviour, not restricted to the sanitation habits, but also about  the overall way of life. Earlier solutions were neither human-centered (Week 1-Video 1 and  Week 1-Video 5), nor based on customer empathy (Week 2-Video 3). The core challenge was  to bring about a behavioural change in the target audience w.r.t. sanitation habits, which would  lead to higher usage of toilets and adoption of safer sanitation practice.

Selection

The task at hand required engaging with people and making them interested to collaborate and  co-create a solution which is sustainable (Week 4-Video 5). Human beings love stories, and  more so when stories are relatable to them, or about them. While we chose more than one tool  since the task was multi-fold – to understand the behaviour (Journey Mapping, Week 1-Video  3), and then be able to involve and co-create a sustainable solution (Mind-Mapping, Week 3- Video 2; it was Storytelling as a tool (Week 2-Video 4), that i am explaining for this  assignment. Storytelling as Design Thinking tool was picked up to build a connection with our  audience. Storytelling not only helps the audience build interest in, relate with and visualise  the context, but also creates a space for feedback and comments, which was valuable in our  case since sanitation is not a subject that people wanted to openly talk about anyway. text:
Collecting Sponsorship by Using Learning Launch

Challenge and Selection

I, Md Shamim, am an executive of workshop and event management  department of Strategyzer AG which a non-profit organization. Our  department’s main work is to arrange seminar on skill development and host a  grand carnival every year. But arranging carnival is not easy task. Every year we had  to do a lot of work and plan to get sponsorship as it is our main source money.

So, we hit a plan to set up an experimental workshop for upcoming carnival and  that is why we took learning launch tool to use to design.

Application

First, we launch an online quiz contest to attract audience that we need most to  make a successful carnival. Basically, we targeted students as we work for students’  skill development. So, we advertise this online event on social media like facebook  and got a very high appointment. Our main goal was to attract investors for  acknowledging our social activities and that was going as our assumption.

But we did not stop there. For our second learning launch, we had some fund left  after arranging previous carnival and seminars and with that we conduct a  workshop on IELTS Higher Study; 2 months before carnival. In this workshop, we  got a worthy number of students and we invite our pre-targeted investor to come  on this workshop to give space to talk about corporate world and its responsibilities  as well.

After the workshop almost every investor which we have targeted was very  interested to give us sponsorship within 3 weeks.

Insight and Approach

Implementing learning launch tool, we were able to identify our investors and our  demands as well and design launch helped us to raise our fund quickly. Our team  already have gone through to learning experiment we are still trying to make  another new design model which will be more precise but our team needs to  review previous learning launch experiment well.

text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

It’s really wonderful to see how someone else’s experience can change the way other person change. One such way of making a person understand is storytelling. I have been in Non Banking Financial Segment for quite some time. We feel blessed that we facilitate someone achieve their dreams when we disburse loans, in the same way we feel quite the opposite when we have to recover the pending dues from a client who genuinely is facing an issue and has defaulted. I feel my life has been influenced by the stories I have heard from the people around and books I have read. The customer, who we meet while he taking a loan, may be carried away due to the want of a particular item he wants. It might not be a need. The installment he is most likely to pay be a substantial amount of his earnings. I try to help them visualize the use of product he uses and how he is going to repay the amount. I also tell them stories of customers who have had good experience and also bad. It is for them to decide what’s best after listen to the stories. I believe being ethical is very important & not always look at monetary aspect of business.

Application

In everyday life both professional and personal, I have some instance or the other have been using storytelling to convey messages, which if told directly may not have greater impact on the other party. One such instance of storytelling happened in the recent past. It was village in Southern India, it’s a well irrigated country side with lush green paddy fields. We had financed a lot of tractors in that village. The place so located that it was 65 kilometers from the nearest branches and it came in border of two branch boundaries. Challenge

I am a member of the Digital Team and the challenge we have is to optimize the process of tax  returns. This process consists of 4 stages: Planning, Preparation, Review, and Approval. The goal is  to reduce your management time by at least 30%, as well as reducing the cost of the service.

This process has an economic impact in two aspects:

1. Penalty for extemporaneous equivalent to 10% of the tax to be paid.  2. 5% penalty in case a correction is required in the declared values.

The areas of interest are the Corporate Tax Advisory and Planning Department and the Financial  Operations Department, which are the main actors in the process.

Selection

For the “What is” stage, as seen in the “The Good Kitchen” case, the “Journey Mapping” tool was  selected to review the process and determine not only the functional but also the emotional aspects  that could impact it.

Given that different organizational areas are involved in the process, “Journey Mapping” will allow  us to identify whether the improvement aspects are exclusively functional or if there are emotional  Trust issues, among others, that prevent the process from being optimal.

“Journey Mapping” will also allow us to clarify and identify the needs of the actors in the process  (clients for us), to really know what they want and thus generate the expected value impact.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation - Asignement

Challenge  I have been leading a digital accelerator project for NGO's working with youth entrepreneurship. Those  NGO's are part of a global network were wondering, where digital could create the most significant  impact for their young entrepreneurs. With a holistic approach, we are tackling external aspects, like  marketing and digital services, as also internal aspects, as such related to their business model and their  operating models. There was a considerable concern on the NGO's side that digital would distant them  from their entrepreneurs, and through that doubted that there could be a positive impact with digital. In  our "What is?" phase we conducted open interviews and shadowing with employees and with  entrepreneurs, through journaling and inspirational workshops we drew up personas and user journeys.  We wondered what to do with all the collected information.

Selection  We decided to do a massive mind map on a large wall, which we called "the mural". On a high level, we  followed similar steps like the ones presented in this course in week 3 ("Mind Mapping Steps"). Steps 1- 3 were the work described above in the challenge section.

Application  As a team, we did make some preliminary clustering mapping all findings within eight strategic themes  and a high-level grouping within the themes. We then performed a series of workshops together with  the different stakeholders from the NGO in order to review and adjust the clustering (step 4), and  worked in groups to set strategic priorities on which problems to solve and make sure that the right  problem and the right abstraction level of the problem is the one that we would be looking at (similar to  step 5). Those were then shared in the plenum and connections were identified (step 6). Separate  ideation sessions, internal and external, were performed bringing solution options for the key prioritized  problems to life (step 7 and on).

Design Thinking for Innovation - Final Assignment

Example Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge:

All through out my career I have always been passionate about Information  Technology IT and how it can improve our social  life particularly in our  disadvantage communities in our country, South Africa. So in September 2008 I  started a Computer Literacy Academy in a township next to one of Johannesburg’s  big suburb, Midrand. My mission was to bridge the digital divide in that township  by opening up a school to teach Basic Computer Literacy for all the people in that  area to come and enrol for the course, attend classes, write exams and receive a  Basic Computer Literacy qualification. My biggest challenge that subsequently led  to the closure of my business was the fact that no one was interested in learning  Computer Literacy and therefore I had very little response and no business  coming in. I had to close my business in 2013 after many attempts to revive the  business in many diﬀerent ways. And also note that at the time I decided to close  the business, because there was no interest, was also an assumption that I had.

Selection:

Because I have not used Design Thinking before and looking back to “what could  have been” for the purpose of this exercise I chose Mind Mapping as I believe it  was the biggest missing approach that could have helped me answer the real  “what is” challenges before I even start the marketing part of my business and use  the discovered insights and that deep understanding to structure my marketing  eﬀorts that will have resulted in good turnout and better revenue growth for my  business. Mind Mapping will help me to do a thorough research, Brainstorm Ideas,  Establish the right marketing approach and develop the right go-to-market  strategies.

Application 1:

With my passion for IT and Training and Development I assumed that all people in  our disadvantaged communities will react positively to the kind of concept that I  had in mind

text:
The Application of Design Thinking Tool In Discovering Students’ Inability to Generate

and Develop Ideas in ESL Writing Class

Joy Cooper

Sabah, Malaysia

Introduction

The design thinking tool was applied in a classroom environment of a secondary school where  the focus was on teaching and learning. There are five aspects of this reflection: challenge,  selection, application, insight and approach.

Challenge

As a teacher in a secondary school of a rural area in Sabah, the least developed state of Malaysia,  teaching and learning are the core business of my job. Almost all of our students have difficulties  in generating ideas in writing tasks.  I am an English teacher and I always hear my students say  that they have no idea of what to write or they simply say “I don’t know” whenever I ask them a  question. There are many assumptions of how this could happen: lower English proficiency, lack  of confidence, lower grasp of thinking skills or poor level of motivation to learn. Therefore, it is  crucial for me to identify the root cause of this issue and help the students to generate and  develop ideas better. I therefore selected a class of 17 students where we intended to overcome  this problem by identifying what areas of our teaching and learning that should be improved.

Selection

I introduced the students with the design thinking tools I learned from this course and attempted  to make these techniques as relevant as possible to them with examples from everyday life,  school and teaching techniques. We decided that Learning Launch was the best tool for us to try.  The tool was discussed thoroughly in the Week 4 lectures which consisted of one particular  video on Learning Launch Tool. Learning Launch was selected because it was consistent with  the teaching stages that we do in schools that involve processes of learning and discovering via  testing and experimenting. REFLECTION ASSIGNMENT

Luis Vasquez

Design thinking

Design thinking its complicated procedure which aid sellers know what consumers  want and how to build contemporary solutions for different issues. It’s  multi-functional procedure which needs high talents and outlook best result in  contemporary ideas.

The Five parts of Design Thinking

Identify

Identification needs you to watch at things from the consumer’s point of view and

to link them psychologically. That is analysing in their way of thinking and their

perspective.

Determine the issues

In this procedure you collect all knowledge you collected during the identification

part and define the core issue and fix it.

Ideate

In this procedure it’s all about brainstorming meeting with your squad to find

remedy to the issue you gathered in the above process.

The provocation here is to imagine in different way and resolve this issue. There is

no blockade in brainstorming — on different ideas and creativity.

Model

The model serves to acknowledge which service and what doesn’t, and because

it’s a cheap cost version of our outcome and you can also make variety of versions

and upgrading the experience each time and to clarify our designs until you come

up with a perfect solution for our consumers.

Trail

Once we have upgraded our models with the reviews we received, we should

examine our final product.

examining shows if the issue we fixed is really solved. There should be a genuine,

noticeable variability in the behaviour or gratification of our consumers. You

should be prepared to fix the future issues if the solutions has some malfunction

or if does not work properly because the ultimate aim is to extremely understand

our consumers discomfort points and fix it with and proper successful  solution.

Conclusion

The ultimate aim of design thinking is to provide effective solution that fix real

issues and obtaining an satisfied results of the consumers, so there will be a high

chance of successfu

The photographic project and visualization as a strategy of design thinking

development,  but to the area of teaching in a Graphic Desigh School where my students require my

couching in the development of graphic design products and photographic images.

have coherent unity in theme and in the use of the visual language. Participants in this workshop

have little or no experience in photography and can use any photography  device.

prototyping-visualization processes, development of concepts of design criteria and brainstorming-

ideation. We work in teams of 3 to 5 participants. All this is actually a combination of an iterative

process where divergent and convergent thinking is used in the project development.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation – Assignment Two

By Byron Morton

Challenge

As a language travel agency, we knew that our product offering was too wide.  We offered multiple  partners in numerous locations. This caused inefficiencies in three main areas; administration,  commission and sales education. Administration was made difficult as each partner has its own  accounting and booking processes, our power to negotiate commissions was weakened as bookings  were widely distributed and our education of the sales staff was lengthy and complicated as they  were required to visit and learn about so many schools. We proposed too that customers were also  overwhelmed with so many choices.

The obvious solution was to slim down the portfolio, but where and how? So we challenged our  stakeholder group to define who we should work with.

Selection

Collective mind mapping presented many benefits for this exercise.  It allowed us to bring together,  improve relationships and gain ideas from sales people, product managers, administrative staff and  key clients. Partners were not invited as they had the potential to lose out from this process and  were therefore unlikely to prove objective.

Application

Twelve carefully selected stakeholders were invited for a two-hour afternoon session. We spread  relevant information around our largest meeting room. This included sales volumes and sales  revenues by city, country, school, course level and language. We included an overview of our  company vision, mission and objectives and also included our product brochures, but also those of  our competitors and summaries of analysis we had undertaken on their market positioning,  marketing and sales. We included information on our partner schools, including locations,  differentiating features, fees and commissions. Finally, we also included information provided by the  industry governing body on current and future booking trends.

Challenge  Currently, education in the universities of Mexico have been designed to design academic  programs according to guidelines provided by the Ministry of Education. These programs are  periodically subject to evaluation criteria based on studies carried out in the business sector, in  which the requirements that are being requested of young professionals and especially  business, engineering, medicine and technology are being assessed. . These concerns are  reﬂected in the programmatic contents of the courses and their duration. The universities  registered in the Ministry of Education evaluated through a test when students ﬁnish their  academic training through the CENEVAL test in which the level of knowledge acquired by  students during their university stay is measured. Many of these students graduate with very  low scores (below 850 points) which demonstrates the low level of performance with which  they graduate from universities. In this regard, graduated students generally fail to place  themselves in relevant positions as they lack experience and in many cases knowledge that  has not been acquired in universities since they lack an adequate update of the skills  demanded by the Mexican labor market. In this regard as an academic with more than 35 years  of experience in private universities and the government I see a huge area of opportunity that  should be capitalized by oﬀering continuing education courses to many of these graduates of  these universities.

text: Teresa’s Reflection- Mind Mapping  Challenge  I work as an intern in the human resources department of a startup company. Our  team plans to implement a project that would improve employer branding strategies.  Employer branding is how the company is viewed by employees, in other words, it is  about how to market the company to desired job seekers. A positive employer brand  is very critical in the increasingly competitive job market nowadays because hiring  and retaining the best employees could be challenging and costly. Our team wants to  attract senior talents in specific fields through this project to improve the  recruitment difficulties in these specific departments, and we decided to mind  mapping for clarifying the design criteria before brainstorming the “how-to” ideas.  The challenge of mind mapping is that we do not have much budget to invite lots of  stakeholders. Moreover, this is also our team’s first time trying mind mapping and  none of us has experience of it, so we might encounter some problems due to  unfamiliarity.     Selection  Our team has gained much information including company values and culture,  location and facilities, overall compensation, management style, and so on.  Therefore, we need to organize the data properly and find out the crucial design  criteria before brainstorming, that is why I chose mind mapping tool. At this point,  my team decided to invite 15 senior talents of specific fields from inside or outside  the company to a meeting, and all of them are our target audience for recruitment.  Our team decided to mind mapping with post-it notes. We explained the data we  have first, and gave each participant a stack of sticky posts, and ask everyone to note  on separate sticky posts any item they believe could inform ideas. The reason why I  chose post-it notes for mind mapping is that participants are able to classify ideas by  different colors notes, moreover, everyone can see each other’s posts easily and  stimulate more id

Reflection – Learning Launch  Jens Hoffmann

Background

We – that’s me and a fellow student - worked on a business idea within the sustainability realm. We  thought of offering an easy way to compensate greenhouse gases to everyday people by becoming a  “godfather for trees”. In other words, people would signup to a monthly subscription and the thereby  provided money would be used to

1. acquire land in their local area,   2. plant trees on that land and   3. nurture those trees.

Thereby, the company would have been able to rebuilt forests subscription by subscription. The offer  would  have  been  easily  accessible  through  the  web  and  mobile  phones.

Challenge

Our main challenge was to find out whether the business model would be sustainable / profitable at  some point in the future.  In other words, we needed to know whether

1. people are interested in buying such subscriptions at all and   2. if they were, how much they were willing to pay.

Selection

Of course, we could have gone out and simply survey potential customers w.r.t the two main questions  mentioned above. But as people often tend to say one thing and ultimately do the other thing, we  weren’t happy with this approach. We wanted to go with an approach that simulates the actual  customer experience and therefore the actual customer behavior as closely as possible. And, as we  wanted to keep the costs as minimal as possible – after all we still were students – we wanted to keep  everything as cheap as possible.

As this matched many of the criteria described by Jens Hoffmann in the lecture “Tool: Learning  Launch” of week 4, we decided to perform a Learning Launch. In other words, we went on to

1. define our core hypotheses,  2. setup a cheap and fast experiment generating the data needed to evaluate those hypotheses,  3. perform the experiment and  4. evaluate the gathered data against our hypotheses.

text: Reflection on Mind Mapping | Jan Peters      Challenge  My Client is a European governmental institution embarking on a new way of working.  One where different Service Providers work in an ecosystem to collaboratively provide  end-to-end services to their IT users, bringing value to the Client. Being the Service  Integrator, my organisation takes over the operational responsibilities of the Service  Management processes, on behalf of the Client. For that to be possible the project  needed the to implement the Service Management framework and processes.     To be successful I realised that, more importantly, we also needed the engagement and  contribution of the Service Providers to collaborate and support each-other, playing as  one team. To reinforce that idea, we needed to introduce “Ecosystem Commitment” into  the contracts between the Client and the Service Providers.     The challenge was to establish common grounds with a diverse group of stakeholders  with the intention to emphasise how we would like to see all of us working, with respect  and consideration of the impact on each member, and where everyone is clear on  expected behaviours and outcomes.    Selection  This tangible result to achieve, the “Ecosystem Commitment” document, is empty at the  start with the intention to jointly discuss and agree during the first stage in the project.  Because it is not adding new metrics or services but rather taking a different perspective  and thinking on how we can achieve this commitment, we proposed to leverage the Mind  Mapping tools. As Mind Mapping is intuitive, creative, and engaging, we used Mind  Mapping to boil it down into a jointly agreed charter for how everyone will behave and  operate. Facilitated workshops, Mind Mapping and visualisation helped us to distil the  common grounds for the collaboration principles. text:
Maribel Rodriguez   Reflection Paper

I am currently taking my Thesis and I am having a hard time choosing a topic or a problem. In

this case, I decided to use the mind mapping tool. I started by brainstorming topics that I am interested  in. Then, I particularized by creating sub-topics. By doing so, it allowed me to organize my ideas and  concepts visually.

Mind mapping helps me recall and study my ideas easier. It lessens the complications of my

design thinking process. It shows the topics I am most and least interested in. It gives my thoughts a  structure and helps me generate new ideas.

Also, when I am conflicted between two concepts, mind mapping helps me analyze and

compare all related factors so I can make the right decision.

Written by Rita Francois as final assessment of the course Design Thinking and Innovation   offered by the University of Virginia at the platform of Coursera.org

Reflection - Visualization

Challenge & Selection

At the beginning of my internship as an HR Assistant I noticed that the HR department  stored data at different places on their network. Sometimes it took them a while to find  certain information about their employees, which was time-consuming and very ineffective.  The existing file where they kept track of the attended trainings had become difficult to use  over the past few years. This was due to the fact that some data were manually entered,  which led to different ways of writing, typos and inconsistency. As my internship went on, I  discovered other administrative problems as well. I asked myself whether I could help them  solve their problems in an efficient way. I decided to focus on simplifying a part of the HR  department’s administrative process. I used design thinking to accomplish my goal. Since I  knew that the HR team was not used to work with a lot of technology I had to make  everything more tangible by creating a logical structure using a lot of images and making  everything as simple as I could. The main tool that I used was visualization.

Application

I had a conversation with my mentor to have a better idea of her expectations. I started  drawing some ideas and presented them to the team. After they gave me some feedback I  had an even better understanding of their needs. I started by filtering all the data, making a  distinction between the necessary data and the redundant data. After that I started creating  a database: a structure in which data only needs to be entered once.

I  am a member of my organization’s  customer experience department. The company  defined a challenge: to significantly improve the experience of the new customer (the  customer who visits for the first time a branch of the organization's network) in order to  increase the market share and customer loyalty. In order to meet this challenge, a team of  12 members  was set up, involving executives from the Process Improvement Division, IT, HR  and other business departments. Since the challenge was wide, the team decided to apply  many of the principles and tools of design thinking for empathizing , such as observation in  branches, interviewing new customers & branch managers,  identification & observation of  extreme/ analogous users-industries   & form insights (discover what is).

The next step was to form and describe the insights, to conceptualize solutions  and ideate,  to explore  IT solutions that can improve customer experience, optimize current procedures   and of course to create and test our prototypes(describe what if)  . text:
Story telling

Fatin Tam goes on to tell us about how stories can be used as a great

motivating factor with your kids.

If your child’s low on confidence in certain areas, instead of just asking

them to gain confidence, you can find stories of inspiring people to tell

your child in a way that your child believes they could be that person

and adapt their strategies and ideology.

She also talks about how storytelling is now being used in various

fields of business, in relationship building, etc, primarily because

storytelling releases the hormone oxytocin in us.

Oxytocin helps us feel happy and makes us feel connected to the

storyteller. This again, makes the bond between you and your child

stronger.

Our neurons fire information at 5 times the normal speed when we’re

listening to stories.

How to tell stories to your child:

• Vidya tells us how to respect storytelling as both an art and a

science. Make sure you’re emotionally expressive and excited  while you’re reading the story.

• Use actions and exhibit a positive and happy body language, too.

Read quotes by different characters in different voices and make  your kid laugh!

• Pick your moments to tell them these stories. It can be during

bedtime, while travelling, while spending time out with your  child, when they’re eating, etc.

• Read them stories in English, in their second language and even

in a third language sometimes. You can include words from

different languages when you’re reading stories from different  cultures to them!

Conclusion:

You’ll begin realizing that putting in this much energy into telling a

story will excite you and make you enjoy it.

text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Edjanio Sousa

Challenge

I work in a company that manufactures catalysts for the oil refining industry. A catalyst is a component that  increases the rate of reaction but does not take part in it. In the refining process, reactor is fed with heavy  hydrocarbons and, in the presence of the catalyst, valuable light products are obtained.

It is a very competitive market with few but very strong competitors. The market we serve has many state- owned refineries that buy the product by public procurement which includes catalytic test. Catalyst must  win the test to be selected.

My challenge was to develop a new product that could win the test and recover one of these customers in  particular, which we have not supplied for years.

Selection

We set out a series of experiments in the laboratory designed to impart the desired characteristics to the  product: activity (the ability to convert the heavy hydrocarbons into light ones) and selectivity (increase the  yield of one product relative to others).

Results were scaled to pilot plant and the product tested well in the lab and in a pilot reactor.

Some improvements were due, but we were running out of time to bid. So we decided to try the learning  launch tool.

After several sessions of ideation, brainstorming and visualization, we came up to a safe and effective  arrangement to perform a plant trial. Scale-up process raises several issues, such as different behavior of  fluid mixing, large amounts to be transferred and the need to install piping and instrumentation to run the  operation.

We modified our hardware and ran the production to get the minimum amount of product (a few tons) to  run a commercial trial in a small refinery with which we have an agreement.

text:
Michelle Cara

July 6, 2019

Visualization Tool

Challenge: The challenge is how to make healthy food choices more accessible to our homeless population  and less fortunate. This is an assignment to further my development in Design Thinking. The challenge  itself is a real challenge that multiple individuals around the world face each day of their lives. Most often  individuals will make a poor food selection choice due to not having the funds to purchase foods that are  healthier. Let’s face it, unhealthy food at fast food restaurants is quickly accessible at a low cost. Whereas,  the average individual cannot afford purchasing fruits, vegetables, and grass feed animals products from  high end grocers such as Whole Foods.

Selection: Visualization is an intricate part of design thinking. It is visual thinking that illustrates the idea  in picture form instead of using words. This also gives a visual understanding of your idea, which can often  assist in getting your point across. Creating visualization is simplistic as using circles, squares, arrows, etc.  Designers use Visualization and it is also used during each phase of the design process. Photography is  also a great way to use visualization. During synthesizing or pattern finding is where you begin to think  visually. Ideation and concept development is another phase in which you can bring your idea to life with  pictures, photographs, sketches, and diagrams. I am choosing to use Visualization during my assignment  to bring forth my vision which is a solution to the challenge of making healthy food choices more  accessible to all. Providing a picture of the solution will assist when describing this solution to others.

Application: I used the Visualization tool by sketching out my picture of a Co-Op Garden on a lined piece  of notebook paper using a pen. This effectively assisted with creating the vision leading in to the  prototyping phase. This was a quick and inexpensive way to get my point across to other

Assignment

Mind Mapping

Challenge: In the Organization that I am working in, which is a highly regulated Pharma Industry, we  have several procedures and standards that need to be applied while implementing or developing a  computerized system. It has been a challenge for associates to know all the standards, regulations and  procedures, visualize them all at one place and apply them appropriately based on different scenarios.  Using Design Thinking and Mind Mapping tool technique tried to resolve this challenge by providing a  mind map of regulations, standards and procedures at one place in a single frame or window for  associates to refer.

Selection: Found Mind mapping tool to be very effective to solve this problem or challenges since the  mind mapping technique creates a very good analytical representation in a very user friendly way. Using  this tool, could successfully create a mind map of all regulations, standards and procedures including  different categories of computerized systems so that application development teams can apply them  easily rather than spending too much time figuring out what are the relevant standards, procedures, were  are they? What to apply in which scenario.

Application: Using the mind mapping tool, came up with a high-level pyramid structure and mapped all  the Standards, Procedures, Guidelines, Controls with different types of computerized systems and what is  relevant for different categories of computerized systems. The rollout will not exceed 60 business days and the solution should include feedback from over 50% of  the initial population of the 1,000 participants.    Our focus will be to understand which strategies the initial population consider to be the most effective  with regard to our proposed prioritization workflows. This launch will be the experiment that will quickly test our  key prioritization concepts and help us high-grade the main prioritization initiatives.  This will inform the  path toward full implementation across the larger population.    Application   For our first learning launch, we produced several video modules. text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Submitted by: Steven Richards

Date: November 25 2018

Challenge and Selection:  My first experience of using tools related to Design Thinking was the  Learning Launch – or Experimentation.  I’ve been working with a number of global consultants from  all over the world in seeking hypothetical, disruptive innovations that World Wild Foundation might  potentially consider commercializing and scaling as part of their existing Consumer Health portfolio.   This was an entirely hypothetical example for them to consider – and may never see the light of day  – but we need to show them how the innovation process works and what it might produce.  As part  of that innovation phase – a critical part of it involved collecting external data from pharma  executives, technologists and actual consumers to validate if any of the rather zany products or  services we were creating might actually have merit in considering.  Thus a Learning Launch was  undertaken to develop a hypothesis for each of the proposed products (10 in all), and we quickly  realized that, as many of our ideas utilized the same technologies (block chain, VR, big data, nano- technology, wearables, etc.) we might be able to consolidate 10 product Learning Launches and  reduce that number to about 4, as we had very limited time and needed to move fast.  Learning  Launch provided us the critical platform to take our rather wild ideas and see if there were any  issues, worries, challenges or out-right fails associated with chasing these further down the  innovation path.

text: Learning Launch: The Helpers Club  by Guadalupe Khan    Challenge  I am a journalist, working for a big publishing house. Because of the changing reading habits  through digitalization my company seeks for different ways of interaction with readers.  Therefore, it offered an innovation-competition. Together with four colleagues from  different fields (marketing, research, technical support) my team and I applied.    Selection  By using different techniques such as mind mapping and brainstorming (we also tried to  visualize readers) we asked ourselves the design-thinking questions: what is? and what if?  Then we came up with an idea: What if people could not only read stories (passive) but  could become active? We wanted to create a club for readers. But every club needs a  purpose for its members. Someone had the idea to set up a club for readers willing to  engage in social projects. Immediately we came up with a great name for our idea – the  “helpers club”. We were all enthusiastic but did not know if readers would like to become  members of this new kind of club. Therefore, we started a learning launch to test it.    Application  At first, we did research and selected data to come up with a hypothesis. According to  analysis from our department for reader research a lot of our readers are willing to spend  money if they read stories about hardship, bad fate, or catastrophes in our magazines. Other  social studies show that in general even more people are willing to help personally than to  give money. We thereby confirmed our hypothesis that our readers might be willing to help  others.  We then decided to start an ethnographic approach, we wanted to look for potential club  members, and ask them about their pains and needs. Therefore we started a call on the  homepage of one of our magazines. We asked readers if they would be willing to talk with us  about social engagement. text:
Maria Garcia

Design Thinking Reflection

January, 2021

Challenge

This reflection is based on a recent experience in my job at an orthopedics company. Orthopedics is  based on bones and joints, and I was assigned to develop an business plan for a product used the treat  bone spurs in the shoulder that can cause severe pain.

I conducted extensive customer research including ethnography and third party data reviews to support  this opportunity. Each month I’d diligently prepare and present my findings and recommendations to  the Executive Committee and was routinely sent back to collect more data on various points.

Application

It seemed to me that the execs were focused more on the numbers than what the product had to offer.  So I decided to dispense with the data and try a new approach that involved storytelling, to make the  opportunity something they could relate to on a personal level.

I started a meeting by asking everyone in the room to raise their elbow. I then explained that over 2/3 of  people experienced pain with that maneuver, frequently due to bone spurs. Suddenly, I had everyone’s  interest! They wanted to know more about how the proposed product would help to alleviate and how  quickly I could get it to market. The financials were briefly discussed and my business case was approve.

Insight and Approach

The insight that I gained was that Executives are super-busy and have information thrown at them all  day. The need clear and consolidated information and a way to relate to the opportunity by a method  such as storytelling.

I think the main thing I would do differently next time is to make sure to plan a story into the  presentation as it is being developed to keep the audience engaged. I suspect that will save time and  minimize the number of edits and re-presentations needed to obtain business plan approval.

Consistent positive onboarding experience across 7 offices in Central Eastern Europe, Middle East, Africa and Turkey

Challenge: In the summer of the year 2008, our company introduced a hiring program with the objective of increasing the number of sales people in the field sales organization by 20% of EMEA sales headcount. The intention was to extend offers to the selected candidates during the autumn 2008 in order to get the new hires to the company between November 2008 to February 2017. In absolute numbers, our company was about to hire approx. 400 new sales employees.

The growth of 20% of headcount was not evenly distributed across EMEA. For the emerging markets gathered under the region of Central Eastern Europe, Middle East, Africa and Turkey (abbrev. EXCOM), the allocated headcount was disproportionately higher as opposed to mature markets in the Western Europe (as EXCOM was expected to experience higher growth in demand and number of customers). EXCOM headcount in sales was expected to be on average 35%, with some of the offices growing as high as by 50%. The major number of new hires was expected to start in December 2008 and January 2017 (standard notice period in the region being 2 months, standard time to find, interview and hire a suitable candidate being 3 months, the hiring kicked off in early August 2008).

This steep headcount growth posed a particular challenge in EXCOM (as opposed to e.g. the Western Europe) due to the fact that the sales offices in EXCOM are small - on average around 25 employees - with no support functions (such as receptionist, office manager, internal IT, HR or finance) present on site locally. This means that any new hire that comes on board presents a tough load for the local team - who needs to help the new hire set up not just business-wise, but also from the perspective of setting up computers, email, entry cards etc.

Example Reflection – Storytelling tool.

Challenge and Selection

I am an SME Account Manager for a big telecommunication company. My organization every year  (before the pandemic) organize a weekend for all B2B sales employees including back-office. We are  gathering in a hotel for an “all-together weekend”. During this weekend a lot of activities take place.  One of the activities, which includes bonding activities like games, is brainstorming in order to make  create ideas for the organizations for future launches.

My team decided a few years ago during one of these weekends, to ask from the Organizations to  create a software tool which every Account Manager would have at his tablet and when he visits any  client would have in real time all the information that he needs about the client phone lines. He could  also use this application to create new contract for new phone lines of existing customers.

The tool we used to make our proposition is Storytelling. We need as much as possible information  about this software tool.

Application

During this weekend time we discussed with all the account managers about their needs explaining  to them that addressing their needs could have a huge impact for all of us. We discussed about every  day activities and how this tool would improve the meetings with the clients. We also contacted with  some clients and asked them about their opinion, what kind of information they want from their  account manager to have with him during their meeting. We also discussed with senior managers  about the privacy issues and what information would the organizations allowed us to have in real  time during client meetings. Everyone helped us and our proposition prepared.

text:
Perle Kamdem  Design Thinking – Retirement Coaching Mind Mapping    Challenge & Selection

I’ve been observing the challenges realized by recent and soon-to-be retirees face as they transition  from one phase of their lives to another. As a trained coach, I’m aware of how helpful coaching can be  through transitions and find myself wanting to help individuals as they struggle through the process. In  fact, an acquaintance who retires in just a few days confided that he doesn’t have an answer to the  question everyone is asking him, “What are you going to do when you retire?” The challenge is this: as a  coach, what services could I provide to help retirees understand that they should have an answer to this  question and what should I offer once they come to this realization?

According to the lecture given by Sophia Zamora, mind mapping looks, “for patterns and insights in a  large quantity of data you collected during your exploration of what is the current reality.” Because my  goal is to establish criteria for the what-if idea generation phase, I chose this tool for this iteration in my  design thinking journey.

Application

Because my network of recent and soon-to-be retirees is geographically disbursed, I wanted to be  creative in my approach to the “art gallery” and make it a virtual event. Before this, though, I needed to  add to my own observations and ideas with qualitative data on retirement coaching. I verified that the  need is real and gained further insight into angles that can be taken to address the needs of retirees. I  also outlined information I’ve noted from conversations I’ve had like the one above, noticing what  unmet needs have surfaced.

I complied a series of “napkin pitches” from this data that included ideas for individual coaching in  person or via Skype, group coaching, discovery sessions, lectures, etc. I was careful to cover areas that I  found compelling but also those that might not personally interest me. text:
Wow!  I am writing a book

Challenge:   I am a home maker married for 21 years now and enjoy every bit of my  family life.  My challenge is to write an impactful handbook on the  dynamic role of women in a family. Why I took “writing a book” as a  challenge is because for a long time, I did not know where to start my work  from and what would be the tone of the writing, serious or funny.   I  wanted to put in all my life experiences into it, but I was afraid it would be  very boring or sound too philosophical for young married girls to read.   I  wanted that my book brought an impact in women’s lives, but I was afraid  that my book would become too heavy to digest.    Selection:   So, after listening to the four design thinking technique lectures, I selected  the “Story Telling Technique”. It struck me that I can make short stories in  my book for each chapter as it has emotional connection to the reader.     The video in “week 2 lecture” about story telling gave me 3 ideas.   The first one – “Know your audience, where do they come and what they  need”.  So, I thought I must meet both accomplished women and insecure  women to hear their stories first so that my book will be more realistic,  covering different real stories and not just mine.  The second idea – “Clear sequence of events”- So I thought I can take the  reader through a journey of married life from young to old age slowly  covering the common events in life.  The third idea- “Create suspense questions and answer them; don’t leave  them hanging” – Now I thought I should give hard facts and real solutions  to help women solve their problems rather than just sharing only the  problems of life.    Application:   I have started off with the preface of the book.  I have imagined that my  daughter would be reading my book 10 years later and started the first  lines with my story 20 years back. On a positive note, I have listed the many  roles women can play in the family and how she should enjoy every bit of it

text:
Isabelle Laurent

Design Thinking assignment – Horse Industry

Challenge:  I was a member of a high-end saddlery company. This company is specialized in making and selling  luxurious leather equipment for riders and horses.   One of the company’s goal was to modernize the horse industry and bring novelty to the field.   They came up with a little piece of electronics and two sensors that would allow to evaluate the  quality of horses’ canter and jump when approaching an obstacle and landing, the regularity of  strides, the symmetry, the speed, the height of the jumps, and especially locomotive recovery after  effort. Detailed and valuable indicators for measuring performance and progress with certitude.  Information would then be sent to a mobile application after every training session.  The company wanted this product to be portable and easily switchable between different kinds of  equipment.  We had all the company’s means at our disposal as well as the many stakeholders that came with  it. For instance, employees from various departments such as sales representatives and international  riders. The one rule was to spend as little as possible given the high price that had cost all the  research and development as well as the cost of the materials themselves.  The challenge was to find of way of displaying those three pieces of electronics on a horse in  constant movement.    Selection:  We chose to use visualization to help us identify how people would imagine this 3-piece product  would fit on a horse.   Visualization allows people taking part in the experience to put on paper what they imagine in their  minds without giving them many barriers such as feasibility. Knowing what people that would  actually be using and/or selling this product are imagining in their minds was the appropriate tool  choice. Luis Sierra

Mind mapping.     Selection   Mind mapping is one of the most powerful tools in the design thinker's toolbox. It's used to  look for patterns, for insights, that lead to more creative solutions to your design challenge.    Formal definition:   Mind mapping looks for patterns and insights in a large quantity of data you have collected  during exploration of what is the current reality. The goal is to establish criteria for the what-if  idea generation phase.  This phase is pivotal in the design thinking process. Mind mapping  provides a segway from what is to what if.  In design thinking we use the mind mapping process to capture and represent the minds of our  customers. We involve our colleagues in order to develop a common mind among them  regarding the current reality of a design challenge.  Through mind mapping, we extract meaning from data in a way that lets patterns and insights  emerge.   Mind Mapping is a great way to align the organization around a common understanding of the  current reality.    Challenge   I use this approach often with my clients to understand the mind of their´s  customers. I am an  independent consultant, so Iam used to  work  applying new methodologies or developing  culture transformation process in different companies.    In this case, I used mind mapping in a bus transport company that wants to  develop  a new  management model, with news  KPIs  to monitor and simplify the management of the area.
