REFLECTION – VIZUALIZATION

-  By Zohaib Ashraf

Being a design enthusiast, I had an opportunity to participate in the Design thinking workshop  held by Odisha Design Council chairman, Akshay Kumari. It was a 3-day workshop and  included 18 participants. During this workshop, we were divided into teams of 2 and given a  challenge to solve using design thinking processes.     1. Challenge  During the post-lockdown phase, many citizens have started returning to their native and are  in a dilemma to find a suitable place to self-quarantine for 14 days. We were asked to provide  a simple solution to help these members to curb the spread of COVID-19 by taking a specific  case into consideration. This included a client, user, and the area which needs to be  considered to find a solution. Self-quarantine measures had to be taken into consideration.   I was teamed up with Matheus Kumari, a graphic designer from Odisha, India. Based on the  problem statement, I had to design solutions for Matheus Kumari, and he had to develop  solutions for me. From my perspective, Matheus Kumari was my client, and he decided that his  grandfather is returning to his house. Hence, in this case, the user is Matheus Kumari's  grandfather. The problem statement area was a 1 BHK house, and there were a total of 3  secondary users (Matheus Kumari, his dad, and his mom) and a pet (Cat).   I had to find a solution to ensure that his grandfather will be able to quarantine himself while  the rest 4 will be able to live in the house while minimizing contact but ensuring that they are  there to help his grandfather whenever required.     2. Selection  Being a hypothetical situation and not knowing his grandfather, I had to use Visualisation and  details provided by the client to understand the problem statement from their point of view  and make them see the solution from my point of view. Zoozo Visualization

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, to know a shared understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of customers before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are the actual customer of our products and how they react to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their services to their customer, in terms of business. The technique of using a "Zoozo" a cartoon based visualization of a problem and easy to understand how it works with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a diverse group of customers to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions and for better result.

Application

I started the process by creating a "Zoozo" graphic similar to a straw man character of the problem domain. To develop the "Zoozo" graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, I took the reviews from few of the people like how I could improve it with a set of questioneries.

Like The Zoozo graphic is simple, using simple shapes and icons available in Visio or on the Internet. If the front-stage/back-stage view doesn’t work, then I will create a different type of visual, either based on reviews. The visualization showed the problems with which the customer could understand the add and how convincing it was to everyone. For the activity, I will divide the customers into groups of 2-3 participants each representing a different location or area of interest. text:
Design Thinking

Feb 7, 2016

Al Kain

Design Thinking Tools used for Aspira Diagnostics Ltd

Background: I run a small biotech company in India – ICT Center It is predominantly  focused on making diagnostic reagents. The company has a young and knowledgeable product  development team. Within a decade of its initiation, the company has established itself in the global  market as an assured source of quality material. The top diagnostic companies in the world are our  customers. However, the segment we have chosen is small and niche and there is limited scope of  expanding the business.

With this background, we set up an internal team to review possible options for diversification. The  obvious choice was to forward integrate and make diagnostic kits. However, this was a risky option.  One, because it meant directly competing with our existing customers and secondly the business  needed complete change of the model we had followed. The top team was not willing to jeopardize its  relations with the customers.

I was therefore given the responsibility of looking out for options for expanding the business. One of the  possible business option was to go a step down the value chain – to set up a Pathology Lab so that we  would not compete with our customers and in fact become their customers. Logically, this seemed the  best strategy but we knew nothing of the Pathology Lab business and there were established players in  the market. In order to develop an innovative business model and identify value preposition from the  point of the stakeholders, I used a combination of following tools – Journey Mapping, Visualization and  Mind Maps. A brief of the insights obtained, points of differentiations identified and the development of  business model is provided in this note.

text:
Mario Pedrini’s Reflection

Design Thinking for Innovation - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection    Once upon a time I got a major in engineering, thereupon I was “formatted” to see and  work with numbers, applying math, physics and some other exact sciences, which should  not represent any inconvenience to overcome my day-to-day on my own.  When I started my company, I could be a particularly good engineer dealing with most of  the problems given to me by my clients, and I could test my knowledge as well as the ways  to solve the issue.    As an entrepreneur I had to overcome diverse angles in management, those that I had just  glimpsed during my days as student, and one of the must -terrifying- situations was selling  my services to strangers, specially over the phone performing a cold call, no matter having  a script in front of me.  Generally speaking, when trying to convince potential customers to purchase my services,  the conversation was too technical, and the context lacked feelings.  Often both parties  were heading different destinations, therefore I had to use an extra effort to persuade and  get my goal. When the job had been finished the appreciation was good in terms of time  and quality of delivery.    Application    Hence our proposals fulfilled the requirements, the relation client-contractor was not  totally satisfying because a touch of magic was missing.  Let’s not forget that B2B is done  between people.    At some point and since technology has evolved like greased lightning, -storytelling- arose  as a helping hand when dealing with emotionless operations.  As a touch of magic, the use  of real stories when talking about businesses made the clients turn and pay attention in full  when required during the process of sale.     Insight & Approach    When using storytelling, stress was cut of the situation and emotions were involved  immediately when talking about common past experiences.  It is a must to put some “heart”  to touchless situations

text:
Using Visualization in Business Coaching

(Design Thinking Assignment – by Vipan Rashmi)

Challenge

I have recently started practicing business coaching for young entrepreneurs as a full-time  career after almost 27 years of corporate software professional experience. During my  coaching sessions with young entrepreneurs, it has always been challenging to understand  their vision, product roadmap and business plan as nothing is ever documented. All the  ideas and plans are in their head and every time I meet them, I used to get a different  version of it.

Selection

After the Design Thinking lecture of Module 1, I decided to implement visualization technique  in my coaching sessions to make it more effective. I started using “In-Time Timeline”, “cross- road” and “future visual” to pen down their ideas and plan. I picked the “In-Time Timeline”  tool so that I could visually make them traverse time to get better understanding of their  business plan and product roadmap. I used “cross-road” to put their various options before  taking a decision. I also use “future visual” way of visualization for them to imagine a live  event happening after a year that gives them maximum happiness and satisfaction (like  giving a speech after winning a trophy/award, spending time with family at a hill top resort,  opening a new office, etc.). These tools were selected so that I could go back to these  visuals to arrive at a common meeting point.

Link between research and commercial

products/services

Challenge

The main problem that I face in the research institution I work for as a Business Development  Manager is the lack of understanding of potential outcomes of research projects which can be  used to develop new products. Many of my team members have an academic background,  i.e. working as PhD or Post-docs with less industry experience. Therefore, their first priority is  to work on research projects and focus more on theoretical concepts rather than practical  concepts. However, in my case, I am responsible to derive potential products/services from  those research projects which is indeed a very difficult task and requires great imagination  power. This would help to make my team members better understand the real  value behind the products/services which can help industry clients to reduce certain pain  points with less efforts.

Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge: My client is one of the largest electronic payment company in the world. The client

was working to build a global merchant database product & while building the datasets the client faced  a lot of difficulty in identifying correct brands in different dispersed geographical locations.  The Problem  the Product team/Technology Development Team was having to create business rules which will  correctly identify the merchant. Like BP is a global oil giant, but does it mean all the Merchant which has  some sort of name variation close to BP globally (BP GAS, Harry BP GAS etc..) are all same brand or they  are diff entity.. The Product team needed to on board with different business cases & different scenarios  so that the Business Logic to build the Data Products can be modified & Fine Tuned.

Selection:    I used the process of storytelling to engage the product office/business

team/engineering leads & created several storytelling concepts for Brands to make the Product team  understand the crux of the issues. Storytelling helps user to visualize the problem makes them more  connected, makes them more aware of the scenarios & make them relate to the scenario.

The technique that I have used here is the FREYTAG’S PYRAMID method.

Application:

FREYTAG’S PYRAMID is a widely used Storytelling application that consists of five elements. Exposition,  rising action, climax, falling action, and resolution/revelation/catastrophe. I have used this  concepts to create an scenario replica of my client product managers to understand country  wise business dynamics/Business Policy Condition/Policy Condition & how all these conditions  should be used/Considered for the product development activity.to fine tune the Data Strategy.

text:
ADNOC Classification: Internal

Design Thinking for Innovation 01 Nov 2015.

Peer-graded Assignment: Reflection

Submit by Dec 25, 11:59 PM PST

Submitted for peer reviews by Dla Xalid   Email: vmartinez@hotmail.com

Refilling fuel at ADNOC Petrol Station at Abu Dhabi City.

Challenge to avoid the Bottle neck for Rush hour, busy service providers at Pump filling  point, Full Car Parking, Crowded at Payment point.

Storytelling Tool is selected to resolve the issue of time delay and cars crowed during rush  hours at Petrol Station.

1. Collected Data for time duration and Customers service staff engagement at Petrol

Station.

2. Collected number of cars awaiting during rush hour.

Using the tool provided options to resolve the issues:

1. Once car enters petrol station to select appropriate filling pump lane.  2. Avoid rush hour and plan alternative time for refilling fuel.  3. Pay for fuel by bank Credit card.

The benefit of applying the above options while communicating with customers and Petrol  station service providers:

1. Positive Feedback from Customer stories, the Satisfaction and Happiness.  2. Able to serve customer with an efficient.  3. Enhanced timing requirement to refill fuel.  4. Win to win situation

I might use similar tool for challenging cooking and delivering Pizza to customers on time  delay after placing the order and serve hot Pizza.

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge    Last year I was part of a team that had the task of analyzing the causes that led to a  small club in my city not being able to add new members. Application    Two days were held at the club's facilities to test the ideas and prototypes. Design Thinking for Innovation Alex Perez

Reflection

Storytelling and Visualization in marketing for the bleach industry

Challenge & Selection

Working for the leading brand of bleach in México, we developed a case to build upon

brand values and product performance in order to maintain leadership considering we had a

90% of penetration in the Mexican households. Taking into account that bleach is considered a

commodity (a low price and poorly differentiated product), there was a challenge of keeping

white brands at bay while keeping our current consumers. The case would detail a deliverable

that would help us trigger further actions for this challenge. Even tough bleach is a product

commonly used in Mexican households due to its multi-purpose benefits such as: disinfecting

surfaces (bathrooms, toilets, counters and floors), disinfecting fruits and vegetables, purifying

water and whitening clothes. These benefits were widely known in the Baby Boomers

generation, but nowadays the millenials don’t fully know the many benefits of the product due to

the many alternatives in the market and many misconceptions around bleach (such as alleged

toxicity or it being highly damaging for clothes). The challenge was to find a way of

communicating with those consumers and deliver the benefits of bleach in their home.

The tool selected was Storytelling, in order to map all the brand’s touchpoints with their

consumers and define which of them would be the communication hub for all the brand’s

benefits. Besides, Storytelling allows us to discover underlying or unseen causes to the problem

that can really connect with an audience.      Application

Normally brands take upon themselves to communicate their benefits in the way that you

would tell in a TV commercial: fast and clear droplets of information that you can fit in 20 or 30

seconds. Sometimes they tell stories, sometimes they tell facts, but overall you don’t get much

space to share details. In order to app

Date: May 15, 2021

Author:  Arath Sanchez

1. Challenge & Selection.

In order to understand de context and all variables indeed in this problem I selected the  tool of visualization. We have had the challenge of mapping correctly our value stream  for the number one product in our company, this task needs to involve all our internal  costumers of the different areas, who are production, sales, delivery. Every single area  had one manager in this project in order to share ideas, situations, internal problems  and every single variable that helps the mapping being successful.

2. Application

As a first step, all those involved were invited to a meeting, we explained the context of  the problem and proceeded to go through the entire value chain for the selected  product. In posters we began by drawing a flow of the process that had been previously  raised, which will serve as a basis for making any necessary modifications. On paper and  with the help of the always useful post its we start with the first intervener of the  process.    First, the material must be melted, in this case the raw material used is plastic. The vital  information we must obtain is what type of machinery is used, as used, processing  times, machine preparation times, and the volumetry of the raw material to be used.  While we were commissioned to carry out this activity continued to tell us how the  activity was carried out questions were arising, these questions are completely  necessary in order to be able to question the current activity and to look for options for  improvement both for the process in general and in that specific activity. Sarai Diaz

1. Challenge

We received a Housing Project in which the local citizens of a community were opposed  because they think it will affect the environment thanks to the corrupted information some  people has spread. The challenge the company presented us was to change the perception  of the Project in that community to have their support when the construction finally started.

2. Selection

I selected visualization because in order to change their perception first I need to  understand the real needs and concerns of the people and identify the messages they have  received from the opposing groups that are currently affecting the image of the Project.

3. Application

First, I needed to enlist all the stakeholders involved because it was not only the immediate  community but while digging I found out there also there were political interest, local  government, schools, and all kind of organizations that needed to be included in the  campaign. Then I needed to know what the people thought about the project in a deeply  perspective, because I couldn’t change what I didn’t know they think. That took me to small  interviews with key actor of the community and the identified groups to better understand  what we were dealing with, to let them express themselves, in these interviews we used  pictures of the project that lead us to emotions, when we showed images of the project  people were: angry, frustrated, sad and some of them tired of hearing about the project.

4. Insight

text:
Defining the ‘Sony’ identity - Mind Mapping

Challenge

I am part of a nonprofit climbing organization, called Sony <a Quechua word meaning ‘misbehaved’.  In this case trying to symbolize the rebel and free spirit of the group>. Sony was created a year ago  by a group of mountain lovers and a group of specialized guides part of the oldest mountaineering  foundation in Ecuador. Their idea was just to get together and climb the Ecuadorian Andes. It all began  to take shape and the group has now 50 more members. A wide diversity of people from architects,  government officials, agronomists, young, old, men and women are part of it.

The challenge arises when the thought of formalizing the group and giving it a true structure is brought.  Due to the great diversity of members’ backgrounds and vocational trainings, the task seemed  impossible. There were too many ideas, all so disorganized and “floating around”, that nobody knew  even where to begin. The big idea, and mainly its execution, was starting to create chaos, more than a  real contribution to the group. The big question was how to capture everybody’s impressions, take  advantage of the group’s diversity and set a route for a possible solution or sets of solutions.

Selection

As Kenia Jj says, “mind mapping is looking for patterns and insights in a large quantity of data you  collected during your exploration of what is the current reality.” This was the main problem to be solved  at this stage. There as a vast variety of ideas and thoughts, which at this point didn´t say anything at all.  This huge amount of data needed to be somehow organized to stablish the current reality: the identity  of the group. After that its structure, formal organization, objectives and more could be defined. This  was to be done getting the members to feel involved so the best of their thoughts could be presented in  clear patterns and insights.

text:
Enzo Richards, Design Thinking for Innovation

Example Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge

I work in Product Design & Development for a consumer electronics company.  Our products typically  perform very well, and receive great critical acclaim, but in general are primarily adopted by an older  demographic.  Our company had done both analytical and ethnographic research, both of which showed  that we had products that customers were aware of, but younger audiences were unable to move past  the consideration phase of the purchase process.  We had tried different advertising, with different copy  as well as more youthful images or scenes, and time and time again they had only managed to barely  move the needle, if at all.  We also saw that there were competitors with similar product sets that were  able to gain more interest (and later sales) with their offerings, which made us question what the  differences were and how we could improve.  My team was challenged to look at our product offering  as a whole and find a way to resonate better with the younger demo (Millennials).

Selection

The challenge was levied upon my team from an executive management council, who knew we were a  group that was very connected with the product, but also had a good deal of understanding of the  problem, given that many team members were millennials.  I preached that we needed to maintain a  sense of consumer empathy, and that while we were at work, it was easy to ‘drink the kool-aid’ and  have an inflated view of how we were perceived.  Given our heightened understanding as a team, and  the need to present a compelling argument to make some potentially radical changes to the products, I  knew we would have to use storytelling to provide a convincing argument.  With that in mind, we  worked together to sell the challenge that we had identified, of updating the image of our products to  enable them to resonate more with Millennials.

text:
Dawn James

29/10/2016

On Design Thinking: A Reflection On Reworking A Novel

A year ago I began working on a novel with the idea that all I needed was a cast of characters, a

world and a plot that went from A to B. I could not have been more wrong. Around three-fourths of

the way through the novel, I found myself writing without direction, caught in the nitty-gritties of

detail, worldbuilding and characters; unable to extract the story and push it in the direction that I

wanted it to go in. Towards the very end of the writing, the story had spiraled out of control, into

something that had too many motifs and themes to be truly thoughtful. It was directionless and

frequently contradictory – even incoherent, in places, with incomplete character arcs that ended in

the classic rookie writer’s problem: they simply disappeared off the map altogether.

This is, perhaps, an unorthodox example to pick for a design thinking project. But as I listened to the

lectures on design thinking, I was forcibly struck by the similarities between the description of the

process – what is, what if, what wows, what works – and the ways in which this process parallels the

creation of a novel. Early on in the lectures, Diaz picked apart the concept of the Moses

myth of creativity, i.e. that creativity resides purely in genius and is not something which can be

cultivated or organized. This was when I realized that all along I’d been treating the novel as a

mysterious entity which could only be produced through genius, rather than a project which could

be managed systematically – which, dare I say, could even be created by using design thinking

principles.

Selection & Application

So I went back to the drawing board and decided to treat the novel as a project, rather than a

mysterious entity which would spring fully formed from my mind. I selected the Visualization tool

we’d explored over the five weeks for this and began to rebuild my novel from the ground up. The

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

I’m a member from customer experience department for an organization who is into jewellery retail  and there was a major challenge with our department on absolute number of buyers declining this  year over last year. With the current pandemic scenario the marketing spends were very limited and  the challenge in front was to double the buyers and make a 100% buyer recovery over last year.  Stores were only allowed to do tele calling / Tele marketing activities and no in store celebration /  customer connect activity is allowed to bring in walkin. Incentives of the sales person is linked to the  buyers and there by the employees were demotivated. The challenge was to bring in customers and  motivate the employees simultaneously

Selection

We have selected mind mapping tool for this process to understand in detail from the customers on  the frequency of their jewellery buying and on what occasion do they buy jewellery also why do that  choose that particular occasion over others and if given an opportunity which occasion would they  choose to buy every year and what could motivate them for buying every year on that occasion. And  similar process for the store employees were made to understand what motivates them, what kind  of customers are they confident about in terms of sure buyer conversion.

Application

In our first Discussion about the challenge with the team we found that both customers and the  employees needs to be motivated and delighted simultaneously and the review of buyers need to  happen weekly once at least to bring rigour in the store team , We have conducted ethnography  from few set of customers with varied purchasing frequency

REFLECTION ASSIGNMENT FOR THE “DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION” COURSE

PREPARED BY Gonzalo Rodriguez (sheena82@yahoo.com)

MARCH 2017

Challenge:

The challenge that I face is how to improve the sales process of new and emerging technologies- like  Internet of Things - that is often falling under a cycle of over promising and under delivering creating  confusion and deception among our customers. In the last years the sales process of technology  solutions has follow a path where the IT area of a customer is briefed on the advantages of the  technologies and during these briefings the technical components are described as well as reference  cases where the technology has helped to solve customer pains, and the next step normally required  to/from the customer is a Proof of Concept (POC) in order to show the legitimacy of these technologies  in their own business/challenges. These proof of concepts require the coding of the specific solutions,  done by developers and architects, and the process takes from 2 to 5 weeks.

The challenge of using this exact same journey as a way to sell these emerging technologies is that per  the “cool’ factor that is inherent to them, it makes the customers want to jump even quicker to a Proof  of Concept but without all the required internal alignments that these new solutions need. Especially  since these solutions are mostly aiming to deliver value to the Business areas of the organizations (i.e.  Operations, Sales, etc) and not only to the IT area, and therefore the traditional process is leading to  unsuccessful POCs of these very promising technologies, not because the final code/solution of the POC  does not work, but because the initial POC created  for the IT areas then needs an extra step of being  validated/sponsored by the Business areas that have incremental perspectives and requirements  making very lengthy, expensive and many times unsuccessful Proof of Concepts when the customer or  the vendor stop having capacity to in

text: Leveraging the learning launch tool to test innovation formats  Alexandra Beyer    Challenge:  Within my organization, I am working in the innovation lab and responsible for developing  innovation formats that will attract many clients, helping them to create innovative ideas for their  business. These innovation formats are supposed to serve as an initial inspiration phase, in  which we elaborate with them future business development opportunities that will help them  grow. Ideally, the clients will request future services from us such as the implementation of the  generated ideas or further workshops with a wider range of colleagues from their organization.  The challenge is to identify a set of innovation formats that suit to the potential client’s  requirements, budget and time frame and that provides the right environment and methods to  ignite the client’s ideas and future visions. Together with my team, we have developed several  innovation formats in theory, based on previous workshop experiences and innovation theory,  but we never tested these newly created innovation formats with potential client’s yet. It was  unclear to us, whether we could use the innovation formats within different industries and  whether the format would fit to the client’s way of working. My decision was inspired by the IBM story, which leveraged the trade show  Sibos to validate their concepts in real life. text:
Reflection Assignment, submitted by Jose Lopez

Visualization Tool

Challenge

After more than 20 years working for large corporations, I have decided to take on the challenge  and the opportunity to reinvent myself as an entrepreneur. Luckily, a few weeks after I left my  previous job I met a college professor who was looking to build a startup but had not had the  time to develop it into a working business. I offered to help and we got started on our early stage  startup (code name: “The Box”).

It has been an exhilarating time, doing research on problems we both have encountered and  are eager to solve. We have very different backgrounds, so we needed to create common  ground so we could communicate effectively and efficiently in order to build trust and  commitment to our newly found mission together.

Selection

Previously, I understood visualization as a creative exercise that consists of creating a realistic  mental image of the future one desires in order to facilitate its realization. However, the  Visualization tool for Design Thinking is quite different as it consists of using visual artifacts to  express concepts, ideas and relationships in order to bring them forward in a way that words  cannot.

My cofounder and I quickly learned that we were having trouble understanding each other  because we would use terms that mean different things depending on the context. We soon  figured out that by making sketches and drawings we could reach mutual understanding much  faster whenever we got stuck. Thus, we intuitively adopted the Visualization tool and made good  use of it for our purposes.

Application

We started working on “The Box” as an ecommerce marketplace for subscription-based  shopping, as we both knew many young entrepreneurs who are having trouble retaining their  current customers and thought it would be a solution to their problem. My team and I were challenged to  develop a Construction toy to sell along with our existing starter kit. The toy is geared for kids  ages 5 and up and consists of flat base pieces or blocks that can interconnect and gears that  can be pegged into the multiple holes in the base pieces. It has holes on top and bottom of the  base piece and they're like puzzle pieces that fit together and make a larger base. The gears  can mesh together so they can be turned by a battery operated motor.  My team and I were  challenged to create an advanced kit to sell along with our existing starter kit. The advanced kit  will include more pieces to build bigger models and also include instructions booklets to build  special theme characters to develop lateral thinking and planning skills. We went through  market research, competitor analysis and idea generation to develop some themes for the  advanced kit. We wanted to test the different themes and see which ones are marketable, fun  and challenging. It has a visual of the themes toy on the cover to identify  the instructions booklet.  We asked towards the end which toy they liked best, the least, which  ones were easy or too hard. Visualization Tool – used for designing a payroll prototype solution

By Raffaella Perillo

Challenge and Selection

I work as a business analyst and technical ETL consultant. Depending on the role I have on my  assignments I either discuss about and document business requirements with the business team or even  design and implement technical solutions based on the requirements given.

On one of my recent assignments, I was working for a large EU financial company to help them switch  form a 20 yo payroll solution to a newer more flexible and user-friendly solution provided by my  company.

Discussions had started via teleconferences and some documentations was provided by the client, but  we were not closer to coming up with the best solution as their system was old (it was implemented a  long while back) and nobody knew all the rules anymore.

Application

To move things forward I decided to take advantage of my upcoming onsite visit to meet with the key  users involved in this process, sit down with them, and get to the bottom of the issue.

To make the most out of this meeting where I had the opportunity to discuss with the business face to  face, I decided to would use the Visualization tool which I’ve recently studied in this course.

I was hoping that using this tool would be the most appropriate and would make the transition between  the technical and business processes easier to follow and hopefully get us to the point where we agreed  on the new solution that best suited their current needs (and not just copy what their current system  did).

Assignment: Reflection               Chris Humphries

June 11, 2016

Challenge:  The issue involves how you get your customers to understand the value of the services that  you offer to them in an intangible environment.  Working I the insurance industry we are basically  offering an intangible product that has generally been looked at from a pure pricing standpoint.  Having  the customer understand the value that you bring to the table is basically a foreign concept.  We are not  in a product world where Apple is able to sell upgrades the product and people want the next version.   Think about it, does someone really go out, read their insurance policy and want the latest and greatest  version?  No, they want the less expensive price, until something goes wrong and then they may realize  that they needed additional or different coverage(s).

Selection: There are two tools that I think can be used from standpoint to assist with the challenge,  visualization and storytelling.  I am going to use the storytelling model, as I believe it is the most  appropriate, however, good visualization in conjunction with storytelling is important and would need to  use at times.

In listening to the lectures, be able to tell a story that is compelling about an issue in the insurance  industry may provide insight to the customer as to why your policy or services are better.  One great  example about the story telling is the Farmer’s commercials on television.   Farmers insurance have had  the ability to relay true data driven claims stories to the audience to allow you to understand some of  the issues with insurance policies.  They basically explain, what has been covered in the past and it may  put doubts into your mind about your own insurance policy.  Would my insurance policy cover that type  of accident?  Being able to relay these commercials in short, 30-60 second commercials might be an  effective manner to get your point across.

COURSERA:  DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION   Instructor:   Sue Abdeldayem, UVa

Final Assignment: REFLECTION (05/26/20)     Student:  Karina Starks, Pearl Academy

Project Title Garden State Studio/MANVILLE   (An academic architecture studio)

PHASES:    Phase 1/Digging, Phase II/Planting, Phase III/Growing, Phase IV/Harvesting

TOOL:   Mind Mapping

Challenge     As the professor in an Architecture School Studio, I taught a complex project on a 10 acre site  with environmental, social, regulatory and technical constraints. It was a graduate studio of  students with a mix of qualifications to tackle such a complex design problem.  The academic  setting was seen by county officials as a way to bridge the distrust between the stakeholders  (developer, the local citizens, and the adjacent business owners).  My largest challenge became  the moment in the process after the ‘What is’ research (Phase I/Digging) into the ‘What if’  (Phase III/Growing) phase of a Design Thinking process.  The challenge was to establish the  Design Criteria for our studio that would also respond to the ‘minds’ of our stakeholders and  create teams for the next phase of work.     How would we organize individuals into teams that would take the leap between research, field  work, site analysis into Design Ideas?  We needed to establish Design Criteria for the project but  also find a theme unique to each team. Designers are good at IDEA GENERATION and  overcoming constraints but needed the discipline to work with the stakeholder’s criteria within  thematically coherent creative teams.  DESIGN CRITERIA needed to engage Stakeholders into  the process.  The success of the teams would depend upon how invested they each would be in  the teamwork thereby directly affecting  the quality of the output. The eventual ‘output’  needed to encourage discussions that could increase trust among stakeholders in a previously  contentious situation. Mahmoud Shaker

Challenge & Selection:

I am a learning manager and I selected the storytelling tool to on-board our business  partners and learners to implement our L&D strategy and the new ways of learning.

In our company, employees are reluctant to use e-learning, they are much more  comfortable with face to face training. At the same time, change is accelerating; full  day(s) available for face to face training is shrinking and digital learning is spreading  offering much more opportunities than the classical e-learning.

The challenge is to modify the way we organize our learning model and to make sure  the trainings we deliver are more efficient, are more connected to the day to day  business, adaptable to the size and rhythm of our learners and are a direct leverage  in the upskilling.

Application:

I had to meet a business partner that was reluctant and refused to modify the existing  learning program (on technical expertise) that was built with her team and delivered  to other teams, especially new comers.

During the interview I had with the manager, I understood that his reluctance was  based on the believe that theoretical training was key to on-board new comers and to  make sure that everyone was aligned in terms of knowledge. By Ratna Kumari (4th Nov 2019)

Challenge

I am working for an Automotive OEM design & manufacturing 4 wheeled vehicles  for passengers. As a member of my organization’s R & D department for  Suspension parts and our challenge is to make and Suspension for existing 7  seater Rear Wheel Drive (RWD) gasoline vehicle to an Electric vehicle for an  Government exhibition which would have   1. Min changes in terms of vehicle-suspension attachment points   2. Should support rear wheel drive.   3. Should support additional weight of Battery Pack  4. Should keep investments to minimum as it was not for sale.

Resources: Project scope includes   1. Electrical Design Department and Body & Brake Design department with whom  we have to work closely.  2. Project is limited to internal resources (i.e budget & employee time)  3. Project should not exceed 18 months from date of initiation including design  and vehicle building.  4. Project should not involve dedicated members but needs to be executed as an  additional task over and above regular model development responsibilities  utilizing common employee Pool.

text:
Jose Garcia

Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

When I was in high school, one of my teacher told me that I was a great storyteller,

in that moment I did not understand what that means. Currently I am a student of

Administration in Balatas ES (Politecnico di Milano) and I realized

that my teacher was not wrong about me.

Nowadays I am in conflict with one of my college team. The main issue is that he is

zero empathic with people and situations, that is the cause of many problems

because the decisions that we have taken is becuse that kind of thinking, affecting

the others and seeing just for our benefit.

As a lider, I am trying to manage the team in a empathic direction, is not easy

because they really do not understand a diferent point of view of themself. That is

the reason why I am practicing the storytelling.

Application

I have been using storytelling more than before, when we are discussing about a

project, I always find a moment to use this tool. I start talking about a specific

situation of the project and then I connect that situacion with a personal one. I finish

the story making a personal reflection, in that way, they can understand very well

different point of views clearer than just go in a direction.

For example, the last session that we had was the last week, we were talking about

the diagnostic needs of training. It was a very hard topic because they propossed

some agressive techniques for the collaborators, when it was my turn to speak, I

commented my story with the training and how I felt about it, I recalled to them when

we were on a similar situation and how a lot of them felt so dissgusted, in that way,

we are working to do making better deccisions focus in a humanistic approach.

text:
Amit Sharma: Company General Use

Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge:

The challenge I had was to deliver a technical informative session to non-technical  colleagues. I’m an electrical engineer working in a massive oil and gas organization.  The department I worked on decided to have “knowledge sharing” sessions and I was  selected. I had to deliver a presentation about the country’s electrical grid network  to non-engineers which is quite the challenge since they do not have the basics in the  field.

Selection:

I selected Storytelling as I think it is one of the best available options to deliver the  subject presentation. The presentation will have to be smooth, non-complex,  interesting and easy to follow; thus, the selection.

Application:

First of all, while I was developing the presentation, my main goal was that the  audience will understand EVERYTHING. I didn’t want to explain a certain function or a  piece of information, that I might think it is easy and intuitive, but the audience  wouldn’t get it. So, I started developing the presentation slides showing visuals step- by-step telling a very “zoomed out” information then diving a little bit in and  explaining the details. Since I work in oil and gas company, instead of presenting and  telling that 5 MW is transferred here, I’d said a power equivalent to 200,000 barrels of  oil had been transferred in the form of power through these lines etc.

Insight:

For the above specific application, I really had learned that selecting complex  complicated words doesn’t make your presentation or work smarter, it is just complex  and complicated! When talking to an audience, talk in a storytelling approach which  would attract the audience attention which is ultimately the goal. The material was  presented to audience of approximately 100 colleagues, and I honestly got a very nice  feedback, people got interested and were asking questions. Challenge

I am part of a startup which is focused on providing Ready to drink cold brew coffee for the large market of Indian consumers. Selection

Application

Reflection – Visualization

Talaat Mohmmed

Challenge and Selection

As noted during the course, “visualization uses imagery to make abstract ideas more concrete and  public.” During the innovation process, it’s easy when explaining an idea like a crowdsourcing platform  to colleagues for it to take shape in various divergent ways in their heads. Though divergence is often  helpful during the ideation phase of the innovation process, it sometimes is necessary to be able to be  able to achieve a mental match, and the visualization is most effective in doing so. An idea can only  move beyond the conceptualization stage, only when consensus is reached. I tend to use visualization  during every stage of the design thinking process. As you move throughout the process, the visuals  mature and a concept become less abstract, kind of like an image becoming less pixelated.

Application

During a recent design sprint, throughout the problem-framing and ideation phases, my colleagues and I  thought we had narrowed down who was the end user was for a crowdsourcing application for the  humanitarian sector. We were being tasked to solve why local and indigenous knowledge of eco-system  based early warning indicators of floods are not integrated into disaster risk reduction programming,  despite the awareness that they work. Several problem trees led us to the root cause of the problem,  which was that humanitarian aid workers lacked the documentation and validation of insights from local  knowledge holders on utilizing nature-based indicators for flood prediction.

Insight and Approach

Only by drawing out a diagram connecting the information providers (indigenous and local communities  of natural hazard prone areas) to disaster risk reduction practitioners (humanitarian aid workers), we  realized that a major and obvious component of our solution was missing and that we indeed had two  end users. Design Thinking for Innovation Application: Visualization

Chris Martinez

Challenge  My entire team was laid off two weeks ago so I do not have a work challenge to leverage for this design  thinking activity. I wanted to get the most out of practicing design thinking though, so I selected a  challenge that’s real and immediate for me: Identifying the essence of a role I’d love to do so I can more  effectively recognize it when I see it.    The challenge for me is that I don’t have an exact position I’m targeting. I have facilitated training and  developed courses for over 20 years, have facilitated cross-functional teams and have coached people in  a variety of roles. I love that work yet am ready to do something new.     Positions I’ve considered include managing a training and/or instructional design team, program  managing learning and development programs and coaching people in instructional design.  At the same  time, I am drawn to other creative roles like working in an innovation lab co-designing and developing  new products. Innovation and design thinking are very exciting arenas for me.    Fortunately, I don’t have to take the first position I am offered. I have financial flexibility, so I’m using  this transition as an opportunity to obtain a position I’ll love.     Selection   For this activity, I selected the visualization tool. We use this tool by putting concepts into visual form  with colors, shapes, symbols and images. We can create maps, sketches, videos, photos, PowerPoint  graphics and more.     My understanding is the primary purpose of visualization from an individual perspective is to access the  non-linear parts of our brains, and for a group is to foster a common understanding. text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Date : 8 november 2021 From : Philippe Elle OUSSOU

Challenge & Selection : Shelter Pets for Veterans is a startup based in Gabon (Africa) whose mission is to ensure the academic success of students. According to the NOT PII, Gabon has the one of the highest school failure rates in the world (>20%) and this is due to 2 major problems: the lack of school infrastructure and the poor quality of school monitoring.

As Shelter Pets for Veterans could not replace the State in the construction of schools, it decided to address the problem of school monitoring by developing a platform that allows each stakeholder in the education sector to have, in real-time, all the information needed to ensure quality school monitoring and, at the same time, prevent school failure.

The challenge was to understand the daily realities of each stakeholder, to identify the relevant information that each of them needs, to find a way to make this information available before it becomes obsolete, and to propose a solution that allows both the transmission of information instantly, but also the processing of this information to obtain the necessary data for decision making.

The choice of the learning launch was the best way to test our solutions while learning more about the daily realities of the beneficiaries. Learning launch is a small experiment that tests your new idea in the real marketplace. This tool was essential to improve our solutions and make them as effective as possible. We needed to talk to our customers very quickly and we needed to test our assumptions about what kind of solutions we will need to deliver.

Application : Our goal was to enable every stakeholder (students, parents, teachers, and administration) within a school to communicate more effectively and have access to the information they need. We found that the best way to do this was through the tools that the vast majority could access: the Internet and cell phones.

June 22, 2017

Jose Gil – Final Assignment.

Design Thinking for Innovation.

Reflection – Mind Mapping.

Challenge

I work as a Consulting Manager at an IT consulting firm in Mexico City. We specialize in the  implementation and support of ERP systems for clients of different industries. We started working  with a new client, a hospital. Another consulting firm had already implemented them an ERP  system for their financials and supply chain management. Although the new system is one of the  best in the market, the client had been facing many different problems with it: the nurses had to  wait a lot to place their medicine replenishment orders, clients had to wait a lot of time for invoices,  finance could not close their accounting periods on time, and so on.

As you can imagine, this situation had caused a big displeasure to the Board of Directors, and a  great dislike among end users (operations, IT, nurses, etc.), because the implementation of the  new system, instead of making their work easier, it was making it more difficult.

The managers of Operations and IT didn’t have a clear idea where the real problem was: if it was  the system configuration, the interfaces, deficient training about the system, etc. They had no  idea where to start, and they also didn’t know what to offer their end users to improve.

There were several challenges in this situation. In first place, to gather all the problems that the  client was facing in the different areas. Second, to make end users to get involved in the problem  and not only complaint all the time, so that they could provide their evaluation about the current  challenges and contribute with ideas on the improvements they believed could make each area  to provide more value to the company.

Mind-Mapping

Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

We have recently partnered with an external Content Provider A, in order to expand our

product offering and thus be more competitive in our local marketplace.  However, the

partnership has created some challenges in these early stages - which is to be expected.

Multiple departments are affected by this new integration, which negatively impacts the

time they have to focus on their own unique KPIs.  This partnership is new, and people

naturally avoid what is unfamiliar – not ideal when trying to iron out the creases of a newly

introduced additional process.

We needed to improve internal synergy in order to seamlessly intergrate the external

Content with our existing SaaS platform, and manage consistent timely delivery to our

Reflection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared

understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to  identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers,  who are government agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission  or the delivery of their services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens. I have used the  technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts  for discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of  defining the scope, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain points and  opportunities for improvements or solutions

I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw

man graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The  existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing  materials, GAO or other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal  interviews with one-three of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the  initiative. If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from  previous research, and discussed in Victor Fernandez’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front- stage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service  – has customers with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the  organization to provide the service. Testing the Buddy Program (Human Resources) Tool: learning launch Author: Natalya Kotov March 22, 2020

CHALLENGE I work in HR for a big multinational. Over past few months we have been  deep diving into employee experience of new hires. After interviewing tens of  new joiners across several countries and conducting journey mapping  sessions with them, we have identiﬁed a recurring pain point. Most of new  hires did not have a buddy (guide) to support them during their initial weeks.  What was missing is someone available to answer their questions, introduce  to other people, show around the ofﬁce, describe company culture. New hires  were highlighting the social aspect more than a need for a speciﬁc technical  onboarding. Despite the support from their hiring managers, formal induction  programs and team lunches, the problem was clear: new hires felt  unsupported.

SELECTION To tackle this problem, a team of 5 HR professionals from different streams  was formed. I was the project leader. During our ideation session we came up  with a volunteer-based Buddy program. We draw how the ﬂow would look like  - how a buddy and a new hire would meet and what would be the mechanics  of the program. We have identiﬁed one major risk - what if no one wants to be  a buddy? what if no one volunteers?  We needed to test the program on a smaller scale: for 1 location, 1 legal  entity and 1 month (1 round of new hires), to see if our assumptions will be  validated and learn what works well and what does not.  Learning goals:  a) if we ask employees to volunteer to become a buddy, we will have enough

volunteers to cover all new hires in a given month (around 20 new joiners  were expected. No rewarding scheme offered, just positive motivation and  an opportunity to meet new people).

S u b m i t t e d  b y  –  Abdul Rohim   1 | P a g e

Reflection –

Learning Launch

Challenge  I work with the product team in a technology company developing state of the art  software for banks.

While we are aware of the disruptions COVID-19 has created across every single  economy globally, creating unforeseen challenges for businesses. It is about how  quickly we adapt to such challenging times by finding new opportunities. Banks  sitting at the heart of every economy are also sailing through turbulent times.

With people facing confinement or adhering to social distancing, the hardships  relationship managers (RMs) are facing towards customer retention or new  acquisition during such times are challenging, especially with no in-person  banking. These challenges can be addressed if the bank extends its digital  Interface/UX to its corporate customers who wish to avail the Transaction  Banking Services directly on the bank’s portal leading to the higher conversion  rate for RMs on customer acquisition through True Digital Transformation.

Selection  As a team, we decided to use the learning launch tool. We believed this will help  us design a simple yet effective technology that the bank’s prospects can easily  navigate. Working remotely with some corporate bankers and relationship  managers from the banks we have gone through several design thinking activities  to come up with a go-to-market prototype. Doing this activity has helped us in  selecting the learning launch tool for our challenge. This tool will help us go  through an iterating process that will improve our solution. Working with the  prototype will help us experiment with the idea with a larger group of corporate  bankers and relationship managers.

Reflection - Storytelling

Pietro Gabrielli

Challenge & Selection

In this course of Design Thinking I learned the basics about several design tools. One of those is storytelling. Storytelling is my favorite because it is so simple and easy to apply. It involves presenting your product or business in a story format that truly intrigues the potential customer or investor; while also creating a cause for a problem and making a list about different ways to solve it.

Application

Most likely, each and everyone of those reading this have gone for some shopping in some kind of clothing store and used a fitting room at least once in their lives. If you have used a fitting room several times, you must have felt that stress of not knowing when the employee might come knock on your door and open it because he couldn't hear you reply "taken" for some reason or another. Maybe the music inside the store was too loud, maybe you just panic and don't know what to do or say, or perhaps you happen to be deaf and/or mute. So, what happens next? The employee opens the door and there you are with barely any clothes on and some other customers catch a glimpse of you almost naked. If you go shopping regularly, then you must know the fear that I'm talking about.

While I was shopping myself I wondered: what if I were to design a device (either automatic or manual) that lets the employee know whether someone is currently using the fitting room or not?

My audience in this case, would be the customers that go shopping in clothing stores regularly, as well as investors and stores’ owners.

Kara Deniz               July 24, 2020

Design Thinking for Innovation           Peer Graded Assignment

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

Visualization was my tool of choice to convey the vision for my new company to potential board  members. Visualization is a great tool for me to use when I am attempting to communicate ideas that  are more complicated, such as compartmentalizing structures and developing new systems.  My  challenge here was to accurately convey my message to potential board members so that they could  clearly see my vision for the company.  I conducted a hybrid style visual presentation that included  usage of power point slides and white board.  I decided to include the white board, not only because I  wanted to show them the processes that we use & the flexibility of development, but I also used the  white board for them to convey their interpretations and how they viewed their individual roles in the  company’s development.  Considering that this is my first start up business sharing control with a team, I  wanted to ensure that my message is clear and concise.

Application

I began my presentation with power-point slides of the company vision & mission statements and then a  diagram of the company and its ownership structure.  At this instance I used the white board to show &  explain the ownership transitions that will occur after second quarter and the effects that this could  have on the board.  Next, I needed to convey their role in company decision making and with their  relationship with the President/CEO.  This is important because this established a clear picture in their  realization of how Holding Companies operate differently that operationally functional Companies work  and their relationship to those ventures. Reflection on Learning launch

I am the lead of risk and litige department, which is part of the business services unit of a company  that operates in payment system and digital.

Selection :

We opted for the Learning Launch which is quick to execute and inexpensively.

It’s a great tool to test if our idea can meet customers ‘needs and create value for them before  decisions with financial impact are done. Even if the outcome is not as desired, the loss is minimal as  the investment is low

MIND MAP

1. Challenge

Currently, my friends and I did a start-up about self-development applications.

Sometimes we found some difficulties in working together. For example, most of the

information comes in a non-organized, non-structured way, making it harder for me and

can we improve our start-up by structuring information we handle in a simple, can be

visualized and knowing the relationship between that information that we have.

2. Selection

Our team uses a variety of design thinking tools, one of which is the Mind Map. Mind

Map is visually organized information that is designed to help us in collaboration and

communication.

3. Application

I use a mind map for structuring information to make it simple, can be visualized, and

knowing the relationship in a way I do organize the dozens of things that the team has to

coordinate. Every project basically contains the same items: scope (what’s in, what’s

out), timeline (dates, milestones), costs, resources (people, equipment), risks, and

assumptions. but, the hardest part of learning a new subject, is visualizing how big it is

and how its concepts and details are interconnected.

4. Insight

My insight about one of the design thinking tools, which is the mind map. I think by

making a mind map in the team, we have an idea of the performance we have been

through. In addition, we can also understand each other's ideas efficiently, the purpose of

Giuseppe Longo: Company General Use

Challenge & Selection        Although there are couple of promising vaccines in the world, still we have been significantly suffered  from COVID-19 since 2019. It also critically affected to me and entire my life, family and my attitude  to other people. Therefore, I think it is worth to investigate how people are feeling on the COVID-19  and come up with innovative ideas and solutions to cope with the challenges related to COVID-19.      I thought the mind mapping such as empathy map is a suitable tool for this study as everyone has  his/her own feeling on the COVID-19. That is why I selected the mind mapping as a tool and tried to  collect all feelings from my colleagues and friends and tried to identify what are the challenges.     Application        First, to identify challenges, I made an empathy map categorized as six as following. And I distributed  it to my colleagues and friends.

•  Say: What are the explicit things the person says?

•  Think: what are the implicit things the person believes?

•  Do: What are the explicit things the person does?

•  Feel: What are the implicit things the person feels?

•  Pains: what are their fears, frustrations and needs?

•  Gains: what are their wants, hopes and objectives?

After collecting empathy map, I deleted duplicated empathy and consolidated all information. Then, I  tried to understand and reframe challenges by applying an abstract ladder. The reframing work was  conducted as following 5 steps.

•  Challenge?

•  Why is solving this challenge important?

•  How could this challenge be solved?

•  Discuss all options and decide which challenge to use for ideation

•  Insert “How might we” at the beginning of your selected statement

1. Challenge:

The first tool I used was the tool of Storytelling, to attract the attention of the participants,  and to introduce my topic in an interesting way, before stating the problem and the  solution. Storytelling is a kind of showing the problem from a real perspective.

For example, I have used the story of a little girl which is my neighbor, who did  a great impact on the whole neighborhood to start recycling. This story improved my  concept that says: if we want to change the fruit, we have to change the root, what I mean  is: if we want a change, a new behavior in society, we have to start from the youngest  generation, which is our kids, and then, the solution will sure achieve the expected results.

Submitted by Jo Kelly, PHR, SHRM-CP

May 12, 2011

Challenge & Selection

As a Human Resources Professional, employees often seek me out to discuss questions or concerns they  have regarding any number of topics – policies and procedures, compensation and benefits, hiring and  staffing, and everything in between – and what a viable solution may look like.  In many of these cases  there’s a pretty straight-forward answer to their questions, but the challenge comes when there isn’t  and a more personalized response is required.

Over the course of my career, I have found that taking a moment to sincerely listen and empathize, not  immediately search for a “one size fits all” answer, goes a long way.  It has also proven most successful  for establishing trust and finding a mutually agreeable solution.  Often, I rather naturally gravitate to a  storytelling strategy (sharing my personally inspiring experiences and / or those of others) to support  the employee in defining a simple solution and compelling them to take positive and effective action.

Application & Insight

Recently, an early career employee requested some time with me to discuss our performance  management process and their latest performance rating, which was causing them much concern.   While the rating and subsequent feedback pointed to them being a solid performer, they believed their  work over the course of the previous year had been exceptional and thus a rating indicating the same  more appropriate.

After listening to the employee share their concerns and ask for my guidance, I opened with a story of  my own sharing how I’d been in a very similar situation just a few years prior.  While I’d done some  great work, I was also rated as a solid performer much to my disappointment. text:
Design of digital sales process

Ivica Marija

The challenge I had was designing a new, “digitalized” sales process for lending products for  large corporate clients. In my Bank, “Large Corporates” refer to companies that have more  than €500 million yearly turnaround and require multi-million financing deals for their needs.  Negotiations and contracts are commonly very complex and can last for weeks or months.  Despite having many systems available, the whole process was still mostly manual: data  required for a credit application was manually copy-pasted from source systems to  predefined forms in Word; calculations of exposures and limits were calculated in variety of  Excel sheets and also copy pasted to these forms, and these forms were sent by e-mail to  different approvers who would review them, print them, sign them and send it back in pdf  format. Finally, data from contracts was manually entered to booking systems. Only this task,  due to complexity of contracts (>100 pages) was usually taking 4-8 hours(!).    The initial set of requirements we got could be summarized with famous quote from Henry  Ford: “give me faster horses”. Despite having very modern digital workflow systems and  Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system, everyone expected “easier way of  handling documents”. “Problems” that were identified were mostly around >20 systems being  used, primarily to extract data needed for the application, but nobody thought about big  picture. We could do that, of course, but that wouldn’t be digitalized and automated process.    In order to give participants the sense of complexity, I decided to use visualization – a tool  well described in video of Angela Myer in Week 1. I often use Visualization, primarily for my  own better understanding of a problem, but also to ensure that there is a shared  understanding of the problem and possible solutions among groups of stakeholders. text:
Reflection - Learning Launch

By Yaser Mostafa      Challenge    The challenge that I’ve selected is related to the Covid crisis. Many people are going hungry  due to the lockdown and the government has been incapable of managing distribution of food  supplies to the destitute and hungry. A program is to be implemented in select areas where  people are finding it difficult to eat two meals a day. The data for this has been made available  from the government’s local bodies. The team for the implementation of the feeding program  has 10 members in each locality including volunteers, and a separate Central Management  Team. There’s a limit of budget and labor-time. Safety of volunteers, food supplies, and  recipients is another concern. The program seeks to eliminate hunger issues as a result of  Covid in the targeted areas. The program will last till the end of 2015, and continuation will be  contingent upon review.       Selection    At this point, various other design thinking tools have been used to identify the kind of meals  that people would need, the best time of day to serve, the local volunteers ready to help out,  and so on. We are trying out the learning launch tool that tests a prototype from our solution  idea. This tool will test a prototype in target areas, which will give us feedback on its  performance.       Application    The first part of the learning launch focuses on the feedback of the recipients about the food  distributed. The program decides to deliver low-carb, high-protein food with a selection of  vegetables. One fruit is provided to each recipient per day. The meal is varied each day and  feedback is collected from the recipients. Besides, volunteers observed the recipients  mannerisms while they were eating and the amount and type of food that was discarded. This  was done for a period of two weeks, at which there was enough data to decide efficacy and  make changes.    The second part of the learning launch focuses on the coordination

Moreover, this strategy is great for  keeping track of the small moments of the class that  are missing empathy  with students; in this way I can  improve the activities inthe  class to make  the process smoothier and meaningful. As the first approach to the innovation process, this tool unlocks my thinking, unleashes creativity as  well as improves the way I communicate my ideas to the people I work with.

By using visual elements like charts and graphs, I provide an accessible way to see and understand  trends, outliers, and patterns in data and discover possibilities I have not seen yet.

Application

In my company, I am the manager of an area called Responsible Care. I usually work together with  my team, so this tool allows me to approach, identify, organize and communicate more effectively  the ideas within the group. I find it helpful to focus on the idea and guide my team members to the outcome I am looking for. more on the technical aspects and a Business developer would do it from their POV

the project.

up useful time which would otherwise be wasted explaining all the information to bring

Design Thinking Tool: LEARNING LAUNCH

Challenge

One of the challenges of a company that is steadily growing is to be able to retain its employees  and contribute to their growth. Particularly for one where the program is at its early stages, and  especially in a remote work setting, engaging employees to take advantage of learning and  development (L&D) opportunities offered by the company can be rather futile. Employees tend  to be occupied by other priorities that L&D take a back seat in their careers. The L&D department  of Company BLD is now trying to find ways on how they can effectively address this challenge  and have decided to apply Learning Launches as their approach to design thinking.

Selection

For this challenge, the members of the L&D team have done brainstorming sessions and came  up with a list of possible ways to encourage learning in the company. The learning launch will  allow the team to conduct experiments quickly and inexpensively to gather data to determine  which of these possible solutions, if any, will most effectively promote L&D. If none of those  solutions will hold, this design thinking tool will allow them to pivot their approach through the  data gathered in the experiments.

Application

The first experiment is to gamify the learning process in the company. An efficient gamification  strategy has been found to have positive effects on motivation and engagement when  implemented in real-world situations. Learners tend to achieve learning outcomes more  effectively via an engaging journey rather than a traditional training approach. Adding that most  of the company’s employees are between the ages 23 and 40, this experiment is expected to  appeal to them.

text:
Margarita Gould

Reflection Paper

I'm working on my thesis right now, and I'm having trouble deciding on a topic or an issue. I

choose to use the mind mapping tool in this scenario. I began by making a list of topics that I am  interested in. Then I narrowed it down by dividing it into sub-topics. As a result, I was able to graphically  arrange my thoughts and conceptions.

Mind mapping makes it easier for me to remember and research my concepts. It makes my

design thinking process less complicated. It displays the topics that I am most interested in and those  that I am least interested in. It helps me organize my thoughts and come up with new ideas. Also, when  I'm torn between two thoughts, mind mapping assists me in analyzing and comparing all relevant  elements so that I may make the best option possible.

text:
The Communicative Power of Visualization

Author: Yareli Thomas

Challenge

As a user experience designer within an organization that builds web applications, I work with a broad range of stakeholders that include

clients representing a diverse set of vertical markets, sales and marketing professionals,  project managers, project owners within an Agile software development framework,  backend and front-end developers.

In order to build successful web applications, we must start by building a shared understanding of the users and their contexts. Often neither written nor spoken language alone is suﬃcient for that to happen across the diverse knowledge domains represented by all stakeholders.

Visualization is a perfect tool that allows me to translate concepts across disciplines without losing the fundamental meaning to the jargon of each represented profession. By leveraging story boarding, journey and ecosystem maps, ﬂow charts, or simple diagrams, I facilitate the process in which all stakeholders build a shared understanding of the problem at hand in order to collaborate on an optimal solution.

Application

In working with a client on a new web application, I begin with a discovery process. Sometimes I facilitate a discovery workshop that allows all stakeholders to spend time with our team to build a shared understanding of the problem, and to start co-designing a solution. Activities that are part of a discovery workshop include creating user personas,  drawing journey maps, ecosystem maps, or story boards.

User personas, a tool I use frequently, while not entirely visual (there is a lot of written information included in them), contain one important visual element—a sketch or a photo of a person. Humans have an emotional response to faces of other humans. Course : Design Thinking for Innovation

Reflection: Visualization applied in teacher commitment meeting

Challenge & Selection

I am Karla, a mathematics teacher in a private grammar school in Abidjan, the city capital of Côte

d’Ivoire. In our teaching activities, we have to solve often problems about the curricula, pedagogy,

teaching content and bests practices, etc. Consequently, the commitment of mathematics teacher

takes meetings once per month in order to reflect about the current teaching challenges and take

decisions helping each one to be effective with teaching materials, approaches and learners.

To lead these meetings, we often use Visualization as tool of design thinking. Indeed,

Visualization is “an approach for identifying, organizing, and communicating in ways that

improves work processes and focuses on bringing an idea to life, simplifying team collaboration”

(Jeanne Liedtka and Tim Ogilvie, 2011).

Our approach is to identify the key points included in our pedagogic practice in order to overcome

the challenge of productivity, excellence and sharing best practices with colleagues, learners and

other administrative stakeholders in our school as opportunity.

Application

In our commitment room, a blank board is used in each reunion to write the own observations

about our teaching approach and identify the ways to solve the gaps by a thinking process including

factors having effect on the academic excellence issues.

Often, this blank board is more used for the brainstorming when we must solve a serious problem.

In this case, the board is divided in three columns corresponding to students, teachers, and

administrative workforce.

Then, the brainstorming is led by a series of question:

Assignment: Design thinking refection                    October 2020

- What is the problem?

- What are the facts?

- What are our responsibilities?

- What must we do in order to solve it?

- What are the evaluations criteria of improvement?
