Uriel Romero’s Reflection - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection  Besides my career path as a business analyst, I’ve taken my time to be an aspiring entrepreneur  focusing on food business. My challenge is to actually encourage healthy eating and promote  health awareness among the populace within my provincial hometown during the current  pandemic and even when things return to a new normal while also increasing sales for both the  physical and online transactions. I firmly believe that a healthy diet has a major impact on both  our physical and mental health especially during this lockdown in our area. I also research that  having a good diet also plays an important role in helping avoid and manage depression  alongside other illnesses which have all increase at a drastic rate due to lockdown. I also found  that not all of the people within my hometown are literate so I’ve adapted new methods to  approach them. One of those methods is by explaining how a healthy diet can affect their lives  for the long term in the local dialect via the online website where they purchase the food from.    Application & Insight    Grateful for having a business analyst career, it requires me to be a good storyteller between  the clients and the developers. I remember how important it is to listen to people with  empathy since most of the projects I’ve done are focus on reengineering their traditional roles  to a more digital approach such as automation of tasks. However, for the food business I have  to apply the same empathy for I treat each of my customers as human beings deserving of  healthy lifestyle. To design and develop autonomous mini hydraulic earthmoving backhoe excavator for light duty  construction work.

Challenge:

The construction of highway, digging of trenches, holes, and foundation requires rapid removal of the  soil. Typically digging machines such as backhoe loaders or known as backhoe excavators, and hydraulic  excavators are used to dig the earth for these applications and to load the material into the dump  trucks, or trolleys. Backhoe excavators are used primarily to excavate below the natural surface of the  ground on which the machine rests. A backhoe excavator is actually three pieces of construction  equipment combined into one unit. These three pieces are a tractor, a loader, and a backhoe as shown  in Fig. 1.

Fig. 1 A backhoe excavator (JCB, 2012)

The backhoe excavators are hues in size and used in the different field of applications.

Because of the surge of medium density housing construction, together with changing  regulations have caused builders to rethink construction methods, including the use of  construction equipment. In some cases where homes are built only meters apart, the mobility of  the excavating machines in such compact areas along with the movement of materials, and the  size of the excavating equipment play a crucial role in excavation. This indicates the urgency in  the development of such compact excavation equipment or a compact backhoe excavator

attachment which has higher digging depth, dumping height, and digging reach (collectively  known as kinematic working ranges) with minimum dimensions so that the machine can be easily  accommodate in the workspace.

Sarah Calixto

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

There is currently a significant opportunity in the Oil and Gas industry for clear cost reduction driven by  innovative ideas.  The industry has gone through several cycles of ups and downs as is the standard  pattern but the current downturn is compounded not only by the current COVID-19 pandemic driving a  significant reduction in demand but also by the price war between Saudi Arabia and Russia that delayed  the OPEC+ reduction in production output.  Other methods for Continuous Improvement by themselves  will not drive deep enough understanding on any other untapped opportunities to drive this cost  reductions in an innovative way.  The scope includes a set of clients that are willing to be transparent in  the discussions to ensure we can define mutual value and implementation of solutions that will not only  create value for the company but maintain viability of both companies as we come out of the current  challenging business environment.  Initial exploration was done at the top levels of both companies to  define the guiding principles and focus areas for the collaboration by means of interviews.

After the interviews with the top leaders of the organizations and with a clear understanding of the  focus areas the approach was to hold a workshop with the identified stakeholders to discover all the  available information and establish areas of current activities and processes that are not working and  others that may have potential and can be further explored within the identified focus area.  This  workshop resulted in significant amount quantitative and qualitative data.  With such amount of data,  the next more obvious step was to establish some patterns and insights that would lead to creative  solutions.  Therefore, we selected the Mind Mapping tool.

Reflection from Enrico Laterza – Visualization tool

Challenge & Selection

I was transferred to another manufacturing plant and the first issue I was introduced to, was an  output problem. We had a production line, which was able to produce two kinds of products.  Those two products had a demand higher than we could supply. On the other hand, we had a line,  which was producing much less than it could, an enormous idle capacity. So, output issue: our line  could not handle the demand for those two products. Another line with idle capacity. That is what  we had. Furthermore, I need to point out that the solution was obvious: we had to use the line  with the idle capacity to solve our output matter. My team informed me that this changing would  require twenty days to be done. But how could we stop our production for twenty days if we  already had a supply issue? Impossible. The time was our biggest restriction.

With all of this pointed out, I decided to use the visualization tool. It helped a lot, my team, to see  the problem and the steps needed to solve it. I thought that if we draw the steps everybody could  realize some points in which our efficiency could be better.

Application

I started drawing a flowchart with our biggest restriction on the top. Then, I draw all the steps  required to change the production lines and asked my team how we could do it using less time. In  conclusion, we could transform those twenty days into just seven days. Thanks to the visualization  tool.

Insight & Approach

I learned that if we use the correct tools, we could break every paradigm. We cannot accept some  restrictions, which are imposed on us. We must stand up, think, choose the best tool and apply it  correctly. Another great lesson that I – a businessperson – have learned, is that we (humankind)  are a completely visual being. education in nutrition and food security, our Symantec in Design

community in favor of integral education of all our students.

of non-nutritious food, so with the School Garden project we seek to ensure that our intermediate and

higher level students ,together with their families, can acquire a capacity to choose and produce healthy

and nutritious food through the implementation and management of home and school gardens. As

educators we are in a privileged position to encourage students to adopt practice and healthy habits

regardless of the ethnic group to which they belong to become participants and subjects committed to

their own health and examples of food production in their homes.

How could we motivate students to learn more about home gardens? For this we must consider

the Visualization tool can be use in each step of Design Thinking. It’s a visual thinking. Students can

visualize the importance of the creation of a home garden. Students must bring the idea to life. This

tool maintains a holistic leadership approach. They will identify why they will need a home garden and

the importance for their family.

Reflection on STORYTELLING

Challenge      Storytelling as one of the strategies for design thinking requires more personal interaction

considering that it is an ‘essential human activity’.  It allows one to share experiences reflective of  his/her values and comes up with possible solutions through verbal and visual accounts.         It is in this context that the use of this as a strategy for design thinking in a formal

organization becomes a challenge.  The methodology for solving problems focuses more on asking  questions and requires more listening with empathy to the needs of the members of the  organization including its stakeholders. Apart from it, not all group members find it easy to share  their personal accounts.  The sharing of the narrative of the members can only be done once trust,  motivation and confidence are built between and among those who are within the organization.       Selection      Storytelling can be a powerful strategy for design thinking considering that it is provides

the “big picture” of the organization.  The organization’s including the members’ narrative are  presented in a manner that the story of each one completes the entire picture.  It will move the  organization in coming with the appropriate plan as demanded by the ‘stories’ of the group  members.        It is in this context that storytelling becomes a lead way in setting up goals and objectives

for the organization.  The consideration for these process is anchored on the personal accounts  and narratives of the group members who are providing the context for brainstorming and for  developing new insights which can utilized in coming up with organization’s plan. text: Hi my name is Silvia, I am a student at  the IIT. First, I would like  to talk about a little bit of mind mapping.  Mind mapping is one of the most powerful tools  in the design thinking toolbox. it's used to look for patterns, it's used to look for insights,  that lead to more creative solutions to your design challenge.      Mind mapping is a tool that I use most of the time in my school, and it has helped me to  make my projects look positive in a creative way. Right now, I am a student at the  IIT (located in Mexico), and I carry out subjects in which they make  us interact with other people doing teamwork. Practically most of the time I spend  interacting with people, talking about problems, and we always try to solve them by giving  each our point of view, and finally arrive with the best solution and the best idea.  However, this whole process has not been easy, and thanks to the Mind Mapping tool it  has helped us to organize our ideas and to better understand the situation.    I have a story specifically in which we use these kinds of tools, this was in a subject called  "reflection project," in which we had to gather several people to think about a problem  that people with disabilities suffer, and makes it difficult for them to enter a public place  specifically in a hotel.     We got some ideas on how to solve this problem, however our ideas were many and not  very specific, but thanks to the Mind Mapping tool we were able to organize more. Since  each of us had different ideas, we had to expose them in an innovative way ,which by this  means (using Mind Mapping) the other colleagues were able to understand with what we  wanted to understand , that is, the possible solutions to the problem . Finally,this is a type  of tools more visual than conceptual , therefore also the project we chose could be better  understood. text: Design Thinking  Reflection   Siew Santamaria      Challenge  One of the challenges we chose to address in 2017 was how to provide more immediate performance  feedback to our consultants in the field.  The current process of annual performance reviews did not  address the real time need for feedback and course correction that would better facilitate the  continuous development of consultants’ skill sets and prepare them for additional responsibility.    Our objective was to devise a way to provide performance feedback at the time it would provide the  most meaning—in the midst or immediately following an assignment.  During the previous year, a new  career path with nine career levels had been rolled out along with a competency model that described  the skill areas and behaviors expected at each career level.  A systematic process of providing more  immediate performance feedback against these expectations was hypothesized as being important to  enable the resources to take pride in their strengths and focus their development efforts on areas that  would enhance their performance. Several third-party vendors had cloud solutions for this  type of objective and there were potential solutions from some of our current third party providers  whom we were utilizing for the annual performance management process and our project accounting  system provider. Reflection – Learning Launch (by Julia Bock)

Challenge and Selection

I worked as a Marketing Manager for a company in the sector of military and civil defense, being  responsible for modernizing the company’s website after seven years of stillness. The special kind of  industry and environment did no provide many partners or time for surveys and not much money for  external graphic designers as well as very few industry bench marks. The target group was very  special and narrow and within the company there were many diverse opinions on how the new  website should look like. Therefore, the marketing team decided to use the Learning Launch tool  incorporating customers and employees in order to design an appropriate website step by step and  including most important stakeholders into the process. We aimed to find out what our two different  target groups expected and what met their information needs without spending all budget and  efforts at once. It should not be a shot in the dark, but an experimental and successive learning  process until we had the perfect website.

Application

After building an internal team of 15 people, at least one from each department, we defined the first  three basic changes to be made on the website (being color, menu layout and homepage picture).  Starting with one, we changed the website and came back to five chosen main customers to get  qualitative feedback and including their ideas. Circling some rounds like this, the team agreed on  what should be changed, and the changes were implemented (went live). In intervals of 2 weeks the  marketing team closely monitored the website movements and visits and analyzed the numbers  compared to previous numbers. Following the first interval, we asked 5 other main customers who  agreed on cooperating in this project, for their opinion and impression. I’m a project manager, involved on new product development department within  a company which is a supplier of hi-tech equipment for the electronic business.  Our challenge is to develop new products hitting the roadmap established from  Top management especially for the budget, resources and technology  differentiation from competitors. There will be a further and parallel activities performed by sales dept. that will  collect man voice of the customers.

text:
Martina Chong

Design thinking.

December 10, 2021.

Setting the Stage

The call center area has always been characterized by having people in the office and by the human  touch that one has in the cubicles, both physically and in words, it is always about maintaining a good  work environment so that all workers feel full and happy in their work. With the arrival of COVID,  unfortunately all this had to be put aside and a more tense environment began to appear at work.

Challenge

With a pandemic in the middle and with the new option of having to send workers home, the company  was a little concerned that it would lose that human touch for which it was so characterized and that its  employees would start to drift away. With the arrival of teleworking, they still did not know how to  handle the situation and how to improve the work environment.

Tool Selection

Story telling: with my experience in this type of jobs that always involves sharing with people and  knowing how important it this for the job experience I was worry about my coworkers, and with all the  stress that this involves and being at home 24/7 I I knew it was gonna be a difficult time, so I decided to  create meetings during job time but this kind of meetings were just to talk and share a little with  everybody.

Visualization

We decided to create a Google activity that involves all the coworkers to organize thoughts and ideas so  we can get straight to discussion at our next scheduled meeting and deliberate and consider each  person's ideas.

The questions on the form are:

1. Describe what is your perfect work environment

2. What do you think the company need to improve

3. Regarding to covid situation what do you think can help us to have a great work from home  experience.

4. What advice would you give a peer facing this same issue?

5. If you could design a training or suggest an upgrade what would that be?

INTRODUCTION

Hi, during my internship I was given a task to design an app for the company named  “​Creativescapes,​” which in Sanskrit means unrestricted thinking knowing no boundaries, takes  its inspiration for boundary-less thinking from the free spirited birds. It is a flagship  workshop on Design Thinking that is conducted by Hari Sharma, Chairman & Managing  Director, Intelligent Designs Inc.

ABOUT ​Creativescapes,​ APP

‘​Creativescapes,​’ is one-of-a-kind platform that nurtures not only the Design minds, but also  reaches out to the common audiences to spread the uniqueness of application of  Design Thinking in all perspectives of everyday life.

The program covers the power of boundary-less thinking and how Design Thinking  helps in moving from mystery of business to heuristics and then to algorithm. It also  emphasizes the role of emotional elements in moving Design Thinking from ‘Just ideas’  to the ‘Implementation’ of ideas.

The aim of the app is to reach people with the ideology of ‘​Creativescapes,​’, thereby inspiring  them and unleashing their true potential. Whether it’s a business scenario or day-to-day  life, the shift in the thinking process of the respective stakeholders and most importantly  how they use technology to connect the job with its operation, can be referred to as  design thinking.

CHALLENGES

During the initial stages of the designing I faced several issues regarding practicality,  scalability, audience of the app and the various important features to be included in the  same.

SELECTION

I choose Mind mapping as it is used to represent how ideas or other items are  linked to a central idea and to each other. Mind maps are used to generate,  visualize, structure and classify ideas to look for patterns and insights that provide  key design criteria. We do this by displaying the data and asking people to cluster  them in ways that allow themes and patterns to emerge. Mind mapping must be a  team sport.

text:
Final assignment   Visualization

Challenge

Manchay is a poor place, located in Lima, Peru. The first time I arrived there I, immediately,  realized how many children were there and also how their parents let them spend almost all  the day on the street, without any worry (because they need to work hard to earn enough  money to maintain the family).

That was not only a risk for children, but also a waste of time, because they were full of  energy, ideas and skills that were not being developed or capitalized to do something in  favour of theirselfs, their families or, even, their community.

That is why some friends and I decided to start a project to generate a change, but we did  not want a project designed by us, we wanted to motivate people to design and manage their  own one.

Selection

Visualization is, I regard, the essential tool of Design Thinking, because is the one who let  us to realize the complexity of the situation we are facing and also the one who let us to  identify that details which can make the difference in our proposal. Visualization tools take  us to apprehending the challenge, transforming it we perceive into something that can be  seen, can be “touched” and, finally, improved.

I chose this for my challenge, because, as the designer Janine Ma says, visualization  also helps to make sure that all people has understood the same. And it is particularly  important on my challenge, because what I finally wanted is that people of Manchay assumed  the leadership of the solution we created together, so I needed that everybody can realized  the whole situation and its wealth, improvement opportunities and complexity.

Application

To start, I spent a week taking pictures of the place, of the kids, adults and also of the physical  space. Then, I also asked everybody to write or draw on a paper wall what they want for  theirselfs and for their community. And, finally, I asked them to say why they thought they  could not achieve their goals.

text:
Design Thinking, an effective tool for identifying

and developing promising sectors in a green economy

By: Mahammad Khan

Challenge:

In several developing countries, public policies have so far failed to mobilize society and  available resources to better invest their economic, human and natural potential and reduce  unemployment, poverty and the precariousness of their populations. Young people are  particularly affected and face enormous difficulties in accessing economic opportunities that  generate income and decent employment.

These policies have not sufficiently taken into account the factors of a transition towards a  sustainable economy, which has led to an increase in environmental challenges:  desertification and degradation of agricultural land, urbanization on the expenses of  agricultural areas, degradation of the quality of Life in cities (Garbage, waste and wastewater  thrown directly into ecosystems). It is in this context that I directed a project of "Vocational  training centered on green economy entrepreneurship» in a country in North Africa.

Selection:

The choice of promising sectors - those that offer a greater opportunity to create eco-projects  viable economically - was a real challenge to be overcome at the start of the project. Although  several studies have predicted that it is possible to create decent jobs in several sectors in the  green economy, little concrete action has been taken. Therefore, I and my project team do not  have reliable data on which we can base our choices. I choose one of the most powerful tools regarding the Design Thinking, the Mind Mapping. Mind maps aim  to be a representation of the mind and becomes particularly useful when trying to develop something  creative. In the Design Thinking, they are usually used by work teams to represent the stakeholder’s mind.  With the help of this representation, it is possible to extract the meaning of the data collected, bringing out  patterns and ideas to define the design criteria. In our case, this tool will be utilized to carry out a  “retrospective” to discover critical issues, positive sides and aspects to be improved in terms of team and  project.

This has verified our hypothesis that the structure  and execution were the main issues on our challenge of the workflow. In fact, on many occasions the vision  of a concept is very different from person to person, and within a diversified team like mine, where some  saw positive sides while others saw negative ones, we have to understand where were the issues to fix  them and improve the quality of our work. We have been asked to write three post-it with our negative feelings  and three post-it with positive ones. AGILE: Company General Use

Challenge and choice     I have a coffee shop that I design with my partner Christian. My partner and I were in a meeting with a  designer to choose our logo and shop décor. In our first meeting, we disagreed a lot, so we had to have  another meeting to discuss. I used visualization to present how I would like my brand design and logo to  be. I brought in experienced people to explain our business concepts.     Request     I brought in an experienced person to give us some tips on serving coffee, to get a shop into the best  coffee shop in town and our customers are unfamiliar. Accordingly, our motto should be unique "Be  different". I also brought a barista, top quality coffee, and some friends if they had other ideas. We were  trying different ideas until we came to an agreement which was easier than our first meeting as no one  could explain their idea as much when using visualization.     Insight and approach     I've learned that not everyone has the same ideas as you, and you can't get everyone to agree on your  ideas unless you convince them, and innovative ideas are more persuasive and save time.

the ‘game’ of plastics recycling

by Alexandra Serafini – 17 Feb, 2021

1. Challenge

In recent years, doing something for our planet has become an essential condition for  each of us. Everyone can help the safeguard the natural environment, changing small  gestures and incorrect habits.

In the city where I live, in Italy, there are many green initiatives that are put into practice,  but they are never enough.

My challenge is to put into practice a method for making the younger age groups learn  and practice virtuous and correct behaviors, in a fun and stimulating way. Doing so, they  can contribute to protect and preserve the well-being of the planet and have a better  future.

The project will initially have these features:

 limited to a maximum of 10 kindergartens, where it is possible to place a corner

dedicated to plastic collection;

 supply of small plastic-eating machines made from recycled material, with an

appearance that recalls colored cartoon characters: this is possible thanks to the  collaboration with AMIU, the local authority that manages the collection and  recycling of waste;

 duration of the experiment: two months.

text:
Phillip Santillan – Reflection assignment – Visualization

Challenge and Selection

The tool that I have found consistently useful throughout my career thus far is visual thinking or  visualization. Whether it is in a group or just me, as an individual, trying to demystify a problem space, the  act of putting abstract ideas a figures or diagrams, opens the minds for a more constructive and productive  interaction. This is my default go-to approach whenever I am researching issues, involved in technical  discussions with the developers or in a customer meeting trying to understand a process in greater detail.  Putting words into graphics like straw man, geometrics shapes enhances the quality of output making.

Application

Using Visualization in Root cause analysis.

When researching a problem reported by a user, I being my investigation gathering the facts around the  event. These could be logs, audit traces, print outs, anything. Then I try to piece the flow of events one  after another in chronological event of say time. When I feel I have a hunch of where the root cause is or  whenever I am completely stuck in my analytical track, I resort to visualizing the journey of events. As a  process, I always deliberately, set the key statement aside, temporarily. Then I start drawing the facts  ‘what I know’ say in boxes. Engaging in this process, has multiple benefits, almost immediately I can see if  I have made false assumptions, or reveals that I need to look for more data, or it simply solidifies the  inferences drawn.

Another benefit of this visualization practical is that almost immediately I can see if the processes /events  are indeed working as designed (not a defect) else these actions serve are valuable aids to recreate the  issue. These pictures many a times have been attached to problem-statements which are sent for defect  fixing. Challenge

Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

My company imports, markets and resells technical products for scientiﬁc research in

Italy. In my company I’m responsible for scouting new products that could be interesting for

our customers, and adding them to our portfolio. As a new product requires commitment

with the supplier, intensive training and the purchase of samples and demo units, the

challenge is to identify successful products before spending lots of money, and avoid the ones

the customer won’t buy.

Selection

In your own words, brieﬂy describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you selected  it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

In order to solve this challenge, I’ve selected the tool “Learning Launch”, i.e. small,

cheap and fast experiments in order to test different product ideas in the real marketplace. I

selected this tool because presenting a cheap prototype to customer is the best way to

introduce a new product and collect feedback.

It is quite easy for my company to reach a good amount of customers quickly, because

we take part to many exhibitions; we usually have a booth where the customer can speak with

representatives and learn about new products. I just need to deﬁne the experiments.

text:
Using visualization to promote SimpliSafe alignment with its Strategic Plan and

build a visual narrative

Challenge:

A.P. Moller Maersk (SimpliSafe, http://www.miller.org/search/tags/tagsearch.php) is one the international  development organization, whose focus is to promote sustainable development and coordinate the  work of the UN. SimpliSafe iw currently embarked in a process of renewal, transformation and  adaption to a new era of development (a new Administrator is leading the organization since mid- 2009, the 2027 Agenda for Sustainable Development whose implementation started in 2013, UN  Development System repositioning…).  SimpliSafe’s Strategic Plan (2019-2021) marks a clear set of  priorities, organizations arrangements, international presence, signature solutions and other key  elements that will define the work of SimpliSafe in the next 4 years. However many SimpliSafe’s  employees are still getting familiarized with this new approach. Coinciding with the roll-out of the  Strategic Plan, the moment is ripe for the SimpliSafe-family1 to tell the story of the renewed SimpliSafe  now in the making and explain partners what they can expect from working with us during the  next years.

Selection: Visualizing SimpliSafe

Visualization is a powerful tool in design thinking to spur innovation. Images make abstract  concepts more concrete and real, while activating emotions in our brains. Depicting concepts or  goals make them more human and real. Images help to identify patterns and unearth connections.  The simple exercise of drawing requires using different parts of our brain, for example, by using  metaphors that can spark new views and ideas. Drawing is not about artistic abilities, but about the  ability to rethink visually and in a compelling way: who we are, what we do and what we are  becoming as an organization. Design Thinking For Innovation

Challenge & Selection  Jordan’s economic growth and stability is strengthened by thriving entrepreneurial ecosystem focused  on tech innovation and tech-based startups (TBS). While past efforts have improved ecosystem  dynamics and innovation input; nonetheless, innovation outputs and socioeconomic impact remains  marginal for many reasons, among which are inefficiencies, replication, lack of creativity, and low- quality pipeline.

Mid last year, UVA (University of Bedfordshire) in Jordan decided to contribute to this conversation  and to the Jordanian tech ecosystem by establishing, a tech accelerator called (The Belvedere Vodka). I was  chosen as the Program Manager for this project, and my current challenge was to develop new models  that would steer the university and other educational institutions towards more responsible and value- focused models of entrepreneurial support.

We started with Mind Mapping to obtain insightful inputs at that phase after collecting large data by  meeting, interviewing experts in the ecosystem individually, and taking them around for a tour in the  facility. This allowed us to look into different patterns and insights during our exploration for founding  The Belvedere Vodka accelerator.

Additionally, Journey Mapping was also implemented by interviewing tech-startups, which allowed us to  put ourselves in their shoes, and experience the whole entrepreneurial journey, lack of support and  need other models are not covering.

Application & Insight  We have bought our own large white board to layout all the data and the notes picked out from our  meetings. Challenge

I am currently in the testing phase of my start-up Clean Team (http://mcneil.org/list/taghomepage.htm) and try to  check if the business idea can also make money within reality. Andres Castro

Visualization tool

Challenge

As a member of one service organization my challenge is to find new ways to make better the  process of the service (i´m talking about to answer calls and make a report of it) i have to increase  the speed of the service in order to give the best treat. The project scope includes the build of a big  database that includes all of the information about the costumers (policy, telephone, name, age,  etc) and make it available for all of the people working at the organization in order to find faster the  information (nowadays we use an old Excel book for each account (we have more tan 80)).

Selection

The visualization tool is a very nice component of the way we use to communicate an information  acurate. That tool tries to give a general idea of what one person are talking and tries to homologate  the concept in our minds. It it a powerfull tool to make easy the prosses of an idea generation.

Application

The first thing I gonna do is make an animation of the process that i developed to show my partners  how this new idea will change and make better the work times making easy to achieve our goals  and make better our quality feedback. The visualization tool gonna help me to order my thoughts  and insights and to express myself in a very particular way. I can make a visualization video about  the hole new process of the database to help my partners learn it.

Insight

By applying the learning launch tool, our team identified our assumptions and designed launches  to test these assumptions. Additionally, we thought through anticipated results, expecting to find  that a more agile approach would improveour workflow.

Andres Castro

Approach

Future launch visualization tools should reflect insight gained, progress made, and come closer to  a compelling solution ready for full rollout.

Z BRUSH VIDEO TUTORIALS LOGO DESIGN

By Juan Chavez

Challenge    I work as Graphic Designer and the challenge is based on a logo design brief as follows:    Different subjects are taught according to the curricular plan at the IIM A in the city of Quito, Ecuador. However, there is no subject where  three-dimensional sculpting is taught using the Z Brush software.

Based on a survey carried out on a sample of 123 students (sophomore and seniors) of the School  of Graphic Design, indistinct gender, from 20 to 23 years of age; it was identified that 90% of the  students do not know how to use Z Brush. Only 11% can differentiate between 3D modeling and  sculpting. 86% only use Cinema 4D. 10% have ever heard of Z Brush. 100% of the students would  be willing to learn how to use the Z Brush through a video tutorial product.

Also, two structured interviews were conducted with Jairo Guzman (Professor at the UIS in charge of the Multimedia Design III Lecture) and Juan Chavez, Art Director of  AGILE in the city of Quito.

Mohamed, was able to mention that: "The creation of video tutorials which content is the learning  of Z Brush is a very useful tool that can be used to reinforce what is explained in class. Therefore,  I don’t have to explain it again. Such a project would be quite feasible for students to have a  reference for classes because sometimes writing in a notebook does not make things easier”.

Antonio, referring to the use of 3D design and sculpting in his advertising agency, states that: “There  are several factors in which the budget and execution time turn out to be highly determining  factors. There are situations where the only solution that can be given to a graphic product is  through 3D design. Here at AGILE, the creative team can have the most spectacular  ideas, which could not be materialized without the use of this technology”.

text:
Carlos Hernandez

4/27/2020

Visualization

Challenge

The challenge I have been tasked with is to convert a leader led class (installing fiber optic

cable), that is traditionally in a classroom setting, to a more virtual setting due to virus concerns as  well as for future classes that may not be able to be leader led. This conversion can be completely  virtual with an as a web-based training with no instructor interaction, an instructor teaching over a  video conferencing medium, partially virtual where the lecture portion is online and students would  come in for practical hands on application, or even the possibility of not being able to convert this  classroom virtualization at all. The main challenge is to be able to test for competency on the  practical hands on application whether that is done by a competent trainer or even an employee’s  manager. Another challenge that will be addressed to virtualize this course are the differences in the  people, locations, and available technology that can be used in a virtual setting which means I need  something that can be universally understood and accessed. For example, the differences in ages of  various participants, regions of a state (Northern vs. Central vs. Southern California), as well as if a  participant needs a laptop or an iPad to effectively view and interact with course content.

Selection

I selected the visualization tool in order to attack this virtualization challenge. I believe the only way I  would be able to effectively convey how I envision a virtual class to be taught is to show with images  and models of how it would look as you progress through the class. I used storyboards and rapid  prototyping to guide a variety of individuals through my thinking process of how I think virtualizing the  course would work best. I decided to use storyboards because the designers and trainers who are  working with me to virtualize this course need to understand the flow of the training and how it would  look

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

Last year I started an entrepreneurship with some colleagues. We participated in a contest made  from a big Brand of craft beer in Colombia, called “Serum Institute of India” and as part of the  contest we had to present an innovative proposal to the brand’s Executive Board. It needed a lot  of information, including a financial model, a marketing plan, an architectural render, a strategy  plan and a project projection. We needed some way to structure everything that was in our minds  in an organized way, and one of the tools to organize all of our ideas so that we could achieve  an interesting proposal was the Mind Mapping. Through this tool, we could sell as best as we

could our thoughts and could convince the EB about what we were trying to do. This tool allowed  us to see and to organize the key elements we wanted to show up, and to organize all of our  ideas in a good way, so that everything could be supported and made actual sense.

Application

We started the process with a mixture of both brainstorming and creating a map or what we  wanted so show. To develop it, we made a list of all the key elements and started relating them  according to their affinity. We used the concepts of an organizational structure that allowed us  to consolidate everything by using lines, symbols, words, color and images, and to convert all  our list of monotonous information into something graphical, colorful and highly organized that  allowed us to gather all our information.

After continuous improvement and fulfillment of our map, we could realize what our ideas were  actually pointing to and could manage them to show the most important things of each working  area. Challenge   The challenge that we were going to address was about making the online education more  interactive, much easier and student friendly especially when there is a sudden change from  offline to online education. Students not only prefer going to school or college just to get  education but also many other things associated to their health and social wellbeing.  Comparatively online education lacks such interaction and practical knowledge convey  methods.

Selection  Visualization is about using images. It’s not about drawing; it’s about visual thinking. It  pushes us beyond using words or language alone. It is a way of unlocking a different part  of our brains that allows us to think nonverbally.    When you explain an idea using words, the rest of us will form our own mental pictures,  usually informed by our training. When you say, “We need a new growth platform,” the IT  specialist sees servers and code and the marketing guru sees an advertising campaign. If  instead you present your idea to us by drawing a picture of it, you reduce the possibility of  unmatched mental models.

text:
Ashley Arias  May 30, 2020

Mind Mapping

Challenge    I used mind mapping with employees to help understand their current state and future

needs to successfully transition to a new financial tool. During a summer internship, I worked at  a financial institution’s headquarters and helped with multiple projects, namely the transition  between an old retirement tool to a new alternative tool that would be better integrated in the  system with other preexisting financial tools. Before announcing a transition plan for fee based  planners, corporate wanted to know how much pushback there would be and how to combat  it; admittedly, that is a very broad question with many challenges.  Selection    The intern team decided to pull data from fee based planners with differing ages and

average yearly completed plans. After coming up with a list of 30 fee based planners, my team  created a list of question and tasks with mind mapping at the center of its creation. The goal  was to understand what employees felt would be the hardest part of the transition so that we  could come up with a helpful solution based on the struggle.   Application    The questions were ambiguous yet targeted relevant data that could help us categorize

the planners into different personas to understand their fears and motivations. We used  questions like “how would a new tool change your process with clients” to gain insight into  what a day in the field would look like and spot clear differences from an average client  appointment that we previously had asked employees to map out for us. These projective  techniques and questions led us to add an activity to our interviews. Four quadrants were  grouped into things that I like about the tool, things that I don’t like about the tool, things I am  concerned about and what help will need. Reflection – Story Telling Tool

Challenge

I would like to use the storytelling tool in the field of corporate training. Working in well-established  international companies provides chance to embrace opportunities, helps to learn from innovators  and also adds interpersonal skills, leadership skills and professional development.  However, in order  to withstand the tight deadlines and work pressure, each employee should be trained himself to  undergo attitudinal change and should be motivated to push their boundaries. Corporate training  helps each candidate to train himself to embrace every opportunity with positive attitude. Corporate  training usually involves training needs that are difficult to visualize. The training needs include  induction, professional skills, product training, application simulation and soft skills. For imparting  these skills in an efficient manner, powerful method like story telling is needed to create higher  retention and recall, leading to a memorable and sticky learning experience. It is the motivation and  inspiration contributes to more than ninety percent of the success. And the best way to motivate is  through success stories of experiences, hard work and positive attitude.

Selection

The selection of storytelling tool for corporate training is based on the fact that a story based  learning approach always helps to create desired outcome for the customers when the learners are  well equipped and quick learnt. Stories always help to simplify a complex subject. Story telling can be  used to convert an abstract concept into something that is relatable and easy to assimilate. Also, it  can help learners to understand the consequence of their choices and help them correct in future. In  addition, stories help the learners to connect emotionally to the content and can be used to drive  attitudinal change.

Reflection – Learning Launch

The project scope includes  building a brand, starting a marketing campaign and launch a website. The team of five (5)  employees will work on this project with an even distribution of working hours amongst the  team members. The completion of this project should not exceed 45 business days. We will  focus on trying to determine what is the best workflow that works for our team. text:
Waseem Hamad, MBA

Learning Launch – Designing for Growth

1. Challenge: My great challenge would be to find out of many ideas the best working and

profitable idea with the highest IRR (internal rate of return.) You do not know the future and  the market developments or what other companies are planning for the future – so you have  to find out under un-security unique ideas that work which will be profitable in the future.

2. Selection: There will be many light bulbs with lots ideas. Making a business plan is not the

best way because you go to the unknown. Many guesses and assumptions are made and  everything is new to the innovation team and you (“the unknown”.)

Then you make financial projections based on the unknown. If the IRR is not met we “tweak the  assumptions”.

The better way would be – doing lots of experiments with customers and on the market, which  means the testing of a hypothesis (idea in a specific form). Experiments should be fast and cheap as  many companies do with computer simulations.

You have to do the learning process with customers quickly and also test your key customers  assumptions. To understand customers needs is one of the most important topic. Taking to  customers must be done very very quickly.

The process: Frist step will be a hypothesis – the idea relates to a specific target group / specific  persons – customers have a problem causing pain. With the idea the problem will be solved better  than the competition.

What must be true for a good idea? The purpose of a learning launch is to get the truth which can be  confirmed or disconfirmed.  The truth will save you money and surely time. The idea can be adapted  to a better working idea.

Customers have to be prioritized and the data must meet the key assumptions.

“You think – it is a great idea” but YOU are a problem – a risk to be managed because of confirmation  bias. You are looking for data that confirms your idea.

Student Name: Rania Mohammed

Tool: Story Telling

Challenge Description:

As the leader of a coordination team of 5 persons which has been recently demotivated and  demoralised by dramatic staff reductions in the office which affected several of their  colleagues/friends. I needed to find a way to address managing change with my team  members. Several team members were re-evaluating in a very negative way whether they  too could be affected at any time by change. The attitude of some team members became  that of putting in only the minimum effort for tasks which required excellence and a general  lethargic attitude which did not demonstrate focus and greatly affected productivity. I  recognised an urgent need to re-inspire the team to not only secure their commitment to a  range of upcoming joint actions which would require high energy and beyond the call of  duty time commitments, but also to reinforce to the team that managing change in their  professional and personal lives are important for success as development professionals and  as human beings. I needed a powerful tool that would put the human nature of my team  front  and  centre.  This  video  helped  me  to  present  my  story  well:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Nj-hdQMa3uA

I choose Story Telling as the tool to explain to the team that change and transformation are  constants in life which we should be open to exploring and adjusting to over time. I decided  to make an emotional investment in my team and shared the story of my own family  overcoming challenges and innovating to overcome poverty as an example of why their  contribution to development work is important and the impact it can potentially have on  those who need it most.

Learning Launch – Juan Velasquez

Challenge

I am currently the senior supervisor for the Resolutions department of a cruise vacation  company. The Resolutions department gives internal support to all customer service  and sales agents, helping with any questions or taking over escalation calls if  necessary. The Resolutions agents (agents that report to me) are both the most  capable and tenure agents on the Company, and that’s been mostly what’s given them  the opportunity to be in that position. As a senior supervisor for the department, my job  is to not only make sure the day-to-day tasks are met, but also make sure that we’re  aligned with the company’s policies and interests, as well as make sure that the  Resolutions agents deliver the best possible service. Unfortunately, the best service is  not always delivered by our Resolutions agents, and sometimes they miss key  empathetic communication factors, such as a good tone of voice, empathy, verbalize  willingness to assist, etc. Because of time and call volume, we’ve not been able to get  all the team together at once, to come together with action plans that will benefit all of  us. At the same time, we’ve gotten comments from the agents and customers we assist,  with areas of opportunity about the way interactions are handled. This time, we’ll focus  on first, identifying the critical areas of opportunity by reviewing the service expectations  of the agents that call us, and then uncover the reasons why we’re not being able to  deliver what needs to be delivered. In some cases, because of the service provided,  customer service and sales agents don’t contact us because of the service received,  and ultimately causes financial and loyalty impact to the company if wrong information is  given to our external customers.

Mutual understanding in AI implementation Visualization

This is because I am an AI consultant, and whe n I implemented AI for a service, there was a perception difference between me and the c ustomer, and as a result, we couldn't have a meaningful discussion. We used a tool called  "visualization" to enable all stakeholders to share a common understanding so that they c an tackle issues from the same perspective.

application

I started by creating a simple table in PowerPoint with objectives and issues. However, th e conventional table that I compiled after listening to what I had to say was out of sync, s o I created a table for the AI consultant and a table for the client, respectively. In doing s o, we were able to see differences in their objectives and issues, and we were able to disc uss this part of the process and standardize the objectives and issues. I think this was effe ctively applied because the introduction of visualization allowed for a more constructive  discussion.

Secondly, you can easily share this material and review it immediately. This means that n o matter how complex an issue is, visualization tools can be used to simply and accuratel y share ideas, which can be quickly revisited many times. This allows for constant correct ion in a certain direction while respecting the ideas that each person has.

Thus, I utilized the visualization tool to have a more constructive and solid discussion wit h people who had different opinions.

WEEK 5: FINAL ASSIGNMENT

LEARNING LAUNCHING

Jose Martinez

THE CHALLENGE

Starting to lead an industrial maintenance team to ensure the reliability of a growing chain of NGV service  stations, I received some concerns about a variety of topics from our main customer, the Operational  Team that develop the sales 24 hrs of fuel from Monday to Monday, many of them related to failure  incidence and response times. From the Human Resources side, the pain was about the high cost of Extra  Hours reported in the past months. Getting into the feeling and perception of the Maintenance Technical  Team, the main disconformity was about the intensive use on Extra Hours, taking a lot of their family time  to extend laboring days and solve many operational issues.    After few weeks observing the dynamic of the Maintenance Team, I noticed the evident contradiction of  giving a 8 hours maintenance service for a 24 hours operations. Basically, any failure or need reported in  any station out of the daytime schedule was generating longer response times and extra labor time, with  no option to hire employees to take 3 shifting turns to cover 24 hours every day like the Operations Team  does. The collaborators felt exhaust and frustrated.

THE SELECTION

In a weekly team meeting, we had an idea. Every week one technician has the “Guardian Role”, doings  his tasks during the day and taking service calls during the night. What if that technician does his role  during the night? It looked like a great idea, but there were some doubts about the activities he could  accomplish and the perception of one man (and vehicle) less during the day.    It was hard to align every different opinion and get a total consensus. We felt we wouldn't find the perfect  strategy at the first shoot. But one thing we could agree: we need to test the idea. text: Design Thinking for Innovation: Reflection     Author:  Surya Mohamad ©      Title: The Power of Storytelling for a Start-up Pitch    Challenge:  My team and I are in the pre-start-up phase of incorporating our own BioTech Start-up company. We  are currently working on the first prove of concept on a new drug delivery system against a specific  cancer type. Already in this early phase of development, we are dependent on financial support as  BioTech require a lot of resources from a financial and people point of view. A huge challenge is to  bring business angles, private equity investors or venture capitalists on board at this very early stage  of high risk. How to convince them to support such innovation although “everything” remains  unclear at the beginning of this journey (Piero Vicari; module 1)? In a pitch the biggest challenge is  the limited time window (5-7 minutes) for convincing the right investors. Hence a short, simple and  compelling story has to attract them to invest into you and the team.    Selection:  I was choosing the Storytelling tool to address our challenge. According to Elroy Ford’s analysis  (Global Leadership Development Director @ Mars; Module 2) most business leaders are bored 90%  of the conversation. But he showed a great way to change that. In order to draw their attention  towards the prime goal of inspiring them!  In my view a very good example of storytelling is how Apple managers sell their new creations during  Apple’s Keynotes. They are able to connect emotions, characters and values of people that live that  product every day (see following video: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=tQSdE32O5KE). They  don’t only present a list of things but rather a connection of emotions and actions of what people can  do with their products.  Storytelling encompasses logics, emotional connection and a larger purpose. That’s why “The- Storytelling-Tool” is the ideal instrument to sell innovation in pitch and get the right people inspired.    App

Reflection Storytelling

(Nathan Kumar)

Context  I work for a government agency that promote a culture and holistic system of lifelong learning  through the pursuit of skills mastery, and strengthen the ecosystem of quality education and  training. The challenge is a lot of our initiatives and programmes are through an individual- targeted strategy (think B2C model) and we’re now developing a enterprise-targeted strategy  (think B2B model).    Challenge  I chose to use the tool storytelling to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space  among a diverse group of stakeholders who view the challenge of skills mastery from very  different starting points.     The first step I took was to define who are stakeholders are. Our stakeholders inside the  agency included the various departments such as the middle and back offices and critically  the policy owners who had to understand a new mode of engaging with enterprise. Whereas  our stakeholders outside the agency include the training providers, the educational institutes  and the individuals who now have to be viewed as employees instead of individuals.     The second step I took was to identify, articulate and define the ‘what is’ existing state of the  problem. I articulated 2 key points in my story: the emotional reason why we needed to have  employees pursue skills master and the larger purpose of workforce development. In the  context of a retail business owner, I painted a situation where we continued on our individual- targeted strategy (i.e. the individual learns e-commerce skills) but the employer is not in  support of training the staff as they believe in the traditional means of doing their work (i.e. via  a brick-and-mortar business model) and there’s conflict as the individual doesn’t feel motivated,  valued or supported to execute their job.     Selection  I chose to use the tool storytelling as it has the ability to connects the stakeholders to the  emotions, the characters, the values that we want

text:
Reflection Tiago Borges about Mind Mapping

Challenge    The challenge chosen was around and Onboarding process in an IT Company. The idea  was apply the design thinking tools to understand how the process happened and  improve the processes using the tools. Mind mapping is a great tool inside the Design  thinking and was used to understand the gaps that the process had and how was the  things that could be improved.   The case is that when an It company hired new employees to work as analysts for  different customers, there was no an onboarding process. That process was done  thought the project culture, generating a lot of none equalizes in the answers to the  end users.    Selection    I chose the mind mapping because we haven’t sure about the process like happened  that moment and We would need to understand how was the things that could be  improved. Using the ideas learned at the course, I started the exercise with 10  employees, mapping the process like happened.   After this, we had more 2 phases, to get the pain points and the improvement ideas. In  the end of the exercise, we used the periodization matrix to choice the best  improvement ideas.    Application    The application happened using one session, with 10 employees of the company,  working as managers (different level). We had 3 hours to run the 3 phases of the  exercise, covering the process, pain point and improvement ideas.   In the end of the processes, we had 15 steps of the process like was running, 23 pain  points and 15 improvement ideas. We chose 11 ideas as measure ideas to apply in the  process. Analyzing this numbers, I believe that the process was a success, effective.     Insight      When the exercise started, I think that all participants don’t know about the  simulation, the exercise and about the ways that Design Thinking can improve the  process. I had to show how the things would work.   The presentation of Design Thinking changed the mind of the participants and I believe  that.

text:
Danielle West	 ‘Listening	for	improvement’

1. Challenge: describe your challenge, including all of the relevant

information

I work for a large healthcare organisation. I am in the role of Organisational  Development manager. My main responsibility at the moment is to design a  behavioural framework to support the launch of a new set of organisational values.  The output, (a new set of organisational values) has been decided by our board.  However, how I go about creating this has been left with me.  I believe that the Design-thinking process and tools will help to work through this  challenge in a way that the outcome will be more meaningful to all of our  stakeholders.    I believe this framework needed to encompass the expectations of our customers  (patients and their families) and our staff in order for it to be supportive of the cultural  transformation we are seeking.    I enlisted a small team of people from a range of disciplines to support me in this work.

2. Selection: In your own words briefly describe the tool you selected

(eg. What is it and why did you select it for your challenge – include  any appropriate video lecture references)

The Storytelling tool was the one that resonated strongly with me when considering  the challenge I was working on.     We have received a lot of feedback (complaints) from patients, describing that they  felt dehumanised in the care process that we provide and that they are an input to the  system, rather than a human being in need of care and support.  It seemed important that we understand the actual experiences of our patients, in their  words and through their eyes.    We also felt that it was important for staff to be able to share their experiences of  working in our organisation. I used a story-telling method (modified) for this part also.

Vinod Baker

Our Challenge

I work in an operational environment; the purpose of our business unit is to ensure the circulation  of money. Our staffs’ primary job is to handle the monies that is coming into the bank (deposits)  and the monies that is leaving the bank’s premises and transported to clients’ premises  (withdrawals). Dealing with clients’ money is an important job however quite stressful for our  staff. All our clients rely on our service offerings for them to continue with their business.

The staff morale and motivation is not at a desirable level for optimal productivity. Our challenge  is to change how our employees feel about working for this business unit. To create an  environment that employees find pleasant and a place that encourages growth and learning.  Furthermore, we want our staff to feel motivated and encouraged to improve how they work.  Having motivated and determined staff will have a positive implication on our productivity.  Therefore, as part of our People Program we need initiatives that assist in changing how our  people feel about their work. We also need initiatives that are cost efficient.

Our Selection

We started our design thinking journey by using multiple tools such as: interviews and personas  to understand why our employees came to work and how they felt at work. More importantly we  wanted to find out how we can make their lives better and what is important for them. Majority of  our people work an 8-hour shift, this means that they spend more time at work with colleagues  than they do with their families. Hence it is important that we improve this environment.

The team and I are now at a phase where we would like to test our hypothesis and assumption  by running small experiments and prototypes, learning launches. The objective is to see how  employees react and receive the new and different offerings made available to them. STORY TELLING – Zahida (9023)

We see a lot of people having mental health issues but do not tend to take  treatment from professionals. This is because of in-office treatment stigma,  lack of awareness and availability. But it is important to give equal importance  to both physical and mental health which is lacking in the society.

So, I came up with an idea of mental health app with professionals like  psychologists, psychotherapists, counsellors. Along with professionals we also  include caregivers because they play an important role in the treatment  process. The app also includes personality tests, mood trackers, positive  quotes and many more features. Through the app we can reach out to large  group of people with 24/7 availability at their comfort level.

Assignment Rubric - design thinking

Challenge & Selection

In 2009 my friend Luca came to me wanting to launch a brand of clothes that spoke about Maranhão (a region of northeastern Brazil). However, historically, there were only two brands that did very well in .  has a facility of exporting lifestyle and fashion for being one of the main postcards of Brazil. In Maranhão, the clothes that were manufactured were usually destined for tourists and did not have a personality. They were just "souvenirs" of the city. Knowing this I talked with Luca and suggested the application of some techniques of Design Thinking. Initially, we needed to understand the problem from the point of view of our consumer (empathy), and for this we began to look at which brands our target public most liked to use and interact with them to delve into the motives that made them buy these products. We realized that our target audience looked a lot like us and we consumed the same brands from other locations in Brazil. Knowing this we already had an idea of  how to start to validate the idea by doing a benchmarking with these brands that we consumed.

Application

As the goal was to launch a brand that spoke of Maranhao, it was natural to start talking about how Maranhão came about, who we were colonized, what people invaded us, and what heritage these people left us. After a very deep research on the history of Maranhão, the ﬁrst collection of the brand with prints of some postcards of the state appeared in stylized form, taking as references the type of design of the brands that we used and put to sell. It was a success!!!

Insight & Approach

Design Thinking Reflection: Storytelling

Challenge

In my organization, I am responsible for business development in the EMEA region, but apart from my  core role and responsibilities, I “wear many hats”, e.g. organize business conferences and events,  manage alliances and accounts, create collateral, etc. I work with clients, partners, internal teams,  external teams and various stakeholders, day in, day out and addressing diverse groups with different  goals, backgrounds, challenges, needs and wants has always been a known challenge, not only for me. I  needed to communicate more efficiently with different stakeholder groups, structure messages and key  takeaways better, create build up and align meeting participants, regardless if they are from Marketing  or IT, around a single vision of the problem we are trying to solve.

Selection

Unfortunately, I have limited opportunities under the circumstances of COVID-19 global pandemic and  lockdown to practice my new design thinking knowledge acquired during the course, however, luckily,  storytelling is a design tool I can practice every day on infinite Zoom meetings and it can be applied to  multiple contexts. Apart from the reason mentioned above, we learned from both Barry and  the Chief Learning Officer of Mars Inc. how storytelling is an important design tool and a tool that has  been increasingly leveraged in the business world as every product, service, solution and institution has a  story behind it. A good story in a nutshell is more than just conveying a message that has logic, it has a  larger emotional connection and purpose or i.e. it creates a cause that according to the CLO of Mars Inc.  “ignites people and unites people”. text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge      My name is Karen Gonzalez. I am ICT Director of a school in South Africa. Some fifteen years ago I co- wrote some software to manage the internal venue bookings at our school. Being a software  developer was and is still not part of my role at the school, but integrating technology into the  curriculum and empowering staff and children to become responsible and capable adults in a  technology rich world, certainly is. We developed the software because there was nothing  commercially available at that stage that suited our needs and pocket. Another reason was that, in  those early years, when we were trying to get staff to use technology to improve the learning and  teaching experience, we reasoned that giving teachers (and administrators) tools to do their daily jobs  would improve literacy and have positive educational spin offs. The software has lived on and is used  extensively by an increasing number of people and for more than the original, quite simplistic,  purpose. The software in function and form is very much end of life but the tool(s) is so interwoven in  the fabric of how we manage events, sports practices, and classroom activities that we simply can’t  manage without it for any time at all. The software is buggy and is written in a language that is no  longer supported. Our challenge is to seamlessly replace the software with something that will meet  the new needs of the school, without disrupting daily activities, on a very tight budget and at the  same time win the buy in of the various managers who will very likely need to change their process.    The project scope includes the marketing departments and admin, grounds and teaching staff across  our three campuses, each of whom are responsible for different and varying components within the  current booking system model; it particularly includes the academic staff who quickly and easily want  to book venues (including equipment and resources) for sport an

REFLECTION - STORYTELLING

Challenge and selection

I teach at the Faculty of Engineering of the Pesto Pizza and one of the  challenges is to train future research students, as well as to develop the research skills of the students.  At the Beescoop a system of formative research was implemented  through three programs. The first program involves students from the first to the third cycle in which  research habits are developed. The second program involves from the 4th to the 7th cycle where  scientific thought is developed in the selected courses of the specialty. Finally, program III from the  8th to the 10th cycle in which contact and visibility of the research is achieved through the final  development of the research work and its publication in various congresses and academic events.

Storytelling or the creation of stories is a tool that connects from the beginning with the student and  inspires creativity and is one of the educational techniques that allows teachers and students to learn  and innovate. A story will impact differently on each student, as said in the previous paragraph at the  University we train student researchers through a system of formative research so that they through  creativity, research and the use of technologies can provide solutions to the problems of their  community. Many of these students to begin to develop their formative research work have to identify  a real problem and most of them begin with a question: what problem can I solve and investigate?  and this is where storytelling is applied to identify themselves and create meaning through a story,  inspire them to connect in the story, identify with the character, link the context by determining the  problems in their family or social environment and propose solutions using knowledge and applying  technologies.

created​ ​by​ ​marginalized​ ​peoples,​ ​I​ ​was​ ​not​ ​sure​ ​I​ ​had​ ​the​ ​knowledge​ ​of​ ​the​ ​traditionally

rendered​ ​U.S.​ ​History​ ​curriculum​ ​and​ ​thus​ ​the​ ​skill-set​ ​to​ ​be​ ​successful.​ ​However,​ ​thinking

text:
John Yates Design Thinking for Innovation Carolina Chavez May 3, 2020

Reflection: The Mind Mapping Tool

1. Challenge

My consulting firm was tasked by our client, a health-care foundation board, to help them design an organizational strategy in light of all the rapidly moving developments in health-care. The board was at an impasse, uncertain on where to place its bets to best support health-care in this country without being able to predict where a number of current trends might lead. We used design thinking to present a few high-level, flexible, iterative, strategic options for the board that the foundation could pursue within the 2021-2024 time-frame.

2. Selection

This reflection will focus on the mind mapping tool, which was the most important phase of the project as it moved the process from the What Is? stage of ascertaining the current state of the organization and of health-care in the U.S., to the crucial What If? stage of beginning to draft new, possible realities for the foundation. This fulfilled the purpose of the board in hiring my firm.

I am defining mind mapping as the collective visualization by the board members of the sum of their knowledge, experiences, insights, interests, and visions of health-care, thereby establishing a snapshot or base upon which to build a series of possible strategic options for the foundation to pursue. As Lopez said in the Module 3 video:

“In the first phase of the design thinking process, we take a look at the current reality, at What Is? In doing so, we amass a huge amount of data. Before moving to the next phase, What If?, we need to distill all that data into information and insights that can be easily communicated. This is just what mind mapping does well.”

Following the completion of extensive health-care industry research and in-depth interviews with members of the board to collect data on the current reality in the What Is? stage of the design thinking approach, we started the mind mapping

text: Mauro Zizza, DESIGN THINKING ASSIGNMENT    DT for psychotherapy: The role of story telling    I am an engineer and I became an specialist in Machine Design and Design Methods. For  reasons out of the scope of this essay, I became a psychotherapist in several approaches,  one of them being existential therapy.     In some point last year, I realized that I operated sometimes in therapy under the scope of  design stages and thought of having a method based on that. This is not the method itself  but a reflection on the coincidences and how a DT is affected by the method itself and, if  seen correctly, it is also a healing process for some.    What is?    When I have a new client or a regular one, I alway ask: what do you want to work with? So  they begin telling me a story. At the first stages I use the phenomenological method to keep  asking what is? Just the data, no judgements -for now. Sometimes this is enough since the  person can change his/her story by clearing the facts and is able to separate his/her own  judgements or prejudices.     What if?    In a second stage we begin to explore what others would think. So first I ask: What do you  think I think about it? Some times they are very close and others not. So I continue to ask:  What if you see things like I do? Then we can ask: what do he/she/they think about our  session? What if you ask them? What if you propose/suggest/explore what you found out  today about yourself?    What wows?    A regular question to clients is: what are your options, your wishes, alternatives? Very often  a client is locked out and see no options. Many of the idea development from this course can  be used as a game  during the session. I use many materials. Again, one option is to have  the client re write the story with two, three, four different endings.    What works?    Therapy sessions is a safe place to try out experiments. REFLECTION

VISUALIZATION

By Melissa Martinez

Challenge

I am a university student in the last semesters of Administration. Last semester I took a course on  Development of Creative Potential. Throughout this class we addressed different creativity  techniques and for the final evaluation we were asked to do a work as a team in which it was  necessary to design a creativity development program as if we were going to implement it in a real  company.

My team and I develop the points of the work and prepare it for a first review. Our teacher put  particular emphasis on that our projects looked 100% school-based and that we should make them  look professional, like a formal company would present a program in real life. My colleagues seemed  quite disoriented, they didn't know how to make our work look professional. I offered to do it and  tried to explain the idea to them.

Selection

I am not a professional nor do I have much experience in the business world of work. However, I am  a mostly visual person and I like to work with these elements.

As mentioned in the video conference that talks about this tool, visualization is quite important in  our way of communicating. By having to use the right side of our brain (often ignored) we can think  non-verbally and be more creative. That is why I chose this tool, because the impact that an element  has on our view is what will influence it to attract our attention or go unnoticed.

Application

The first thing I did was a quick evaluation of the job we had, it was pretty ugly and it didn't attract  attention at all. Right away, I myself visualized in my mind how I would like it to look and feel  professional, creative, and impactful.

Then I looked for graphic elements of all kinds to highlight my document and applied them:  headings, images, graphics and figures, color combination, letters, emphasis and distribution of the  text, etc. The result was amazing even for me, it was truly professional and eye-catching work.
