text:
Example Reflection-Mind Mapping

By Karina Duque

Challenge and Selection

Mindmapping is a tool I used in my office; however, I was not aware that I was specifically  applying it although with a limited approach. It came to me first by instinct. I mean, I gathered  with my four-member team and we used to brainstorm ideas purposefully to solve an issue.  I  work in an International Organization in the Environment field. I am responsible for the  financial and administrative monitoring of environment projects according to the  organization’s and donor’s rules and regulations. These projects have their management units,  we call them PMU. Sometimes we forget that in those PMU, real people are working. We don’t  see these people we only see financial and administrative processes and requests coming from  them. The challenge we face is that these processes are not smooth and do not represent our  vision of “impeccable administration”. Therefore, project’s targets are delayed due to paper  work, bureaucracy, errors and long time processing.

Application

After learning what mind mapping really is, I decided to get close to my PMU colleagues. I’ve  been generally “judging” what they do from my supervision role rather than having a more  empathetic approach. First, I organized monthly meetings with my team to motivate them to  be more people centered when providing a course of action. Then, we started to interview, to  talk to people. This time, we made it with a different approach, using the invitation to “the  garage sale” event. We offered this time questions: ¿What makes your daily work difficult?  ¿What would you need to improve the processes you send to our Unit? ¿ From 1 to 10, how  empowered do you feel in your position to deliver a high-quality work? What do you want to  share? Well, we got surprised discovering that many of the challenges they have come from a  poor understanding of the reasons behind a regulation. As a manager in a global consulting firm focused on assisting companies manage their  global workforce, I interact daily with a multitude of stakeholders. These include client  HR Mobility professionals and expatriate employees, third party relocation and  immigration vendors, colleagues across 100+ countries, my own direct team as well as  our offshore compliance team. All of which with different perspectives and reality  leading to different inputs and expectations throughout the entire process.

Although moving employees abroad isn’t a new phenomenon, the globalization that  started in the early 90’s and the advancements in technology created opportunities for  companies of all sizes to venture into new markets, therefore increasing exponentially  the need for employee relocations in traditional and new locations. This brings me to the  challenge we faced – our 15 year-old system became outdated and inefficient despite a  few ad-hoc attempts over the years to fix it and integrate it. It was clear to me that the  conventional linear analysis would neither properly identify the underlying problems nor  arrive at a solution that would resolve it effectively and wow all of us.

I used the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to gain a deep understanding of the  current system’s capabilities and shortfalls and the possible solutions. I knew I needed a  compelling story to gain support at all levels of my organization and secure resources  and the team was key.

text:
Rob’s charisma

Learning Launch design tool

Lucas Medina

Design Thinking for Innovation

Challenge

Selection

Application

In my town there is a small shop of many years to which we want to lend a hand.  The owner is Rob, a friendly guy who knows the whole town and likes talking to the  neighbors very much and it seems that they do too. He and two other employees run  the store where they sell many types of products. However, in recent years his sales  have fallen because new companies have arrived and Rob does not know how to  adapt to the new competition. Rob is a tough nut to crack to deal with changes. It has  too many products, many of them sell poorly because they are not current, but Rob  does not want to get rid of them. He says “they are slow selling, but people like it.”

Another problem that Rob has and why sales have fallen is when it comes to charging  because he stays talking to customers for a long time and slows down work, and  some customers who want a quick purchase become desperate. Plus, it’s so chaotic  and disorganized that a new customer always has to call an employee to find the  product he’s looking for.

By establishing our key assumptions, after carrying out a preliminary study of the  market, we agree that the sector to which the store is exposed cannot vary much,  but the image, distribution, experience and scale of the store could be improved,  focusing on the products that most They sell and leave those who cannot compete  with other companies. In addition, Rob must be relocated, to speed up customer  charges.

Because we have strong competition and limited time, we selected the Learning  Launch design tool to do quick tests to verify that our hypotheses are on the right  track and convince Rob that the changes can be good.

Jennifer Medina

Reflection

Challenge

I am among of the staff of the planning section of our Department that is working for  disaster management.  Seventy (70%) of our localities are located in highly vulnerable  areas.  The province has a varied terrain ranging from flat, to rugged, to mountainous  that reaches over 900 meters from sea level. The island province is highly susceptible to  landslide, flooding and typhoon. The localized early warning system of the province is  emplaced, proactivity in implementing evacuation protocol is practiced.  The challenge is  the prompt reporting of evacuees particularly at the geographically isolated and  disadvantaged barangays.  The data shall serve as reference of the concerned municipal  and provincial local government units in the procurement of relief goods should  augmentation is necessary.

Selection

In responding to the said challenge, I used the Visualization tool in conceptualizing an  innovation to address prompt, easy and available online monitoring platform of evacuees.   The tool would greatly help me in foreseeing and forecasting the needed activities, tasks  and the logistical requirements in accomplishing the project.

I also organized our partners in the implementation of this project.

Final Assignment – Design Thinking for Innovation

By Katie Wakefield

Visualization Tool

Challenge

We are currently faced with the challenge of shifting the way we do projects within our organization as we  stand up a new digital strategy. Some background information: we are one of the country’s largest energy  producers and have been going through a transformation over the past 5 years. Since our current CEO took the  helm, we have gone from a very favourable economic situation, working to streamline some of our value chains  and identify opportunities for standardization, to one of the worst economic downturns in the past 20 years.  Along with the downturn, our focus has shifted from production growth at any cost to a sustainability mindset.  We realize that we can be part of the solution as the world has turned its attention to reducing GHG emissions,  reducing our carbon footprint and becoming more aware of how the products we use daily are manufactured,  distributed and disposed of.

As the technology leaders for the company, we have recently combined business process management with  innovation and solution design to develop projects in a more responsible and planful manner. We have a  project management methodology that has been adopted from our major projects group, with the mindset  that we can apply the governance, rigour and oversight that has helped control capital and operating  expenditures of our large scale developments to new technology projects. The challenge is really to shift how  our group approaches design and development right from the beginning of a project, rather than  fundamentally changing the activities of our experts – the what. Challenge: Change Management on a proposed process change within the claims organization of a large  US based P&C insurer which will greatly modify how First Notice of Loss (FNOL) submissions are  processed. Change of process will introduce Robotic Process Automation (RPA) functionality and  significantly modify work content and responsibilities for Contact Center associates.

Selection: Selected Visualization, or visual thinking to create a shared understanding of the problem the  change of process was attempting to solve. The approach used leverages pictures to help visualize  painpoints and desired future state in a brainstorming format. The pictures are intended to evoke an  emotional response to real life issues, frustrations and ideals that the associates are feeling.

Application: I conducted several focus group sessions with customers to obtain Voice of the Customer  (VOC) and several focus groups with associates to obtain Voice of the Associate (VOA). The sessions  were held over several weeks to ensure we had a good representation of customers and associates. I  began the VOC sessions with a high-level process map to represent the customers experience as they  traveled along the process of filing an auto damage claim. I then asked the customers to select pictures  that best represented how they felt through the process. Pictures selected ranged from feelings of  frustration, fear, uncertainty, anger, etc.. which were not surprising. Name: Gurwinder Singh

Challenge

I am hired as a change specialist of my organisation to change the existing silo culture into more  collaborative culture to increase customer satisfaction score by 30 percent . There are currently 5  teams with each has 9 members working on five different products that release features  to address  the rapid needs of customers during the COVID period. The existing culture is teams operate in a silo  manner and also product features are selected based on product owners knowledge that is  fragmented about the product and not customer driven.

Selection

As I do have digital product and agile cultural transformation experience and coached the team  members on Agile culture and Scrum framework of complex product development, I am going to try  learning launch tool to test the agile operating model of complex product development.

Application

For our learning launch, I focussed on implementing collaborative culture between three teams first  to ensure that team members can follow Agile Scrum framework in working together. All the three  teams share a common goal of working towards customer centric features identified through mind  mapping tool techniques. I setup a timeboxed, iterative and incremental culture for these teams and  every week, the individual team leaders share the lessons learnt and action required to further  improvement. In this way of experimentation, learning and action on continuous improvements  made the team working collaboratively towards a common goal. After two months of  experimentation, fine tuning and aligning all the team members to work collaboratively, then  implemented the same for the remaining three teams successfully.

MIND MAPPING TO HELP A TRAINING COMPANY TRANSFORM THEIR BUSINESS MODEL

1. Challenge

I run my own marketing consultancy specializing in commercial acceleration. My clients are  large Life Sciences corporates. Exceptionally, a friend who owns a medium-size,  international training company asked me to help facilitate a process to define a new,  digitally-enabled business model for his company, including a roadmap on how to achieve  the end-to-end digital transformation of the business as soon as possible.

The high urgency is due to the coronavirus crisis. While the training company has a strong  proposition and a long, successful track record, it’s fairly ‘old-school’ in its content,  approach and methods; it relies almost entirely on large face-to-face classroom trainings to  get the job done for clients. This no longer works in the era of social distancing and remote  work and must be urgently evolved.

The expectation is to upgrade content, ways of working and customer experience using  technology with the overall goal of step-changing growth. This company not only wants to  survive the crisis but also thrive in the new post-covid19 reality. I will be working amidst  internal and external uncertainty, with a small team who worries about their current  situation and manages budgets tightly. I want to use the Design Thinking approach to  address the challenge. This paper will focus on how I will use MIND MAPPING to bridge the  path from What Is to What if.

2. Selection

I have used mind mapping formally and informally in the past but never as part of the  rigorous yet flexible process Design Thinking provides. In the context of Design Thinking  mind mapping is an incredibly powerful tool which allows its users to translate tons of  disparate data into meaningful, communicable insights which deliver criteria on which to  build innovation.

text:
Cristino Ramirez

29 May 2020

Challenge & Selection:

Our government customer was used to relying on proprietary data collection and analysis tools  specifically tailored for the government operating environment.  Over time, the government customer  realized that commercial solutions offerings existed that could provide highly accurate data analysis to  enhance their knowledge and awareness of their operating environment at a very affordable cost.   When compared to designing and acquiring their own proprietary system, the government customer  realized that our commercial solution could have the potential to enhance their capabilities, but were  interested in understanding how our data analysis system could be integrated into their normal daily  operations.

Selection:

I chose the “Learning Launch” tool for this customer, because it allowed our team to work very closely  and collaboratively with the customer in an environment that closely mimicked how the system would  be deployed if the project proved to be a viable prototype that should be scaled.

Application:   Since the customer was already a receiver of raw data from my company, we were able to  generate a high number of data sets over a 6-week period to include disconfirming data in our test  batches.  The cost of the “Learning Launch” was largely limited to labor costs associated with two of our  analysts and software engineers that supported the active contract with the customer for data  collection.  The individuals chosen to support the “Learning Launch” were very disciplined in their  approach, but also had a history of listening very well to customer and tailoring the response to best  meet the customer’s needs.  Since the nature of the project was leveraging real world data that  generated potentially hundreds of datasets daily, we were able to both develop fast feedback cycles and  present real world examples to our customer to garner their feedback.

Challenge  Being a member of my company’s innovation department, I was called along with my team for an urgent  meeting. Based on our latest monthly report, a big number of our newly employed engineers have  complained about an unpleasant and boring working environment; an unfortunate fact for a company  that relies on young and fresh minds to keep aiming forward. My challenge is to create an environment  in which our employees can perform and endure their daily challenges agreeably and more pleasantly.   The project scope includes our team’s department and the new employees of other departments, with a  limited period of thirty business days. We will focus on trying to uncover and pin point the effective  solutions with regard to a pleasant environment.

With the problem already in hand, I selected the Mind-Mapping tool at this stage of my design. I believe  it illustrates the minds of our employees to finally create a common mind amongst them regarding the  reality of our challenge.      Application  Mind Mapping is great way to brainstorm. In order to turn their ideas into reality, we had to collect data  from our employees.  My colleagues and I have prepared a reunion for all the concerned members of  the company; at first, we have demanded answers from each employee on a survey that tackled their  vision of a pleasant environment. I think that all tools are important and have a lot of challenges, because everything in  the world it’s change all the time, then we have to towards this movement, through  studying, understanding the best way to do it. Also, I truly believe that companies begin  understanding that the quickly evolution is made for people, then we have to specialize  to understand the people, describe what they want? What they dream? What they  need? What can we do to be better for them? After these answers, we can offer right  solutions of them, that’s why I chose Visualization, because it’s a good way to know  these answers.    In my mind, it’s really simple to understand and accept that we have to focus in human,  in their life’s, their needs. This is the gap that we can work and increase value.

Select

For me, I would like to start my challenge with Visualization, because in my opinion when  we begin to analyze any problem, we have to break down the first barrier if exist, it’s to  get a start a good relationship with stakeholders and users (if are not the same person),  because these people give us all the information that we need, through your mindsets,  your feelings, your emotions, your behaviors, your life and your knowledge, but we have  to search other information’s to complete our job too. There is guy who works as a Talent acquisition professional in a multinational organization, his day to day  activity revolves around interacting with different level of professionals, He get involved into the process  of human resource starting from recruitment till separation. He regularly meets with different  stakeholders like hiring managers, head of departments, chief officers of my company also with the  representative of recruitment agencies.   But, why are we discussing about a day to day life of an employee, any clue?  Well, to answer your question this is the story of mine where I tried to show a glimpse of how my days  looks like any fine day. Meeting with various stakeholders require some data, bullets or facts to present  or to provide them update on day to day activities, SLA, projections, selections, forecasting and many  more data and figures. And here I use the method of Storytelling - Storytelling is an art as well as science  and it helps us presenting any data or facts in an interesting way.     Application:  I will tell you an incident of one fine day. There was a product presentation, which was related to my job  area mainly related to some automation. However, employees in my organization were very skeptical  about change in process and most of them were having fixed mindset. Using sTOYrytelling by Roberto Pink

http://www.frederick-curtis.net/posts/wp-content/categoryauthor.php

Challenge & Selection    The purpose of this challenge was to discuss how the communication between users and  developers influence the outcome of a process of developing a software. Specifically  contextualized from the agile development perspective the proposal was to discuss how  narrations of history could enhance and improve elicitation process requirements. So the idea  was to adopt the storytelling paradigm directing the focus of studies for application in  software engineering processes. The storytelling is closely linked to the development of  mankind, and use techniques and strategies they use narratives to capture the audience's  attention and lead to certain actions of subtle and natural way has become quite effective.

Application

These photos are bottom of the page, we were discussing how to innovate in products created  in technology companies, using design thinking. Was applied storytelling using toys,  participants rode on the scene and with it we can see that the focus should always be on  customers / users. Before the process within the company for software creation was  bureaucratic, we thought only within the time limit and agreed financial values. But now  processes have changed and customer satisfaction comes first.

Insight & Approach

It is often necessary to teach your client some things, from instructions on how to use products  or services, to strategies and best practices in the use of tools. Normally, manuals and step by  step guides are boring and too long to fulfill the role of teaching what is needed.

Use characters (who are also representing the consumers themselves) within a story is the  best way to teach something more absorbing content, illustrating situations and desired  solutions.

Every client has a history and it can be good enough to promote your product or service.  revolutionary ideas usually solve old problems.

Reflections on Visualization

by Gonzalo Wong

Challenge: The Fuzzy Mess

I choose Visualization to see how it would help me resolve a problem in our support escalation process.

I had a bad experience escalating a service outage to the correct people at our company.  Several of my  peers who should have known about the outage were not made aware of the problem. We discovered  customers were not aware of the solution when it was put in place.  These breakdowns in  communication left me wondering where our process was broken and what we need to do to fix it.  I  gathered our team to walk through the process and experiences of different people to see if we could  identify the source of the communication breakdown.

Selection: Helping Others See the Same Challenge

I chose to draw out the events that revealed the problem in a visualization.  The visual representation of the communication flow overcame the complexity of the issue and the likelihood of confusion in our  conversation.  How could I keep the group on the same place as we reviewed the escalation events was  the challenge.  Because visualization supports congruent understanding I thought it would help keep  the group together as we reviewed the escalation process.

Application: Draw, Discuss, Repeat

I drew a representation of each of events in the escalation sequence as it was reviewed and discussed.  Once all the events were in the visualization the team was able to reflect on places where things went  wrong.  This led to proposed fixes being added to the visual. We were able to keep the discussion  focused by reference to parts of the process in the visualization.

Insight: Point of View

The use of visualization helped the entire team see the problems in the process from a number of  perspectives at the same time.  The discussion was focused. We were able to jump to new topics  quickly by pointing a place in the visualization.  The team stayed with the different aspects of the  conversation quickly.

Final Assignment by Anna Russo

Challenge

I am an HRBP & OD Manager at a desalination and water treatment  organization. we are spread over 5 different geographies. Within my  responsibilities are the complete training and development of our ~450  employees worldwide. Organizational development holds many different areas.  For this assignment I focused on the managers development program, which I  build based on my own agenda, OD trends that I collect, and statements  regarding performance from managers in our routine meetings, or from the  performance management review process.

Managers Development programs usually try to gather the employees and not  only teach them techniques but to become a group of associates, that opens  about managerial issues and dilemmas. In the current state that gathering is  banned creating a 6 meetings program seems unreal.

Selection

I decided to try a learning launch. with all the data I collected, after my team  gathered and thought together what our possibilities are, I decided to try a first  session for our Team Leaders that will be on-line and will try to achieve our  managers development goals.

Application

I set a date and scheduled the meeting. Found a sales and marketing manager  to share a case study regarding decision making. We built the presentation  together by colliding the theoretical background with the actual way decisions are  made in my company. Exploring our GO-NO-GO procedure.

Instead of a serious of meetings I built just the learning launch. Tried to set  specific slides for queries so that people will not be silent during this session and  they will have to participate.

Design Thinking: Peer Graded Assessment                                                                 Claudio Said

Email: john03@yahoo.com

Challenge

I was working for a Consulting Firm and was on an assignment/project to reduce operational costs from  an IT Infrastructure department. The client company’s Infrastructure (data center) was built in an  unplanned fashion as they were facing a significant spike in their Operational Expenditure as the system  lacked a Governance Model. As a Program Manager / Consultant it was a Herculean Task for me to  identify the different pieces of puzzle and see how these fit well so that I could define a Project’s Scope  that would give an Estimate for the Business Case to be generated so that the project could be initiated.

The client Infrastructure had many aspects like Power Distribution, Cooling, Disaster Recovery, Test and  Production Environment, Virtual / Cloud Appliances etc. that were contributing in a large carbon foot  print of the data center.  The steering committee were more concerned about the Production  Environment as it supported 21 Airline Companies’ Reservation Systems across Europe and Asia and for  them their customer impact could cause a huge loss in credibility and market share.

Selection

Since, the management wasn’t clear on how to proceed in budgeting a new project since, they had some  unusual data (numbers) but no visualization on the negative impact if the project is not executed.  Visualization tool was selected by me to provide a mind map of how things could potentially affect in  the longer run if the project isn’t initiated.

Application:

The depiction on ‘WHAT IS’ phase was done with a Fishbone diagram (Ishikawa Diagram) in which the  cause and effects of the present situation was shown which could directly be related to potential cost  overrun happening.

Example Reflection: Visualization.

Challenge and selection.

The first tool I used was the visualization of other team members, because it was

necessary to understand the needs of the people and have a common idea, and then I

was able to start planning possible solutions to the problems that could arise in the

development of the event.

The scope and limitations are other aspects that we want to develop, what kind of people

we will attract and how many people we can improve, so that people feel more

comfortable than when they compete.

Application.

Initially, the brainstorming process began, and then the information and information

gathered by customers' employees was used to create charts and sketches of the

company's new organization. This is very useful because customers are part of the

change, they allow us to improve and they warn us of the reasons for the failure of our

company.

We chose to add a template to this method to divide the customer's suppliers in order to

incorporate detailed company information so that we can work more efficiently.

Insight and Approach

What I have learned from this knowledge is to broaden my horizons and to be able to

see more clearly. Many tools that I think are temporarily not essential, but, on the

contrary, are essential for the correct development of thought. Sharing ideas is a good

way to create a unified environment, as other team members have the confidence to

participate and can analyze the data together to reach an agreement and specify the

most appropriate conditions for the company.

Ever since I discovered the visualization tool, I have realized that it cannot open its eyes,

but concentrates on daily work. Visualization allows us to open our minds to understand

the needs of those around us, so that we can use it to provide services that can benefit

them.

REFLECTION – LEARNING LAUNCH    Abdo Cortes

January 9, 2021   UNIVERSITY OF VIRGINIA – DARDEN SCHOOL OF BUSINESS

Challenge:

I founded a watch company in the Philippines a few years back with the aim of becoming the first Filipino- owned watch company that assembled its timepieces locally.  Being a physicist and a technical watch  enthusiast, I wanted to plant the seeds on developing watchmaking in the Philippines.  So, without having  any business background, I decided to conduct a Learning Launch to test my idea through an experiment.   With the gap in my business acumen, I was fortunate enough to come across a book called The Physics of  Business Growth which happened to be written by Tom Garza and Rosa Cortes.  By coming  up with an analogy of putting up a business or an idea through the scientific method, I was able to grasp  the process.  The analogy was very helpful.

At the very beginning, the main task was to decide on the kind timepiece that will be launched as a test.  The test would be to test the brand’s name recall and retention, targeted market acceptance, and, of  course, sales.

Selection:

I gathered three of my friends who were from different industries to join me in developing the initial  model and asked them for their insights.  Apart from this, I also held a separate brainstorming session  with my lead technician.  I believed that through the product ideation, we had a good product to test.

Application:

During our learning launch, we focused on the creation of the brand and in properly sending out the  message about us and the product that we launched.  Given the limited financial resources we had then,  we decided to launch a high-quality basic dress timepiece as it aligns with the brand’s image.  We launched  the timepiece in a boutique hotel’s restaurant and invited friends from the press and some showbiz  personalities. text:
Mind Mapping

By: Charlotte Jones

Challenge and Selection

At the National School of Arts and Crafts Casablanca, I am a member of the EAP Student Committee. The Student Advisory Board assists the Business School with improving the student  experience by providing a student perspective on issues facing academics, communication, and  career development opportunities. To better understand the student population’s wants and needs  we conducted a large in-depth interview at the Business School. All 15 board members,  including myself, each interviewed 10 business students with a range of grade levels and  degrees. We covered the main focuses of the admission process, academics, career preparation,  and overall communication.

Once we completed the interviews we were left with a massive amount of information.

Our challenge became decoding patterns in the data to discover where to focus our efforts. The  challenge promoted our selection of the Mind Mapping Tool. Mind Mapping is a term used for  the process of discovering patterns within the information you collected during the beginning of  exploration or the ‘What is?’ phase. As noted in the Mind Mapping Video, with Wendy Lopez,  mind mapping is a visual process of capturing the perspectives of customers, or students in this  scenario. The tool guides the team through a process of laying out all of your information,  observing trends, and noting clusters. The Mind Mapping process is a way for the student board  to narrow down issues for consideration.

Application

To start the mind mapping process, each student board member collected their data from

the interviews. On giant sticky notes, we all creatively wrote down the things that are working  and the things that are not working, based on conversations with students. What the likes and  dislikes were divided into two sides of the paper. DESIGN THINKING ASSINGMENT

DARDEN BUSINESS SCHOOL – COURSERA

OFF-GRID REFRIGERATION CHALLENGE IN ABUJA-NIGERIA

Habibu George

Abuja, October 30, 2016

CONTENTS

1. CHALLENGE; Market penetration  ……………………………………………  3

2. TOOL SELECTED; Learning Launches …………………………………..........  3

3. APPLICATION and INSIGHTS ……………………………………………………..  3

4. APPROACH  ………………………………………………………………..….. ..  4

CHALLENGE; Market penetration

Power is a significant challenge in Nigeria. In about two decades this nation has expended  over twenty billion U.S. Dollars yet our total power output is about Five thousand  megawatts. This is a country with a population of about a hundred and seventy million  people occupying about a million square kilometres of land. Many people need power to  run their fridges, freezers, air conditioning etc but this lack of it created a challenge and an  opportunity. So we set up a factory to produce blocks of ice that we could provide the  people in our state to use in meeting some of their refrigeration needs. Because of the  burning nature of the need and huge population we believed this would be a no brainer  and would hit the market in a huge wave. This did not happen. As a matter of fact, we  struggled to make sales of 20 blocks a day from a 1000 block a day factory. This was not  sustainable and we had to take significant action and fast if were not going to shelve the  business.    This way we would get hard facts on why the market was reacting with such poor reception  to a product that was designed (as we thought) to meet an ardent refrigeration need.

TOOL SELECTED; Learning Launches

Lucky for us I had this challenge in mind while taking the course and it seemed sensible  to use the learning launches. This would keep is in the market experimenting to get to the  truth we required to take a decision on our current business and or, model. The whole idea  was that we would get the true market feel and information we would use. From the videos  Estela Perez

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

I am a member of the organization’s product development team. We are a multinational company from  the textile industry, and our challenge is to grow the sales of our line products. P&D works closely with  the Sales team, which brings us the feedback from our B2B customers, with our Trade Marketing  department, which brings us the feedback and information from the market, and the industrial  development team at the industrial plant.    The company spent a few months in a process of mind set and cultural change, when the employees  were trained in agile methodologies, to use them as new tools for the developments of the new product  process, and also solve problems in which the company has found difficulty.

Selection    After the training our team has already followed up with some parts of the "What Is" (Journey  Mapping, Value Chain Analysis), and now we have reached the stage of Mind Mapping, which is why I  choose this tool for reflection.    Application    First, we chose a large room in the office. Then we paste all the data that we collected during the  previous phases on the walls. We gathered a group of twenty people from the areas of sales, trade  marketing, product development and industrial, so they could look at it. Gradually everyone made  observations, and we followed the processes of insights formation and clustered the data so we could  proceed with brainstorming.    Insight    After the use of mind mapping, we could perceive a series of links and patterns among the interviewees,  and in this way, it was possible to observe some problems and feelings of the consumers that we didn’t  know before. text:
Linda Moore REFLECTION – VISUALIZATION

CHALLENGE

While working for my previous employer, a large defense contractor offering products and services from undersea  to outer space, I managed all tradeshow and sponsorship activity for a sector headquartered in Herndon, Virginia.  Before I arrived, each business unit was managing their own pool of funds, deciding which shows and sponsorships  in which to participate/contribute and there was no overall structure as to the total sector spend. Decisions were  being made with no regard to sector priorities, large contract bids or future bid considerations. Additionally, there  was no alignment on any of the branding and marketing material, and more than once different business units  from the same sector were appearing at trade shows, without knowledge the other was participating. There was  an immediate need to align the funds under one umbrella and to develop a unified approach to spend, messaging  and participation at tradeshows and with sponsorships.

SELECTION

For this exercise, I opted to apply the design thinking tool of visualization to first uncover the issue at hand. To help  with our fight to align the budget under one umbrella (managed by me), I first needed to shine a light on just how  many unnecessary (from a business perspective) trade shows the business units were attending, how much in  sponsorship money was being dispersed, as well as the total sector spend in these areas. As we know, visualization  as a design tool (as per slide five in the week one slides) means to “make it tangible and concrete; to draw a  picture, tell a story, take a photo, make a map…” By pulling together historical data about these spends, compiling  it into one location, making it colored-coded and easy-to-read/filter, I was able to get senior leadership to  understand what I was trying to accomplish and persuade them into what I was trying to do for the organization as  a whole by taking the budget ownership and participation m

This written assignment is submitted by Ifeoma Kings on April 28th 2020

as part of the peer-review section of the Design Thinking For Innovation course offered by University of Virginia.

CROWDSOURCING A CHURCH FUNDRAISING ACTIVITY

1. Challenge:

I am leading the youth community at my church, and I proposed we hold a fundraising activity to raise funds to  support the education of a few students from the underprivileged society nearby. The proceeds were to go towards  helping the children with new uniforms, getting them school supplies (like a school bag, notebooks, textbooks,  stationery, etc) and paying their tuition fees.    The church members are used to donating money for church-associated charity organizations, reconstruction and  remodelling of the church, construction of new projects, tithe and several other avenues. They sometimes feel that  the youth does not have their priorities in the right place, and so, the adults are not likely to want to invest time and  money into a youth-led programme, regardless of the value it provides and to who.

2. Selection & Application:

Several design thinking tools like Visualization, Story Telling, Mind Mapping and Learning Launch came into play –  albeit in a mixed blend.    Surveys & Data Gathering  I spoke to the students I intended to help, to understand what it is they need the most and stands in the way of their  education. I spoke to the church leaders to understand who the major donors were and what kind of causes they  tended to contribute to. I interviewed several donors to understand what attracts them to want to donate to a cause,  and how that experience could be improved. I spoke to the school the children attended, to NGOs and to social  workers, to understand the school’s fee structure and how much it would cost to sponsor a child for a month. REFLECTION-MIND MAPPING

CHALLENGE AND SELECTION:

The tool used to solve my problem is mind mapping.mind mapping  always allows meaningful learning.the problem taken by me is the  unemployment among graduates in India.the main reason for the problem is  increase in number of graduates passing out every year.The problem is faced as  many of them are choosy job seekers and ther is also lack of skills and  experience and the quality of education.This also leads to economical problems  in India.I chose mind mapping as a tool as we can get a creative solutions  through it.All data information and can be easily communicated only in mind  mapping.It is looking for patterns and insights in large quantity of data through  exploration.

APPLICATION:

Challenge:

I’m Patrick, from Port Said, Egypt. I work with a charitable  foundation (Life Makers Foundation). Last year we had an annual  objective to empower 100 in need families with 100 micro  enterprises, to make them able to gain their own money rather  than keep getting money from people/donors.    To achieve this objective, our strategy was to raise money through  a one-month street/public fundraising campaign. The challenge  we’ve faced included both: 1) how to attract people to donate, 2)  where to locate our donations booths. In other words, as we had  some limited resources (volunteers, booths, budget, etc..), we  wanted to figure out how to raise money with the most effective  and efficient way.     Selection:

The selected tool is Learning Launch as we wanted to examine our  hypotheses in the real world and to get field data in which we can  rely on during our campaigns. Learning Launch is the tenth design  thinking tool, it allows us to make an affordable experiment to test  the impact of a new solution on the customers. The purpose of  Learning Launch is to get a truthful set of data and insights that  either confirm or disconfirm our assumptions, which lead to either  continue developing your idea or pivot/eliminate your idea.

text:
Pablo Romero Example Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge

My challenge was that I had to found this new society on creativity, leadership, innovation and design.

Therefore, I had to convince people in my college that it was a good idea and I would gain their

participation with this way. So, long story short, I had to influence people along the foundation of this

creative society. Among with that, there were other stakeholders such as society’s collaborative

companies and college management.

Selection

When it comes to affecting and influencing people under your organization, in my opinion, there is no

better choice then storytelling. I have a story to tell them about why the existing societies are not as

good as they should be, and there is no society that would excel students’ soft skills. If you want to

create, you need to create. You cannot just listen to people who create and then become a creator

yourself. This idea led to turn my thoughts to a story then to tell people. Some say storytelling have

four P’s: People, Place, Plot, and Purpose. Therefore, I chose storytelling to be able to show these

aspects.

Application

Before assembling people together for the board of this society, I have took them one by one and spoke

privately with each. Emotional branding is the key point in here for society and I have tried that. Each

individual was from different disciplines, because this society is a multidisciplinary one. Hence, I aimed

for their needs and how this society can have benefits for their faculty as well. Apart from that, our

collaborative companies had their needs as well. After all, it must be a win-win relationship and I told

our story according to that. I explained the benefits of cooperation with telling stories. People had to

chance to show empathy with this storytelling applications and were all eager to participate in it.

Insight

text:
Giuseppe Alberti – Design thinking for innovation

Challenge

I’m a professional photographer, based in Brazil, and weddings are my

main niche. Through this course I’ve learned some tools and methods, and now

I’m able to put in practice some ideas that lived in my mind for the last year.

As I talk to my clients, I hear some frequent problems that brides go

through, when planning their weddings – things that go from finding the right

professionals to the way that a ceremony must happen.

Selection/Application/Insight/Approach

Based on that, my idea was to develop a course, so that the brides can be

more prepared to the problems that appear during a wedding plan.

And here enters the design thinking: I’ve interviewed some brides, being

or not my clients, to have a deeper understand of the issues that they go and

gone by.

Focusing on the problems of them, I’ve learned about the core pain they

face, and confirmed my assumption, that the course will solve some serious

problems. I will now proceed and test ways to do. If it becomes necessary,

pivoting and looking for alternative paths to solve the problems I hear about so

often.

I’m already using the knowledge acquired in the course classes.

text:
USING MIND MAPPING TO UNCOVER CLIENT INSIGHTS

CHALLENGE The big challenge in my project is extracting the most signiﬁcant insights from the important quantity of information gathered from  quantitative research and qualitative consumer interviews. These insights will be used both to structure our offers to clients and prioritize mass  communication messaging in a new market.

SELECTION I chose to use mind mapping to help us develop a common understanding of the challenge and agree on the most signiﬁcant insights.

APPLICATION We invited 20 stakeholders in the project to a full-day session. In the ﬁrst part of the session, participants were invited to visit our  « gallery ». All the information, quotes, statistics, pictures from consumer homes, were put up on the walls. The room was covered in information  (picture 1).

Participants captured on post-it notes the information that felt most signiﬁcant to them as they wandered throughout the room.

We then divided participants in teams of 4 and asked them to share the information they had found signiﬁcant to ﬁnd overarching themes (picture  2). We asked them to look for patterns in the information they had collected but also to be mindful of anything that stood out as being particularly  different. Their overarching themes were noted and developed on large ﬂip charts (picture 3).

In the second part of the session, each team presented its themes to all the participants for discussion and comparison. We were then able to ﬁnd a  common understanding of the « So whats? » and start working together on the design conditions as the project moves forward.

Regina Parker — November 2016

INSIGHT Most participants in the Mind Mapping exercise never truly experience our destination as our clients do. Their visits are carefully orchestrated and mapped-out.  Mind Mapping was truly enlightening for them as an occasion to understand the client experience without the ﬁlter of a report or analysis.  Mind Mapping opened many  eyes.

Challenge

The hotel industry is a fundamental part of tourism in Mexico, and contributes millions of pesos to the national  economy; In addition, the average national salary of a hotel manager is MXN $ 71,616, so it is very important for  a hotel manager to have quality, guarantee, safety, good customer service, a pleasant atmosphere and, above all,  generate a good experience in clients at the time of their stay at the hotel, since this makes them stand out from  the competition and the promotion of a good experience makes the client return to the hotel and can be  recommended.

In this case, I will talk about the Riazor Hotel. A business hotel located less than 5 km. from the CDMX International  Airport, where you can not only stay and rest, but also hold work meetings, sessions or social events. For years  the Hotel Riazor has been a 4.5-star hotel, but in recent months, there have been multiple complaints where  guests claim that the environment is not pleasant because the attention and service provided by the workers is  not adequate, something that directly affects the experience given to guests, in addition to damaging the hotel's  image and decreasing the number of visitors.

Selection, application and approach

For this problem, what I would do is solve the main problem, which is the unpleasant environment due to the  poor attention and service given to the guest, for this I would begin by interviewing customers to find out their  complaints more accurately and accepting suggestions In order to improve our service, I would later brainstorm  the best way to fix the problems, then experiment with all the best ways to solve it using a design tool called  visualization. “Visualization is one of the essential design tools. TOOL:  Visualization

Diego Campo

Challenge & Selection

I work as a bodywork quality engineer at an automobile assembly company. The factory where I  work has a low percentage of automation and the welding processes are manual by operators.  Because of this there are many quality problems associated with poor welding application. We have  resorted to all kinds of strategies to find root causes, we have changed machines, installed aids in  the stalls and nothing worked. At that time, we realized that we were not really understanding the  needs of welders for them to apply welding well. They also did not understand the reasons why we  made so many changes in the factory, there was no effective communication. At that time, we  decided to use the visualization tool. As we saw in the first week of the course, this tool allows us to  activate different areas of the brain to understand information differently.

Application

To better understand the difficulties and problems of the operators, we decided to create  personalized meeting spaces. We formed groups of 4 workers together with 2 engineers from our  quality problem solving team. The first step in the meetings was to ensure that we all understood  the quality defects that we had in the same way, for this we used visual tools such as photos of the  defects, videos showing incorrectly applied welding beads and some cartoons that showed the basic  rules to follow. The second step in the meeting was the opposite situation, now the operators taught  us visually in the workplaces the difficulties they had in doing their job well, each worker went to  his post, carried out the operation and taught us his problems so that together we could find a  solution. text:
Example of Reflection - Value Chain Analysis – Jhonatan De Oliveira

Chalenge & Selection

I, as a business consultant, usually use “value chain analysis” to better understand the  routine of the organization I am studying, so I can identify what inputs are needed to  perform a given activity, what value is generated in that activity, and what the outputs  generated.

The reality of each organization is different, so it is important to carefully study each of  the realities and try to identify inputs to be able to improve the day of these companies  and consequently improve the impact on their customers.

Application

Recently I had the opportunity to apply Value Chain Analysis tool to a public health  organization in the city of Rio de Janeiro / Brazil. The main challenge was to understand  how the logistics process of the health supply chain works. In this way, the challenge  began with the purchase of medicines and ended with the delivery of these drugs in  specialized pharmacies.

During the study of the process it was possible to validate previously raised assumptions.  One of the biggest problems of the whole process was the delay and bureaucracy in the  purchasing process, more specifically in the bidding process. A bidding process could last  up to 360 days, which impacted directly on all pharmacies and consequently end users.

Challenge & Selection     Coming from an English Literature background putting things into a story seems second nature  to me. Storytelling is one of those things about humans that makes us drawn to one another and  feeds into our curiosity.   I work in a media agency with numerous diverse clients that all belong in different industries,  and i’m challenged constantly when tapping into the client’s mentality and making sure that our  creative content stays relevant to the brand’s guidelines and still maintains a creative standard.     Application    Working in an agency that has client fluidity has multiple creative challenges, you are faced with  numerous creative blocks having to steer from one client to another. However, applying the  storytelling tool clears away a lot of confusion in the sense that it narrows your creative thinking  into a smaller scale, not by limiting the possibilities, but by focusing on what makes every client  unique by centering on its key points.   For example, one of our clients is a tongue scraping product that wanted a campaign to raise  more awareness into the products’ sales. First thing I suggested was to know more about the  product itself and all of it’s characteristics, what makes it stand out? Why isn't it selling? Who is  it targeted to? Design Thinking for Innovation (Jan – Feb 2018)  Final Assignment - Learning Launch     Submitted by Jyoti Ward – 2 February 2018    1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

My company has in invested in Microsoft Office 365 – a suite of software services and apps to aid  collaboration, document access and productivity. Whilst adoption is gradually increasing, our staff  are not yet taking full advantage of these tools (and so not harnessing savings and benefits to the  company). Some people are relying on ways of creating and sharing documents that they have  become familiar with over many years, but which don’t have the benefits new functionality offers –  e.g. they will email a document to colleagues rather than collaborate online through the enterprise  social network, Yammer.

We want to foster a mindset and skills base across our workforce where the digital tools offered  by O365 are routinely used, providing demonstrable benefits to the way people work.

Using a ‘design thinking’ approach, we carried out some ‘skills insight interviews’ in November.  Assisted by a group of around 15 Office365 (O365) champions (individuals who have taken on a  role to support colleagues in the use of the Microsoft Office 365 suite) we sought to understand  what’s holding people back. We have used these insights to formulate hypotheses that we can  test. This covers the ‘What is?’ and ‘What if?’ steps described in the Design Thinking for  Innovation course.

The next step is to test some of the ideas we generated using experimentation. The ‘Learning  Launch’ tool provides the means to do this in a practical setting with real end-users. This will allow  us to test whether the action taken meets our requirements: namely to increase the skills and  capability of end users in using O365.

With the country  regarded as ever resilient, it is concurred to foster a national image of a strong nation and uplift  the disposition of each of its citizens. However, the resiliency of the Filipinos has also been  irrefutably contentious. Recent arguments claim that the people in power relations incline to  brush off adversities like that of the deadly pandemic and frightening calamities as something  commonly dealt with on a daily basis. The present-day society outwardly overemphasizes and  overplays Filipinos’ resilient trait. The very same resiliency is the one conjuring up the dismissal  of risks in an advent of another insignificant event. text:
Wilma Dekker – Design Thinking for Business Innovation    February 5 2017

Reflection – Visualisation      Challenge  In my work as a leadership consultant, my team and I help companies that need change but don’t know  how to lead it; the journey into the unknown. I work for clients and their high-educated young professionals  in the professional services sector; i.e. consultants, lawyers, accountants, sales professionals and  marketeers. They are often not used to be asked what could be the ‘what if situation’, they are more likely to  be conditioned to know the ‘right’ answer.     Selection  I was working for a client, a big consultancy agency and I coached a young woman; let’s call her Alice. She  and the rest of her peers got the order from management to set goals for the year and the goals had to  contribute to a more business development focused office. I was asked to help each of them. Alice had a  hard time in knowing how she wanted to grow in the coming year, develop goals accordingly, and make  them business aligned. I choose to help her with using the Visualisation tool (module 1 video 6). I first  helped her set the ‘what is situation’ and than help her through the ‘What if situation”. Finding your own  person in goals to set is very important for intrinsic motivation reasons; people that set goals that align with  them personal are more likely to succeed.

Alice  Alice is around 28 years old, pretty, a smart woman and we sat down in the conference room for  her first meeting with me, she got me some water and we got started. She asked if this  conversation was confidential and I told her yes. Than she talked for 20 straight minutes about  what she didn’t wanted this year, what she hated about her job, it felt like she really needed this to  get of her chest. She told me that she was tired. We really established the ‘What is situation’ at that  point. Getting into the ‘What if situation’ was harder for her. That’s where I used the visualisation.

Peer-graded Assignment: Reflection – Visualization    Challenge and selection.    One of the tools I have used in problem solving/idea generation is the tool of visualization or visual  thinking, to understand a research problem and areas to work on before attempting to come up with  different solutions to the problem. In order to design the solution, first we must build a good  understanding of the problem that we are trying to solve. Visualization tool helps to build connections  between different findings and understand the bigger picture. I have used the technique of using a  research wall to display all the relevant research outputs, in one place. The visual aspect of the wall  triggers idea generation and enables project members to better understand research insights.    Application    I start the process by creating a graphic of the problem domain. To develop the graphic, I will draw from  any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be existing  research data, manufacturing methods, market data and/or customer feedback.     For the activity, I will divide the researchers into groups of 2-3 participants each specialized in a different  area of study, such as chemistry, engineering and biology. Each group receives a copy of the graphic of  the problem domain that they can write on directly. They will get following questions to answer,

1. What are the customer pains and weaknesses of the existing problem?  2. What are the improvements you would make to eliminate existing pains and weaknesses?

Each group gets 30 minutes to discuss and answer the questions on the graphic. Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge

My name is Alberto and I’m a middle manager (one of many directors) of a Technology practice in a large  consulting company. I play the role of a project manager (or sometimes team lead) in the  implementation of complex corporate IT-systems, such as an ERP system or a corporate Data  Warehouse / Business Intelligence system. My clients are big companies, usually leaders on local  market. They work in different industries – oil & gas, metals & mining, coal production, power  generation and distribution, agriculture and so on, – but often have typical / similar problems and  requirements, so my experience is relevant to many of them.

I’m basically a technical (IT) specialist, dedicated to ‘delivery’ – system design and implementation. Sales  and marketing are not my favorite skills. But over the past three years I have been responsible for  developing an interesting complex functionality (Commodity Trading application) for a large coal  producer, and it makes sense to bring this accumulated experience to the market (to the C-level  management in the relevant companies).

Selection

Storytelling looks like the right technique for promotion of our skills and experience in CTRM  (Commodity Trade and Risk Management). My project team, together with the client, has come a long  way, made some mistakes (not fatal), learned many lessons and finally achieved good results, so I can  tell some interesting stories based on it.

Application

I have prepared two types of presentations about our project and CTRM experience:

•  Long story with a description of our client, business objectives, project approach, technical  architecture and many details and examples. It was addressed to a rather narrow audience – for  example, the participants of the metals & mining conference.

text: Example Reflection - Storytelling - Jose Brown    Challenge & Selection  Storytelling can be a great communication tool to utilize. You can be  presented with a project or task and drill down to the actions items but if you  know the “why” behind the actions it can make all the difference in a  successful project.     I am in the healthcare industry and I work with IT on various projects and  enhancements. A recent project request from our OBGYN team to reduce  delays in getting critical report results for high risk pregnancies back to the  physician so they could take needed action. The current manual process  included faxing results and many times took hours or even a day before the  physician would see those results. This could add to an already risky situation.     This project seemed straightforward and the benefits obvious to everyone on  the team. But twelve months into the project and we could not get a  successful test completed. Many factors contributed to the stalemate. We did  not have a test environment to utilize and we had to use the production  environment to test. We experienced turnover in key roles, COVID 19 delays,  restricted physician availability and several other factors that added to the  delay.       Application  I opted to create a process flow to assist with testing so we could visualize  who was responsible for a specific task. We scheduled a meeting and opened  with a specific patient story that illustrated the risks these delayed reports can  result in without the change. Others on the call opened up about examples  they have experienced. We discussed the length of time this request has been  in process (many months now) and opened up the forum for ideas on how  best to tackle these delays. Many heads with valuable expertise are better  than my head and my limited experience with this report system. I also expect the team to define the problem  and solve it in a visual way. we want to create a set of  questions and answers for our problem. The team must  construct the responses as simply as possible. because it is  really a key part of the way we communicate, whether we  are aware of it or not. It allows us to think non-verbally. I  also know that the most important thing is to visualize the  idea first, because then you will be able to test the prototype  in the wild. Each of the subsequent prototypes should be  built with the user in mind and answer a specific question.

text: Bruno Milani    Challenge – How might we cultivate creativity in the workplace?    I chose the challenge of increasing employee engagement in the Federal Government by cultivating  cultures and leaders who inspire and unleash everyone’s creativity.  Studies show that only 65% of  Government employees are engaged at work.  It’s lower in the private sector.  But, as managers, we should  ask whether we are contributing to their disengagement.  Are we allowing them to share their ideas? To  discover their talents?  Are we bringing them along on the journey?  To meet this challenge, I reached out  to a group of leaders in the Government in charge of training and talent development and management.   This like-minded group faces this challenge too, but may not see it in the same way.     Selection - Storytelling    To reach my audience, I turned to storytelling. I find that telling stories is a powerful way to connect with  others and persuade them to listen to my ideas.  We all grew up hearing stories.  Of far away lands.   Princesses and dragons.  Magical spells.  These stories fueled our imaginations and captured our attention.   But what exactly is storytelling, especially in the design thinking context?  As we learned in Week 2,  storytelling is a design tool we can use to put human beings and their experience front and center.   Storytelling is not only educational and compelling, it is informative and inspiring.  The stories we tell can  raise questions and offer our audience opportunities to contemplate the status quo and how we might  redesign it.     To address my challenge of driving more innovation in the Federal Government by creating cultures that  support everyone’s creativity in the workplace, I told the story of the current environment. -  Rashid Kt

Challenge    I am a member of a company with a product range from cosmetics, soaps, detergents, soda ash  and so on. The company has positioned itself as a niche in the low-end detergent and soap  market. However, now the challenge is to retain upper middle-class consumers who will  occupy the high-end market eventually. The project is to launch new products for the high-end  market.     Selection     I have already considered various design thinking tools like visualisation, brainstorming, mind- mapping and their pros and cons. There are lots of ways but the most appropriate one for this  challenge is Learning launch. Briefly speaking, the tool of leaning launch revolves around the  fact that a business plan may not be the immediate reaction to any idea. In reference to the  video lecture by Michael Ebert, business plan is a traditional approach where we tend to assume  financials projections like returns based on our judgement. But in the end, they’re just guesses.  And we end up tweaking them until we hit the rate. Instead, going for an experiment and testing  a hypothesis is an assertion.     Application    The experiments done were fast and cheap. I made a hypothesis: Launching new products for  the high-end market will help to retain the upper middle-class consumers. A group of persons  in form of the upper middle-class had this specific problem in form of a need for products that  solve their high-end needs.   The learning launch of the new product we did surveys to find out these needs by quickly  engaging with the customers and testing our assumptions. We advanced in the challenge under the  design thinking approach, empathizing with the interests and needs of  Doctors and Sales Reps, looking for a value proposition that fits in  this service. In my company, a large bank, we encountered the problem that a large part of our  customers didn’t want to login online to use our banking tools.   Instead they went to our brick local branches, in far larger numbers than our competitors.  That was a big problem, because the costs of the physical banking activities at the local  branch are far greater than the costs of online banking activities, thus creating a large  competitive disadvantage.    In the past there had been efforts to optimize the login process. In the end this resulted in a  better technical login, but not an improvement in numbers of new customers that login. Our  challenge was described as: “improve the login process so customers who now go to the  local branch, use our online banking tools instead”.    Selection   How could we stay away from the trap of only marginally improving the login? We decided  to use Visualization. This would help us to get to the core problem and come up with more  creative ideas. We could then combine the insights and really leap forward.     Another major reason to use Visualization was to get all team members aligned: we wanted  to prevent that in an early stage ideas where shot down because they were deemed  technically too challenging. Visualization helps to create a shared starting point for idea  generation, and enforces the notion that we all are going to work together to create the best  possible solution.    Application  We used Visualization in two ways: in presenting the information that we gathered as a  starting point and to visualize possible solutions.    In gathering information, we asked team members for inspirational examples they knew of  login processes. We printed these examples and pinned them on the walls. Reflection:  Visualization

Submitted by:  Ori Abrego

Challenge

Working in the chemicals market segment, I have seen many changes and advancements in products  and processes over the years.  During that time however, the culture and norms had remained relatively  static – until recently.  The industry is now changing, driven by a shift in the generational balance as  Baby Boomers and Gen X starts to give way to Millennials and Gen Z.  This shift is creating the challenge  for our company to shed traditional communication methods (emails, posting memos on bulletin  boards, etc…) in conjunction with fully embracing technology, and find new and better ways to  communicate and pass on information; ways that will be embraced by the new and future workforce.

Selection

One of the strategies selected to accomplish this was to use Visualization.  This was chosen for a couple  of reasons.  First, visualization is a stark departure from conventional communication methods, which  have always been very formal and text-based.  Secondly, the use of pictures, info-graphs, and video in  on internet based apps and platforms as the replacement for conventional methods is in-line with the  expectations of the generational shift and the new work cultures being created.  Finally, visualization  was chosen out of being opportunistic as our company was converting from Outlook to the Google Kite  platform.

Application

Google Kite has many non-email based features that could be an option to put through the processes of  “what if?” and “what wows?”  To facilitate a new and more effective method of communicating  amongst our business team, we settled on using Google Communities as the “what works” in this  project. Paula Collins

1. Change and selection

Storytelling enables me to develop a deeper connection with the audience. I work with teachers  and I prepare  them in their permanente teacher’s training. I consider that storytelling is a  fundamental human experience that unites people and drives stronger, deeper connections. I  spend my time finding ways to inspire teachers. Sometimes they don’t want to participate in  courses because they have a lot things to do and they don´t earn enough money to participate  in courses but I use this strategy to motivate them to study as an inversion. I share stories of my  life in order to help them visualize how we can get success and get more incomes. I through my  story they connect and I can realize what are their needs for training. With this information I can  design courses according to their learning needs.

2. Application

I have a story about using storytelling. When I have to motivate teachers to participate in  teacher’s training courses I tell my story. I was a professor for 15 years at a university. I was a  teacher very recognized by my students. But one day I decided to study for a master's and  doctorate. There I met very successful professionals who presented their experience and work  throughout the country and the world. I lived in a small town and had never traveled to teach  at other institutions. One day, a friend invited me to give a conference with teachers. She invited  me to give a topic for an hour to 500 teachers and although I had never done it when I finished,  everyone applauded and the director of an institution of the capital of the country spoke to me  to prepare directors and teachers in the capital of the country.

In that moment, I realized the great impact that my presentation had caused. I went back to my  university and started looking for specialized courses in my profession..

text:
Peer-graded Assignment: Reflection

For this activity choose Storytelling (Module 2) Mind maps (module 3) in order to successfully

carry out a very important networking project in the construction of the Accenture headquarters

building in Buenos Aires, the challenge was to change the mentality of the team of technicians

who were unmotivated and did not work as a solid team I was very thoughtful because the

project had to be delivered on time but the obstacle was the technical team, there were no

other barriers, neither economic nor infrastructure, materials and equipment, we had

everything, but the lack of motivation and lack of companionship was overwhelming putting the

project at risk.

My idea was to hold daily meetings of 15 minutes applying agile methodology with the

technicians and we chatted about the performance of the work, but also about soccer and

tactical stories and thoughts of famous coaches, for example Pep Guardiola among others, this

decompresses the work environment and everyone They are passionate about soccer, these

tactical stories and epic matches motivated them and changed their mood, the performance

was increasing and thus they themselves were able to create their mental maps and contribute

ideas to the meetings.

In summary applying Storytelling (Module 2)

Mind maps (module 3) I was able to achieve a collective mentality change in the team of

technicians, solve a problem creatively in the Design Thinking style and as a result close the

project in a timely manner.

Jimena

Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

I am a cofounder at https://jones.com/tags/wp-contentpost.html , a agtech Startup specializing in setting up  and operating farms and also consulting other farms to be efficient.   Hydroponics is a practice of growing greens and veggies on a water and is one of the  solutions to feed more with lower resources and carbon footprint.   In one of our projects, we were called up to solve a failed crop cycle in one of the farms  in India. The farm had been commissioned on schedule and all plants failed to grow after a  40 day cycle leading to a wipeout of all produce. We went in to rescue the farm.

Selection  In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you  selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

We selected Mind Mapping as the tool of choice.   The hydroponics is an evolving technique and lots of unknowns in the field. It was very  important to leverage the combined ideas from all and brainstorm to solve the problem and  identify the cause of the error.

Application:  Describe how you applied the tool you selected to your challenge (e.g., what you did

and how the tool was applied effectively or ineffectively).

Without prejudice, we all sat in a circle time every day  twice to speak the mind. text:
Reflection - Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a very helpful tool to creatively relay what we want to say. In a job where the processes and  policies are complicated to understand, I have been often told that the easiest way to make our audience  understand is to tell a story, incorporating what is needed to be discussed by relating it to factual  experiences. We use storytelling to help our them visualize, for us to gain a more authentic feedback  about what they understand and on what else we can improve. Then we try and use this information to  improve and develop our strategies.

Application

I have tried applying storytelling when we entered a competition about process improvement. We were  discussing our suggested process changes to a panel that consists of unibankers. However, our mindset  was to explain the process in the simplest way possible so that anyone, especially our clients who are not  knowledgeable of the in-depth operations of the bank can easily understand it. So, we started with true- to-life experiences of our clients and slowly built a connection to convey the importance of our proposal.

Insight and Approach

By using the storytelling tool, we were able to successfully explain the need for our proposal and shed  some light to what our clients are actually struggling about. Our team were able to establish the proper  connection and it worked really well, it was easily understood and the benefits were recognized.

Sometimes we think that storytelling may not have that big of an impact, but if we try and listen to the  stories of the people around us, we would know how all of the events in our lives are interconnected and,  in a way, we could get insights on how to better ourselves, and our work. We could use this tool as a  means to think of breakthroughs that can help others.

Football Academy Challenge

Julian Ramirez

Background and Challenge

I work in a foundation in Chile which plans and develop football programs for children

between 7 and 15 years old. The foundation started very local in a vulnerable neighborhood

with just a couple of kids. As the neighbors started hearing about it the academy grew more

and more every year. For many families, football is an important part of their life and for

some even a way out of poverty. This year we wanted to expand to the neighborhood next

door, and we carried out many surveys and went knocking door to door to collect helpful

data about the people who lived around the football field so we could plan the insertion into

this new market satisfying the community necessities. The challenge was to properly

understand and analyze all the data collected to get useful insight about the costumer’s

behavior and preferences related to the football programs.

Selection of a Design Thinking Tool

Taking advantage of the tools learned in this course, I proposed we use the Mind Mapping

Tool as Patricia Rodriguez said this “is looking for patterns and insights in the large

quantity of data you’ve collected during your exploration of What Is”. We needed to better

understand the consumer and come up with the perfect program to maximize the social

benefit and I believed that carrying out a Mind Mapping exercise could be extremely helpful

to achieve our goals.

Application of the Tool

Using the step by step presented in the Design for Growth book by Gaby Martinez and James Allen we develop a Mind Mapping activity which consisted in the following:

1. Creation of 5 different possible football programs, including days of the week, hours

of the day, activities, games, number of coaches, number of students, orientation of

the project and type of accessories and equipment, using the data the community gave

us.
