text:
Overcoming the Known Unknowns by Applying “Learning Launch”                                    May 30, 2020

Yogi Yates

Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

The company I consult with has been trying to move toward the Agile methodology for project management,  initially through the software engineering group and slowly expanding to other parts of the business. The  main challenge that I encountered as a change management consultant is that, where software developers  have used Agile for most of their career, most of the engineering disciplines favor the waterfall approach. As  a result, project teams struggle with the notion of iterations and sprints when they are used to having the  entire project plan in place before starting. In order to adapt the change management planning approach, I  first had to get the project teams comfortable with the Agile methodology.

Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you  selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

In my initial assessment of the problem, I identified two key issues: first, familiarity with Agile was not  consistent or uniform across the project teams, and in an engineering organization, that level of ambiguity  and open-ended planning creates more than a little bit of angst. Second, the adopted methodology for  change management across the corporation is heavily anchored in waterfall processes, and is, all by itself,  very rigid and bureaucratic. To bridge the knowledge gap and begin moving in the direction of a more Agile  approach, I selected the Learning Launch tool as a way to test some assumptions and possible approaches  without creating unwarranted disruption with the ongoing project efforts.

text:
Luis Hernandez

STORYTELLING

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is an excellent tool that design thinking gives us. It helps us a lot  because the process of empathizing is the most important thing in design thinking  and through a story we can make our audience feel included, understood and even  make them smile. I select this tool because personally it is my favorite since I love  the way the stories are told, I find it fun for the public and also because it is  something so well elaborated you can reach many places with it. The fact of  studying, analyzing and developing a story for the promotion of our product is  something fun and often moving. I share stories that have marked both me and my  family in order to generate a special bond with our customers, and I also use this  link to improve because thanks to your comments I can improve either my product  or the way I share it with the public.

Application

To carry out the storytelling I can think of a story in which people feel included,  for example, a household product. The story begins by revealing a person who has  a boring routine and who does not enjoy being at home, nothing interesting  happens in his life but one day he finds a bird that follows him to his home, he is  bored lying down when Suddenly he realizes that the bird poops on his table on the  terrace, he is forced to clean but then he realizes that he had not been on his terrace  for months, without enjoying it and with that the idea comes to him of having a  party in it, and when you have everything ready, you realize that you need a grill  and that is where the solution occurs: a semi-professional grill at a good price and  easy to order. It is a story that occurs to me a bit quickly, I could refine some  details, but this is the way that storytelling is carried out, with this I can go to a  company that is in charge of selling this type of product and tell them how we can  promote their products.

Learning Launch

By: Abbas Hernandez

Challenge:    Problem:

• At company X we have an ongoing issue with employees complaining that their ideas

are not being heard. This is due to a lack of transparency with ideas that are submitted.  The current process includes submitting an idea via an online form and receiving an  email confirmation that it has been received. Another issue is the backlog of ideas  received cannot be processed by Management. This has led to decreased morale within  the organization.

Project Scope:

• I am the project manager for the Change Management department implementing a

transparent ideation tool that will allow management to quickly evaluate ideas based on  the following scope:

o Goal: Implement a new ideation tool to provide transparency and boost morale.  o Audience: 4000 employees from various departments within the organization.  o Budget: $300,000  o Completion: 3 months  o Resources: internal and external  o Departments: Communications, IT, Legal, Compliance, Human Resources, and

Change Management.

Selection:    The team conducted 40 interviews across the organization that included every department.  From the interviews personas of the entire employee base was established. Using those  personas, the team felt the learning launch tool would have the most impact. It would provide  transparency and boost morale even if the ideation tool was a failure, at least the employees  would see that the company is trying to fix the issue quickly.    Application:    Our learning launch was the pilot implementation of a 3rd party crowdsourced ideation cloud  based SaaS platform called Faucet.   Faucet had several benefits that made them the obvious choice.

• Deep understanding of our industry.  • Cloud based platform. This made implementation very fast. 3 months exactly.  • SaaS (software as a service) platform allowed us to keep costs at a minimum. $250,000

Design Thinking for Innovation  June 12, 2020  Elizabeth Pedraza          Challenge    Our consulting team worked with a Planning and Scheduling Division of a family-owned pasta  company with inventory problems resulting in lost revenue. The company had times when they  had either too much inventory (food was going bad - obsolesence) or too little inventory (back- orders or shortages), both situations resulting in unhappy customer relationships and lost  profits. Our team was brought in to understand and find solutions to the company’s inventory  problems.    Selection      The team decided that a time-series visual view of the historical actions taken by the relevant  parties would illuminate opportunities for improving inventory-related decision-making.  Seeing  what happened, people could then discuss what happened and why.  This should lead to ideas  for process improvements to solve the shortage and oversupply issues.  We believed that doing  this would help reduce waste, increase margins, increase revenues and please customers.    What the team chose, after careful consideration, was the business intelligence visualization  tool Microsoft Power BI. Power BI allows the creation of interactive graphs, which a user can,  without any skill or training, manipulate or filter to show multiple scenarios or views of the  underlying data.  This was a simple, visual way for everyone to gain insight into the problems  and thereby trigger useful conversations leading to collaborative solutions.

Application   In addition to quantitative data gathering (and cleansing), particularly sales order, production,  shipment, and inventory status data, the team spent many hours interviewing officers and line  people. text:
Miguel Herrera

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge    I work for the Loss Prevention Department at the largest oil company in the world located in Saudi  Arabia. I have worked as a safety and health professional for my entire 20-year career. As a senior expat  employee, I am recruited to take on special projects and mentor younger staff. Recently, I was charged  with creating the Loss Prevention Brand and enhancing my department’s image throughout the  Company, which is essentially throughout the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. The challenge is to transition  from an approach of strict compliance to a customer service approach where our staff are looked to as  partners instead of police officers.    Selection    Several years ago, I took a short Lateral Thinking Course and decided to use the skills from that course to  conduct a lateral thinking workshop with a group of 20 employees who represented both genders,  different experience levels and different nationalities. The intent of the workshop was to generate ideas  we could put into action to improve our image. Before the workshop, I took a refresher Lateral Thinking  Course through Udemy.    Application    Since the workshop took place during the COVID-19 Pandemic, it has to be conducted through Skype.  Ideally, this workshop should be conducted live with flip charts all over the room; however, after a year  of everyone being forced to learn how to use Skype, the execution of the workshop went very well. I  provide a background on the lateral thinking concept to warm up the group and then I facilitated four  group exercises. One Skype meeting was established for all participants. In addition, four additional  Skype meetings were set up for the 20 employees who were divided into four groups. After each  exercise, everyone came back into the main Skype meeting to debrief. The four exercises were; 1) Check  Your Assumptions, 2) What If the Opposite were True, 3) Break the Rules and 4) Ask Questions.    Approximately

Challenge & Selection

As a curriculum designer assigned projects to create training materials and programs for call centers for a large  corporation, sometimes our training requests are very vague. It is up to the designer to work with the client to  determine the actual needs and goals of the client. In order to create an effective training program, the materials have  to improve or meet the client metrics or goals. If those goals and needs are not determined at the beginning of the  project, the training is a waste of time for the participants and a waste of money for the client.

A  visualization method I use frequently with clients is a method created by Cathy Moore called Action Mapping. “Action  mapping is a streamlined process to design training in the business world. Its goal is to help designers:

  Commit to measurably improving the performance of the business

  Identify the best solution to the performance problem

  When training is necessary, create challenging simulations, not information presentations”

To implement the method, I set up a conference call with the client and set expectations to discuss the client training  needs and. The client is to bring examples of why the training is needed along with the expected outcome of the  training. For example, which metric or goal should the training achieve? text:
Alejandra Padilla

Final Project: The family trip

Challenge and selection

The tool that I will use for this project is the mind mapping because I consider

that it is one of the most important alternatives, since it allows us to look for

patterns and perspectives to problems solution, and we can explore our creativity

with this. I like the mind maps because I use them for my schoolwork and is very

easy to use them. I think is the best way to synthesize information clearly. The

mind map it is a creative, intuitive, visual, and attractive way of presenting

information that is confusing.

The challenge that I chose to apply this tool is about choosing a destination to go

on a trip with the family, we want to be 7 days in the city, we are looking for a

city that has many things to do and know, like museums, restaurants, parks,

monuments, and others. We do not have a specific place, we just want to know

some place in Europe, and we can travel any season of the year.

Application

We must first clarify our ideas. The first step is to choose 5 alternatives of

countries or cities to which we want to go, then select 2 options that interest us

the most. The next step is making a mind map of each option. In each map we

will include basic things, starting with the places we can visit in that city, what

activities are there to do like: museums, restaurants, parks, and others; what is

the best season to travel, prices of flights, hotels. We are going to complement

the map with the information we find, trying to be brief. Once the maps are

ready, we will make a comparison with the information and choose the option

that best suits us.

List of 5 cities:

1. Madrid, Spain.

2. Paris, France.

3. Rome, Italy

text:
Jose Jackson – Design Thinking for Innovation

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

My challenge that I have selected is setting up my own company! After many years of being a CEO of an  Economic Development organization I have decided that I will open my own company.

Selection

I have selected the Visualization tool, to achieve an understanding of the opportunity and problems for  myself as well as a reference group to identify and define viable solutions to the opportunity. I also have  selected this so I can use a diagram to visually see all the components in the process of defining the  scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain  points and opportunities.

Application

I used this approach with myself first to start the process by creating a straw man graphic (like a mind  map) to do a brain dump of all the components of the opportunity. To develop the straw man graphic, I  will draw from any existing material and experiences that I may have available to understand the  environment.

There is supporting material to assist in this process such as Jack Canfield ‘visualization techniques to  manifest your desired outcomes’ to assist in the process. The template I often start with also has a  column on the left to identify Partners and Collaborators and a column on the right to identify Threats  such as competitors, Industrial relations constraints etc. After I complete this I will then undertake the  same type of process with my reference group.

After the group looks over the whole idea I will then look to break up the group to work on the  independent idea ‘clusters’ that have developed for a deeper dive into the areas that have been  articulated. I will ask each group to use questions such as 1) What key elements are missing? And, 2)  What would you change? Then I have each group report out on their answers and explain why for the  rest of the group to understand the logic. This feedback and different

Storytelling solutions for stories that need telling

By Joe Hernandez

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge.

We define storytelling as the art of telling stories. Therefore, the first thing we must do is agree on what a story is.  A general definition may be a succession of events ordered in time, but, a very important element is missing… our  emotions. It is our emotions that create bonds between people. Our emotions link us with one another and create  relationships. Relationships will then allow us to sell our services. It does not matter whether you are a small  entrepreneur or a large company. If you do not know how to generate positive emotions in your potential clients,  you will not sell. And good stories can generate very positive emotions. It is important to remember that without  emotion, there is no story. My challenge is to be able to promote the island’s (in which I reside) project to convert  it into a SMART island , in order to reduce the damage that has already been done, and to improve the quality of  life of all of those that enjoy this beautiful island.

2.Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected

I chose the Storytelling tool. There are many ways of storytelling, especially when wanting to captivate a certain  audience.     I chose the “who are we?” type of story. This type of story is used to introduce ourselves, to have the public get to  know us and our mission. It is our own, personal story and, as in any good story, there must be a conflict. In other  words, a challenge that we have had to face and from which we have emerged. Becoming a more reinforced  company, which has helped us grow. People like to see that the speaker also has problems like them and can  overcome them, because that creates inspiration and help.

text:
Innovation on Cafe

In our local area, I found a café which was recently modified. Before that, the  business was not that high, but the business has increased rapidly. The  modification means the Structure of the café, Tables, and the atmosphere of the  café by setting new things. With the increase in the techniques and the varieties  of coffee around the world, it is time to evolve to other processes and Methods.  The café has introduced new offers for the customers and taking the feedback to  increase the availability of the products and new concepts. The chance of  innovating new techniques is multiplying, and we, the users, can modify the  needs how we want and make use of new things. To create new things, we have  to think in a new way and allow ourselves to think differently. We can choose the  varieties that people like and should know what things people are interested in  and modify what we don’t know. So we should select accurate tools and select  new businesses. Designers come up with their thoughts and ideas and help to  generate new ideas and grow the business. A growing company has many tasks as  compared to existing companies. They should increase the market of the business  and expand the business. They have also given reasonable offers for the  customers and made things happen. We should improve the tools and give more  time to increase the business.

By Sharan Chauhan

Date: 22/09/2020

Name: Farjana Iqbal

Challenge and selection

Storytelling is a spectacular tool to reach out to people's minds and feelings. It's a great technique

that I use with our clients. I work with individuals who have Alzheimer's disease, who need support

and intense care. I spend much time inspiring and focusing on their feelings rather than using

words. I struggled a lot to understand their desires and emotions, so I devoted a specific day in the

week to communicate with each other and to share each story they have, even if it's from their

imagination. They always have a different story to tell. I use the information I gained from these

sessions to ascertain their goals and interests and figure out different plans and strategies to know

what they lack and need to overcome

Application

The real story behind using storytelling started when I was in a campaign to support orphans. I

tried to explain the importance of hearing people express their feelings and addressing their

individual needs. I found out that the organizing company failed to contribute to the children and

did not know what each child desired. Although it seems hard to ask each child what they want,

it's an excellent opportunity to create a better environment for them. I started posing a situation

that confronted me when I was at school. I remember an orphan girl who had always been bullied

and scorned in class. She used to set outside class to cry every day. I could tell she needed

immediate help. When I encouraged her to challenge her fears and not be ashamed to say to the

teacher. She started realizing my words and noticing it might make a difference. All she needed

was support and love! I started telling her my story when I was bullied in the school bus, I was

beaten and insulted every time, but I confronted my fears and told other people who helped me

text:
ENSURING UNIFORM FRUIT QUALITY

By: Lalisa Cruz

Challenge

In my last employment, I worked in a start-up food manufacturer in Metro Manila.  I was the sole R&D  personnel in that company, and part of my job was sourcing suppliers of fresh fruits.  Having no prior  experience with procuring fruits, it was a huge challenge for me to find a good, reputable supplier to  transact business with.  As soon as I was able to find a few good ones, the bigger challenge for me was to  ensure that the quality of the fruits is uniform among the suppliers I found.

Selection

I selected the storytelling tool for this particular challenge because I believe that it is the best tool in  obtaining the relevant information I seek.  Since the challenge was for me to ensure that the quality of  fruits is uniform among the suppliers, I had to know the postharvest processes that each of the suppliers  employ.

Application

I talked to the suppliers individually.  In a casual manner, I was able to obtain non-proprietary information  from them through the storytelling tool.  They shared with me their postharvest processes and from there,  I found what specific processes produced the best quality fruits.  As such, I was able to determine the  particular supplier to use as benchmark.  With the supplier’s express consent, our company adopted these  practices as subsequent process steps for those lower quality fruits coming from other suppliers in order  that all the fruits have uniform quality.

Insight

This tool effectively improved the uniformity of the quality of fruits.  From the experience of using this  tool, I was able to gain the following insights: (1) storytelling is as effective as objective approaches; (2)  storytelling gives us relevant baseline information which we can work our improvements from; and (3)  design thinking, in general, utilizes the lean six sigma approach.

text:
Using Mind Mapping to Study the Issue Related with Online Education

[Amira Ali]

Challenge

The challenge I have chosen is to study how the college experience can be optimized in the

post COVID-19 world of online learning. With the global pandemic, most colleges have

switched to an online mode of learning. This means that many students now attend classes

from their bedrooms. I want to look at this from the collegiate level as I am a recent graduate

who completed her undergraduate course through online mediums. The college experience is

not merely an educational/learning one, the socialization functions also assumes importance.

Something I have noticed, for example, is that a lot of talk about what people miss about their

college is the ancillary programs, or even just the ability to speak to their friends between

classes. By choosing to look at this challenge, I want to gain insight into all the different

kinds of issues that come up with the switch to online learning.

Selection

The design thinking tool I have selected to implement is the mind mapping tool. I have

chosen the tool as I am still in the „what is‟ stage of the challenge. I am still identifying the

problems, and trying to establish patterns and linkages among them. According to the „Mind

Mapping Tool‟ video with Amira Moore- “Mind Mapping is looking for patterns and

insights in a large quantity of data you collected during your exploration of what is the

current reality. The goal is to establish criteria for the „what if‟ idea generation phase.” I will

be creating a personal mind map, of my own thoughts and reflections on the subject, as I am

attempting this challenge for personal insight.

Application

Submitted on: 17th April 2020  Submitted by:  Om Ahmed Teto

Challenge

I am a staff member in Strategy team at Sanella which is one of the leading federal higher  educational institutions in the United Arab Emirates. It is noticed that the KPI argued of %Graduates Employment in 12 months where Sanella keeps  scoring poorly and low (less than 30%) despite all the efforts/plans made is reflecting negatively on the  image of the federal institution and damages the reputation of its graduates at the local jobs market.   Hence; it has been decided to uncover the reasons and discover elements behind slow achievement and  low rates of graduates’ employment by considering some elements via conducting the tool of storytelling. The design thinking tool chosen of DT box is “Storytelling” simply because it puts human experience front  and center knowing that we’re dealing with graduates in this example. Pong Ng – Reflection – Visualization

Challenge    I am a Product Manager in the digital space. My current project is to implement a complete  redesign of a government agency’s website. The goal is to drive up interest and therefore  increase the number of quality candidates applying to work at this agency. My team tackles  design challenges using a human-centered approach. We started our project off with a  Discovery period where we employed ethnographic research and affinity mapping to draw out  users’ deepest pain points and effectively synthesize those findings.     The challenge was figuring out a way to quickly translate those insights into designs, to validate  those designs with users, to update those designs, and to revalidate before pushing to  Engineers. We wanted to get the designs right as to avoid the additional cost of excessive  rework down the road.    Selection    I felt the best way to handle this challenge was with rapid prototyping using the Visualization  tool. Visualization is the act of translating thoughts into a visual format so it can be easily  shared and discussed among teammates and users. As opposed to written notes or just verbal  explanations, Visualization enables people provide an easier and more effective way of  communicating information. It provides context and helps jog peoples’ creative juices.    I selected Visualization based off Angela Myer’s discussion in Week 1. I learned that helping  folks visualize something may improve the chances of achieving a sense of agreement and  consensus. Visualization would help draw out conversation and solicit feedback in a way that a  verbal overview would not. In the end, it was the best tool to help align our designs to users’  mental models. text:
WHY PEOPLE ARE NOT COMMITTED TO RECYCLING IN LIMA (PERU)?

by Miguel Caceres

Challenge

I am a member of a start-up focused on solving the challenge of recycling in Lima (Peru), with the

aim of achieving greater awareness in the citizens about the importance of recycling. We found

that in Peru more than 18 tons of garbage are generated daily, half of which is generated only in

Lima (capital of my country) and 2.4% is only recycled1. The reason: The lack of culture by the

recycling of the Peruvian. Therefore the scope of this project is to understand this situation.

Selection

The tool I used was visualization, for have a broader, deeper and clearer understanding of the

problem, so we share the problem with citizens in Lima.  To do so, I selected some techniques as

ethnographic interviews, “5 Why´s” 2  and Empathy Map with a set of questions or guidelines to

know stories and discuss about the problem of the recycling culture, with the objective to delimit

the scope of the project and key elements to discover opportunities, and then, define possible

solutions and prototypes.

Application

I started the process with ethnographic interviews (25 citizens), I prepared a set of questions that

included from general overview, like as: “Could you show me/tell me how you usually throw the

garbage?”, “What like/dislike from this process?” with the aim of discussing patterns of events. I

used too, the technique ´5 Why’s´ for seeking the evocation of stories, in order to explore in depth

the emotions of citizens and recyclers concerning the problem. After that, I unpacked all

information collected on the first step, with ´Empathy Map´3 graphic to synthesize, I wrote the

answers in 04 categories: What say, do, think and feel, organized with sticky notes on poster. Later

text:
Reflection – mind mapping tool (Sergio Camilo)

Challenge

The challenge is to develop MOOC course about digital transformation that involves a lot  of staff and needs to be specified to a specific audience.

Selection

I selected mind mapping, to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a  diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to  the problem. I use this approach often with our instructors, who are technologists working  to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their services  to their customers.

Application

I start the process by posting sticky notes of the problem domain. I draw from existing  research material available to understand the environment. The existing material may be  operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, and other  courses.

For the activity, I divided the stakeholders into groups of 5-6 participants each representing  a different organizational division or area of interest. Each group received a poster-size chart  and sticky notes to make comments. To answer: 1) What is this persona (from 2 personas  we picked earlier) needs to know about digital transformation to advance the organization?

Insight &

What I have learned from conducting this exercise with several groups is that while the  working alone and generating ideas on the sticky note is important for reinforcing their  understanding of the problem they are working to solve, the more valuable aspect of the  activity is the shared insights and shared learning that occurs while they are working to  define their problem space.

Approach

Next time I would try and make the activity more collaborative and balanced between self- work, teamwork and group-work.

Design Thinking for Innovation: Final Assignment

CHALLENGE

Last month, a friend of mine  a software developer at a local tech startup  asked if I would be  interested in designing the UI for a mobile app that he and a colleague had begun developing in their  free time. Before committing to anything, and interested to learn more, I asked If we could all get on a  call. I wanted to know what inspired the project, who its stakeholders were, and why they would care  about our solution. They agreed, and we set up a time the following day.

The next day, as we walked through these questions, I noticed that something  or rather someone   was missing.  Yes, there were prototypes and a growing list of features, but where was the user? What  did they think? How would this fit in their day?

Listening, I felt that decisions were being made without an adequate understanding of what is. In other  words, an app was being developed without a story to support it. Surely there were things we didn’t  know that were worth knowing?

After raising this perspective to the group, I was  understandably, met with some resistance.  What I  suggested wasn’t part of the plan; it wasn’t within scope. And with that, I had my challenge.

In order to create alignment, I needed to demonstrate that our understanding was insufficient. Our  product’s story lacked depth; and without it, it’s value would be significantly reduced. Moreover, I  needed to demonstrate that this knowledge gap was worth exploring.

SELECTION

Beginning with the current state, a journey is  envisioned and articulated; revealing the actors, emotions and motivations which propel the user and  connects them to an offering.

text:
Mind mapping a design tool – Abdul Khan

Challenge & Selection:

Mind mapping is an important tool that can be used in design thinking process.  Especially when a new  initiative or design decision to be made.   We use mind mapping to choose a Pharmaceutical product to  be launched and when to launch and where to launch.  It is important to make apt decision on what,  when and how while launching the product.  Success factor of the product launch depends on the how  well organized and affective the product launch is being done.  Market acceptance and effectiveness of  the product.   Normally the products are launched to the market somewhere between one to two years  from the decisions are made.   Since our products are pharmaceutical products, product registration  process will take few months before we get an approval to market.   As such we also need to see the  feasibility of the product foreseeing a year ahead.

Application & Approach:

Initially a team consists of key members of Production, Marketing, Sales, Logistics & Product Manager  will have a brainstorming sessions on various potential products using mind mapping tool.  Prior to the  mind mapping session, the Product manager will give an overview of the selected products and then we  will have separate meetings on a different date, this gives time for the participants to think on the  products that were projected.   During the brainstorming session meetings, we make separate sheets for  each product to draw the mind mapping for each product name and then branch out all possible  scenarios including a SWOT (Strength Weakness Opportunities and thread) analysis.  Initially we won’t  focus much on the financial and ROI part.  However, after streamlined the best two options will be run  through the financials for a better decision make process.

After the financial process, a final proposal with business plan will be submitted to the CEO for final  approval.   This process normally takes between 1 to 3 months

Luis Gonzales  Savitribai Phule Pune University Student

Castles in the Sky – Design Thinking through the Visualization Tool

Challenge

Today we face a challenge unlike another; with a magnitude so considerable that it’s made

countries literally quake. Forsooth, the pandemic known as COVID-19 has come to create a new segment  in history that generations after us will only be able to read about in their textbooks. Partially, this creates  an opportunity to take action; to do things right. In the other spectrum, our “What Is”, the context in which  we live in, also creates what could seem like an abysmal chasm from where we’re standing today and  where we want to be, our “What If,” if you will.  I believe it is important to put these things into concept  because like with all innovation, big or small, we must be able to understand what we’re dealing with so  that we can make informed choices. Change is inevitable, dear reader. It is a constant and perhaps the  only one that we’ll be able to distinguish in our lives. COVID-19 has brought this change and it’s up to us  deal with all the aftershocks that have ensued because of it. Now, forgive me if I’m being dramatic, but it’s  true. To elaborate on this, I take quote from Virgil’s Aeneid: “Through chances various, through all  vicissitudes, we make our way…” What this quote leaves us with is nothing more and nothing less than  the inspiration to do things right; to go out there and innovate and act as best we can.

With that said, I ask that you picture this: A very small class of young economists and the

respective lecturers for each course. These people form part of a slightly renowned university known as  Savitribai Phule Pune University in Guatemala City. VISUALISATION

I am a part of a small yet developing project about Russian culture that is called  ‘kesyov’ ( ‘our’ — in Russian). To share our research and projects with the society we  use different social media: such as Instagram, Telegram (popular web-channel   for sharing your thoughts and ideas in Russia), Facebook etc.    In order to widen our audience coverage we decided to create our own website  and that was the point when the big challenge appeared: How exactly will it  look like and why? What will be the graphics like? What will be the tone of voice  with which the website talks to a customer? How can we become closer to oua  audience etc).   After a session of brainstorming we realized that to create a ‘Russian’ website we  need to understand what ‘Russia’ is in terms of words, tags, pictures, drawings,  images and so on. However, our team is very small (only 3 people work on this  project), which means that just our personal answers to those questions will  be not enough to create an exact common image that is required.  To achieve the best result that is possible we’ve decided to ask our viewers  (potential and existing) to actually visualise ‘What is Russia?’ in their opinion. So  we will be able to analyse this data and create something that is based on the  general statistics. We did this little game-challenge at the one of our free-en- trance exhibition. We created a ‘drawing corner’ with the necessary materials  such as sheets of paper with the text of the task (‘what is Russia in your opinion?  1) Draw 2) Write 3) Visualise however you want), markers and special tape to  make sure that after people have completed the task they can share it by placing  their work on the wall, so other people (and our project team) can look at it and  analyze it.

text: Nani Peroni  Design Thinking for Innovation Assignment     Challenge & Selection  In a previous role at a small business lending startup, I was responsible for the company’s customer experience across  the entire journey. While a small company, our departments were siloed and employees focused on delivering the best  experience they could to customers in their roles (sales, underwriting, collections, customer service, marketing) but  weren’t aware of the full relationship a customer would have with the company. This lack of awareness impacted  customers as they shared in their feedback with us. In order to bring value in my role, I wanted to build a connecting  thread between these groups so that we could deliver a cohesive and differentiated experience for our customers. To  help bring transparency to the entire customer journey and foster collaboration to drive a better experience for our  customers, I decided to run a visualization exercise with business partners. My goal was to create a visual and interactive  journey with specific touchpoints that our customer has with each one of our businesses to encourage discussion  around how we can build a better and connected customer experience.     Application   I invited representatives from each of the customer facing businesses to a two hour visualization exercise where I placed  key customer interaction points on the wall of our conference room (Awareness, Research and Consider, Apply, Repay,  Return/Attrite) to kick off the discussion. I provided colored post-it notes and pictures that represented channels, and  feelings. After walking the group through the intended goal for the session, we started talking through the different  customer stages and drawing touchpoints and feelings a customer would go through when interacting with the company  on post-its and paper. By Michele Schmidt

Better Commute Reflection - Visualization

Challenge

I have in the recent past worked with a few of my peers (group of 6), on a design challenge that is  human centric and was focused on ‘Designing a Better Commute’. Some of the framework we applied  in selecting our target audience after discussion were as follows:

•  The commuter had to be residing and working in a Metropolitan City.

•  In order to narrow down to the most critical commute in a metropolitan city we would  particularly focus on participants commute to work in the morning.

•  Each commuter should have access to and apply atleast 2 means of transport.

It was decided to conduct a 15-20 min interview with 3 commuters, as a group. We noted down the  interviewees experience, needs, wants, likes, dislikes and asked them to make visual representations  of their experience. Our group met to share our observations and then continued to make further  visual notes on our understanding of the problem to come up with some radical solutions. Even the  solutions were approached through visualization.

Selection

Visualization is a tool that is extremely effective in engaging the creative side of the brain. Even those  who are not used to sketching can get past a lot of noise (in the information) and come up with some  innovative insights on the information available. For the stakeholders, visualization generally provides  a deeper meaning into the problem or solution. The advantage of Visualization is also that it can aptly  be used in almost every stage of Design-Thinking. Whether one is trying to gather information from  stakeholder through ethnography, or trying to mind-map in order to come up with design criteria, or  brainstorming for portfolio of ideas, or developing concepts that need to be prototyped or even  creating early prototypes – Visualization can be used and evolved at every touchpoint of the Design  Framework. Challenge :  I’am the head actuarial department at NSIA Participations – holding of insurances companies based in  west africa. My Job consists in creating insurance products for all local market covered by my  organisation.  In my country – Cote d’Ivoire- only 10% of population had an insurance product and the  other 90% are uninsured and they  consider insurance product as a luxury.. However, to  realize the full  potential of insurance and particularly to increase our market share it was important for us to understand  why the large part of the population are not interested in insurance products or what kind of insurance  product could we propose them. So, the top management  charged me (as project leader) and some of  my colleagues to rethink our products and their distribution channels in line with the specific features  of local markets.  My colleagues was disappointed and thought that we would fail. The reason was all  our competitors failed by  trying to propose insurance product to people who work in informal sector  (the 90% who are not assured). My challenge was to motivate my colleague and lead the project to  success.    Selection  I have used storytelling tool to achieve my objective.  For me, storytelling is the art of producing an  existing story, or rather to master the art of creating. It is one othe the best way to connect us with our  audience and share feelings with him. Storytelling is also one the oldest way to deliver a message – or  to explain things or problems. Our parents used storytelling tool to give us advice even if we don’t call  it exactly that. text:
CHALLENGE

Being a part of an international organization aimed at addressing real world concerns on health, literacy,  poverty, and sustainable development proved to be challenging at times, despite the fulfillment that  one gets as a catalyst of change. As a member of Manuela Beltran University, I often deal with people from different walks of  life where we share moments that would be mutually beneficial and where we could learn from each  other’s experiences. A big challenge in this is the reality that we do not all share the same privileges and  sometimes, it is hard for us to conceptualize one’s story simply because we weren’t given the chance to  experience what another person has experienced. This explains how storytelling can be so powerful in  this line of work. It enables both parties to somehow allow the other to live the moment through  creative narration.

SELECTION

In carrying out the organization’s mission of serving humanity, one must get out of his comfort zone  literally and figuratively and visit places wherein the said person can make a difference. At first, the  receiving community wouldn’t open that much to you. This is understandable since we all undergo a  process of familiarization when encountering new faces. Story telling will allow you to creatively and  confidently introduce yourself and your advocacies so that you may encourage them to cooperate with  you.

APPLICATION

In one of our humanitarian trips to an island down south, we were briefed by our local government  partners that we should expect that the local community doesn’t get to experience interactions like  these too often, and that we should find a way to soften them up if we want to interact with them.  Fortunately, we share the same language and they understand our casual dialect, which gave us ample  opportunity to get close to them. We told stories of our group’s purpose and what we’ve been able to  accomplish in different communities around the globe for the past few yea

text:
Final Assignment – Learning Launch

By Komal Li

Challenge

I work in the planning department of a transit company. My team has been tasked with the challenge of  dissecting and redesigning our current process of bus stop checks. Bus stop checks are done twice each  day by different employee for the purpose of inspecting the physical stop for possible damage or  updating the posted transit schedule. Currently, each driver drives a pre-determined route that is  provided by the planning department. The driver is given the route printed out on paper from an excel  document at the beginning of each shift. The driver then progresses through the route, inspecting each  site, and writing down their evaluation on a pad of forms. After the driver completes the route, they  submit the completed forms back to the planning department where the information is transferred to  an electronic document.

While brainstorming this current process, the main issues and inefficiencies were identified as:

•  Missing forms that either need to be searched for and located, or are never found  •  Potential data entering errors while transferring the information from paper to electronic  •  Transferring the data is time consuming

Selection

Throughout the brainstorming process, it was quickly identified that there were a couple steps in the  current process that were outdated and could be modernized. Technology has become an easily  obtainable and inexpensive tool that can be implemented in order to maximize efficiency and minimize  room for error. Based off that assumption, it was clear that the learning launch tool would work best for  our challenge as we try to introduce technology into the process.

Tool   of   Choice:   Visualization

Challenge

1. The  challenge  I  faced  is  about  organisational  design:  how  to  identify  and  understand  our

target  customers,  define  a  product  model,  then  marrying  the  two  holistically  in  order  to

enable  the  company  to  deliver  against  the  real  needs  of  the  customers  in  the  most

efficient  way  possible,  also  achieving  consensus  between  every  stakeholder  in  the

company?

2. In  addition,  people  involved  in  this  exercise  (a  total  of  10,  plus  myself,  including  C-Suite

members)  came  from  a  variety  of  backgrounds:  one  hand,  this  ensured  a  wide  range  of

different  and  valuable  inputs  but,  at  the  same  time,  implied  that  each  of  them  used  a

slightly  different  language  and  had  in  mind  different  concepts.  This,  in  turn,  implied  that

stakeholders  weren’t  able  to  agree  on  what  the  “ask”  of  the  task  was  really  about  or  what

the  problem  we  were  trying  to  solve  exactly  was.  In  this  context,  I  was  tasked  to  allow

these   stakeholders   -   me   included   -   to   reach   a   positive   conclusion.

Selection

3. The  environment  was  clearly  multidimensional:  the  variety  of  mindsets  involved;  the  fact

that  stakeholders  weren’t  clearly  able  to  articulate  what  the  problem  really  was;  the  huge

amount  of  data  available  (in  the  form  of  technology  components,  financial  analysis,

personas  and  quantitative  analysis  on  customer  behaviours).  All  these  aspects  made  me

believe  that  this  challenge  fit  the  definition  of  “ wicked  problem”  (according  to  the  definition

clear   cause/effect   relationship   (   compatible   with    CBSDT,   1’58” ).

text: Example Reflection – Learning Launch   Challenge   I am Luca Ciccone, Egyptian, Teaching Assistant at Teaching Assistant at  Macmillan and Innovation Ambassador at  Ho branch according to  Communication Ministry. Our problem in Egypt is the big gap between  scientific research and practical application in the labor market. Our team  is working to try to find a solution to this serious problem.     Selection   Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools,  so we are ready to try the learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the  learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an idea and  prototype.     Application   For our first learning launch, we focused on trying to find a way to link the  university parties and companies by obtaining a website to communicate.  For our second learning launch, we focused on the meeting between the  two parties where contact was made with the MLAND and the  J Gs Cupcake store company in Benha, as well as the Zurak Cancer  Foundation, and  thus our hypotheses were validated.    Insight   By applying the learning launch tool, our team identified our assumptions  and designed launches to test these assumptions. By practical experience,  we found the companies ’need for university research to develop their  products, but the company cannot fully finance the research or purchase  the basic equipment needed for development. Through this result, the  project was modified through the introduction of an intermediary  company to finance equipment from Saudi Arabia and the United Arab  Emirates. The ongoing incorporation of insight is particularly important at  this stage, as launches come before a full rollout in the design thinking  timeline.    Approach   Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools,  the learning launch is the appropriate tool.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation

Author: Paolo Rossi

Reflection

Tool: Mind Mapping (Module 3)

1. Challenge and Selection

I work in an engineering company and it often happens that my team has to  create new concepts of new products that will have to be placed on the market.  Often these products have to be innovative and have to solve problems in an  ingenious way so that the customer is positively involved in using these  products. I chose the mind maps tool because it is based on creative abilities,  they can be created with colors and images, on processes that spontaneously  restructure information and that each time leave more than one interpretative  key open. For these reasons, mind maps are particularly effective for processing  thought and creativity, and this thought process can be very useful when  technical solutions to real problems need to be found.

2. Application

Concept development begins with brainstorming sessions, and mind mapping is  used to work out the relationship between topic information and new ideas. In  this brainstorming, each participant is encouraged to think out loud and  spontaneously come up with as many ideas as possible, no matter how wacky or  crazy it may seem. The problem or question is written in the center of a large  sheet of paper and the solutions are spread over the entire surface of the sheet.

The focus is on the topic; it is written in the center of the sheet and enclosed by a  circle. Branches branch off from this circle that divide and fan out the topic in  its individual areas. The keywords are written on the branches. The topics  represent the main branches. Details are written in the branches.

After creating a mind map, branches can be combined again or branches that  were not previously connected can be linked together. In addition, you can  search for missing branches to identify gaps for troubleshooting /  brainstorming. Mind mapping can also be understood as a continuous process in  which you start with a

Assignment on Design Thinking    Mickael Richardson

Challenge: As part of the Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) activities of our multi-business  organisation, we run a volunteering initiative, whereby employees are encouraged to offer time and  expertise in supporting CSR projects undertaken by the independent companies constituting the group.  While there are large number of employees with the right skill and those who could spare time for  these projects, the number of actual volunteers are very few. It has been our challenge to get more  people to volunteer. The various stakeholders involved in addressing this challenge include: i) Group  level CSR team – responsible for developing the program, ii) Individual company CSR teams – who  identify relevant CSR projects from several requests for help that each company receives, iii) Existing  Volunteers – who have already pledged their time for supporting the projects, iv) Non Volunteers –  employees who could possibly participate, but haven’t yet volunteered, v) Representatives from CSR  projects – who specify their requirement for effort/skills required for successfully completing their  projects.  Even though the present volunteering efforts have surpassed the targets set, since this is an  ongoing initiative, the aspiration is to tap the immense potential amongst those not on board yet.

And What  Works? are perfectly applicable to the challenge. There are two tools that one could use in my efforts:  mind-maps and story-telling. Both mind-mapping and storytelling may be useful in all four stages, and  for all five stakeholders (as mentioned earlier) albeit with some degree of difference in application. Sometimes it’s hard to explain that it is the only solution for their problem.  Storytelling is a very good technique to solve this problem. Design Thinking for innovation

Tool Applied : VISUALIZATION

challenge and Section

It’s almost impossible to tell if people are engaged or involved  with what you are presenting, that’s why i  consider visualization one of the most interesting concepts to put people in . In addition to that, visualisation  is really important for the process of design thinking, it is a way of unlocking a different part of our brain.  Since I adore programming , i found an interesting way to present my ideas , using the well know programing  languages, and espacially python where we found a library called Manim , which makes me able to animate  and illustrate pretty clear any idea i have in mind , and present it  in an interesting way to others .

Application

I start by making sure i understand the idea i want to present, and make even more sure that i am not going  to execute it in a linear way , when there is an easier way to do it.

After that , i write down all the ideas to be included in the animation (so i won’t get lost) , and start creating  the animation !

The first scene, is usualy a simple quote to illustrate the idea , which will be discussed, after that , i start  creating all the animations, I will create a different type of visual, either based on a high-level process flow  with swim lanes for different stakeholders, or another format.

For the activity, (while the animation is playing) i start asking question, it’s always import to make the  audience participate in the presentation, some of those  questions  :

1) What key elements are missing from the graphic?

text:
Frankie Kwan – Coursera – UVA Darden

Executive Education - Learning Launches

Challenge  I am working on a project creating executive education programs for middle to  senior managers, in collaboration with business schools. We have 3 team members  and have business development budget and 6 months of time on the campaigns. We  have already several hypothesis but we need to learn about our customers and  figure our their essential needs.    Selection  We implemented methods of learning launch tool, since we don’t have sufficient  data and we are looking for innovative solutions. We want to learn through quick  tests and affordable failures.    Application  We made a simple launching site and gauged 80 target customers for a quantitive  online survey, meanwhile through our personal network we got 10 participants for  qualitative interviews. Before launching the survey and interviews, we have  internally agree on the questions, content, and metrics, and we have also made trials  with a small group of people and made optimizations before launching.    Insights  After the survey and interviews, we found 8 pain points and 5 different type of  personas among our participants. We underestimated the diversity of our target  customer group and the priority of their key problems.    Approach  We decided to first focus a specific target group of potential customers, reframed our  hypothesis, prioritize key assumptions according to value creation upon specific needs,  our execution capabilities and competitive advantage. Then we designed the test for  those assumptions and conducted the tests.

text:
Example – Reflection – Mind Mapping Tool

On many occasions we are invaded by our thoughts and ideas, either as a result of our present  activities, as projects, objectives or goals we want to achieve. However, understanding and  projecting this information from our mind, for ourselves or for others, becomes in many cases, a  challenge, where we can fail in the attempt, if what we intend to communicate or capture a creative  idea.

The need to organize our ideas and the context of it is a challenge that all human beings have. In  particular, in the learning process, using a tool such as mind mapping, allows students or any other  group to be directed, to more easily appropriate the data and concepts that they want to offer. REFLECTION  Mind Mapping

By Muhammad Leonardo

Challenge  A large corporation’s internal Leadership Development Organization (LDO) planned an  overhaul of its curriculum. LDO leaders engaged its internal agency, Creative Services,  to help them execute on their stated objective:    Clearly communicate that courses have been updated and are aligned with the  company’s mission and goals while enticing leaders to enroll in the new program.    The curriculum revamp included significant changes in the following:   Content   Audiences (ranging from new, emerging leaders to executives)    Tailored training   Delivery – offering online training (similar to these Coursera classes) for the first  time      Selection / Application  After reviewing the LDO’s new curriculum and conducting interviews with stakeholders  within the organization, Creative Services recommended a design thinking workshop.    Attendees:   Members of the target audiences   LDO teachers, facilitators and leadership.     The session began with a 360° Empathy Map exercise focusing on each end user group.  Workshop participants were asked to consider what end users experience within the  “current state” of the LDO.     The following questions were explored:    SEEING  What are leaders at the company seeing when they attend the classes?

-  Networking opportunities  -  No visibility of opportunity/resources  -  Positive viewpoint (pie in the sky)

HEARING  What do they hear when they are there, or from co-workers who attend courses?

-  Classes are just a physical space (school), not an experience  -  It’s a privilege to attend  -  More interaction is needed

DOING  What do they do while in the leadership development courses, or afterwards?

-  Back to business as usual  -  Developing  -  Networking

SAYING  What feedback are they providing or disseminating to peers and their leadership?  -  Great experience, too bad it’s over…  -  It makes sense to go  -  Wish I could have gone sooner

Mind Mapping

Challenge    I work for a family owned group of companies that provides services to the Oil and Gas industry  in Mexico, with more than 60 years’ experience. The third generation is entering the family  business with a fresh and renewed vision, including institutionalization and diversification goals.    The son of the Group´s CEO is interested in real estate projects and has asked me to review  several opportunities with him. Due to his entrepreneurial profile, the challenge was bigger than  just reviewing stand alone projects. Swiftly, the discussions turned more interesting: “How do we  make a real business out of this?” and “How do we want this business to look like?” type of  questioning.     We decided to start our journey with strategic planning, which looking back, after this course, I  know that we partially did a design thinking process. Final assignment

Sujeet Ruiz

The Netherlands

17th of June – 2021

Challenge and selection

My main field of employment is within mechanical engineering, which I’ve only been working

in for a short period of time as a fresh graduate mechanical engineer. My technical field is mostly

centred around automated construction methods, most of which are (completely) new. One of my

functions in my organisation is to continue where I left off after my graduation thesis, where I

researched a conceptual design for a new type of construction machine. This meant already working

some steps of the processes described throughout this course, mostly focussing on the “what is” and

the “what if”. After being rehired at this company to continue my thesis project, I’ll now be further

developing my conceptualised machine and it’s further phases.

My challenge for this project is to continue a strong development curve along the timeline of

my employment at this company and perhaps even continue after the completed project.

Already (somewhat unknowingly) using some methods of visualisation, I feel like I barely

skimmed the surface of what this design method has to offer. Therefore I’ll be attempting to broaden

my use of this technique and its implementations across the different phases of the creation of this

new machine I’ve been developing.

Application

As a more literal application of the title of this course, I’ll be using the techniques as ways to

of a variety of design concepts that could be implemented into the machine. However, I kept these

explorations, experiments and developments mostly to myself. This course showed me the possible

depth these visualisations can provide if I share my thoughts and processes with others.

text: Name: Ravinder Pal      Challenge: Fixeen Project    The Fixeen project seeks to strengthen the labor system by injecting transparency into  it. To explain the above, we ask the following question: Is the labor system okay today?  the imminent answer is NO. Since, as, even we have witnessed ourselves, if you do not  have a positioned brand, an acquaintance who recommends you or market strategies  to which few have access, you can quite possibly be the best at what you do, but you  will hardly be able to survive.    So what solution does Fixeen propose to this problem? We created a web portal where  both empiricists, professionals and companies such as contractors and obviously  contractors, who would be the contracting users, can socialize.  What is the plus of this? We propose to generate a national ranking by work,  employment, or dedication where it is the same market that qualifies "the best in each  profession or occupation"      I selected the visualization tool    I chose it because I believe it is the best tool for exploring and expanding our ability to  innovate.    It is the easiest way to obtain information about something, it also allows us to think in  a non-verbal way and helps us access parts of our brain that we do not normally use  and this is very important in design.    The first thing I did was see the serious problem that the labor system has in most  countries and that at first glance it is clear that this system needs to be changed, I used  the visualization tool to realize the errors and then create a kind mind map and put a  logical and innovative solution to the problem. They receive these calls and support  callers with simple advisory on possible actions for recovery through recommendations and  referrals to medical centres close to caller’s location.

The budget for running this centre has been increasing year on year and management is seeking  a cost effective and technology based options to keep the centre still running and at the same  time extent operations to new user groups. I am working with a team both internally and  externally to fix the current problem statement to find an innovative model to deliver a more  cost effective and smart solution adoptable by today’s people. Challenge and Selection:    The tool I chose was storytelling, I believe it is a great way to inspire and set apart our

differences and bring empathy to those who are struggling. Storytelling has helped me realize  that others go through similar struggles and sometimes worse than my own, which helps put my  problems in perspective. I also enjoy storytelling to uplift others and give them a new standpoint  from my eyes. I use this approach in many different settings, but mainly in work situations. In  these work situations, I have worked with many different people from all walks of life. Because  of this, it was important to utilize the right story at the right time to convey a message. In every  job I have held, there have been many stories told and many that are forgotten. Many of us have  now begun to understand the struggles of our coworkers and realize the similarities many of us  have which helped us come together as a team. These stories ranged from hilarious, depressing,  to inspiring. Storytelling helps energize my workplace and bring a more open environment. It  was a great way to “walk a mile in their shoes” as the saying goes. Immersive storytelling can  put you in a different world and can be a great learning experience. Everyone has their own  stories of battles and triumphs they have had in their life; it is about finding the right story to tell  at the right time to inspire.

Reflection – Mind Mapping Tool  Kenya Export Processing Zone, 27.1.2018  Maria Meier

1. Challenge

I’m working for a health insurance company as HR Manager Training & Development.  Our challenge is to transform the existing training programms into pragmatic, future  oriented programms along the strategy with real added value for the company and the  employees and therefor for our clientes. At the moment, our training programms are not  very aligned with the strategy. They have grown in the past, but very uncoordinated.

2. Selection: Mind Mapping Tool

When we did research we collected lots of data. We interviewed managers and  employees, we did some research and benchmarking with other companies and we  scanned some of the important university programms. We decided to use the Mind  Mapping Tool to look for patterns and insights in all the data.    The Mind Mapping Tool helps to analyze information and break down complex data and  idea into patterns and insights. It is preparation for the „what if“ phase (video Mind  Mapping Tool, week 3).

3. Application:

We invited different stakeholders for a workshop. For the workshop we prepared various  „walls“ and sticked all the data and ideas we have collected on the „walls“. When the  workshop startet, we gave the participants some time to walk through the walls and go  over the data. Then we did short introductions and explaint the data an ideas. After a  short break we asked our participants to pick out the things they think that they fits or  doesn’t fits. An mark them on sticky notes. Then we asked them to go in teams (5 people  each team) and then to cluster the things they have choosen and to look for the insights  as well as for connections between the clusters. text:
VISUALIZATION

I always use Visualization design tool to find out the solutions and alternatives to  the problems. It has given me the best ideas to overcome the challenges I’ve faced.  Visualization is so simple yet complex tool to communicate a message. It has really  helped in getting desired outcomes. is any technique for creating images, diagrams,  or animations to communicate a message. Visualization through visual imagery has  been an effective way to communicate both abstract and concrete ideas since the  dawn of humanity. Visualization today has ever-expanding applications in science,  education, engineering (e.g., product Visualization), interactive  multimedia, medicine, etc.

Visualization techniques have been used by successful people to visualize their desired  outcomes for ages. The practice has even given some high achievers what seems like  super-powers, helping them create their dream lives by accomplishing one goal or task  at a time with hyper focus and complete confidence. In fact, we all have this awesome  power, but most of us have never been taught to use it effectively. Visualization is really  quite simple. You sit in a comfortable position, close your eyes and imagine — in as  vivid detail as you can — what you would be looking at if the dream you have were  already realized. Imagine being inside of yourself, looking out through your eyes at the  ideal result.

BENEFITS

Using Visualization techniques to focus on your goals and desires yields four very  important benefits.  1.) It activates your creative subconscious which will start generating creative ideas to  achieve your goal.  2.) It programs your brain to more readily perceive and recognize the resources you  will need to achieve your dreams.  3.) It activates the law of attraction, thereby drawing into your life the people,  resources, and circumstances you will need to achieve your goals.  4.) It builds your internal motivation to take the necessary actions to achieve your  dreams

Example Reflection - Learning Launch

Challenge

My name is Caterina Mauro. I am a mechanical engineer and my profession is heating and cooling system  designs. Moreover, I am a member of garment care department at my company. My challenge was  increasing ironing performance for handheld irons. It was my first iron project and I had not got  adequate information about this issue.

According to user experiment studies, every Turkish people want to wear ironed clothes. Wrinkled  textiles are not acceptable for them. For this reason, my department kicked off improve the ironing  performance of our irons.

There are two main parameters for improving ironing performance. First factor is steam rate and  second one is temperature of iron sole plate. If you increase steam rate and temperature of sole plate,  you can improve your ironing score.

Selection

I checked design thinking tools and decided to use learning launch tool. In my point of view, this tool  is more useful for our challenge because I had lack of information about irons and the factor of ironing  performance. In addition, I had limited time for solving this problem. The learning launch given chance  for quick prototyping and test.

Application

At our first learning launch, we discussed above steam rate and sole plate temperature in order to  improve ironing performance. In consequence of first learning launch, we decided to modify sole plate  steam channels. At that point, we designed 3 alternative sole plate channels and asked ourselves “How  do we decide which design is best?” In order to answering this question, we sent these 3 designs for  quick and cheap prototyping.

As a result of first tests with these three prototypes, we arranged second learning launch. We  evaluated test results and sole plates during this learning launch. Moreover, we choose best sole plate  channel alternative and improved the design of this alternative. We tested again with improved sole  plate. According

Paola Romano

Challenge & Selection I

I work as leader of an information technology team, training adults. I have a team of young instructors who are very technologically skilled. On many occasions, I have used storytelling as a way of bringing technology to be used during the day-to-day life of our students, who must use it in their daily professional work.

Many of our students are employees in large companies with middle and senior management positions, who are dealing with the way they work through new technological platforms.

When it is working with young teachers and students are sometimes twice their ages, students feel fear of learning new technologies, the use of storytelling facilitates the creation of bonds of trust and empathy.

Shamsun Fawzy

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

Mind mapping is a powerful tool that I use to look for patterns and insights in the  large quantity of data. Together with my design team, I work in a home  furnishing retail company, creating inspirational, beautiful and functional home  furnishing solutions to create a better everday life for the many people in our  local market. In order to turn their dreams into beautiful, functional solutions; we  conduct home visits. We visit 30 homes every two years and collect qualified and  detailed information. We interview people with different living situations to  understand their needs, their physical surroundings, the activities at home and  their dreams. We take photographs of their homes.

The physical spaces that they are living in, their living situations, their tastes, the  income levels and their wants and dreams differ a lot. Once we gather the data,  we look at similarities and we categorise the people into personas. In order to  generate ideas, we mind map our findings with a group of diverse background  colleagues. This gives us an opportunity to translate the insights into design  criteria. With the design criterias we pick, we create solutions in our media to  solve the needs and dreams of our customers.

Fernanda Moreira  School Head  Department of Education-Philippines

REFLECTION

ESSENTIALS IN OUR SCHOOL IMPROVEMENT PLAN:

VISUAL, MIND MAPPING, STORY TELLING, AND LEARNING LAUNCH TOOLS

Challenges & Selection

As a school team composed of school head, teachers and stakeholders, we make sure that in everything

we do is for the betterment of our learners. We are a learner-centered institution which main goal is to deliver  accessible and quality education for all. Our challenge is to identify the priority improvement areas which need  to be addressed for the attainment and improvement of learner’s performance:  We choose Visual, Mind  Mapping, Story Telling and Learning Launch tools in our school’s design and innovation because we believe a  combination of all these tools will give significant change in our school.    Application

In our school, we have a so called School Improvement Plan. It is a 3-year roadmap  of interventions

undertaken with the help of the community and other stakeholders. It serves as a basis for the Annual  Implementation Plan (AIP) and Annual Procurement Plan (APP) formulated based on evidences, results and  intended outcome for the learners.

The SIP is prepared by the School Planning Team to ensure the success of all learners for the fulfillment

of the DepEd mission which is to emphasize the stewardship of the school administrators and staff of the school  who will ensure an enabling and supportive environment for effective learning and developing life long learners.  Through visual, mind mapping tools, storytelling and learning launch tools we are able to come up with our  school priority improvement areas such as;

Reflection - Learning Launch

My name is Gary and I work for one of the biggest Universities in Brazil, SA Power Utility. Now, I’m in charge of entrepreneurship area of the TTO of Scotiabank,  called Innovation Initiative. One of my challenges is to increase the number of  spin off generated at the University. The context is complex, even more so if it is a public  university. In Brazil, Public Universitie’s professors can not open companies and work on  technologies developed by them at the University. However, students can open businesses and  license technologies developed at the University. However, these students usually have no  business background. Besides this, there is little incentive to start-up technology based in Brazil  beyond all the complexity of maintaining a company in the country, generating fear in this  public.We have a considerable number of companies formed in our incubator, but my  hypothesis is that we can do much more, reducing risks and working in an integrated way with  partners.     Our team has limited resources (time and budget). The proposed project has the purpose of  increasing the number of university spin-offs from technological clusters of interest to  companies. For example, we would call and select ideas in the health area, and the incubation  process would be carried out in conjunction with a healthcare company. Our team would enter  the incubator's expertise and the company would come up with resources to enable MVP  spin-off. It is a win-win, we generate more companies in the University and the company  leverages its process and open innovation.

text:
eBooks Assistant

In this Design thinking project, I’m going to tell about my  project which name is eBooks assistant.  This is a website in  which there are many types of books are available and one  can also read any books in this site.

Now these are the features about this project.

➢ Nowadays, people are busy with their own busy

schedule. So this website helps to find books of their  choices easily.

➢ Also our website is user friendly, so one can easily

interact with it and can easily find its suitable book.

➢ This website is available in 3 languages.

➢ In this, one can find famous and popular books.

➢ In short our website is:-

• One device , many books

• Accessible Everywhere and for anyone

• Easily update

So these are all about my project. I also write some stories  regarding my project which are given below:

there was a boy named Sameh, a student of global school .  Once a book fest held in his school. So he participated in it. In  fest, everyone has to find best books.so raj also started for  searching books. He googled it but cannot find there. Then he  went to nearby libraries. he searched there also, but could not

find it. He became very frustrated and worried that he could  not get books and did not registered in fest. This is a sad story.

Now happy story regarding my project:

once in a school, the G.K. quiz was organized, so, Vikas  wanted to participate in it. By coming home, he went to  library to find it there. He visited another library but the  situation was same. Then he came in contact with one of his  friend. Then his friend said that “don’t worry about it because  I am already having a G.K. book.”  he gave his book to Vikas  then he happily participated in quiz. So these all about story  boarding regarding to my project.
