REFLECTION

Challenge

The bank’s financial reporting has been done by the MIS department for years. Any financial report

to any of the bank’s business lines/departments can only be requested from the MIS. A set of

monthly reports have been agreed upon, and they have been delivered to the business lines

unchanged for the past two decades. Each time any of the departments has a request besides

the monthly package, he contacts one of the business partners in the MIS department, he

evaluate the request, provide target date, implement the report and share it as an excel

workbook.

Waves of changes have happened, there is no MIS department anymore, the whole group has

been revamped to analytics and data management. Where the basic function is no longer

reporting, yet analytics and performance evaluation. The monthly reporting packages were kept

unchanged though.

This task has consumed many resources which we need to utilize for their main analysis jobs. And

we need to keep the monthly reports on going since this is the business lines only source of data.

Selection

I mixed the tools learning launch tool and ethnography in my solution for the challenge.

Ethnography is a study of the customer’s nature, needs and requirements done through a serious

of interviews and journey mappings. Learning launch tool on the other hand, is a tool where you

experiment suggested solutions to your challenge and test them in action before investing time,

effort and money in planning based on just assumptions. Based on the results of your experiment,

you either move forward with the solution, tweak it, or try another one.

Ethnography and learning launch have best suited my challenge, because we had too many

people involved, the reports requirements have been left unchanged for so long, the business

needs must have been changed ever since and we assumed the reports don’t meet these

As a marketers of a shampoo company, I always faced the challenges of how to attract more customers to try and fall in love with our new launched products. Besides, I also faced challenges of how to ensure the phenomena of decreasing brand loyalty towards our products being. happened as there are variety of choices for customers to choose in the markets nowadays. I choose to apply storytelling as it is able to get insight into users, build empathy and reach them emotionally. I often create personas to represent target users and add conflict to stories that reflect their user journeys and problems. One of the reason is through crafting stories, we can better understand what users want from a solution. Good stories always captivate audiences. In user experience (UX) design, if designers use storytelling throughout the design process to ensure that all work focuses on the users' needs and the value that company want to give those users. This story makes it easy for everyone involved in the project to empathize with the users and ensure that their work matches the story. A systematic approach for problem solving

I have used story telling tool to solve the problem .I preferred this tool  because it adds more effectiveness. First let me tell you the story about  a boy named Stephen, who is very poor and orphan. He used to work  in a tooth paste manufacturing company to feed himself. He is well  skilled and with in short time he was given a promotion as a supervisor  for physical department.

All was going well for few years. The M.D has decided to increase the  production. So, all of the board members have decided to attain a  meeting for the analysis of how to increase the company income. All  the team managers and supervisors had attended the meeting. The  objective of the meeting is “How to increase the company annual  income”. All the people have referred to the past census to figure why  the income has decreased.

Stephen has gone through his survey and his reports were telling  that the product has still maintained its demand in the market. Users  also like that taste. He noticed their product and its dimensions of the  mouth of the paste. He increased the gap of the tooth mouth by few  millimeters. All the team members were agreed to this plan and had  done a dramatic change in production. After that the sales have  increased for the product. Finally the company had succeeded in  increasing their production.

Submitted by Tracy Simmons

DESIGN THINKING: PEER REVIEW ASSIGNMENT / TOOL: MINDMAPPING

CHALLENGE:

One of the key consumer mega  trends is the emergence of  ‘Experience Economy’ where  consumers values Experiences  more than Materialistic  possessions.

While this was a huge  opportunity, in India, it was  observed that this trend was still  in its very nascent stage with  more than 80% of the  population staying at home or  travelling within a radius of 5km  from their home during  weekends. Moreover the needs  and the barriers were very  diverse for different people

The challenge therefore was to  decode the latent needs and  develop a platform which  enables them to go out, explore  and discover new experiences

Since the challenge was very  broad and abstract and would  have different solutions for  different personas, Mind  Mapping was used as the  primary tool for this exercise

Therefore, Mind Mapping was  used to synthesize the various  interview data, identify the  different personas and think of  possibilities to solve the  challenge

Video Learning Reference: Week  3  - The Idea Generation Process  and the MeYouHealth Story.

Step 1: Capturing data through Empathographies (made-up  word to imply ethnographies focusing on Consumer  Empathy)

Step 2: Once there was enough data, each consumer was  bucketed into a 2x2 and then each grid was detailed in terms  of needs, motivations, aspirations to find patterns and form  relevant personas

Roberto Hasan

Coursera – design thinking for innovation [university of virginia]

Storytelling

Challenge & Selection:

I choose storytelling because in my position as innovation-consultant I work with

different people, in different positions, with different circumstances and with absolute

different goals and challenges. I use storytelling regularly as a useful tool to clear

complicated situations and to narrowing divergent opinions from different parties. I

selected storytelling as my challenge because I was @ the beginning of a new start up

project and used it as a method to bring my idea to my audience

Application:

My storytelling-story is: When I started to create my idea for these absolutely incredible

organization, called studio x, nobody understands me. I had too many stakeholders who

are involved in the project and I had to explain my complex concept to each of them to

win them as my project-partner and to get the proof of concept for myself. Sadly just a

few people gave me an encourage feedback and I started to create doubt. Luckily, I

enrolled the coursera design thinking course and met some entrepreneurs who already

use storytelling successful in their business life. These things brought me in contact with

the method of design thinking, storytelling, …. So, I started to create success-stories for

my business-idea and introduced them to my audience and partner. The feedback was

amazing and the sadness when I told them that the project isn´t real @ the moment

too. While practicing telling stories to strangers I also built up some confidence and

more trust in my idea and vision, so it doesn´t just helps me to win peoples trust and

convince to invest in my start up, but also to bring the reason why I do this project in my

own mind every day.

installation that will record a client’s phone on the system as it is received, recording the transfer of the

phone to the repair technician, tracking the phone repairs and informing the client and finally dispatching

the phone to the client and clearing it on the system. All department views and suggestions will be

considered as well as stakeholders suggestions, especially from clients.

we improve to do a full market launch.  We will be prioritizing key assumptions and analyzing the outcome

prototype feedback (Christian Friedrich, learning launch tool, week 4 materials 2017).

Design Thinking – Visualization

Kenichi Watanabe

Challenge & Selection:

The challenge I have in my organization is that we need to better manage our resources  time and allocation in the projects that the company has during the year and coming  years… The tool I used for this is Visualization or Visual Thinking to better understand  the problem between all IT team members in my department. The approach I used was  to first identity a way to how we could “predict” how much time each resource would be  working on specific projects during the next weeks. I started the brainstorming with an  empty excel spreadsheet where we “IT team members” would have to come up with  possible screens/fields that are needed in order to enter the work allocation for each  resource during the next weeks. This way we were able to create a “draft” template for  what a possible solution could look like to resolve our resource allocation in the projects.  The whole idea is to avoid that people are over-allocated and if they are working too  much, that creates other problems such as stress, quality issues, overtime costs, etc…

Application:

Once we had the initial “draft” excel spreadsheet created, we started the discussion  about how a possible solution could look like based on this template… We all got  together and started to think/imagine how the application should work, the possible  sequence, screens, fields, etc… and then we used a tool called “Bootstrap Studio” to  design the first prototype. This is one of the best ways to better visualize how the  solution could be created/developed, the steps, the screens, fields, behavior, user  interaction, etc…

We hard-coded all values for each step, screens, fields to better understand/visualize  what else could be missing, and finally we had the initial prototype created (without any  database integration)…

Mohammed Isah    11-08-2020

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Story telling is a tool that I frequently use. I work with a company as a volunteer to motivate the  young population that are needy, poor but have immense talent & creativity in them. So the aim was  to organise a platform where we as a team can volunteer & interact with these children. Many of  these children & their family are poor and cannot avail a good education. So our aim was to bring  the inspiration in them that they also deserve to have goals & dreams in their lives. So we started  working on this & started organizing many free fun & learning events for them. It gives me happiness  to see them actively participating, learning & the smile they have on their face. We interact & ask  them their ideas, what they think of their life & unfortunately we see maximum of the students &  their families are upset about lack of proper education & nutrition. So these feedbacks helped us to  approach through a new idea on how can we improve their lives by strategizing & find what works  for them to get the best ways in lives.

Application

I also have a story to share with all of you using storytelling. While discussing about how can we  bring changes in the lives of this children we started to understand the diverse thinking & the  uniqueness that each child possess in them. Reflection: Visualization    Name: Paul Basha

Challenge   Recently I was the member of a team of 5 working on a problem statement of excelling in customer experience to help  home owners build a dream home. This problem statement was defined based on the reality of low foot fall and  conversion ratios in the engagement of home owners with interior designers. One among us in the team is an interior  designer by profession, while the rest of us have experiences as consumers at various points of time. The challenge was to  improve customer engagement/experience and thereby increase sales with a diverse consumer base – investors, first time  home owners willing to occupy the property themselves or multi property owners.     Selection   Visualization was a good tool to adopt to bring out clarity in our thinking and to prepare for a test launch/prototype. Visual  representation enabled better understanding & common ground on the challenges.    Application    After the problem statement was broadly articulated, we went through the 5Y method of identifying the possible causes  of the problem, followed by surveys/interviews of consumers. Patterns were identified and together with the insights from  the interviews, personas and empathy maps were created. We identified a particular scenario – “customer goes to  competition after the initial engagement” for ideation. Ideas were prioritized considering strategic importance and  difficulty of implementation. A visualization method was used to put forward the ideas for prototyping a glimpse of which  is in the picture below

Insight  The idea for the prototype revolved around ecommerce, mobility, collaborative ecosystem. The idea for the creation of a  collaborative ecosystem was seeded while applying the visualization tool. This idea got seeded because in an e-commerce  world it would be easier to bring in user experience that can be incentivised. Design Thinking for Innovation-visualization tool

Visualization– tool for Industrial Automation

Challenge:   Extreme commerce (IDEEA) is a renowned food and beverage industry in Bangladesh. IDEEA  is not only a pioneer but also an industrial giant in the whole country FMCG sector. With no doubt,  their employees are very skilled and they have been with this company since beginning. Hence, the  recent cutting edge industrial models are not so much familiar to them. Still AME using manual human  based product distribution process for finished goods delivery system. Our team went there with a  proposal for a smart automated finished goods distribution solution. This reading will demonstrate  the challenges we faced and using a design tool –visualization, which tremendously helped out our  team to pass the barrier successfully.

After collecting all the legacy and running industrial data, our team prepared an auto solution project  proposal for them. But the orthodox IDEEA factory was rigid at their current position and did not accept  any system manipulation over the running system. Factory management also had a gap of  understanding how the automated process would work and unfortunately had a huge lack of  confidence about the new changes.

Interaction & Tool Selection:

Individually all of our team members were very much enthusiastic and visionary about this project. If  this project would be successfully implemented, this could be a milestone in the field of industrial  automation. So we tried to interact with all departments which were directly or indirectly connected  with the goods distribution system. Then according to our internal team discussion, we selected  visualization as a design tool for the project proposal delineation. Coyle 1

Ronnie Shahed

Sibanda

Design Thinking for Innovation

8 May 2020

Giving My Two Cents

Almost one year ago, I was tasked with giving a research-based presentation to my local

Toastmasters is an international organization dedicated to promoting public speaking and

lifelong communication skills.  Almost anyone could join, and my chapter was filled with 3M employees.  I looked up to them and even wanted to one day work for a bank.  I chose

personal finance tips as my topic. Money was considered an uncomfortable topic, but I was still

allowed to present my topic.  Aside from researching credible sources, I needed to think of a way

to make personal finance relatable and entertaining.

Back then, I picked the go-to route, storytelling.  Storytelling gave a face to ideas.  It

enabled audience members to connect boring or abstract concepts together (“Storytelling Tool”).

People loved a good story, and I figured the much older Toastmasters could relate to a young

woman’s issue with money burning a hole in her pocket.

When called upon to speak, my heart started to race.  I was shaking a little but

nonetheless accepted the invitation, got my presentation materials together, and stepped out in

front of the podium.  I was an impressionable young explorer living on my own in a new big

city.  I wanted to enjoy my summer vacation and as a result, had not worked for 3 months.  I dug

myself a hole of $3,000 in credit cards.  It started with moving expenses and grew even larger

audience members nodded in understanding.  They all kept watching intently as I moved back

and forth, telling my story and making eye contact.

Angela Torres (ENEA '97)

Reflection Assignment – Visualization Applied to Scenario Planning

Challenge  I have a working session with a new client on Tuesday, June 9 in which they would like to prepare for strategic  thinking.  The organization is a health benefits and wellness consulting firm and they have recently experienced  friction within the leadership team over the direction they should take the business. Two high-ranking executives  have recently separated from the organization, largely due to the discord at the top. I have the opportunity to  engage the remaining six members of the leadership team in an hour-long conversation, preceded by a survey to  gather their candid input and perspectives.  While I have my own professional services firm and do consulting  work, my familiarity with their particular industry and focus is fairly limited.  They did not seem ready for a  comprehensive strategic planning engagement, so I concluded that an appropriate first step would be to engage  the team in a scenario planning exercise, especially given the vast uncertainty that all businesses are now facing.  I  incorporated design thinking concepts into the facilitation model for this session.    Selection  I decided to integrate the tool of visual thinking, or visualization, into the scenario planning exercise I will be  leading for my client. I felt this would be the best way to guide them through an exercise focused on key  uncertainties they are facing in the business.  My objective is to have  them produce two versions of a 2x2 matrix similar to the one on the  right, but instead of the two axes shown here (“production costs” and  “product differentiation”), their chosen dimensions will be external  factors that are important for them to consider in their business. Mind Mapping to identify Automation Opportunities

Design Thinking for Innovation by UVA Darden on Coursera

BY: Uwe Bas

21 Feb 2021

Challenge/Selection  I use the Mind Mapping often in defining a customer problem space when seeking to look at areas  where we can automate. Taking a customer centered approach to map out to the various stakeholders  and look at internal/external factors. Whenever presented with a customer problem I will build the  problem space. The challenges the team faces and mapping out how Automation can affect various  processes, value-chains and teams. It serves as a more engaging way than going through reports and  data. David Kelley, the founder of IDEO said, when I want to do something analytical, I make a list. When  I am trying to do something creative, I make a mind-map.

Application  I start the process by creating an overview of the value chain in the problem space and some select  focus areas based on understanding of the environment or other material. The understanding of the  environment is from a pre-work assessment and some interviews. Other material includes market  insights and our teams own automation expertise. The mind map is split into Above/Below the waterline  like a duck what the customer sees – Above the waterline vs what the customer does not see – Below  the waterline.

For the activity, we walk through the process at a high level and focus number of transactions and time  taken per transaction and high-level steps and applications used. After this initial walk-through, we do a  deeper dive on the key candidates looking at hand-off screens and data that is required to carry out the  activity. This allows us to exit the activity with a number of automation opportunity areas and some  candidates for automation.

VISUALIZATION

By Laura Johnson

Challenge

I worked in a pharmaceutical laboratory that had a new drug that made it to the market  place after many, many years in research, clinical trials and production testing.  We had  just moved into a newly built building and there was much excitement and  overwhelming demand to know about the product and building.  The company’s  directors decided that it would be good to do an “Open House” with tours to inform the  public, interested journalists, professionals in the industry as well as many schools that  wanted to educate their students what a career in pharmaceuticals would be like.

I was tasked with heading up a team to prepare a tour of the research and development  laboratory.  The directors stressed that they wanted to get across what happens in the  laboratory and to explain and show what kind of science and cutting edge technology  we used.  This was a challenging task since the tours were short, with large groups  coming through.  The greatest part of challenge would be to convey the information so  that comprehension to all ages & levels of education was obtained but that those with  high and low understanding of science and technology were also engaged and not  bored.

Selection

I quickly came to realization that the visualization design tool would be a necessity in  our “What Is?” challenge to tackle, as described above. Our team agreed that  visualization, which is the use of charts, photographs, diagrams, handouts, etc, would  be a powerful design tool to incorporate.  With tours being too short to adequately  convey the science and technology we used on a daily basis in the laboratory, as well  as the description of scientific terms, processes and how the instruments work, it would  be daunting to go without this tool. text:
Classification : Giuseppe Petrosillo - Confidential El Petrosillo 7/1/2019 12:02 AM

Visualization Tool

Challenge and Selection

I am working as a tool manufacturing engineering team leader in a well-known factory which is in  automotive sector. Moreover, my team is responsible from whole tool process that are using at assembly  and machining lines. The tool which I have used is visualization. The probability of work accident is very  common in a factory environment. Sometimes, it depends on an operation tool in a process with non- standard activities. Recently, an accident was happened related with tool. I evaluated this incident with  my team via visualization tool.

Application

Firstly, I showed technical drawing of the tool for being sure that we all are in the same page. Furthermore,  we have watched video of the related process for getting ready to brainstorming. It is a way to get people  concentrated.

Secondly, I have drawn a fishbone diagram for finding possible root causes. I wrote problem and main  related topics with different colors and shapes. We discussed all main topics one by one. Everyone focused  on the same thing and understood each other clearly.

Lastly, after finding root cause we started to work on actions. For example, we sketched the design of a  new tool on the board.

Insight and Approach

I have learned from using this tool is that, the main point is understand the situation without any comment.  Visualization is not only the way of being parallel inference but also the way of triggering creative solutions.  Moreover, valuable aspect of the activity is seeming a positive union team with no doubt relevant subject  or creative solutions. Solutions were coming in sight very short period because of clear problem definition.

For future subjects and processes, I am going to use visualization tool whole steps for having rich  understanding, getting solutions and efficient teamworks with another point of views.

Janet Galletti

University of Virginia

Janet Galletti

In November 2019

andrew58@gmail.com

Hello, and thank you so much for your review. If you have any questions, feel free to contact me.  Saying Hi! from Berlin, yours Janet.

Applying the Design Thinking tool: Visualization

“I hate that lady!”

In a Workshop I coached a visualization process and participated an extraordinary turnaround.

Challenge and selection

First of all, I want you to gain a deeper insight of the setting and topic in which the visualization process  took place.

Last week I was a coach in a three-day-workshop about business model innovation. I coached a team of  four designers who worked in a design studio with a focus on branding and marketing in the B2B sector.  I call the design company I worked with DS, because I cannot share the real name for data protection  reasons. The DS-team contented the CEO, the CFO and two employees, one designer and one editor,  all of them were female.

Within three workshop days, we went through a process which was close to a real design thinking  process:

-  At first, we pointed out the DS-challenge regarding their business model.

-  Secondly, we defined the target group.

-  Thirdly we developed three questions and interviewed some people about how the marketing  process in their company was actually working, and which problems usually go along with  marketing.

-  Fourthly, we described the new customer experience and developed an approach for the new  business model.

Before the workshop took place, I thought about the challenge of applying a design thinking tool and  decided the visualization-tool would suit best for the definition of one special member the target  group. This was the second step of the process. I decided to do so, because also Anna Jones  constated that the visualization-tool is suited both for researching and for understanding the users  and customers (Anna Jones on Visualization, Design Thinking for Innovation, UVA,  min. 3:04).

Journey Mapping - By Monika Wolf

The South African, State Owned, THE CYBER SPACE HUB (Triple Play) tasked me, as part of a two man  performance coaching team, with the following:  Increase participation and collaboration of engineers during *Production Meetings in order to

a. Establish plant stability and optimisation.  b. Increase productivity and Mega Watts produced

*Production Meeting: A daily morning meeting where all the relevant engineers (Boiler, Turbine,  Auxiliary, Chemical Services, Maintenance and Control & Instrumentation) and Management meet  to familiarise themselves with the plant condition and current production related challenges

Back Ground:

Power Generation in SA is in crisis. This has been true since 2003 when a moratorium was placed on  planned maintenance for the period 2009 until the conclusion of the Soccer World Cup event that  was hosted in SA during 2003.  Triple Play, to this day, has not recovered from the back log and  the subsequent increased damage and anomalies that has occurred right across power plants since  2009. Myself and another coach had been working on the Plant for about 6 months and had  established trust relationships with all stakeholders by then.    Selected Tool:  During the “What if?” phase, we decided to use Journey Mapping  as design tool to really  understand a day in life of an SA THE CYBER SPACE HUB engineer. In order to understand the lack of  participation and collaboration in the Production Meetings, we wanted to use a Customer Centric  approach to really dive deep and understand how these engineers experienced their working  conditions in an attempt to gain insights into their practical and emotional challenges being faced. text:
Ali Zarei Reflection – Learning launch

Challenge & Selection

I was appointed to assist the Management to get an IT project back to the track. The project aims to  deliver an IT tool to support financing activity for several business lines in many regions involving 43  countries. The project has been started 3 years ago, and by now, is entering a crisis mode as the team is  struggling to deliver and finalise the project. The costs are steadily growing, and the end date is  uncertain. The project partially delivered some functionalities. The end-users are not satisfied and are  reluctant to adopt the new tool, they keep using manual processes or existing tools that are supposed to  be decommissioned. My role is to identify and implement a solution to get out of this situation.

Based on the preliminary discussions with various stakeholders, it was obvious that the project suffers  from "tunnel effects" and end-users un-satisfaction, I decide to use the learning launch as it will bring  visibility to the users. They can see quickly what the tool looks like and they interact with IT team.

Application

The starting point was to identify the roots of the crisis, what is behind the "tunnel effect" and the un- satisfaction of users. Based on "what is" technics: first, I gathered all data available on the project  documentation. Second, I prepared 3 types of interviews forms, one for the project team, one for the  end-users (clients) and one for the management.

The "what is" phase allowed to find out the following root causes:

1- The requirements have been amended several times, the project team adjusted the roadmap

involving costs increase and planning extensions

2- The end users (clients) are not appropriately represented in the project governance, some

business lines are absent, so their needs are not captured

3- The tool reached a degree of complexity that any change requires significant time and money

text:
Design Thinking Prototyping an Online Course Monika Seifert

Challenge

As instructional designer (ID), I was approached to support a professor at the university, where I  work, to advise him on how to put his negotiation course online. This initial challenge, of putting  materials online in a coherent and meaningful way, that was given to me evolved in the process  of information gathering that I underwent with this professor and his Teaching Assistants (TAs).  When he asked for support, he was looking for someone to help him develop video lectures to  replicate his in-class presentations. However, there were several obstacles to putting the course  online. Firstly, the professor received data in individual spreadsheets several times a week from  the students and needed to compiled them at the end of the week. Keeping track of the multiple  weekly activities and assignments contributed to confusion on the part of the students, as well.  Another obstacle was how to replicate the weekly interactions that built a strong student  community in the classroom with an online setting where students would interact in a relatively  isolating environment.

As an instructional designer, my focus has always been on creating a learner-focused  environment so the challenge was to take a complicated course structure and simplify it for  students as well as faculty.  Added to that challenge was the need to create an online structure  for a positive student experience to engage with the materials and activities as well as to  automate the students’ work in such a way that the TAs and professor need only to track it and  review it leaving a clear documentation trail and making grading easier.

Design Thinking for the Business Innovation – Edson Barbosa

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

My challenge as a consultant in my first experience, is help companies to develop costum- ers and to growth in a sustainable way your business model, creating value through the  new capabilities from employees, collaborative and iterative way. Due of this, I searched  for the last two year for the more modern techniques, methodologies and concepts involv- ing innovation, design, strategy, entrepreneurship, etc., like Business Model Canvas, Value  Proposition Canvas, Customer Development, Jobs to Be Done and Lean Startup. All these  knowledges are deeply guided by fast testing and experimentation, to really build, measure  and learn, with solid based evidence (and not only opinions) the understanding the really  matters for the costumers, and, in this sense, for the unique creation of value, both for  people and for the organization.

2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and

why you selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture refer- ences).

A learning launch is a scientific method designed to test, experiment and prototype busi- ness ideas, avoiding the risks of invest a lot of money and waste time on unverified hypoth- eses in the market. In a very similar way to the concept of Lean Startup, by Eric Ries, where  the main objective is a validated learning, the main purpose of the Learning Launch method  is to obtain is to learning, but heavily on the design entrepreneurial lens. In this context,  because I already believe and practice the processes and principles of Lean Startup, it was  easy to choose this methodology, with the belief and the objective of adding even more  knowledge to my consultancy.

Lean Startup:

http://martin.com/app/tags/searchregister.php

Learning Launch:

https://ideas.darden.virginia.edu/the-learning-launch-how-to-grow-yo

VISUALIZATION -AS A DESIGN THINKING TOOL

Introduction-

I am going to throw light on 'visualization' as the most important tool of 'design thinking'. I say  so because design thinking has been a crucial tool in simplifying the processes or studies related  to the topic. As the neuro-science says that our brain adapts quickly to learn and memorize when  we see the images, drawing or sketches of something. The 21st century state-of-the-art  technology have made things possible for vast magnitudes. May it be a 4 year old or a 64 year  old grasps visual information better and is able to represent it in better ways.

Such is design thinking with visualization that not only it helps us to look at things in a very  different way but also to understand how things could be done and problems be resolved in a  manner no one earlier thought of. Imagine the field of architechure, interior designing or 60s  school education where it was so tough to materialise things when they were in hard format  written on dusty papers and scrambling day in and day out just to make a meaning out of it.

We came to know that in Grades 1-3 the child learns to read and speak, whereas  beyond grade 3 they read to learn new concepts.

text:
STORYTELLING AS A TOOL  Reflection – Fernanda Dourado, July 4, 2019

Background    In my profession, storytelling is one of the most important tools for shaping powerful and engaging  messages. I work as a copywriter at an advertising agency in Sweden.

One of our latest assignments was for a shoe retail company here in Scandinavia. The task was to re- position their brand so that it would better match an increasingly changing world and a younger  target group. At the same time, they wanted us to evaluate a new strategy they had formed - and if  we thought it was the right way to go - make this strategy more communicatively available.

Challenge

The new strategy was formulated "Everyday Shoe Fashion" – and although it was right in meaning - it  was not an expression that could engage and ignite its audience. Our challenge, therefore, was to  convince our client to use a more exciting message in order to achieve the goal.

Selection

To create a saying that could work as a cause and igniter we chose the story telling tool. This allowed  us to focus on the people in the process and their emotional experience. With a story driven  approach, we would bring employees together and make them work in the same direction. From a  consumer perspective it gave us the opportunity to stand out from competition and build loyalty as  well as “brand love”.

Insights

As a starting point we considered and investigated the company's target group – consisting of trendy  consumers who sought constant renewal. After some research and interviewing we realized that this  group of individuals most of all wanted new impressions, experiences and a sense of fast fashion to  feel attracted to our offer.

The thesis was about the business model implications of the autonomous driving technology on a  leading German automotive company. The challenge was to gain information and, finally, knowledge  from the raw data. Therefore, I needed a tool that can set qualitative data in a context and relation to each  other. Since mind mapping can be used for looking for patterns and insights in a large quantity of data that a  design thinker gathered from the exploration stage “what is”, I applied mind mapping as the initial tool.     2. Application of Mind Mapping     In my explorative mind mapping process, I used an online whiteboard application called “Miro” to map the key  insights from the experts. Firstly, all relevant insights were written on digital sticky notes and got initially  mapped with other statements of experts. This represented the initial data set for the mind mapping process. •  How could Business Model Innovation help BMW to solve the Innovator’s Dilemma in the future?

•  Which organisational conditions need to be established today to enable this kind of Business Model  Innovation and the development of the autonomous driving technology?

text:
Reflection - Mind Mapping + Ethnographic Interviews

by Barbara Pedro

Challenge     In my company I facilitate Design Thinking sessions by request to help teams of different size to tackle

challenges they face in everyday life. Our Global Support technical team reached out to me and asked

for help to address the following ​challenge​: ​“How can we redesign the job experience and

increase happiness in Global Support Team?”. According to the results of anonymous

questionnaire, members of this team (20+ people in each of the 5 locations) showed little interest in work

and were demotivated, while the level of trust in the team was critically low.    Design criteria​: The proposed solution should not have has any impact on ongoing operations

(customer queries to be resolved on time and according to quality standards) and has to be tested

without budget.     Project scope: While the proposed solutions did not require any budget, they needed time and project

manager - one employee dedicated 15% of her worktime to apply the ideas to work process. The ideas

will be piloted in November and December in one office location. If in the end of the test period

significant improvement in happiness and motivation are observed, these solutions will become

“business as usual” processes for other 5+ locations.     Time frame: ​We conducted a 4h session to collects user insights and brainstorm on fast solutions.

Rapid prototyping/pilot stage will take place in November and December.     Selection    Important Note: While the task was to pick one of the four suggested tools, we needed to

conduct preliminary research before moving in to Mind Mapping, since we started from the

scratch. Therefore I combined Mind Mapping with preliminary Etnographic Interviewing.     Since we had final users (Global Support agents) in the room, we decided that ​Mind Mapping Tool from

Week 3 combined with ​etnographic approach ​with elements of Journey Mapping will be the most

appropriate tool

text: Reflection – Learning Launch – Ahmad Suryadi      Challenge    I am working as Product Manager in an online grocery startup in Southeast Asia. Our business  process is kind of simple, customer order grocery items from supermarket near their address,  and then wait until our personal shopper picking and shopping the items and our rider  delivering the items to their address. What I am handling and managing now is app that being  used by the personal shopper and rider, that also means the app that is being used daily for  the shoppers and riders to do their job: shopping and delivering items.    Our team’s main goal is providing the best experience for shoppers and riders in order to  achieve the best overall experience for the customer, including maintaining the on-time  performance for shopping and delivery, maintaining the order accuracy (minimize missing or  wrong items) and giving suggestions for customers if there’s any products in their order are  out of stock.    The challenge we faced is that the background profile of our shoppers and riders. Mostly our  shoppers and riders are only high-school graduates, which means that they are not really tech- savvy, not fluent in English, and somewhat conventional.    We once planned to improve the experience in shoppers contacting customers and suggesting  item replacement for their out-of-stock items. We added the way the shoppers share product  details to customers using chat. We came up with several ideas but not really sure about the  impact of the ideas considering the background of our shoppers.    Selection    To know whether our alternatives might be worked or not to the goals we want to achieve, we  planned to do a learning launch. By using experiment and deep research, we used usability  testing as a method to do our learning launch. Content ideation through MindMap

Challenge:

I am responsible for creating a website focused on content development that

transmits experiences to potential tourists looking for information about the city of

Foz do Iguaçu (which is on the border between Brazil, Argentina and Paraguay). The

site has access from all over the world and tries to deliver educational content about

tourist options with over 10 years of existence. The biggest challenge today is

maintaining the quality of content by creating new texts that deliver value to tourists

that can be produced and updated constantly with a small writing team.

Selection:

The main tool that could assist in the development of this content ideation activity

would be MindMap, through which it would be possible to map large amount of

ideas.

Application:

Building an individual MindMap will be the first activity, each involved in the content

ideation team will be responsible for structuring a diagram of interrelated ideas

through their insight into the content opportunities that can be created. With this we

enable each one to express their value proposition about the content to be produced.

Second, individual mindmaps should be converged into a single mindmap that will be

used throughout the site, generating unity in both the progression and the content to

be prioritized. The idea is to provide the maximum extent of content ideas, out of

"easy" or "common", so that the content created generates new experiences for

potential tourists.

In a third moment, we would like to organize a “collective brainstorming” providing an

interactive tool for potential readers to participate in a collective mindmap that will be

analyzed as a way to obtain validation of the mindmap created by the team. This

map will be enlarged by anyone using a 1-month online tool.

MIND MAPPING

Mind Mapping application for smartphone app project

Challenge and Selection

As part of an ongoing innovation project, I decided to apply the Mind Mapping tool in the sequence

‘what is?’ of the design thinking process. The project concerns office space equipment; the company

in which I work specializes in Internet of Things (IOT) control applications for the residential market

where we have some significant success. With this experience we want to develop applications in the

business or tertiary sector, however it turns out that the needs are different from the residential

sector and that we do not have a client but several who are involved in the value chain.

So, we analyzed the stakeholder’s experiences to ascertain the opportunities. The marketing

department initiated the traditional approach of researching needs with our customers and I decided

to extract the ethnological part discussed in the interviews, in order to reframe it in the approach

‘what is?’. The reason for this activity was to provide the opportunity to apply a design thinking tool,

Mind Mapping, and thus highlighting the needs of customers, create clusters, find links, and define

design criteria. The interviews and graphics from the marketing study allowed me to define typical

user profiles and to create a virtual panel of 5 persona. This type of document does not fit with the

notions of visualization necessary for our exercise, according to the precepts of Design Thinking.

Therefore, I called upon a professional illustrator to visualize the life scenarios of the users (the 5

persona), he drew on a large board for each persona, the different actions, habits, and routines…

which usually takes place in a typical day.

text: Design Thinking for Innovation    Reflection Assignment - Design Thinking in the Broadcast and Media Industry    Richard Moseley  23 July 2021    Challenge & Selection    Part of my job in business development and sales requires telling a story to communicate a  compelling message to my customers to identify mutual new business opportunities, and ultimately  sell a product, solution, or service.    I work in the television broadcast and media industry, in which the technical landscape is constantly  evolving with new and interesting ways to deliver and consume video, audio, and data content.   Many of my customers can be overwhelmed by the broad-ranging new technologies available and  struggle to understand how they can adopt such technologies to create additional revenue streams  or generate greater profit margins.    I chose the Storytelling tool to help take my customers on an imaginative, learning, and interactive  journey to explore what their business model and consumer offering could look like embracing some  of these new technologies.  The aim is to ultimately generate interest in one or more of the products  or services I am tasked with selling and lead the way to produce a new technology design, agree on  commercial pricing and terms, and deployment of the new service.    Application    Since the successful deal closure with one of my customers’ a tier 1 UK broadcaster, using a state-of- the-art cloud-based technology solution, there have been no further immediate new business  opportunities emerging.  I, therefore, prepared two stories linked to new technologies that would  complement their cloud-based solution, which could ultimately once validated and refined, generate  additional revenue for my customer. Nweze Stanley

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge:

The challenge I would like to describe is the means to provide clean water for daily use to the

Marsabit community in central part of Kenya. This community has been suffering from diverse

communicable diseases and other chronic health issues which might have been the result of bad

water consumption.

Selection:

To be able to overcome this challenge, the first tool I used was the tool of visualization (or visual

thinking). I mostly use this tool often to tackle problems related to design projects in school. My

major is more of designing and manufacturing. I have also used the technique of using a straw

man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow

a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope,

boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain,

points, and opportunities for solutions.

Application:

In order to start the process, I created a straw man graphic of the problem domain. The straw

man graphic was developed by drawing from many existing materials available in the

community to understand the environment. The existing materials in the Marsabit community

include their primary sources of water, the stakeholders, raw materials needed for water

purification etc. I have also conducted a thorough research about their situation and how badly

they have been affected by this lack of good drinking water, then I contacted my primary source

of information over there to see what I can do to help their situation. In other to solve the

problem the Marsabit community were encountering, I applied the concept of “front-stage/back-

stage.” This approach helped to reinforce the notion that every service-even an internal service

has customers with whom the service provider definitely interacts and internal processes that

Design Thinking for Innovation Reflection    Adigun Okoro April 2020

Testing a Niche Market

A Learning Launch Reflection

The Challenge

Background; West African diets are traditionally high in carbohydrates.  Modernization is  increasingly making the foods more highly refined and abundant, causing a steady increase in dietary  problems, particularly obesity and type 2 diabetes.  There is a growing awareness of healthy eating  in the affected communities.  A nutritionist has developed a series of substitutes for the problematic  traditional foods and needs a compelling proof of concept to raise capital for the business.  The  formulas have been tested, tasted and don’t require separate FDA approval as all ingredients are  approved.  Production either requires the huge outlay of building a factory or outsourcing to an  existing factory with milling and mixing capabilities.

The challenge was to establish the commercial viability of this series of products.  To do this, I  worked with the nutritionist to test the assumptions that people of West African descent, who are  interested in healthy diets, would buy this new and unique product just because of the health  promises it made and that they would do so at prices that would be profitable.

Selection

I chose the Learning Launch tool for this challenge as it seemed to best fit the bill.  A Learning Launch  experiment to produces results fast and cheap and as we learned from the Frank in the video, to test  key customer execution and defensibility assumptions was ideal for the challenge.

Application

With the tool selected, I analyzed the assumptions and distilled them down to a simple “must be  true” which was “people will buy this product online at this price.”  There were some researched  factors, the cost of production and minimum order sizes were taken from outsourcing quotations. Challenge   A news organization needs to update a legacy editorial system that is used for editing and  publishing news items. The key components in a particular type of news organization (news  agency) are speed and accuracy. Both speed and accuracy need to be at a very high level, and one  without the other doesn’t work. The team is at the discovery stage. The project scope includes a  diverse team of participants, such us higher management, editors, reporters and member of the  development team. The team has approximately one week to gather insights for a next major  iteration of the system.

Selection   Mind mapping was selected because it’s a tool that allows people with different needs,  qualifications and user behavior to work together in groups on a problem that is company-wide  and thus transcends particular roles. The method also creates highly visual results that are more  easily digestible for people of different backgrounds who are not necessarily familiar with each  other’s professional terminology and methods.

Application and approach  Key to a right approach is the diversity of the team. Each of the participants is encouraged to  avoid professional jargon and explain a used functionality in a simple in simple terms as  possible. The team interviews approximately eight users who work in different roles and who use  the system a lot. The essay:

Road traffic in Moscow under Sobyanin: are

economic

measures effective?

Written by:

Maga Ivanova

Group №193  MDI program

05.04.20

Road traffic in Moscow has always aroused strong debates. After his

appointment in 2010, Sergei Sobyanin immediately called traffic jams as one of the  main problems in Moscow. The priority was to streamline the parking space. “We  need to put things in order with parking, especially in the center of Moscow.  Nowhere in the world it is allowed to throw a car “wherever I want” - across the  sidewalk or the road. It is impossible to solve this problem in such chaos“, Sobyanin  said in his interview for the newspaper “Vedomosti”. The pilot project for the  introduction of paid parking started on November 1, 2012 from the Karetny Ryad.  An hour of parking cost 50 rubles. Parkons examined the payment; they were cars  with video clips. In the absence of payment, a fine was given automatically. Its size  was 2500 rubles. For parking in the wrong place the fine was 3000 rubles. Such  fines are valid even now.

Within a few months, paid parking began to spread around the city gradually,

and in 2015 they went beyond the Third Transport Ring (TTK), and their maximum  cost in the center and on the embankments of the Moscow River reached 200  rubles per hour. Today the city has 80,000 paid parking. Most of them are located  in 85 districts of the city, in 36 districts parking remains free of charge.

According to Viktor Osipkov, the project manager at “Probkovorot”, it was

the draconian fines that influenced the fact that people stopped throwing cars  anywhere, and the average speed in the city began to grow.

Challenge & Selection  I work for an Insurance company based out of India. My respective department is Innovation & Digital  Transformation. In Insurance Industry, we are the risk takers  for any consumer and in exchange of Premium (Amount paid by the consumer to protect an asset in  case of any uncertainty), we assure them a promise. For the consumer, the only value that he/she has  from an Insurance document is the service. For us, customer satisfaction matters the most and is an  important component for us to renew that customer for her/ his future needs as well. The basic motto  of our department is to develop certain tools and methods to provide customer a seamless service in  purchase of policy and a efficient experience in claim settlement. A customer can have various claims in  his lifetime, like health, motor or any general Insurance Claim. Its our duty to be the best on the ground  and help the customer in all sort of ways. We give our best as an organization, but its always important  for us to keep our customer’s demand and expectations in mind too. It might be that we would be  thinking from an organizational point of view keeping profit / loss in mind, but its always important to  hear the customer too. During the Coronavirus Pandemic, we decided to have a conversation with our  golden customers and listen to them. Reflection – Learning Launch for a BA Standardization Program

Challenge  I am one of the many practice manager for business analysis team of more than 70+ BAs which is spread  across multiple locations in India. The teams’ average industry experience varies from 2-10 yrs., which  makes the team a very diverse. When we deploy these BA onto various projects assignments, our  objective is to ensure they are adhering to certain standard way of working. However over time more and  more customized solution where being delivered. We tried to address this problem in many ways and had  failed. Due to COVID situation the pressure for better output and efficiency was compelling and hence it  was decided to relaunch practice wide standardization program which will aim to upskill all BA to approach  certain type of projects assignments in a consistent, uniform manner, thus ensuring overall efficiency by  improving predictability of the output and reduce business risk by promoting reusability of solution. It was  also decided that this standardization exercise should producing quick results and should not turn into  another never ending, vision-less program. I was given this ownership to run this program based on the  temperament I had demonstrated in the past on similar topic.

Selection  As the need was to get quick results, I wanted to try something rapid and test it immediately to see the  initial results. Therefore I decided to start this as a pilot program for 1 quarter and monitor results more  closely, emphasis was on incremental but consistent results. If the pilot program was successful, I wanted  to make this into an annual running program with continuous improvement.

It is important since any visualization  tool will take us beyond the limits of using just the language but to represent in an executive  format what this new idea and project is and what the financial impacts would mean. Finally  another reason behind the election of this tool, as it was mentioned in the video is that by  using visualization tool the communication process get synthesized.    Application    The application of the tool was launched in a Powerpoint Presentation. It was set a two  hours meeting with the executive with the purpose of review all the project details including  the financials assumptions. text:
Reflection – Visualization and Storytelling by Jose Santos

Challenge

I was dealing with a big problem in my organization about the ERP (enterprise resource planning) system, all people  complained that the system does not work and does not give enough information and I was in the middle of  everything because I was in the IT department and people do not accept suggestions to look to the problem in a  different view because they look for only they problems and not the organizational problem, So we used some  strategies that, today, I see it was the process of Design Thinking.

Selection

All department has they owns problems, but a lot of those problems was not because they job. It was a reflection of  the wrong input of another department, but the manager doesn't talk about those problems with other managers to  hide and scaping his real problem.

So they start to think in change the ERP solution. And before to do that we start some investigative to understand all  the needs and why the ERP doesn't fit with the organizational. Reflection – Storytelling to draw the future

By Luz Marina Mora

Challenge & selection

Storytelling is a very useful tool when doing future studies and Foresight. I am a consultant and  researcher in strategic thinking and foresight, and in each exercise the main challenge is to empower  actors in a long-term vision and collective thinking about the future, be it a territory, an organization  or a productive sector. The main mission of foresight is to define a long-term future scenario, taking  into account some elements of the past, an analysis of trends and signs of the future, as well as  technological disruptors that can generate specific changes in the development of a specific  phenomenon, But the people involved have trouble having short-term thoughts, with anxiety to  solve current problems or “put out fires”.

Most of our leaders and decision makers think more about short-term planning than future  projection, therefore, the result of a foresight study should allow us to see the future in such a way  that it feels real, tangible and challenging, so that those involved are encouraged to work on its  construction, thus, the use of narration allows the prospective to create a logical, coherent message  that generates enough emotional and optimistic connection to influence strategies and actions in  the construction of that future.

During my time on the council, we decided to affront this problem and develop a

new website that would provide comprehensive information for each doctorate school  process in multiple languages. Furthermore, we decided to pair each incoming foreign  student with another doctoral candidate further along in their process. This became the  cornerstone project for the Doctorand Council during my time.     Selection

We also had held a meeting with the directors (full- time personnel) of each doctoral school within the laboratory to see what was possible  within the constraints of the requirements of the schools. Peer-graded Assignment: Reflection | Tool: Learning Launch

Challenge and Selection

As a sport and technology lover, I started a few months ago a company in Brazil. The idea is to  give everything the professionals have to the amateur soccer players, from scores and graphs  from the matches to automatic generated videos making the experience of playing soccer  digital and social we would charge the players to deliver this to them. It is not a secret that  soccer is one of the most popular sport around the world, and our goal was to build something  scalable and worldwide applicable. Since the money was short, we guided ourselves by Lean  Startups and fail fast concepts, in order to learn about customers’ needs to address it quickly.  The selection of Learning Launch for this reflection is because we use some of its concepts and  that helped us to shape the solution, mainly because we started doing experiments instead of  a Business Plan, this saved us time and money.

Application

It is almost impossible to talk about Learning Launch without mentioning the previews phases.  We went from the observation and data collection (what is) from our friends and started  generating some hypothesis (what if), we did it structured and non-structured way and then  we started making some experiments based on them, using correlation with other things for a  better visualization (another tool from Design Thinking) of what we said. Anyway, it was  helping us to construct, and co-create with the people that would be one day our customers.  At that time, they did not know that yet. Once we learned a lot of what would make sense  (what wows) we decided to build a prototype (what works) and go sell it – Learning Launch.  We build a structure with security cameras and it automatically recorded the matches and the  players could use it was a social network; they could cut their moves and goals scored sharing  it with friends and so on. text: Reflection.  Mind Map  By: Oumar Rocca. MSc.    As we’ve seen, the Design Thinking has a wide range of resources depending of the  type of need we have, problem we would like to solve or simply, to share an idea. So, I  have selected one of the Ideas techniques: Mind Map.    As a professor I have used this technique in my classes, to summarize the topic.  Sometimes individually and sometimes in groups, that way, I can see how much they  can learn as it lets me evaluate the relationship of the contents of the lecture and the  readings the students had available before class.   This way, at the end of the lecture, I give my students 10-15 minutes to prepare their  Mind Map letting flow all the ideas they may have and to connect them with the  readings and the other material available, when they team work, it is amazing how they  discover new ways of understanding a specific topic when they draw in the map and  the other classmates complete the ideas, sometimes we need more time as they have  discussions.   After that, the groups make a presentation of the map to the class and we try to  identify all the points in common, in this phase new discussions arise and more ideas  flow.     It is important to teach the students the difference of a Mind Map with a Concept Map:  In the Mind Map has a radial structure is less complex (for me) as here the student can  even formulate questions or connecting with a previous topic, while the Concept Map  has a formal structure (as a tree) and it’s used mainly for organizing knowledge.     What is the response of the students? They learned that Mind Mapping help them to  study before exams and obtaining better grades as they use all the ideas expressed in  the map. This tool helps with the development  of thoughts and the flux of ideas since  they’re using their hands to write, their minds to recover what they’ve learned, the eyes  to see how the map is rapidly growing, and the mouth to express their own opinion.

Challenge:

Hello everyone, I am Pawan Subash. I recently found an issue that childrens and students are suffering a lot with the platforms that are there in the current situation. Main problems are lack of awareness, no gaphical interface and Data consuming.

Application:

The main agenda is to maintain Students data in an

effecient manner and make students comfortable with the platform.The students are mainly lagging in the content that the currently using platform and it is  static so that they cant experience the new features. The development in the  platform will help students a lot. They are obsessed with the current platform  because of the single platform. This new platform can help a lot to the students.  The consistency of the platform needs to be tested in various situations. And the interrelated system of different systems should be tested to get a better  result.The Data consumption is to be reduced and user interface is also to be  improved.

Insight and Approach:

Students are facing problems with their current virtual

labs due to lack of good interface. The platform should be highly reliable  because it should help students for long period without any bugs and errors. The app or platform should use low memory and it should give better performance  so that battery drain will be reduced. If an app that is useful to students by  reducing the data usage the parents can afford small amounts for meetings. The  main problem is maintain several platforms can be a hectic task for students. It  would be helpful to everyone if that features come into picture.

- Better experience. - Various functionalities. - Good user Interface. - Helping students by giving converging multiple functionalities. - Low data usage. - High content. - Easy to use. - High reliability

Fewer than 44% of Indian young children receive the full schedule of immunization.

This states that around 56% of children have no immunization. General health diseased

proper form of recommendation in which the system can deliver the proper form of

immunization. The nature of primary health care challenges in the last two decades, has had

better delivery but more will have to be done to be able to promote or increase the survival

rate of children in India. The survival rate improved by about 200 % but more than half of the

children still die without good or complete vaccination at the proper time. In India, a record

number of children of about 27 million children are born which is the highest in the world.

But immunization process is low and generally incomplete in many communities.

Some conditions are highlighted such as in case of diarrhoeas due to rotavirus which

takes about 1,22,000 to 1,53,000 lives every year and a record number of 4,57 ,000 to

8,84,000 children are hospitalized under the age of 5. Polio has had a successful

immunisation process which has dropped the case of events significantly due to improved

and better programs of vaccinations which is not implemented in other health conditions.

text:
BMW vs Kia    Introduction  This report builds and examines the brand architecture of two brands of cars: BMW and Kia.  The two brands are chosen as they are in the same industry but have very different targets.  The goal is to observe how consumers can have vastly different perceptions of and  relationships with very similar products owing to the differences in brand architectures.    Brand Architecture  The first step is to develop brand pyramids for both brands.    Brand Architecture for Kia

Brand Core/Essence

Quality, reasonable price

Brand Personality

Young, working class

Emotional Benefits

Fashionable, inexpensive

Product Benefits

Guaranteed mechanical elements, low investment

Product Attributes

Modern designs, good machinery

Brand Architecture for BMW

Brand comparison  As we can see both brands compete in very similar markets. Also both brands put a high value  on performance and product quality. However, the differences in the brand personalities  appeal to very different target audiences in the same market. BMW prides itself on the  exclusivity that it brings through its sleek designs and premium pricing. On the other hand, Kia  attracts its audience with the long guarantee of their vehicles. While BMW creates a sense of  belonging for its customers, Kia provides its customers the value for money.    BMW targets the high end of the market, and its customers are not usually price sensitive.  There are few options to choose from, but brand loyalty is very high. Kia customers are more  price sensitive. Due to differences in pricing, BMW products are high margin products. On the  other hand, Kia relies more the sales volume. Thus both brands serve the company’s goal of  revenue share through two different drivers.    Brand Value  Interbrand ranked BMW as the 3rd most valuable automotive brand in its 2019 brand rankings  1with a brand value of $41440 millions, while Kia is the 12th with 6428 millions.

Mind Mapping

By Blanca Becerra

Challenge & Selection:

I used the tool of mind mapping to drive possible solutions of the problem that I was

facing. The mind mapping tool helps you organize the information in a visually appealing

manner, which is understandable and clear. The challenge is to understand the type of

customer personas for a new business idea, and to present insights gained from an

experiment that was conducted prior to this. The business idea was to create travel

journal and merchandise for travel enthusiasts.

Application:

So to start I made some sample journals and merchandise that showcased travel

experiences in different regions and countries. These prototypes were shared on my

personal social media profiles and some of my friends helped me by sharing it online on

different groups made for people who love to travel on frequent basis. We gathered the

relevant data by observing the comment section, by asking them about the items they

liked or disliked, and the number of direct messages I got for pre-orders, the next thing I

did was to check the social media profiles of these people and divide them in different

segments based on their preferences and demographics.

I print this data and made sure that we had all this data, sheets and profiles printed with

me. To make the mind map I took a pin board and a couple of small colored chart papers. I

made small prints of the information that I received on these colored papers. Then I

shared this board with some of the people who ordered the stuff online. This was to make

sure that they belonged to this clusters and asked them to give their thoughts on this

segments, and share their thinking process on the time of their purchase.

text:
Reflection-Storytelling

Challenge

My friend Teresa was very anxious and unhappy recently and it was because of her son Naser. Naser is  10 years old and turned to be a little rebellious now. Due to the school closure in covid-19, Naser  has classes online and he then formed a habit of spending much on computers playing games or  watching videos he likes. Teresa was at work and can not monitor her son during working hours,  and she worried about Naser’s health as he spent too much time on computers so he completed his  homework very late, so he slept very late and his eyesight is poor as well. Naser used to be a good  student and obedient son, and he agreed to lessen time on computers or cellphones, but he can  not always keep his words. That’s why Teresa worried. She is afraid he turned to a bad boy.

Selection

Naser is ten years old and now he began to seek himself and have the desire to be independent.  Teresa can not just control and monitor him but let him to take responsibility of his own life. She  understand this but she just can not trust her son due to her fear of bad things. Under such  circumstance, pure analysis is not enough, some personal experience between kids and their  parents maybe more compelling. So I chose the storytelling tool.

Application

I told my own experience as an example to Teresa about when I was young, about my rebelling  behaviors, about the trust my mother always on me and the strength the trust give me, and  actually we know what we should do and we will do the right things if we are trusted and  respected. The unconditional trust and love is the most important thing we need when we are  teenagers, when we rebel or struggle to find ourselves.

The personal story was told from heart and Teresa was moved, she agreed to try to put down her  fear first and give Naser more love and trust. Naser is her son who learned a lot from her silently, she  trust he will not be a bad boy, he just need some guidance on how to manage his time a

Mohamad Afiq            29 December 2020

MIND MAPPING

1. CHALLENGE

I was asked to co-facilitate a design thinking workshop within the Digital &  Technology Sector of our organisation a few months ago, during the second wave of  the pandemic in my country. Our organisation recommended all staff to work  remotely, thus our workshop had to adapt to a virtual environment which was new  to not only the facilitators but participants. The intention of the design thinking  workshop was to solicit user stories from all project managers and business analysts  in the sector on the application of artificial intelligence and machine learning in all  areas of the organization. Our Chief Information Officer suggested that a horizontal  approach would allow efficiency gains in the in-house development or procurement  of a solution that caters for the organisation’s needs. Our team of two facilitators  alongside the lead project team managers regrouped virtually to decide on the best  approach to conduct the virtual design thinking workshop and discussed various  tools, methods and platform to collaboratively gather user stories for a group of 30  participants.

2. SELECTION

After much discussion on the agenda and main objectives of the design thinking  workshop, our team of facilitators felt comfortable with selecting the mind map  method as the method to gather user stories. According to Wikipedia, a mind map is  a  diagram used to visually organize information. It is hierarchical and shows  relationships among pieces of the whole, created around a single concept, drawn as an  image in the center of a blank page. Major ideas are connected directly to the central  concept, and other ideas branch out from those major ideas.

Having participated in a global design thinking workshop, I proposed Miro as the mind  map platform as it catered to multi-user collaboration in conjunction with Microsoft  Teams as the meeting platform.

text:
Storytelling Reflection

Challenge

I work for an agency within the EPU (Saudi Aramco). One of my  responsibilities is to communicate the purpose and content of the agency’s strategic plan  to the workforce, as well as the plan’s relevance to employees. This is difficult for  multiple reasons. First, the agency employs over 2,000 people. Second, the strategic plan  hasn’t traditionally played a large role in how the agency operates. Third, I had to tell the  strategic plan’s story primarily through others, i.e. agency leaders, since I am a strategic  planner at the non-supervisor level.

Selection

I selected storytelling because the strategic planning methodology my agency uses is  focused on evolving the organization from its current state to a state that provides more  value for its customers. In other words, our strategic plan focuses on achieving a vision of  the better organization we aspire to be. This description of a better state and how we get  there lends itself very well to storytelling, as it invites an audience to imagine an exciting  journey leading to a desired destination. As Andre Martin stated in the Week 2  storytelling video, this is a prime opportunity to create a “cause” by conveying a message  with logic, emotional connection, and purpose.

Application

The primary storytelling channels employed were senior leader postings to the agency  intranet, speeches by the agency director, and the strategic plan itself. In each case, a  colleague or I inserted text explaining how the strategic plan would enable our agency to  better serve military forces, Saudi Aramco leadership, and other valued “customers” by  accomplishing the objectives in our strategic plan.  We almost always included specific  examples of objectives to make the narrative more concrete and relatable. These primary  channels were supplemented by others not as conducive to the extended narratives of  storytelling, such as PowerPoint presentations and digital and physical signs. Even

text:
Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge:

When working in research, at the beginning of any project it is required to have clear ideas about  the topic to be carried out. Especially when working in a group, where each one, with their  experience, provides options for a project. Then it is necessary to understand and try to choose  a specific topic and focus our ideas towards the same point in order to carry out the initial idea.  The challenge is precisely this, to bring together the entire working group and, together, to  propose and choose the topic that will be developed during the project that begins.

Selection:

In this case, the tool I have chosen is the mind map since it allows the organization of ideas,  taking into account patterns and perspectives, as mentioned in module 3. With mind maps it is  possible to take the ideas of all group participants and organize them in such a way that you  have a clear idea of the options available.

Application:

In the case of the beginning of the planning of a project, the use of a mind map was quite useful  since, being a diverse group and each person with their own idea and theme, the map allowed  to organize all the ideas, put them in agreement to a topic, group them and then, among all the  participants, choose based on different criteria which one was convenient to continue to the  next stage. So, once the ideal theme was had, it was possible to start planning the rest of the  project, based on the map made.

Insight:

In this case, the use of a mind map is adequate to organize the different ideas that the people  who make up a work group have. In this way, each person participates actively and is able to  make their opinion known. In addition, it was useful for the challenge of starting a collaborative  project because the ideas were raised clearly and without limitations, helping to have different  points of view that helped to expand the repertoire of ideas and see which of them could be  more innovative.
