text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge and Selection

Storytelling describes the social and cultural activity of sharing stories and experiences. Every  culture has its own stories or narratives which are shared as a means of entertainment,  motivation and even education. It is also, as I have learned from this course on Design Thinking,  an effective tool in not only solving problems but also creating a cause. Below is an instance in  which I selected storytelling as a way to not only get people on board with an idea but also to  help unite them towards a cause.

During the lockdown imposed due to the COVID-19 pandemic in March 2020, many people  were faced with the formidable task of procuring basic essentials themselves and their families.  In such a depressing and distressing situation, I was faced with the challenge of lending a  helping hand and trying to provide assistance to the most vulnerable in our town. With this  vision in mind I contacted a few like-minded individuals to pool in ideas on how to address this  problem. After a lot of deliberation, we finally discovered a potential solution in the form of an  online store for groceries and other essential commodities as well as a home delivery service.  This would enable those who could not come out of their homes to have their essentials  delivered to their doorstep without putting their health at risk. However, another problem  unfortunately arose. A few people were daunted by the idea. They lacked the motivation and  drive and did not see a way it was possible.

Application

To tackle this problem, I resorted to a narration of a story from my own experience in my  locality. There is an old lady who lives alone and who was distressed by her inability to procure  basic essentials. As neighbours, we all rallied to help her but it was a short-term enterprise. She  needed something more reliable. I told them seeing this old lady struggle to get her essentials  made me realise there were so many more out there

text:
The development of technology has changed the world, has given mankind new standards of living and  allowed it to work miracles that once seemed fantastic. However, the same technologies have led to a  new stage in the development of society, which is characterized by unreasonable expenditure of  resources and environmental pollution.

To solve these problems, technical innovations alone will not be enough. Society needs a new approach  to innovation, which would bring the needs of mankind into harmony with the natural world.

Design thinking can help in this, which is based on the techniques used by designers, but also applicable  in other areas. Design thinking allows each person to use their innate creative abilities.

Once upon a time, designers were engaged almost exclusively in the design of new products. Design  concepts did not go beyond this special area.

Recently, however, the same principles have been applied not only in the design of specific objects, but  also in the formation of consumer experience, in the organization of production and exchange of  information, as well as for the improvement of existing products.

Design thinking is used in all fields of activity, in all markets.

“Design thinking originated in the field of design, but its principles can be applied by anyone in any field  of activity.”

In 2004, the Japanese company Shimano, a manufacturer of bicycle accessories, decided to change its  strategy in accordance with market requirements. In collaboration with IDEO, the company tried to  understand why only 10% of adult Americans ride bicycles, although 90% did so in childhood.

It was decided to analyze the positive experiences of consumers in childhood and the negative  experiences that emerged later. Based on the results of this consumer-focused study, new bicycle  design concepts were created, and not thanks to a technological breakthrough, but based on  observations and interaction with people.

Design Thinking for Innovation                                                                                 Nandan Velasco

1. Challenge

During my Master Thesis in Marketing, one of my course mate (let’s call him Nandan) asked  me and 5 other students to develop an idea. The idea itself was quite broad and not  well defined, and since Nandan didn’t explain this idea to all of us simultaneously, we all  have different opinions and impressions about that. Briefly, the idea was to build a  website where students like us, or just young people, could visit and check which are  the nicest spots in the city, events and so on. Of course, we wanted to make it different  from other similar websites, and this was the main challenge. No one of us had any  particular skill but we were all diverse in our personality and mindset, so we all had  different points of view, which can help in terms of creativity but can make it slow when  it comes in taking decisions.

2. Selection

The tool we selected was Mind Mapping (of course, without knowing it). This tool looks  for patterns and insights in the data collected, and it’s especially used when it comes  to establish some criteria and assumptions for the next steps. Since our team was  formed by 7 people with different “personas”, we thought that mapping would be  better to pull together what we had in our minds in a way that we could all add some  value... some smaller idea into this project.

3. Application

Basically, everything we did was meet and brainstorm, by trying to understand how to  develop this idea in something that was different, more creative... and maybe  innovative?! We had meeting once per week and the week before we always had some  assignment like “write down from 3 to 5 column you’d like to have in the website” with  no restrictions. Application of Storytelling in International Development Programming

In the first quarter of 2019, a country in Western Europe gave $58 million to a specialized agency of the  United Nations (UN) called the International Labour Organization (ILO) for it to use the money to  programmatically combat child labour in the supply chains of cocoa, coffee and gold in Africa. After  preliminary research on child labour in Africa and several consultations with relevant government  agencies across African countries, the governing board of the ILO and the donor country unanimously  agreed to pilot the child labour intervention programme in Nigeria before expanding it to other Africa  countries. The decision was premised on the fact that Nigeria is the most populous African country and  research on labour statistics from the ILO Research department indicates that in some states in  Northern Nigeria more than 50% of children under 18 years who works on cocoa and coffee farms and  artisanal gold mines. I was working at the programme unit of the ILO and the National Programme  Coordinator of the project saddled me with the responsibility of creating a report and consequent  presentation to persuade all stakeholders to summarily green light the project.

Inside the company, I work at the Consulting department specifically attending all  requirements from Finance, specifically Treasury and Corporate Finance.     Actually we are implementing a business model which will be replicated to other locations  and subsidiaries around the world. This business model implies FTE´S- headcount reductions  because all the processes and activities involved would be analyzed and segregated into  strategic and operational in order to build a regional shared service center through  technological drivers and process redesigning.    As this business model requires several complex phases, and taking into consideration the  way how stakeholders involved likes to see presentations, I decided to use the Visualization  tool in order to capture their attention and easily transmit and explain every step and  process of the methodology we were going to use to let them clear and understand how it  will work.     As this business model is complex to explain and understand verbally and in order to create  a visual image for people of how I am thinking, I decided to use the visualization tool; also  to let them understand how we intend this model will work. (As Is Scenario Mapping- FTE´S Identification- FTE´S Validation- To  Be Scenario – Mobilization – Stabilization). I decided to link each of the processes with Smart  Art diagrams in order to explain and let the stakeholders know that each process has  dependency of the previous one. Storytelling as an Effective Design Tool

Challenge & Selection

Completing bachelors and masters with good teaching experience, I understood the necessity  to update myself with new concepts related to my field ie., Management. This led me to pursue  my 2nd MBA (Imagineering) from the Netherlands – master’s in Business Innovation from  Experience Perspective. This was the first time I came to know about Design Thinking and  different design tools like Storytelling, visualization, world café, gamification, Lego etc. I was  enthusiastic when learned and was excited to practice. As part of study assignment, I was given  a project in one of the municipalities in Belgium.

The challenge here was the inactive city centre, where many entrepreneurs were shutting down  their business and the centre was soon to be life less with very less shopping and activity  around. The municipality tried some strategies to fix, but no positive results were seen. This  project was assigned to us through our professor and had a chance to practice the concepts  practically. In the creative sessions with the stakeholders (municipality, businessmen,  customers, suppliers, shop keepers, citizens), I used Storytelling as one of the design tools and  found it useful and effective to unlock the complexities in sharing their feelings with others, to  understand, discuss and solve the problems.

Application

As the first step in Design Thinking, before I begin, I searched in internet about the  municipality, city and city centre and tried collecting some needed data. As a next step, I visited  the city as a visitor and tried to observe the place, people, resources etc. This gave me  information to see and understand the problem. text:
I happen to spend lots of time driving. When I drive, I tend to think about how others

behave on the highway. I’ve always been interested in transportation economics. It was only

natural that I started thinking of the externalities caused by driving to test my idea. Was

it possible that the individual costs of an accident were so high that crash tax would not do any good.

I began my research by refreshing my understanding of externalities and crash taxes,

going back to old economics textbooks. But I needed to know more, so I began accessing other

papers on traffic economics. This would have been impossible without access to the seemingly

limitless information available through the University Library’s Research Port. I was able to

access articles from the top economics journals using JSTOR and EBSCOHOST. I even had to

look up textbooks on fields I was not familiar with, such as transportation engineering. I would

have had little access to these kinds of sources without access to Maryland’s libraries.

I knew of some important articles by reputation, but it was more difficult to determine the

relevance of more obscure studies. By seeing how often articles were cited by others.

I could gauge which papers made significant contributions to the field. By reading curriculums vitae of

the authors, I learned which scholars were experts in which fields. Even these techniques did not

answer all my questions, however. I knew I needed to consult an expert.

I met with Pepe Baker, a transportation professor in the business school.

Baker was extremely helpful in identifying where to find additional information. He

instructed me how to access online data from the Department of Transportation.

After several discussions with my Anthony Adamu and Pepe I decided that I had neither

the time nor the resources to conduct the kind of empirical analysis I originally desired. I still had

enough data and enough ideas to address the topic theoretically, however.

Challenge:

I work for a project organization that deals with multiple projects that are massive, medium and  small. The projects are complex in nature, while often small ones, involves many stakeholders  and includes many stages and activities that need to be well coordinated and the slippage of any  one action contributes to the domino effects and impacts on the other tasks, interface projects,  which in turn affect the outcomes of cost, schedule and efficiency. A challenge to proper planning  is also the effective allocation of scarce resources.

Selection

Our team had already gone through various design thinking activities/tools. Using the Mind  Mapping Approach to learn from each other, involving the project team and multiple stakeholder  groups, in the process of evaluating the scope, limitations, key elements, and relationships  between elements to be considered when identifying pain points and opportunities for  improvements or solutions. We should capitalize on data learned from experiences and come up  with an innovative approach for the execution of the project.

Application

Using this approach, all the data and observations could be conveniently collected and shared,  the aim is to set standards for the generation phase of what-if idea. In terms of scope, stakeholder  expectations, communications, engineering, procurement, resource assignments, risks,  integration, scheduling, expense and efficiency, we will be able to diagram the network flow of  operations and the dependencies. With people speaking out their thoughts, it would be more  visual and more interactive. The activity that fell into the critical route could be defined and the  tasks that needed further effort and have dependencies are labelled. The mind mapping process's  concept thinking would accurately capture and reflect the minds of the needs of our stakeholders  that are collected up-front.

Design thinking

What is design thinking? Design thinking is a method of creative thinking to solve problems, also  known as human-centered design. Design thinking as a skill of the teacher and given that design  thinking is an approach for creative thinking and problem-solving centered around humans, thinking  through design forms part of the participations and deep social structures. Its roots lie in the depths  of mindsets and creative processes aimed at creating opportunities for understanding others and  developing innovative solutions to meet their needs. Through training in thinking about design, he  will have the skill to generate questions, and motivate students to do so, in this case the teacher  becomes a major change maker in the educational process, one of the most important skills that the  teacher will need is thinking through design, which is a method of creative thinking and problem  solving, and therefore The design thinking skill was the skills compatible with student-based  learning, which the teacher needs in order to develop students' learning faculties, because the  teacher thinks as a designer and not just a teacher planning the lesson, the difference here is that he  is trying to start from steps that start with feeling the problem and then generating ideas Help me to  implement the learning process interesting and effective. The Design Thinking Kit for Teachers,  which aims to tailor 2 the process to suit teachers specifically, consists of five stages: Discovery,  Interpretation, Innovation, Experimentation, and Development which are similar to the stages of  generating questions and discovering solutions, installation and experimentation, Thinking with  design also helps the teacher to face the challenges that he meets in the learning environment, in  this case he can look at the available environment to create an enabling environment for the learner  to achieve the possible benefit

text:
Challenges & Selection

It all started years back when a colleague of mine shared with me his dilemma about  choosing between two fundamentally different career opportunities. The classic “Marwa,  would you have a minute for me?” in the office right after the first coffee in the morning.  What initially sprang to my mind to ask him was: “What is it that you’d expect from what’s  left of your business life?”

He replied that he had never thought about that in detail. I continued: “What do you think  you’re really good at?” This is a question that is on the no-go list in today’s formal job  interviews as much as “What do you think you’re really bad at?” because there can’t be an  honest answer. I got trained on that 16 years ago already in my hiring certification classes at  November. However, it is totally OK between two friends in a secluded setting. His answer  struck me as I had a totally different picture of him. At this point it became clear to me that  his situation and decision process would require some formalization and visualization. And  this is how I started to use mind mapping.

Application

I start with general ideas and get more and more specific as my idea develops. Structure  does not develop in my head. Information does. That means that I must put down my  information somewhere and structure it there. Linear representation is difficult to structure.  Hence, a mind map comes in handy: I can see things at a glance and add topics where I see a  gap.

While developing the method, I used a mind map to dump my thoughts and experiences in.  After a while, these topics could be organized into clusters, which then mercilessly pointed  out to me what was missing. I literally saw it! In short: Information creates clusters, shows  missing information and promotes further clustering. A very creative flow. Reflection - Learning Launch

Challenge

I am a member of a team of six who are trying to solve a problem related to healthcare. To tell specifically we are trying to develop a device or a machine that will help disabled person to move around freely and stand upright without any discomfort. By doing research through internet and consulting with doctors about the problems and interviewing the patients we gathered few information about the ill effects of sitting ideally for a significant period of time. Those are as follows:

1) Paraplegic person cannot get stuff from the high raised shelves.

2) Breathing problems.

3) Lack of blood circulation in the body

4) Digestion problems.

5) Bone density is low due to lack of physical activity

Selection

Our team has gone through different tools used in design thinking processes and has selected the learning launch as our tool. Because learning launch is about testing different experiments and see whether any one of them has an impact on the lives of the customers we are trying to target. In the learning launch video lecture Andreas Weber says “They've got that specific need that's causing the pain, and you've got an idea that meets that need or solves that need”. We selected this to solve our problem because we had a solid base of different concepts with which we can execute it and check whether our hypotheses is true or not.

Application

For our first Learning Launch we had developed a prototype of advanced leg braces and gave to four different patients to try them for a week and noted down their different experiences about the device and how it tackles different problems listed in “challenge” paragraph. We found that the leg braces tackled all the problems but couldn’t serve the purpose of utilizing less physical efforts by the patient.

For the second Learning Launch we developed a prototype of an electrically operated wheelchair which has a mechanism which will allow the user to convert from sitting

text:
Reflection- Visualization Tool

Challenge and Selection:

The challenge here for me is, me being a student of an undergraduate course I have to think  about my final year project. Hence ‘Visualization’ can play an important role. Be the  selection of the topic or how to go about the project needs visualizing. Having a prior idea  and the outcome of the project is really necessary. As visualization helps in picturizing  something which cannot be seen or can be helpful to bring out the picture of the desired  outcome my project has to give or satisfy. As it is not about drawing but about imagining and  visual thinking this tool will help me out from selecting a project topic to finishing it well  with a desired outcome.

Application:

As I’m still in the process of using the tool, this tool has helped me think better and get to  know how things work in a better way as just reading about something would not be as  impactful as just picturizing or visually thinking about how it actually works. Not only for my  project, ‘Visualization’ can be used in daily life as well. I’m really using this tool to study my  daily subjects for better understanding. Using visualization for practical subjects is a must I  feel. Usage of this tool to understand difficult topics through picturization is really helpful.  Also, this tool has helped me take ease at some subjects I didn’t like.

Insight and Approach:

Visualization is about using images. It makes us think beyond using words or language.  It is a way of unlocking a different part of our brains that allows us to think  nonverbally and visually. When we explain an idea using words, most of us will form  our own mental pictures. If instead you present your idea to them by drawing a picture  of it, you reduce the possibility of unmatched mental models.

Challenge and selection

Storytelling is a useful tool that I have acquired on a daily basis because I work with many  people of different ages, adults and youth under construction, most of whom have had  economic, social, family or migration problems. Construction is hard work and is generally the  last option for many, and to forget these problems, they need support or an economic  incentive to get back on track and get ahead. That is why I have given my time this tool has  helped me to give a focus to the client.

Application

After a while there was a bit of conflict between colleagues and each time they were repeated  constantly and sometimes for insignificant things, there were even cultural clashes and all with  different design ideas, so when talking to my boss I explained how good the use can be from  storytelling the benefits it would bring for the environment and the workflow and how it  would change all the staff and how effective it would be if the group leader adopted this tool,  then by applying people they acquired more empathy, respect for their ideas and grew  companionship.

Knowledge and focus

Well after this experience, the knowledge that I obtained by applying this tool was how  powerful storytelling can be, it can completely change people's thinking, you gain experience  and you receive advice that will be of great help in the future and all that is something  important for someone who is interested in the course

Completed my Bachelor of Engineering in Electronics and joined IT /IT services industry from start of my  career, I am used to deliver different roles related to technology sales, pre-sales and consulting. During  my maternity break from full time work, I did some freelancing assignments.

Challenge about the new role:

In my last freelancing assignment, I was working with brain training and development organization, as  Marketing and Sales manager. This role was very different and challenging as it required to sell and  promote a concept which in India (my region of sales), where lot of myths acted as road blocks. These  myths varied from perception to interpretation. For e.g.: Brain does not need any development, it is an  inborn talent people born with, Mindfulness is same as meditation, few hours of training will make  permanent changes, why spend money on something which can not be quantified in terms of monetary  gain or short-term benefit, etc.

Other than these road blocks, my biggest challenge was to sell this concept to IT heads and CIOs of the  company, since my network comprised only technology folks. They would be my entry point to refer me  to their HR head, if they like the concept and would want their team to be trained.

text:
A Reflection on the Use of Mind Mapping for Health Professions Education

Challenge

The delivery of healthcare education for nurses, physicians, dentists, physical therapists, social workers,  and pharmacists has historically taken a siloed approach. This approach is problematic because these  individuals are expected to work together in teams to provide quality patient care, yet they are not  trained to do so.  To address the “wicked” problem of how might we increase interprofessional  educational opportunities across healthcare disciplines, a national organization convened a group of  healthcare educators to participate in a design-thinking workshop.

Selection

The organizers selected a mind mapping exercise using sticky notes to get participants thinking  creatively about how we as educators might address the wicked problem.  As we learned in this course,  mind mapping is a visual method for helping others to understand how ideas relate to each other and is  one of the most universal ways to brainstorm. The unstructured setup allows individual ideas and  thoughts to flow freely. Similar concepts are grouped together, allowing ideas to jump around among  topics, rather than forcing them down a list.  I have personally used this technique in multiple  workshops and sessions to address difficult and challenging issues in medical education.

Application

In the most recent exercise using the mind mapping technique, we gathered together in one room 30  health professions educators and divided them into groups of six.  Everyone was given a pen and a set of  sticky notes and sent to their respective groups to begin brainstorming how we might increase  interprofessional educational opportunities across multiple healthcare disciplines. We had only one rule  which was that every idea offered up must in some way be “actionable.”  Each group was assigned a  staff person to manage the sticky notes, to group them on a wall according to concepts, and to refuse  any idea that

Mind Mapping Tool application in an apparent production problem

Challenge

Once I worked in a ribbon manufacturer Company. There was a lot of stopped production machines  and only one of them worked 3-4 hours each day, some of them had no maintenance. Only  considering the only working machine there was a production problema that i could not see. I needed  to know what was this apparent production problem by alanyzing the different sections of the  Company as a system of inner-clients by the different sub-products each section has to deliver to the  next in order to make the final product. These inner-clients has needs beyond the product by itself  and I wanted to discover them.

Selection

By using he Mind Mapping Tool I should get some information about the needs of each Company  section and start to get to a view to the real problem. I should analyze each section as a persona and  then I should know what was the apparent production problema.

Application

I met each section idependient from the other and show the product flow of the process. I told them  to write on a post-it the common issues they watched in the sub-product when it arriver to the section  beside as how the product was planed to arrive (freccuency, quality, etc.). This was a complicated  exercise to do with the administrative section because the sub-product they process is intangible.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge and Selection

I have done a few other online coursed on DT and amongst all the tools that I have learnt storytelling  has become my favourite.  Since it based on story, there is virtually no limit to the imagination that  you can use to craft and weave stories.

I am a customer service and customer experience management consultant. I work primarily with  small and medium companies in the IT Infrastructure services industry and in the hospitality  industry. As a part of my consulting services I also train and conduct workshops for my customer’s  teams on how to improve the customer service they give to their customers. Most of the  participants in these workshops are in the lower and mid-management category and most of them  are in the 40-plus age group. Many of them do not have formal training in customer service. Many of  them deal with irate customers every day and managing the customers is a big challenge. Earlier I  used to do a very text-based slideshow presentation to them.  But I soon realised that I was not able  to connect with them and invoke their interest in the training as they were not used to classroom  type trainings. Their participation level used to also go down. Then I then started sharing stories with  examples of bad and good customer service for each different aspect of service.  Most of the stories  came from my own background in customer services field and the others were what I had read  about. I noticed a drastic change in their participants and some of them also shared their own  experiences through stories and this made the training session very interactive and interesting to all  the participants.

Challenge

I providing consulting services to one of the developing countries. I focus my efforts on making it  relatively easier for citizens to transact with government administration. This has not been an  easy task, since there are a lot of Complex, non-transparent, time consuming, and  incomprehensible government transactions that result in low quality of public services and in  inefficiencies in the public administration. This causes citizens and businesses unnecessary  administrative burdens that cost time and money, undermine the image of the public service,  distract managers from the achievements of the results, and give rise to unofficial payments.  Furthermore, the public administration does not have an effective complaints mechanism to  help facilitate complaints management. My department has launched an initiative to come up  with an idea to identify the bottlenecks of relevant government transactions to have them  streamlined. This would allow the administration to operate in a transparent, efficient, cost  effective, and timely manner and reduce Administrative Burdens on citizens businesses.

Selection

My team has decided to implement a design-thinking concept on this project. Design thinking is  an innovative way to come up with new business ideas. Learning Launches, a design-thinking  tool, helps decide to either pivot or shelf the subject ideas. This is a much more effective  approach than the traditional business planning. The team launched an experiment to quickly  put the idea into a hypothesis (select only five government transactions to streamline), figure  out some key assumptions (citizens and businesses would be supportive), re-design and test the  five government transactions. The confirmation of the hypothesis shall prove to citizens, the  public sector, and the private sector the worthiness of the idea.

DESIGN THINKING - FINAL ASSESSMENT REFLECTION

Challenge:    In my present organization, I am part of the Pre-Sales Solution Design Group, specializing in  service management tools and platforms. My primarily responsibilities involves designing and  setting up tools platform for our managed services delivery teams, designing solutions that  address very specific customer issues and suggesting improvements areas and new tools  keeping in mind customer demand and market trends.   One of account delivery manager has got in touch with me to inform that the current tools  platform they use for providing services is outdated. The Delivery Manager wants  my team and me to look into setting up a modern service management tools platform. text:
MIND MAPPING

Mind mapping is a graphical way to represent ideas and concepts. It is a visual  thinking tool that helps structuring information, helping you to better analyze,  comprehend, synthesize, recall and generate new ideas. Just as in every great  idea, its power lies in its simplicity.In a mind map, as opposed to traditional note  taking or a linear text, information is structured in a way that resembles much  more closely how your brain actually works. Since it is an activity that is both  analytical and artistic, it engages your brain in a much, much richer way, helping  in all its cognitive functions.

A mind map’s radiant structure directly corresponds to the way our brains store  and retrieve information.

A mind map conveys the hierarchy and relationships between individual ideas and  enables you to see the big picture.

A mind map makes use of mental triggers (such as pictures, colors, and  connections) to help your brain memorize things more easily.

The best part: mind mapping doesn’t feel like work!

Mind maps are a visual way to organize your thoughts around one topic using  words, colors, images and numbers to highlight ideas and draw connections.  Invented by Tony Buzan in the 1960s, mind mapping is much more than drawing:  It’s a framework to help you fully think through ideas, and show how topics and  ideas are connected and allowing with more flexibility than an outline or list  affords.

Mind mapping can be a solo or team activity, and they can be used for all types of  tasks: learning, thinking through ideas, strategic planning, mapping out processes  or organizing overwhelming amounts of information. I’ve even come across mind  maps made to plan weddings or organize Thanksgiving dinner.

You don't have to make a mind map—you could just jot a note down on that  napkin, or use an outlining app to list the things you're thinking about. So why  mind maps?

text: Reflection - VISUALISATION TOOL     Challenge & selection  I work for an architectural design company heading up marketing and communications, and  as part of my role I run a lot of events in our own and various hired spaces. My role in these  events is from managing the overall objective setting, concept design, planning, through to  overseeing execution and then event follow up. I work with a team of people on the various  elements of these events, but often I am the only one that is working on them from start to  finish – so in some ways I’m the glue of these projects and the one with the holistic idea of  what we are trying to achieve.    Over time, I realised the whole team needed to be on the same page about what we wanted  the event to be from a guest journey and experience point of view. How should our guests  feel, what should they experience, what should they walk away thinking, what actions do  we want them to take after? All of this is underpinned by the objectives of the event and  why we are doing it.    I started using the visualization tool at the beginning of planning for events, as a framework  and reminder of what we are trying to achieve, so that everyone working on the event was  working towards these holistic outcomes, rather than just taking care of a specific area (for  example, catering, guest check in or event marketing). It’s a reference tool during the entire  event planning process. By visualising the whole experience a person will have at one of our  events, we can map out their journey and think about all the touchpoints (physical, digital,  human) and potential pain points that need to be resolved – literally by putting ourselves in  their shoes. text:
Example Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I will use is Mind Mapping to help organizing information collected and generate ideas for  the next stages in an ongoing personal project. The idea may lead to a startup company and, specially at  an early stage, brainstorming is necessary to consolidate the various subsidiary ideas that may come up.  This is my first time using design thinking tools and from what I read, I find the Mind Mapping tool very  useful as it allows to present the information in a visually brain-friendly method [1].

Application

Following the guidelines provided by Joanna Chavez in her video lecture of Module 3 [2], I will  start by gathering stakeholders (about ten people) in an open space. I will then explain the main idea  and what fits and what does not. Sticky notes will be given in order for them to write their ideas and  then group them in related boards, forming clusters. I expect several boards, each representing a  theme, will be created. As stated by Joanna Chavez, this will probably be the most challenging  part as it will be necessary to break down the several, complex, ideas into simpler ones. Nevertheless,  this is the most gratifying process. The previously mentioned processes represent the what is step.

Following comes the what if step, where possible solutions must be found in order to overcome the  design challenges provided by the previous step (what is).

Insight & Approach

I expect that by applying the Mind Mapping tool, a lot of insights will be clarified for future stages of the  project. As mentioned previously, this is the first design thinking tool that I will use. During the real  experience, there is a big possibility that new challenges will appear, which I must overcame. Experience  provides better knowledge so in the future I will use other design thinking tools in order to strive for  better results.

In order to design the solution, first we have to get a good understanding of the problem that we are  trying to solve. Interviews, observations, desk research and other research techniques that are applied  during this phase generate huge amount of data – data that has to be grouped and analyse. My  business is not in one place and my people work far from home and I have to keep tread on all these  activities?

Creating an activity wall is a great way to display insights, photos, and locations, all the relevant activity  outputs in one place. This approach helps us build connections between different findings and  understand the bigger picture. The visual aspect of the wall triggers idea generation and enables  project members to better understand activity insights. For this reason, design thinkers often use tools  such as persona which give a face to the customer/interviewee.

Visual tools that can be used for understanding the problem are for e.g. personas, mind map, customer  journey maps, mood board, photo safari.

Application:

In his book Change by Design, Tim Brown states that drawing for designers is a way to express their  ideas and only drawing “can simultaneously reveal both the functional characteristics of an idea and  its emotional content.” It is not necessary to poses good drawing skills, as the popular saying goes  “picture is worth a thousand words” and even a simple sketch can tell us more than a 10 minutes’  description of an idea. In a group setting, visualization helps to spark idea generation. Seeing what  other people are drawing, adding elements to their drawing or simply discussing the sketches helps  to build on top of each other’s ideas. The Good Kitchen Story also made reference to this tool as it was used  to prototype the different solutions that came forth from the ‘‘what if’’  workshops.

We collated data from the feedback gathered from prospective employees who  went through our Recruitment process or had experienced a touch point of our  process. The challenge was to improve the financial situation of these farmers by  providing them with a source of self-sustaining income.     My colleagues and I paid many visits to their households and gathered data like their financial  troubles, their other income sources if any, cause of their current situation and more. On  accumulating sufficient data and brainstorming  for several sessions we thought of setting up a  farmers market in our vicinity, this because from the data collected we found that one of the  reasons for insufficient income was the presence of middlemen in the whole buying and selling  operation which meant high possibilities of exploitation. Hence we came up with a solution  which would eliminate the middlemen and provide farmers a sustainable income source.    SELECTION     Setting up a farmers market was the solution to the challenge we came up with but to put this  into reality was difficult and a risky affair, hence we tried the learning launch design tool which  generally speaking is just a small trial experiment where one could try out one solution and see  if the solution is viable. text: Challenge  I am leading a product development team of a company specialising in building IT systems  for government entities. The acquisition of consumer data is fundamental to the system, in  order to build downstream application to support business functions of our customers.  Although the data is acquired through third party providers, using agreed methods, one of  our key customers has highlighted a concern about the poor quality of the data received  from the third parties and lack of systems tools to efficiently identify third parties which are  not complying with the data requirements.     Following an initial engagement with the customer to understand  their problems, we have  done some brainstorming internally to build a prototype for a data quality tool to assist  customers with identification of compliance issues and subsequent engagement with third  parties to address those issues in an efficient manner. The challenge is to build a solution  which is fit for purpose and can be deployed quickly for customer feedback. The portfolio  team has agreed to fund a 3-month project with the relevant resources. Our sales team will  help us to organise testing of the first prototype with a key customer organisation. The sales  team will also help to us to demonstrate prototype to two other customers to build a  product roadmap for other customers.    Selection    We have decided to use the learning launch tool. This will help us build an effective tool that  our customer can use to monitor any data quality compliance issues. We have done some  initial definition of the problem with a customer and worked with our own subject matter  experts to come up with a prototype. Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge and Selection    The tool I used is Mind Mapping, to look for patterns and insights in the comments of

my team during the pandemic. The challenge we have is to develop a nice system of

communication that will allow us to share information easily and to maintain a sense

of purpose and belonging in the team and also not decrease productivity.    The organization is digitally centered, we develop a design and video templates that

anyone can make online and use for their business. But, we have never worked

remotely before, so we have to face the new challenge of team communication so

the workflow could work in these conditions. During the firsts weeks with this

modality of working, the operative members start to wonder how they can migrate

their necessities of the normal pipeline into the work from home scheme. We receive

many questions, and also some complaints about the organization system.    Some of the key concepts the admin team have to start working on were: How does

the backup system would work out if we could not use the server remotely, How we

could keep the same sense of purpose and collaboration in the team, How can we

give the necessary information to each member so they could work individually and

resolve their doubts if they will not be anyone there to help them, How can we still

keep and touch and have active listening to share concerns and make

improvements.    After we identify the main problems we were facing as a team, with the comments of

the members. I decided to implement the design tool of the Mind Mapping, so we

could easily visualize the possible options to resolve the inconveniences that the

pandemic can cause into the team. And then start to make some tests about those

options and get insights with the team.    Application    I start the process by putting in the center of the canvas the context of the problem,

text:
Example Reflection- Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Mind Mapping, to achieve the shared objective of my manufacturing  organization and subsequently it leads to customer satisfaction and enhance brand goodwill in the  market. Being a part of 2 wheeler automobile sector as a quality assurance manager, I frequently came  across with critical defect termed “Part Mismatch”. In automobile manufacturing process, there are  several different types of vehicles models/variants assembled at the same time. This leads to enhance  the possibility of part mismatch/interchange among various models/variants and subsequently results  non conformity of quality standards. Challenge was tangible: Identify & eliminate the process lacuna and  upgrade the skill set of employees in assembly process.

Application

I started the process by analyzing past data of all type of part mismatch cases. It helped in looking for  patterns & themes in data. Process & employee are the two variables which contribute in defect  generation. In manufacturing process change in sequence of vehicle assembly incorporated in  accordance with its attributes like color/model, this results in creating pattern of part recognition for  employees indulge in assembly process. Employees were educated for key visual change point  identification, specifically during convergence of model/variant. It assisted them in reorganization of  inter-model & intra-model part mismatch. Let’s understand with an example for better visualization:

A company produce 3 products titled A, B & C at an assembly line. There are numerous parts which are  interchangeable among them. Sequence of production fixed in a certain way (i.e. BAC) to standardize  the process and pattern reorganization. This leads to assist employees in mismatch identification as they  are now aware about production sequence. Visual identification of mismatch know how were imparted  to them for easy identification of defects.

When I'm faced with a problem, I typically start by doing research or looking at  examples of how this problem has been solved by others. From that research,  I'm able to decide which approach to solving the problem works best for me  and the organization. Then, I decide what actions need to be taken to solve the  problem, and I start putting the process into motion while communicating with  my managers and co-workers.

When I was working as a retail manager, I had a customer who came in to pick  up a dress that she had ordered online. But when I went to collect her order, I  found that the dress had accidentally been put back on the sales floor and  purchased by another customer. I called another of our store locations and  asked them to hold the same dress in the customer's size. I had it shipped to  her home within 2 days for free. A week later, I found out that the customer  had called our corporate headquarters to mention how much she appreciated  the gesture

Reflection – Storytelling Tool

Challenge

A common challenge that I have experienced throughout the general manufacturing industry, is hiring,  retention, and development of direct labor employees.  Often, direct labor employees come and go  frequently, staying for short terms, leaving the existing front-line supervisors and company management  feeling jaded, frustrated, and impatient.  This results in non-existent or unstructured development and  team engagement strategies, as the leadership team assumes, they will be of no use, as each new  employee is just temporarily passing through, until they have proven otherwise by staying after ‘x’  months or years.  The issue with this, is the cause and effect perhaps should be flipped.  We stand a  higher chance of the employee staying if we strategize and execute development activities frequently,  rather than make those activities dependent on whether the employee shows interest and achieves a  long enough tenure.  I am sure this is not a novel idea, as I have read and discussed this on numerous  occasions with many industry professionals, and quite frankly this is a best practice instilled by many  companies globally.  However, the execution of this is still a challenge in many companies and  leadership teams.  And although there are plenty of options around what those strategies and  approaches look like to engage direct labor employees, I would like to focus more on how this challenge  extends to the stakeholders in the previous step, which are the frontline leaders, and how their buy-in is  just as important.  Initial feedback from the frontline leaders was that pay wage was the biggest driving  factor in this challenge.  However, interviews with the direct labor employees painted a different  picture. text:
Reflection – Mindmapping

Challenge & Selection

The most used tool I used at work would be the mindmapping tool due to the need for constant  ideation. This provides a systematic approach to log everything that could be linked to the main  theme. With this tool, the final solution and how it connects to the main theme can be mapped out.  One of the most recent application is the mapping out of what goes into a certain application at  work, as part of the brainstorming session that we have.

Application

The theme was first selected. This was followed by what are the different things related to the main  theme. If the things are one or two levels down, linkages are drawn to show how they are  connected. Typically, once the ideas for a certain branch run out, the team will move on and come  back again to add on if there are relevant ideas discussed along the way. At the end of the day, once  the related ideas to the theme has been mapped, the team can look at categorizing them and  subsequent next steps.

Insight & Approach

Mindmap does not apply just for ideation. It helps to conceptualize thoughts and them into words  and show their relevant linkages. I think that beyond ideation, it can be used for root cause analysis,  to pinpoint what could be the causal factors for certain things that happened. It is a generally useful  tool, which can be done on boards or readily available freeware. At the end of the day, I think a good  tool like this, as well as many others, should not be confined to what they were originally developed.  The key thing, as what is in this course, is to think out of the box and apply things as and when it can  be used.

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

I used the strategy of visualization to describe the confusing contents of one project. When I  was in the human resource department in a student organization, I was in charge of a new  program to support new members. Although I successfully generate the framework of the  program, I found it difficult to convey what it was like. My project was called “Seido,” the Neighbors Project in Japanese, which included a system of paring new members and  senior members to let each new member have an accessible supporter. Although I had to  differentiate my project from the mentor system, which had already existed in my organization,  I was always told that my program was a resemblance to it. Some of my colleagues said to me  that my program was unique and helpful, so I decided not to give up and changed the way I  explained my project.

To tackle this problem, I made use of the benefits of visualization. As Angela Myer said in her  video, visualization helps you to convey what you want to say to others without confusion. It  was difficult to differentiate the contents of my project, especially about the role of the  supporters, from that of the mentor system. While the mentors worked as advisors to help junior  members work on their tasks, the supporters in my project were defined as guides to make new  members familiar with my organization and have more psychological safety. I decided to use  images to depict this role of the supporters to the participants.

RE-DESIGNING HR, LEARNING & DEVELOPMENT IN OUR COMPANY

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

In a recent staff survey many features of the HR, learning and development function were  criticised as being less effective than they could be. In comparison to other aspects of being an  employee, certain activities such as appraisal, supervision, talent management, training and  development received markedly lower scores. Staff also felt detached from and unaware of the  overall corporate strategy and felt that senior leaders were distant from operations teams on the  ground. The OD department was asked to tackle this challenge and begin work re-designing  internal HR, learning and development services to be a more effective driver of staff satisfaction  and business growth.

2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you

selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

I selected the tool of storytelling – Brandon Hernandez the CLO at Mars described the process in his  week 2 video interview as conveying logical messages through stories about an organisation,  from the perspective of people and their experiences, incorporating emotion and making clear a  larger organisational purpose.  I agree this would be more powerful than assembling a list or  matrix of service elements and mapping these to different categories of employee.  I wanted to  make the concepts “come alive” by fictionalising how an employee with particular needs and  circumstances might experience the newly designed service elements.  This particularly allows  us to sell the “challenges” inherent in current employee realities, which colleagues would  identify with and consider how the new proposed service would be a better response than  existing approaches. Challenge: I work for the consulting wing of a large IT Company, mainly consulting on Change  Management and Organizational Transformation. During a pitch to a Financial Services client, the team  was unable to create a create a slides deck that looked meaningful from the client’s perspective and  would attract the client for further conversation about our consulting offerings and how we could help  them transform their IT Vertical to keep pace with the future growth of the company given that the  company went through a larger merger recently.

Selection: To create an interactive presentation that resonated with the client, we selected the  storytelling tool. We selected the tool to create a movie-like scenario where the movie reveals itself in  an engaging, yet sequential manner. It also because we understood that creating our pitch like a story  that unfolds at every turn will help us have an interactive discussion where we are helping the client  with their problem rather than one-sided conversation where we are trying to sell something.

Application: I along with a team of 3 first understood the current requirements of the clients, the  challenges that they were currently facing and their aspirations for the future. Taking all those inputs  along with secondary research data, we created a strawman for our presentation that ran like a tale that  needed to be told. After the strawman, we create individual parts of the deck reinforcing that part of the  story in detail. We filled the slides with information collected thus far with our approach. We also tried  to show visually how the future IT Vertical of the company would look like using references, best  practices, etc. We kept our complete deck as pictorial as possible as images and videos are easier to  relate than words. This helped us in creating an engaging interaction with the clients and getting the  contract for Organizational Transformation Consulting.

CHALLENGES:

I start with a storytelling tool  because  stories help us relate and are memorable  ,  they can ground business stategy and be a powerful tool in any stage of the  innovation process. This undertstanding also holds true in the business world ,where an organization’s  stories , and the stories its leaders tell ,help solidify relationship in way that  factual statements encapsulated in bullet point.

Elisa Ingram

Design Thinking for Innovation

18 January 2018

Reflection - Visualization

Challenge & Selection  I regularly use the tool of visualization to gain a shared understanding in diﬀerent

situations:

When the scope of a concept is unclear because diﬀerent stakeholders use diﬀerent terms

to describe the same object or the same term to describe diﬀerent objects

When the boundaries of one kind of requirement to a diﬀerent kind of requirement are

fuzzy

When user groups of any kind of solution are not properly deﬁned, not selective or

selectable

In my projects to design and architect digital solutions for diﬀerent user groups, it is

essential to have a common understanding of user groups, user needs, and solution

boundaries. Words alone, even when arranged in tables are not suﬃcient to get a clear

picture of what word or label is describing which part of the concept.

Application  We start the process by collecting the central terms, requirement classes, user personae and

groups and trying to bring one object in connection with all other objects. Instead of using

one of the standardized notations of the Object Management Group or similar bodies - like

eg UML - we use an open discussion in front of a ﬂipchart or on a piece of paper. Together

we draw pillars, quadrants, overlapping circles or a spectrum of diﬀerent classes sorted by a

speciﬁc criterion.

�1

Consider diﬀerent types of digital interaction channels with established, current, or future

user interfaces. The team came up with ideas of using mobile apps, sending eMail, oﬀering a

web portal, chats or bots. Which seems to be an selection of ideas, some of them

overlapping, like chats or bots.

Reflection - Learning Launch

Challenge

I am the founder of a company, Which deals in logistics. I take care of all the major strategies  to improve the efficiency in the organization. My/Our Challenge is a wastage of man-hours  due to inefficiency in the process. We have a transport onboarding department in place which  takes care of onboarding the transporters on our platform, But this process takes a long time  due to the inefficiencies in the process. As reported by our field executives, the transporters  take a long time to meet our executives as the meeting is not scheduled on a prior basis. The  average onboarding time of each transporter is around 2 days. The major reasons behind this  delay are

1)Field executives directly reach out to the transporters in the market without any prior  interview scheduled

2)Transport industry is quite an old school, so the transporters don’t act professionally

3)It takes 3-4 follow-ups after meeting to get all the required documents from the transporters

We will try to reduce the inefficiencies in the process by applying design thinking

​Selection

Our marketing team believes that if we advertise online and get the required documents on  phone followed by the field visit, we can substantially cut down the cost and time for each  conversion. The new process is completely different from what we were using previously so  we need to experiment with it to check its efficiency. So we are ready to use the learning  launch tool, Broadly speaking learning launch is an experiment meant to quickly test an idea.  The purpose of a learning launch is not to prove you've got a good idea. The purpose of a  learning launch is to get the truth and then the truth either confirms or dis-confirms your  assumptions. text:
Videocall Shop

Challenge.   I work in a company of a phone application dedicated to selling items via internet,  specifically by videocalls. The main objective is that potential buyers can communicate  in a permanent and instantaneous way with the sellers. Every question buyers want to  ask, can be answered by the seller during a videocall, which is the best way to  communicate online, to avoid misunderstandings and be clear and precise about the  product’s characteristics. Although it is an interesting service, there were few shops  using this method. Videocall shop consumers’ needed to pay fifty (50) dollars per  month in order to sell their products. My idea was to change this method of payment  into a method based on commissions per sell.      Selection.   I decided to go for the Learning Launch Tool. This tool consists on testing a prototype  in several small and cheap experiments. In this way, it is possible to test which aspects  of an idea are correct, and which ones are not but can be modified. In addition, it is  possible to collect information from different places so as to reach a conclusion.      Application.  Firstly, I decided to contact some of the shops that were once users of the app, but  were not anymore. One of their principal causes for them to stop using it was its cost.  They explained that paying 50 dollars per month was no longer a reasonable cost.  Most app users are dedicated to selling small and cheap products. They did not want  to pay a cost they were not sure it would be profitable. So they decided not to take  that risk.  When I proposed to them to pay a fee only for each product they sold, many changed  their minds about Videocall Shop. Paying a commission per sale allowed them to have  some flexibility, as they were not forced to cover the cost. The program can be used to visualize data stored in CSV, TAB, or TSV files. The graph view  allows you to see the relationship between your data's dimensions. The data is represented as a  network of nodes connected by lines.

You can create a compelling visual tale from your raw data with the correct tools. Here are some  data visualization tools that are both free and open source: This open source tool can be used to  create beautiful data visualizations if you know Javascript.

For your convenience, we've compiled a list of the most popular free and commercial Data  Visualization Software, along with comparisons and website links. Xplenty is a data integration  platform in the cloud that prepares data for your data visualization software. It is capable of  integrating data from over 100 data stores and SaaS applications.

The following types of visualizations are appropriate for creating a comparison chart: 1 Column  Diagram 2 Graph in Bullets 3 Mekko Diagram Four Pie Charts Graph with 5 Bars 6 Line  Diagram Scatter Plot 7

We live in the data age. Without it, your company will not be able to reach its full potential.  However, if you don't understand what the data means, it won't help your business.

This is where data visualization can help. Data visualization tools take your data and present it to  you in the form of charts, graphs, and dashboards, allowing you to gain easy-to-understand  insights.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation Assignment  Mind Mapping for Recycling Contamination  Note: Due to the ongoing coronavirus outbreak, it is not possible to actually apply these design thinking  tools at the moment. The following is a plan for how the tools could be applied to a real problem. The  problem I am describing is a real one.

Miami-Dade County’s Department of Solid Waste Management (DSWM) provides solid waste collection  services to over 330,000 households in the County’s unincorporated area as well as contracted  municipalities. This includes biweekly curbside collection of recyclable materials such as paper, cans,  bottles, cartons, and cardboard. The materials are placed together in a large, wheeled cart with a lid and  collected by a collection vehicle with a mechanical “arm.”  Recycling collection is currently outsourced to  a private vendor, who pays the County a portion of the revenue received from the sale of recyclable  materials.

A major problem currently facing DSWM, and solid waste entities nationwide, is a high rate of  contamination in residents’ carts. Contamination occurs when residents place materials in the cart that  are not recyclable, such as diapers or food waste. Another form of contamination occurs when residents  place materials that might be recyclable under certain conditions, but not through the curbside  collection program. This is often known as “aspirational recycling” and examples include the placement  of egg cartons or plastic bags in the bin; these products are commonly recyclable at local grocery stores,  but not curbside. Unfortunately, a high contamination rate results in less material being recycled and  presents risks of revenue reductions or even service disruptions (if the service is no longer profitable).  DSWM has expended considerable resources on resident education, but the problem has persisted.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I was working on the flagship project of the socio-entrepreneurship organisation of my university.  The problem we were dealing with was that of ill management of solid waste in India. What sparked  us to do something tangible about it was a landfill collapse that caused death of a dozen  ‘underprivileged’ people who picked up recyclable waste and lived close to the location of landfill.  We realized the impact of it is, deep and multi-dimensional.  We conducted a research, the major takeaway of which was that maximum amount (up to 50%) of  waste was organic kitchen waste which can easily be treated at home via a simple age-old  technique, composting. We thought, that is it. We just have to make composters and the major part  of the problem will be solved. What we realized after one-to-one human conversations with the  consumers and manufacturers is that more than the problem of waste management itself, we have  to deal with a behavioural change that is difficult to embrace for the entire human race.   And during one of these one to one conversation with a 63-year old lady, we realised that to drive  this change we need to weave a story around why it is so important to do compost our own greens.    Application

We had these two lines of products, the community composter for the horticulture waste and home  composter for the kitchen greens. The community composter was being manufactured by small  scale ironsmith industries and the home composter was a 3-tier terracotta pot structure  manufactured by potter’s community in Delhi whose business was fast declining due to more  durable plastic alternatives.  For the home composter, the consumers were sceptical about this extra load of work in their already  busy life schedules and for the community composting, the community gardener couldn’t see any  incentive doing this extra work at the same wage. Challenge and Selection.

I work for one of federal telecom operators. I’m the Head of Commercial Department in one of the

regional branches. Our main product is mobile telephony including voice, SMS and 4G mobile internets.

To make it more clear the company sells connection kits including SIM-cards with prepaid tariff plan.

Every day we face a great challenge to acquire new subscribers and retain the existing ones as the

competition environment is relentless. The basic channel of distribution is our own retail network. It

consists of mono-brand shops, where a customer can buy our product, connect/disconnect different

services, ask for advice, etc. To increase the customers’ traffic in some of our mono-brand shops

collaboration with the coffee shops was made. The idea was that customers of the coffee shop would

convert in new mobile network users. After couple of months the idea seemed to fail, as the traffic

increased, but the conversion decreased, it was not the result we expected, because that meant that new

customers buying coffee passed by products and services we offer.

So we were to start with question number one «What is?» to find out what the problem is. First we tried

to apply standard analytical approach, but didn’t get any distinct answer. So the alternative approach was

to apply one of the design thinking tools presented in the course. The tool we used was the tool of

Visualization. The idea was to imagine and design a kind of a simple customer journey map for two types

of customers: 1) those who comes only for the coffee and 2) those who comes only for mobile services

and then understand, how these groups of customers move physically inside the shop space. So when we

talk about imagination and visual thinking the tool of Visualization is the best choice. Concerning that

challenge it is the tool to identify pain points and find opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Challenge

I am the operations manager for my international company’s Asian business.  We service the engineering and  architectural design industry and my staff consists of 50 people spread over 6 departments.

We have had just over 5 years of rapid growth with some major success, but I have noticed recently a lack of  production and a decline in quality. To our credit we have retained the majority of our staff over our time of  operations therefore I needed to analyze the current state of operations, our projects and production to determine  what was first failing, and second how to fix the issues.

Part of my role was to restructure the company in an effort to improve efficiencies, production and sales.  To do this  required me to gather the key stakeholders across our departments to determine what we considered to be ineffective  or problematic with regard to the business.

There have been many times over the years where we have addresses some issues in an isolated context and have  generally used assumptions and biases to propose solutions which in general have had limited affects. Our team has  already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to try the learning launch tool.

Selection

I plan to keep the learning launch experimental meant to quickly test an idea and prototype quickly, seeing results  (positive or negative) early.

Application

In the weeks leading up to what I planned would be a learning launch, I individually interviewed each department,  spending time watching how they interacted with their counterparts in other countries and within their team.  Independently of all of the departments I used SWOT analysis to identify common and unique strengths, weaknesses  opportunities and threats that I could use as a basis for initiating agile projects aimed at addressing the outcomes.

Assignment – Reflection – Mind mapping

by Wellington Silva

1. Challenge

There are many actions that we want to do but we are insecure, however if we use the

correct methods we can facilitate the way we carry out our projects. I have a research project that needed to be done, but I was unsure. However, I realized that I could overcome this challenge by using some sort of tool because I knew what I needed to do, but I needed to keep everything organized in the sequence of steps and relationships between ideas. The project was a research on social entrepreneurship and its relation to social innovation. The purpose was to make an article that could  bring  the  relationships  between  the  dimensions  and  concepts  involved  in  the  social entrepreneurship and social innovation from the studies made in the two themes. So what was needed had already been done that was the study of the two themes, but what was missing was to make the relationship between the two. Hence the need for a tool to assist in this process and to achieve better success in this challenge.

2. Selection

From the characteristics of the presented challenge, the best way I found to unite the

concepts of social entrepreneurship and social innovation was to use the mind mapping tool. As said in the course video: "Mind Mapping is looking for patterns and insights in a large amount of data collected during your exploration of what the current reality is" and in this sense the large amount of readings I performed needed this kind of exploration and Analysis trying in a more synthetic and visual way to identify the common points for the approaches of the chosen themes. In this sense, the selection of the tool was adequate for this phase of the solution of the problem for the creation of the article because it shapes what is needed for this moment.

Example Reflection – “Story Telling”

Challenge & Selection:

Storytelling is one of the key tools that can be used in many cases, stories that are meant to inspire  employees, persuade investors, win customers, crafting a compelling narrative is vital to an  organization’s success. Storytelling also improves the understanding of a Business process and its  interconnected process. When Storytelling is combined with Visualization it turns out be a very powerful  combination. Product Branding is all about Storytelling. A Brand represents a promise to the customer, a  promise of what the customer would get or even what they will feel when they own it. It’s the promise  to meet a set of expectations that the customer carry about a Brand. How do we set a promise in place?  How do we deliver a promise to the customer? How do we compare with our competitors?

What’s the best way to achieve all this, while launching a new Brand? Storytelling. This complex  communication with a maximum impact can be done by Storytelling. This is a human-centered problem.  Understanding of this problem is not very clear initially, the organization has to explore the market and  launch a Brand. There are high-levels of Uncertainty. Just an Rollin mentions, “As humans we  respond to stories, they can help us develop deeper empathy in the present and create more vivid  imagery of the new future we are trying to create. Paying attention to the human dimension is  important. To do all these we need a learning mindset, a prepared mind to tap into opportunities.” Not  building a convincing story is potentially result in failure of Brand Launch. Deploying Storytelling toolkit  as part of Design Thinking can increase the likelihood of a Brand’s success.

Challenge:   The challenge I encountered can be described as finding the target audience and the  need for developing a modular kitchen design for different sized offices. Specifically, as  a group project, I have worked on designing a modular kitchen for a wide range of office  environments. During this design process, one of the most important aspects of our  thinking was based on defining and understanding our target audience and clients. As a  group, we have visited several startups and companies around the area and conducted  interviews. After the interviews, the main challenge was to discuss and present our  findings from the interviews to our group members and define a shared problem space  for our selected audience.     Selection:   I selected the visualization tool for the challenge of defining a problem space for modular  kitchen design and selecting the target audience. Visualization is a tool that people can  use to define a tangible, concrete outcome of your findings. By using visualization, people  can visualize and create a common perspective in their minds about a specific problem.  Hence, I wanted to use this tool for my own challenge as I thought explaining and  visualizing our findings from the interviews would help us improve our common, design  perspective.     Application:   I applied the visualization tool in many different stages of the defined challenge. First, as  stated before, I have conducted many interviews with employees of different companies.  During these interviews, apart from asking about their specific needs in kitchens, I simply  handed them a small piece of paper and asked them to draw an ideal kitchen component  that they want to see in an office and how they would use such a component in their best  ability. STORYTELLING

These stories connect with the  emotions, characters, the value of people, every day, using the product. As a  student it is quite tricky to understand the process of storytelling, as not being  as experienced as the experts. For example, while presenting in the class, it  becomes a challenge to touch each and everyone’s mind and heart. We get too  involved in the concept that we fail to bring about stories relating towards it.  Most of the time the motivational speakers or any public speakers uses the  techniques or tool of storytelling in order to get connected with the audience  and to build emotional and deeper connectivity with the speaker. Storytelling is  a great way to make your consumers use your products with much deeper  thought towards it. Any speaker going on about his product launch with a deep  and insightful story, maybe regarding his personal experiences, creates more  value to the product and services that he is rendering to the customers. As a student I would stress more on  this tool since, the way I see it whenever a lecturer tries to make us  understand  about a particular topic, they usually start of with a story. It may not be a story  related towards their personal experience but, maybe relating towards the  people who built it, for instance, a product. text: Challenge & Selection    I'm a storyteller, i create approaches and purposes for corporate brands, products  and business units. This tool is very important for engage multiple stakeholders.  Nowadays, the companies must have a coherence between what they are (mission,  vision and values) and what really they do. As important as coherence is how the  companies shows that do it.    So, when we talk about the storytelling for the companies, we are talking about a  deep resarch about the market, about the others players, the customers,  governaments and all actores are envolved in the bussiness map. And, the last, how  choise the communications chanells, brand voice, style and tone, beeing leader of  the market.    As a company leader of the market, you need to lead innovation in your industry  before your competition does. You need to set the pace, set the course of business.  As a market leader, you need to maintain innovation leadership before competitors  innovate.    In a highly competitive industry, such as banking, fear of failure can be crucial. And  fail trying something new is, undoubtedly, crucial to a career. This is because it's  impossible for a brand deginer think to have a chance to reposition a brand after an  innovation (or lack of an innovation) resulted in the stock market crash.    Application    The year was 2013, i worked for a big bank that was sponsor of national team soccer  and the worldcup.     Our main competitor in business took a stance of showing their customers that their  bank didn't sponsor major events because they acted on little projects that could  really change for the better the lives of each of their customers.    They created a partnership with a city hall of a big city. In this partnership, this bank  afforded a safe cycleway every weekend. It was enoth, the brand of this bank was in  every place on weekends, being remembered by the population of one city woth 12  millions of people. Low cost and very close of the customers.
