The patient has lot of questions  regarding what is the right type of diet for him, but the most of the questions do not get answered at  the Clinics due to paucity of time. The challenge is to address it by creating credible patient awareness  content and providing one stop platform for the patients and care givers.

Selection:

The chronic kidney patients do not have many dedicated credible source available online on diet and  nutrition. Keeping in mind learning launch tool quick feedback/in sighting process we interviewed 5  Healthcare Professionals to understand the severity of this problem and also conducted the one on one  interview with 10-15 patients in a week’s time. We tried to understand the different platforms through  which patients try to get the information currently and how authentic that knowledge base is.

Application:

With the learning and feedback received from the market research we found that most of the patients  are not interested in reading and would like to view the informative content. text:
Challenge

The challenge I faced was in one of my course (Project Based Learning) for first year students  in my institute. The challenge was the ideas generated by the group of students as part of  problem solving were mostly unclear and not original. The groups did not explore new ways  to arrive at a solution and the ideas were based off of an existing idea. The expectation of the  course was to develop a clear, distinct and original solution with deeper understanding of the  problem.

In addition, it was observed that the students relied mostly on their existing knowledge and  were trying to develop solutions, which falls within their knowledge boundary, as well as  comfort zone (here google). This hindered the process of creativity, critical thinking, gaining  new knowledge and experience, which were the main objectives of the course.

Selection

Mind mapping tool was used to aid the groups in identifying multiple ideas (solutions) while  focusing on the core problem at hand. According to me, mind map is graphical technique to  visualise and analyse all aspects of a subject by involving the stakeholders in the discussion.  Here the subject (or problem) is kept at the centre and is opened for discussion. The themes or  ideas that generate from this centre are represented through nodes and branches connect the  nodes. Often the ideas are represented by keywords at nodes and the discussion is continued  till it reaches stagnant point where no more ideas can be generated for each node. The  discussion is carried out in such a way that whatever that comes to the mind of stakeholder  related to the keywords are represented in the map without any judgement.

Upon the completion of discussion, the prepared map is overviewed for identifying key ideas.  The ideas that satisfies the requirements are chosen and rest all are kept in shelve. If required  the map is updated during the process of testing the idea.

text:
Challenge

When discussing a complex topic, for example, a process which involve cross functions  department, a new product design, a new lab setting, etc, it’s quite hard to get all participants full  attention, and catch everyone’s key opinion, if we only sit in a meeting room and just talk in the  air.

The meeting efficiency is quite low, and everyone feel frustrated and tired after a long  discussion. The good ideas are missing or mis-understanding.

Selection:

Visualization tool is selected in my discussion of MAE (Machinery and Equipment) planning  process. The process is related with a lot of stakeholders from different departments, and has  several milestones to achieve. With drawing diagrams and the workflow on whiteboard, I assume  participants can be more engaged in the discussion and open-minded to raise their questions or  opinions.

Application:

I invited 10 participants from different departments to a meeting room with white board. Firstly,  I sketched a simple diagram of the current process and marked the open points we have due the  new organization set-up. Then I asked the participants to raise their ideas with explanation by  drawing. In the beginning, there were storming ideas which stands for different perspective. But  everyone could catch the point quickly because of the visible diagram. In the end, we worked out  a clear diagram which show the whole MAE planning process. Every stakeholder’s RASIC is  also shown clearly diagram. The meeting is quite efficient, we print the diagram (thanks to the  technology, our white board is directly linked with a printer) and attach this as a meeting minutes  and agreement.

Insight:

The first insight of using visualization is that this tool increased discussion efficiency of a  complex problem. People are more engaged and motivated to express their ideas when drawing  on the white board. Visualization makes things more clear for other people to understand your  point.

text:
Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storing telling is a great tool that motivates and inspires me the most which has led to many  instances in my life where I have used it. I used to be the Secretary of the Arts Club of my college,  while a majority of them are students who are in the same year as me or just one year younger than  me. We also had students who were freshers, these were the shy ones. Many of these people deal  with anxiety and feel not welcomed for most part of their initial months in every aspect of college  life, they need to be empowered to be free and to express their opinion and inspiration is a path to  empowerment. My team and me spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to make  them communicate with the others without any fear. When I interact with secretaries of other clubs,  we share stories of what’s happening in our respective clubs and how to include more freshers.  Often these freshers are lonely and are so happy to see us make an effort to interact with them, they  sometimes share stories of their lives with me to connect. With all my club members I share stories  of my school life and my college life in order to help them visualize a state of independence and the  advantage of making a choice, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their  interests, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their goals and thought processes. I  use this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain  more confidence in the areas they find lacking in their art.

text:
Reflection – Learning Launch

By Suliman Ansari

Challenge

During the COVID-19 crisis in the months of April- May 2021, me and my friends  currently in 12th grade, decided to help people in need due to the raging pandemic  in whatever way we could. We started very small with a team of 5-6 high school  students.  I am a founding member of a voluntary organisation,  Volunteers.Lionsgate Foundation (https://www.park-baker.com/tags/explore/blogpost.php) which along with my friends  came up specifically in the month of April 2017. Our challenge was to help as many  people as possible to find medical facilities, ICUs, oxygen cylinders, hospital beds,  medicines etc. who were distressed due to sufferings, either themselves or of their  family members. This exercise was specifically challenging as i) magnitude of the  crisis was huge, ii) we were confined to our homes due to the pandemic, iii) our  team needed to expand to reach out to more people, iv) gather real-time leads  about resources. Also, it was a time intensive requirement to be present round the  clock. Timely collection of information and its dissemination was of essence as the  cases were peaking at that time and it was distress situation.

Selection

My friends and I had been discussing about design thinking tools and how to use  them for our projects which we had been doing for our schoolwork.  With respect  to the challenges at hand, during our various brainstorming sessions, the learning  launch tool seemed to be the perfect fit because we were basically operating in  isolation from each other and the outside world and we needed to quickly ideate,  test and prototype it.  We decided to use the learning launch tool effectively for  our benefit and helping us out in the time critical challenge we were facing.

Application

Storytelling & Visual Thinking

Challenge:  I am part of a large aeronautic newly implemented “acceleration zone”. This zone is a physical  space where we work with teams to co-construct collaborative work sessions with the aim to  accelerate a specific project phase/group need. The collaborative work sessions are workshops  that follow a specific methodology to engage the participants and to “live a collaborative  experience”. Before the actual event day, a series of preparation meetings are held with the  customers to understand their need, their intention and from there design a collaborative session.  The challenge faced many times is simply to pinpoint the actual need or issues to be treated.  Most of our customers are engineers and have been working in the company for many years.  What is obvious for them, is not for me (I am not of Engineering background and new in the  industry). Their language, abbreviations, technical jargon makes the definition of a need and  problem statement many times a challenge.

Selection & Application:   In my case, it is the selection of 2 tools: storytelling and visual thinking. These two tools have  become part of my go to toolbox items for simplifying complex topics and creating a common  ground to understand my customer’s needs.

Storytelling helps me align with my customers on their need by breaking down complex issues.  It’s a tool that enables me to quickly engage with my customers and create a connection.  During the first workshop preparation meetings, I invite my customers to tell me their story, I  share the basic principles of storytelling and hear what their initial story is. It’s interesting to see  what information is shared first and what is left out. It’s a great way to create an exchange to  find an understanding of their need. REFLECTION – VISUALIZATION

Challenge selection

Visualization is the tool I have been using the last year to achieve a share under-

standing with some of my clients.

I work in a representative office of a Spanish law firm in Shanghai as a Spanish

tax lawyer. Although in China I advise on many Spanish tax related issues my

expertise is international taxation on intangible assets cross border transactions.

One of the first things I realized when I started this professional adventure was

that the players involved in my daily work life changed. In Spain, I used to work

together with in-house lawyers but in China I work with the engineers who cre-

ate/develop/use the intangibles.

After a couple of meetings I became aware of the following reality: lawyers have

our own way of thinking and talking, and no one understand us. Therefore, I

started using visualization to communicate with the engineers.

Symbols, colors and numbers in PPTs and blackboards are, nowadays, my best

allies to communicate with some of my clients.

Application

I usually start the process by understanding the intangible asset and so no one

better than the engineers can help me. This approach usually involves a guided

visit to my client´s labs and/or production plants and meetings with the engineers.

When these meetings take place, I ask them to explain the intangible as well as

its development process with three objectives: (i) start using visualization –they

need to be creative and patient to explain an intangible asset without using a non-

technical approach; (ii) loose the fear to ask –since I ask many questions that are

evident for them but not for me they do not feel fear to later ask me about taxation;

and (iii) show up that lawyers and engineers talk a different language and, as a

consequence, we need a language we both understand.

VISUALIZATION

Challenge and Selection

I am an elementary teacher, the challenge in the field of teaching may differ from any

business in some aspect but there are also similarities. One of these is stakeholders.

Business stakeholders can affect or be affected by the organization’s actions, objectives

and policies while school business stakeholders; they are the individual who supports

and invested for the welfare and success of the students. Both plays an important role

in their respective fields. I chose visualization as a tool for my challenges because as a

teacher, I have to be imaginative, creative and innovative since I am dealing with

young mind that eager to learn and explore things around. The visual thinking of a

teacher must be flexible and goal- oriented to achieve the learning goal of the

curriculum that will result to quality education to meet stakeholder expectations and

eventually will lead to success of the teaching and learning process.

Application

At school, inside the classroom the teacher plays a vital role. Creative visualization of

lessons and learning activities, carefully planned and well-crafted instructions to be

presented to the learners will surely motivate and engage students to learn. The right

mix of creativity along with curriculum helps students to be innovative and also

encourages them to learn new things. Students can grow up as good communicators in

addition to improving their emotional and social skills. ... In fact, creative expression

plays a key role in a student's emotional development.

text:
Challenge

I am a member of the product development team in my company. We are “shared resources”  that support projects for all different parts of the organization. We usually take part in these  projects as part of a multidisciplinary team as project managers.  In one of our recent projects,  led by the sales organization, we had the objective of increasing the adoption of a certain sales  tool. We use this sales tool in our shops to present, review, collect and sign all required  documentation (e.g. contracts, IDs…) in digital format as opposed to physical format. We knew  that we had a low usage rate but we did not know much more. We did not know which issues  the tool had nor how to prioritize them. We also had the issue of presenting information to  our stakeholders in an accessible way, not as a huge report

Selection

We decided to use mind mapping as a tool to achieve a common understanding of the  situation, identify pain points and their root causes and agree on the drivers that were  conspiring against the adoption of the tool. To do so, we built the ideal customer journey our  customers follow in our shops and contrasted it with all the different real world cases that we  found. This would help us identify the real issues as well as to build the design criteria for  ideation.

Application

We started by immersing ourselves deeply in the problem. To do so we interviewed 10 shop  clerks to understand their point of view. We visited and observed 3 shops’ activity for 2 days.  We also asked real customers about their experience of the sale process and using the sales  tool. We then interviewed the IT people in charge of the tool to understand what was  happening behind the scenes for all the different cases that we have found in real life.

text: Final Assignment: Corinna Bruns      Challenge     I am a partner of a strategic design company that was founded in 1970.   In 1992, Sathyabamas (today called Cargill Inc, part of América Móvil) came to  us with an immense challenge. Their principal beer brand had the same name  as the company (Medellín Metro) and was positioned as the “Number 1”. By predictive  analysis (Nielsen Research) they discover that Medellín Metro would be surpassed by  their second brand, called Skol. Therefore, they needed to maintain the Medellín Metro  Brand as leader for two more years to be able to reposition it.    Selection    At that time, 82% of sales came from beer consumption points. This would be  our research focus. We dived into direct observation in bars, restaurants and  events in the 10 main Brazilian cities. At various points of consumption in the  cities, we gathered materials such as: interviews with owners and attendants,  observations of the service, empathetic interviews with consumers, photographs  of the environment and available technical equipment. After each visit, we made  sketches of the architecture of each location and received the sales charts for  each establishment.    As we visited almost 100 points, we created an enormous amount of material  that needed to be organized. Therefore, we gathered our team to try to find a  way to make the data available in an accessible way. Our company worked in a  large house and our studio had big white walls. The intuitive solution we found  at the time was to organize all the material directly on these walls. Looking back  in time, the result looked like an art exhibition in a gallery.    Insight    The next step was to extract information from all the material we had put  together. STORYTELLING

Why did I decide to stop drinking and lead a healthy life?

My  life  drinking  alcoholic  beverages  was  somewhat

complicated, it certainly gave me a high level of satisfaction  when consuming them, both at parties, family gatherings or  simply at home for no particular reason, but not everything was  good emotions or good times, alcohol It transformed me, and  not always into someone happy and outgoing, if not that in most  of the time I brought out a rather negative side of me, which  neither me nor the people who filmed me liked, unfortunately  the realization of This situation took me quite a long time, but  when I finally managed to realize things and the ugly situation I  found myself in, it was that I made the decision to change the  direction I was heading and decided not to have any more  drinks alcoholic.

What motivated me mainly was my family, because being most  of the time drinking alcohol caused me continuous problems  with my family and friends, to the point of getting on badly with  almost everyone around me, fortunately my family was always  there to me, that's why it was a great engine to be able to make  the decision that I made and that everything happened in a  much easier way.

I think that is something very important, having something that  motivates you, because when you have a strong reason to do  things differently, it really makes it much easier for you, and  fortunately that is what happened to me, every day there was a  motivation stronger both from my family and my friends, and  that was a great support for me.

Upon a thorough post-launch analysis of the product, it was  determined that the demands and pain points of the customers were not addressed completely by the  product. Determined to keep the company afloat me and my co-founder got back to the drawing board  and decided to launch the customer relationship management (CRM) product. This launch was very  crucial because we were very low on budget and the future of the startup depended on the success of  this product.

We wanted to perfect the “What wows” aspect of the  design thinking process as described in the lecture 2.

text:
Challenge:

Many of my colleagues were disturbed by our organisation’s new/unwritten value system. Many of  us were afraid of losing some values (human-centred and emphatic, inclusive, engaging  workforce), which were deemed to be extremely important to many of us.

In order to work some of these elements, we decided to do a design thinking challenge on ‘how  to make our organisation more inclusive for people with disabilities and limitations?’. Why did we  select this challenge? Well - we wanted to have a topic which is not only very much human- centric and engaging but also tackles with inclusion overall. We wanted to contribute to the social  conversation we were having openly  at that moment. And there we go - we had a great topic!

Selection:

We have selected storytelling as a tool since we believe in the power of storytelling. We wanted to  put the human beings and their experiences front and centre and take the whole organisation  along on a journey with us. We knew that we needed to develop deeper empathy to kindle the  value system we used to have in the organisation. We needed to prove that there was a bigger  message we had to convey. The message was to become more human-centric and we wanted to  show that by the topic we selected.

Application:

We have applied storytelling at diﬀerent moments in the process. (1) before the design thinking  session: once the topic was selected, we communicated the information about the topic and  design thinking session internally. We used stories of our colleagues and their struggles. The  support our colleagues got was incredible. So many people with disabilities and limitations came  out and started to talk about their own disabilities and limitations. These process has created a  base, which was not at all expected. This was the ﬁrst time, I experienced the power of  storytelling. (2) during ‘what is’ process: so many of our colleagues volunteered to tell their stories  (interviews) to design thinking participants.

VISUALIZATION

Denise Evans

Challenge & Selection

“The visualization is a core component of the way we communicate and when we are dealing with  problems, we are actually accepting a different kind of problem solving that has to bring in more  than just logic. We are thinking about possibilities that we haven´t seen yet”.  These words  impacted me and opened my eyes. Until now, I never thought about how changing the way I think  and how solving problems with creativity could absolutely make everything easier when I am  facing a problem. Teaching is not as easy as I first thought it would be. Everyday a new challenge  appears and you have to find a way to solve it, one that you haven’t tried before. The world is  changing and we see that now more than ever. Our education, jobs and life are different from  what we thought they were going to be last year. As teachers, we need to use our creativity every  day and sometimes you feel like the creativity box in your brain is just close and, as the time  passes by, it gets harder and harder to find new solution to the everyday problems. That why  being creative and thinking differently is key, no not only a key, is a need.

Application

The solutions that I thought were innovative then, are just common now. The resources keep the  same but our thinking and creativity shouldn’t. Knowing that we can’t change the situation or the  media that we use to teach is very helpful because that way, we can focus on the things that we  can change and I think that is the most important step to take. Sometimes we put our energy in  tasks or things that in reality are not necessary and all they do is hold us back from developing real  solutions to the real problems or challenges that happen every day. I am working in the technical team. I will be working on gathered old information for finding the data  relationship and creation of searching Rest APIs. This application is useful for internal purpose.

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding  of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define  possible solutions to the problem. Based on visualization we are finding the defects to fix our problems.  This visualization we are using to gather more number of users. I have used the technique of using a  straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a  diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining the scope, boundaries,  key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying pain points and  opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Application

I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man  graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing  material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or  other auditing reports. For the activity, I will take the suggestions and improvements from the team  members. Based on those will create a revised graphic that incorporates their feedback and proposed  changes that they agreed to as a group.

For understanding complex code one  must connect dots from different programs that are there in the project.

A developer has to go through 1000s of lines of code (LOC) to understand  the project structure. This is only possible if you show right focus and analytical skills.

Design Thinking for Innovation – Assignment

Challenge:    I am a final year MBA student with Human Resource Management as the  specialization. The course: “Design Thinking for Innovation”, intrigued me if I  could apply Design principles for HR programs to make them more impactful  simply because both of them are ‘human-centric’. But HR is a vast field and  there are different modules of varying complexity and nature. Thus, I picked  up Learning and Development and tried to apply design principles. Specially.  in the IT sector, a lot of budgets are allocated for L&D because it is a  capability-building program that impacts the bottom line of the organization.  Nevertheless, these programs are ineffective because the organizations follow  a ‘One-size fits all’ model. The workplace is diverse with different age groups  such as baby boomers, Gen X, and Millennials who have different styles of  learning. The Millennials would prefer flexible online learning modules. Baby  boomers could prefer the traditional approach. But I did not want my  preconceived notions to affect my study.    Selection:    I was fortunate to do an L&D Internship in a start-up two weeks ago. And I  was assigned the responsibility of designing a particular training module in  limited time. So, I thought of using the design tool, Storytelling as the  launchpad for the take-off of the training. If you were to ask me, why I chose  this particular training module, then the answer is that storytelling is simple  yet highly effective. Stories are captivating and compatible with different types  of learners. The visual learners imagine the story and picture it in their head  while the audio-learners would enjoy the story-telling itself. Also, all of us are  accustomed to stories from childhood and it’s also all around us. Also, a  complicated topic can be easily explained through a story, and let me tell you  how it worked. I interned as a growth executive in a fintech start-up   which primarily  deals with airline invoice procurement and streamlining indirect taxation operations  through automated platforms. In recent times the airline industry has taken a hit due to less  travels affecting the business revenue in a significant way. In such times, the sales team was  struggling to meet their targets and the existing clients did not do much to add to the ever- decreasing revenue.

So, in a time like this where the work was also getting hectic due to lockdowns and people  not being able to communicate freely on online platforms, it was a smart move by the CEO  of the firm to go for motivational sessions everyday first thing in the morning. In this session  one employee was chosen randomly as the champion of the day and he/she would present  to the team. The session rolled out, people started following this practice of sharing a  motivational video which was more or less of the same content: hardcore workouts, sports  theme and people struggling, fighting hard to get to their goals and so on.

To this, I had a different view as I saw work as not a duty but an expression of the exuberant  life that blossoms within each of us. And I had to take a different approach of motivating my  team, which was, story-telling.

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a tool that I use all the time. I work with multiple populations, sometimes  without education, and economically disadvantaged people. Many of these people deal with  oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and  inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding  ways to inspire them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share  stories for different reasons. Often they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their  lives with me to connect and they find meaning in sharing these experiences as a form of  teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With many clients I share stories of my life in order to help  them visualize a state of independence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to  ascertain their goals, and sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and  thought processes. I use this information to develop different strategies to try and find a way  that works for them to gain more independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives.

text:
Visualisation

Visualisation: It is a core component of the way that we communicate, whether we're aware of it or not. When we're dealing with very complex problems, we're enacting a different kind of problem solving that has to bring in more than just logic. Visualisation is really important for the process of Design Thinking because it's actually a way of unlocking a different part of our brain. It allows us to think in a non-verbal way and access parts of our brain, our creativity. Most design thinkers call visualisation as “the mother of all design tools”, because they are used in every stage of the design thinking process.

Visualisation has a role to play throughout the Design Thinking. It's an incredible tool, in that sense, in that we're using those tools and that part of our brain at each phase in the design process. It's not just something that has an application in one part of the Design Thinking. It has many ways of being useful at different parts of the Design Thinking process.

LIMITATIONS AND IMPLICATIONS:

This paper has been a first attempt to describe visualization methods used in the five phases of design thinking with the aim to inform and support reflection of practitioners and researchers about the role of visualization in design thinking. Limitations arise from the set of examples that were present to the authors, there are many more visualizations in other design thinking projects. We further want to make explicit that those visualization act as illustrative examples and not as the “standard”. We also acknowledge that all five phases include divergent and convergent phases and that the visualizations covered in this article cover only one of those two phases.We hope that by making the functions of visualization explicit in general and showcasing examples for each of the design thinking phases, design thinking practitioners and researchers are inspired to think of and make use of visualizations more consciously in the future. that benefit from SEO include websites, blogs, and info graphics.

There are a number of ways to approach SEO in order to generate qualified traffic to your

website. These include:

On page SEO: This type of SEO focuses on all of the content that exists "on the page" when

I've already gone through various design thinking tools and decided to use the mind map tool. It's one of the effective tools that adjust all these data in shaping to be visually brain friendly.  the mind map tool is more intuitive, enhanced visual, more engaging, and more productive.

I have recently joined an early-stage software start-up which develops software for companies  operating in the commercial real estate space. This industry is generally slow moving and certainly  does not like change. The main users are asset manager, analysts and transaction managers which  are involved in managing, selling, and buying assets. This industry itself has not seen much change  over the past decade and a lot of their processes date back a couple of years. We knew that this  industry was certainly ready for software that speeds up processes and frees up time. This industry  has been using Microsoft Excel for data entry, data storage and the sharing of data for a long time.  However, getting the end user to adopt our software solution and truly understanding what they are  looking for has been a challenging operation. We decided that using smaller learning launches  throughout the development process to test and verify assumptions will help us build a product  which truly satisfies the users needs would be the best way to approach this challenge.

Selection

Understanding what our users truly want and need to do their job more efficiently has been our core  challenge. Using smaller learning launches that test and verify assumptions has helped our team to  run experiments on a small scale which truly uncovered what our clients needed. Generally speaking,  a learning launch is a tool which uses carefully designed experiments or prototypes to test the key  underlying value-generating assumptions. The learning launch is a learning experiment conducted  quickly and inexpensively to gather customer feedback and data. The purpose of these small-scale  experiments is to learn valuable information and whether an idea is validated or not.

Reflection - Mind Mapping

Challenge

I own a custom development software company in Mexico, and we often come across challenges that will be better solved with design thinking. This time I am talking about a project we made for a catalog selling company. These kinds of companies have a very peculiar business model. They produce some items (shoes in this case), design a catalog, and affiliate people so they sell the catalog items to their social circle. This customer of ours, needed to “update” their business model due to the COVID 19 pandemic, because their affiliates cannot longer visit their customers to sell the company products. We needed to digitize the company's service so their affiliates can sell during the pandemic (and attract a younger segment of affiliates with this new digital service).

Selection

The tool we used was mind mapping. Mind mapping is a way to externalize and structure our ideas in a graphic, understandable way for all the members of the team. For this challenge, we selected mind mapping because we need to deeply understand all the steps of the process that make this experience special for both the final customer and the affiliate. This way, we can detect “moment of truth” and pay special attention when designing the final solution.

Application

We started the process by having a couple of sessions with company's stakeholders. There, we document the main objectives the company have with this project; Allow the current affiliates to continue selling the products during the pandemic and attract a new segment of younger affiliates. Then, we created a mind map of the customer journey and selected what we thought were those “moments of truth”, the main points we have to be careful when digitizing the service. I was not even aware that design thinking exists.  Thus, it struck me by surprise when I discovered the similarities between the design thinking  approach (Malak, 2016) and the career coaching process based upon systems theory,  success strategy and cybernetics (Friedrich, Seiwert and Geffroy, 2003, p.23):

Design Thinking  Career Design

What is?  Looking inside: self assessment, analysis, synthesis

What if?  Looking outside: orientation, options, and evaluation  What wows?  What works?  Looking forward: career action plan design and implementation

Design thinking in general with its procedures and instruments appears to be useful in  dealing with career development issues. It may help finding answers to the question how to  effectively design and propose a unique portfolio of competencies in a world of work that has  become increasingly volatile, uncertain, complex, and ambiguous (Laurençon, 2014).      1. Normally,  people are not used to analyzing their own history and development including a reflection of  their values, motivated skills, preferred work settings and satisfiers, barriers and constraints.  However, without a thorough self-assessment a client won’t be able to figure out what might  be suitable and sustainable career options. text: ASSIGNMENT CHALLENGE – LEARNING LAUNCH    CHALLENGE.  Covid-19 hit the hospitality sector in our region really hard. As an island destination, the  economy relied heavily on international tourists. However, the island city is also known to be  the most cash liquid region in the country. The company decided to close down all the  properties it operated (2 small town resorts and 1 city hotel) but as soon restrictions were  lifted, the company decided to take the risk and also address its legal obligations to its  customers from prepaid bookings and vouchers sold.    SELECTION.  The demand for local travel surged with the lifting of border controls. It gave us a very narrow  window of time to plan and deploy. There is also no reliable data to use as comparison and  baseline as covid and its impact is unknown. We chose the LEARN LAUNCH tool to allow for  agile decision making, evaluation and constant pivoting according to market response and any  changes in border control.    APPLICATION. Once this was done we set in place possible scenarios dependent on market  response which were: 1) fill the weekends 2) fill the weekdays 3) expand capacity. An Attractive Carnival – Learning Launch

Challenge:

About a year ago we had to encourage people to actually want to join a carnival that us,  a group of students, organized from A to Z. It was for a project we had to get done. The  problem was that we were not known people. Why would someone want to pay money  for tickets to attend something like a carnival that unknown people who have no history  of having well-organized carnivals or fun days? Also we wanted this carnival to be on a  Sunday. Which was also a challenge because it’s almost everyone’s free day and  everybody would want to stay home and chill and have some rest. We had to convince  people and make them excited enough about our day in a way that makes them prefer  our carnival over the day they wait for every week. We needed to sell about a hundred  tickets. But where do we start from? What do we do?

Selection

We felt like it was kind of obvious which design thinking tool would be most suitable for  such a situation. We went for learning launch as we needed to learn more about  carnivals, what would people be excited about most and how to attract them even  though we are new to doing this. Learning launch would be perfect for us to gain more  knowledge and experience in the real world not just thinking for far away, it would make  us interact with the people and know about them and their thoughts more.

Application

We set up a small booth near the district wear the carnival would be so that we would  know more specifically about the targeted audience who are more likely to come.

We made surveys asking questions like what the thing is that people wished they found  at carnivals even if it’s not applicable or weird. We also asked people what the thing  they would really want to do on their day-off but is not available was. society, and industry experts. It is human centric challenge. In order to be among top colleges syllabus

expectation. We will try to bridge the gap between the current college curriculum and industry

expectations. Students should also get motivated for research and higher studies.

text:
Mind Mapping

What is mind mapping :   Mind Mapping is considered as one of the ideation technique. We  represent it virtually.we can put all our ideas or information in connection by

drawin​g

How Mind Mapping is made?   In mind mapping, generally we use our key word which we represent in the  middle and this should be related to our problem statement or the main  point on which our ideation focuses. The nextpart is , we surround the  middle keyword with are the words or ideas or information that we are  think(generally which comes to our mind)

​Finally, we should have a virtual map with lines and curves. This  should be done by thinking how there ideas or thoughts are commited.                  Lets get breif into Mind Mapping.      ​We have some essential characteristics in Mind Mapping.

● The complete focus is on the central word or central theme of the

problem statement.

● By focussing on the centralword make many words generally

comes to your mind, which are usually called as branches.

● Now these branches need to be connected to the central theme or

central word.

● Here importance of the ideation plays a role to have sub branches

which are decided on their importance .

● Finally we’ll get a beautiful nodal structure with different lines

,colors ,curves connected to the central word.

How Mind Mapping help us?

● To kind of complex problem we get solution or can easily

understand.

● Our thought process increases by thinking various new ideas .   ● We can save lot of time putting it one a piece of paper need not

think a lot on same idea.

● We wont get struck on things or problems we come through in our

daily life.

text: Reflection about design thinking tools    Challenge    I’m assistant professor at a business school in Ecuador. Producing academic content is  one of the main activities of my job at the business school. Academic content includes  research papers, case studies, and articles for local professional magazines. Academic  papers are the most challenging content because they have to pass a rigorous approval  process to get published. Publishing rates are usually below 30% and it takes at least a  year and half to publish a paper since it is conceived.     The process of publishing a paper starts with a research question, then it involves  gathering data to perform experiments or any other scientific method to test those  ideas. Next, results are wrapped up and sent to a journal for the revision process of  publication. The challenge is to come up with a process innovation that allow me to  craft a high quality paper in a shorter period of time.    Selection  Visualization is a key tool of design thinking, because it is transversal to the whole  stages of the process. It allows you to capture and make sense of the current reality of  a problem. It is helpful for sense making because it allows you to have a clearer, and  less biases representation of current reality. I was inspired by how visualization was  used for the kitchen problem. It was interesting to see how it was deployed to  understand the social reality of elder people and the staff that took care of them.  Consequently, I decided to use visualization tool because the process of writing a  paper is highly erratic, and a visual depiction of it felt like a good starting point for  understanding current reality. text:
WATER  PROBLEMS FOR FARMERS

CHALLENGE:

Now a days farmers having a lot of problems with lack of water available. We also seen that,  we have unseasonal rainfalls. Due to this, farmers are unable to grow crops, then at the end of the  crop due to unseasonal rains farmer get damage. We are focus on to capture rain water and store it  in a tank. Then this is useful later for farmers use.

SELECTION:

Our team members already have an idea on it and we decide that we have to prepare a tool to  use this.

APPLICATION:

At first we are going to use this in small land, which is useless. Then we implement it in agriculture  lands. For this sensors are open like an upward umbrella and capture the rain water then stored in a  tanker. This stored water is used for furture irrigation. Due to this we save crops from rain floods.  We use six or seven for an acre.

This also used to save crops from wind blowing during rains. This saves lot of money for farmers by  saving crops.

INSIGHT:

By applying this in practical , at first farmers are not supported . Then we took a land containing  crops for lease up to one year then we try to implement this. This shows maximum result of saving  water. At first this is costly due to fixing of tools and tanks near field.

APPROACH:

Then we are trying to implement to all agricultural lands. We also focus to improve the tools in  better way to work.

Design Thinking Reflection Journal

Thoughts on the Course :

The ability to think out of the box and learning how to think out of the box is  the most exciting thing for me while taking this course. I like to find the easiest  solution that makes sense to solve the problem. I don’t think I strive to make  the solution the best it can be and be as creative as I could with it. I have  always found myself jealous of creative people and have been at awe of what  they can come up with. I do think it will be a challenge for me to push myself to  be creative and think of the design element as more than just a function. I am  uncertain with my ability to think outside the box and come up with great  ideas, I don’t want to let my group down and I want to be able to contribute to  the group projects with creative and innovative ideas. This course is relevant to  my life in many aspects. I work for Scientia and I see all the time how the  people who are able to think linearly but also implement experimental change  tend to have the best results and move up the ladder the quickest. I am getting  my degrees to hopefully be in the management field sometime soon. A part of  being a manager is exploring different avenues that can benefit yourself and  the company.

Author: Vanessa Sanchez    August 15, 2019

The challenge

I’m currently part of the IT Governance Team within my organisation and one of my projects over the year  has been to gather and report KPI information across the various IT departments. The scope of this piece  of work is limited to internal KPI data only and excluded any third party/vendor information. The current  process (which has been in place for the last 12 months) is to collect all the data manually each month,  approx. 300 KPIs across all IT departments. The whole process from start to finish took approximately 17  working days to complete each month. Over 40 people are involved at varying degrees across the month  with this process.

The main problems faced within the current process were getting the data in on time, the quality of the  submissions, confusion around what data needed to be submitted each month and manipulating the  various Management reports error free and on time.

My challenge is to automate the whole process where possible and to get the senior management  meaningful reports out within 7-9 working days.

Selection

The tool I have selected is Mind Mapping.  I have gathered individual feedback and large amounts of data  around the problems faced by stakeholder and customers of the process. Design Thinking for Innovation- Mind Mapping

Challenge-  Mind mapping is an interesting tool that helps me to represent my ideas and plan  systematically before work. Since it is a group activity it also helps me to improve  my relations and understanding with my colleagues in college. I am a part of a  team that manufactures an All-terrain vehicle. We participate in a national level  competition which is organized for undergraduate students. In 2017 our team  stood 12th in our country and now we have started preparation for 2014  competition. Before starting the design of our new vehicle, I suggested my team- mates to use the mind-mapping tool. We all arranged an online meeting during  this lockdown. Our competition has various sub-categories like design, sales,  cost, technical inspection and dynamics, and sub-systems like transmission,  suspension, steering, brakes, chassis, and DAQ. Our challenge was to identify our  shortcomings during last year and come up with out of the box thinking. I  suggested my team-mates use this tool so that we can identify in which sub- category we need to put more effort, proper distribution of man-power, and much  more. The linking tool of mind-mapping helped us identify which task to do first  and which later.    Selection-  Up till 2017, our team had sub-systems. We divided our team into sub-systems  and all system members took appropriate decisions about their work and all the  system leads reported their plan to the captain. This is also a good approach where  a proper division of labor is followed but there is less interaction with others and  less scope for creativity and imagination. So, we followed the mind-mapping  technique where all 40 team members sat together and shared their views in all  aspects. It also helped everyone to know about each other’s work and help them  progress with everyone’s ideas. Challenge

Hi! I am working as Associate Professor in an University and my challenge is to identify the root  cause of high failure rate of the students in Computer Science department and come with methods  to improve the quality of education in the department. The failure rate effects the new admissions  and also lowers the placement score. We will try to uncover the reasons (on part of faculty,  administration and students) that hinders the quality of education being delivered in the classes.

Selection

I selected visualization as the tool to demonstrate the hurdles that are coming in the way of effective  teaching. This tool is a perfect way to show to higher management the scenario being faced by  faculty and students in a class. The management people are not too technical so using visualizations  will be the best method to show what is wrong and what can be done to improve.

Application

The first hurdle identified was the class size. 72 students were sitting a class which was not big  enough to accommodate them all. There was hardly any space for the teacher to move and see what  individual student was doing. In certain situations the class room size is 144 students. This makes the  class teaching less interactive and there is no connection among faculty and students.

The second factor was overload on faculty. A faculty apart from teaching was involved in paper  checking, student mentoring, placement classes, curriculum development, question paper setting,  etc works and had a teaching load of 22 hrs. This leaves them with very less or no time to relax and  prepare well for class. Being exhausted they remain pressured to perform well which also effects  their family life and in turn effective their behaviour in the class. This leads to poor quality delivery  of lecture.

text:
Reflection on the Mind Mapping Tool

A- Challenge

During the IT Management review of Q3-2012 it was reported that in the Dev Ops survey the 39.6%  of the users answered “No” in “Are the application requirements and usability met?” on new released  business applications. By Having the goal of less than 10% the gap of 26.9% needs to be corrected.

To address this a problem-solving exercise has been performed, the data gathered from this exercise  revealed that during application requirements process the following issues are shown: A-Incomplete  User Requirements 36%, B-Lack of user understanding of the system requirements 24%, C-Unrealistic  System Expectations 15%, D-Changing Requirements and Specifications 10%, E- Poor or no Project   Planning 8% and F- System no longer required 7%.

Based on the data analysis it was determined that by improving the user’s requirement gathering  process 85% of the found issues can be corrected. To innovate and try something different from the  regular user requirement gathering tools I suggested to learn about Design Thinking and see if any of  the tools can improve the user requirement gathering.

B- Selection

Based on Week’s 3 video Mind Mapping tool from professor Marian Moore it was found the potential  use of Mind Mapping to improve the gathering of user requirements for business applications. Since  mind mapping is powerful graphical tool used to unlock the full potential of the brain and achieve  clearer thinking of ideas, including the tool in the process will prove more beneficial because by the  use of  cortical skill like words, images, numbers, logic, colors the end user will be able to transmit all  the ideas and toughs about what he requires from the application additionally in this way, we go  through all the extensions of the specific requirements, relations, use case, reports, interactions  identify potential technology usage risks that we would not be able to gather see with a regular user  interview tool.

text:
Inhouse Data Management Platform – Visualization

Challenge & Selection

I used the Visualization tool to get help with Visual Thinking, for understanding the benefits of having an  inhouse developed and owned Data Management Platform and to identify and define possible  challenges that we could get over just by having a unique data as being a mobile network operator. I use  this technique with my upper management to convince them to invest on a long term platform,  including development and data fine tuning tasks, which are heavy effort for any company that has this  size of data and number of customers. Thus, the position of a DMP in digital advertising ecosystem is  very critical for the future of this business.

Application

First of all, every stakeholder should align on, where does DMP fit in all digital advertising ecosystem,  from advertisers, to agencies, to adplatforms (DSP and SSPs) and publihers.. While big data is  instrumental to effective data-driven marketing campaigns, you can’t do much with the raw  information. You need it sorted and converted into a usable form, at least so you can understand what  you’re looking at. This is the power of a DMP.

A DMP collects and organizes data from a variety first-, second- and third-party data sources, and makes  it available to other platforms such as DSPs, SSPs, and ad exchanges to be used for targeted advertising,  personalization, content customization and beyond. Some people describe a data management platform  as the “pipes” of ad tech — connecting many platforms in a neutral way so marketers can use their  powerful audience data when and where they want.

This first-party data — that is the data you own and have collected directly from your own customers —  can be collected based on specific behaviors such as clicks, downloads, video uploads or video  completions, interests like sports, football, parenting, museums and travel or demographic information. text:
Learning Launch Tools Find Effective Fuel Surcharge Methodology

By

Sachin Cordova

Challenge

I am a consultant for a Last Mile Delivery/Less-than-Truckload (LTL or small freight) logistics company in  Ohio. The challenge I have been tasked with is to find an appropriate fuel surcharge methodology that  will not alienate any existing customers, nor be an impediment to attracting new business. The project is  limited to internal resources, with the project team consisting of myself, and members of both the sales  and marketing departments. Other key stakeholders include company senior management and  members of the accounting department. We are focusing on trying to discover what customers will  accept best and respond to most positively. The fuel surcharge will be a new line item, going live as a  new company revenue stream and appearing on all customer invoices beginning January 2.

Selection

After detailed usage of other Design Process activities, including spending time with several Accounts  Payable personnel to understand how current invoices were received and processed, we have been  utilizing Learning Launch Tools. We have been placing “small bets” in hopes of discovering what  invoicing methodology will be most effective now and in the future with clients.

The IBM trade show booth section of the course materials was particularly helpful in this stage of our  process, as the stakes to my client are as high or higher than a trade show attendee not entering a booth  or leaving quickly. The wrong billing approach could lead to the ending of the business relationship. Just  as the course explained, gaining “Greater Comfort” is crucial to adoption.

Application

The Learning Launch has been two-fold: first, testing multiple billing formats, and gauging reaction from  a group of Client Contacts on the receipt of an invoice containing a new line item, breaking out Fuel  Surcharges for the previous month. In  Peru there are quite a few people who carry out their operations through traditional or  physical channels (agencies), these operations include payments to their workers, suppliers  and others, who can also perform via web through "Telecrédito Web", however, many  users did not make their payments by this, despite they paying their subscription monthly,  so users had the tool but preferred to go to the agency instead of use a product for which  they currently paid. During the year, campaigns are carried out to raise awareness of this  type of customers to use digital tools, one of the actions that are performed is to send  emails with the intention of explaining the benefits of using digital tools and contact  channels in case they have any doubts. The challenge in this case, and in general for banks  in Peru, is to migrate all operations from physical to digital channels to improve efficiency.

It seems to me that the process of testing to collect information may be less disastrous than  launching you to the market and correcting errors over the course. EFL Classwork Assignment – Mind Mapping

Challenge:

English as a foreign language instructors claim that online testing in times of covid-19 is pointless  as students are more prone to cheating using different devices, even if tests are well designed. A  few instructors reject the accuracy of “well-designed tests”. Therefore, most instructors suggest  that we should have only one final well-designed test and give more percentage to other activities.  The main challenge is that only changing percentages does not tackle the problem which deals  with testing and assessment. However, there are other views such as the view on students as  cheaters and that they are not reaching the expected skills. I highlight that assessment requires  further discussion and organize a follow-up meeting to start our discussion.

Selection & Application:

The selected design tool is mind mapping. I facilitate the e-meeting as a moderator with a critical  eye on concerns, insights, and thoughtful questions to ignite the discussion. I also talk to a couple  of instructors to play the role of participant observers. One who mind maps the concepts and  connections as the discussion flows, and another one who pays attention to questions and ideas  we shall not forget or leave as outliers.

This tool and strategy are chosen to have multiple input and sources, not only from the facilitation  and observation team, but also for instructors to keep an eye on the direction of our talk, agree,  disagree, express their mind, their emotions, their ideas.

text:
Project: Colour Changing shoes  The color changing shoe is a shoe which can change its color using smart  phones. It is made up of mesh fabric with LED strips under fabric. We can  change colour with the help of mobile application. It has Li-ion battery and RGB  colour codes and it also provides fast charging.    Project Level  What went well in the  project?

What was not so good? What are the key

learnings?

The coordination  between the team  members is very good  which helped in  accepting different ideas.  All the members of the  team are very  hardworking and  dedicated and are ready  to put their heart and  soul into the product.

We had a few minor  setbacks, and weren’t at  our best productivity and  efficiency levels at all  times. We were not able  to meet the initially  planned deadline. The  morale dropped a few  more times than  expected. Conflicted  Opinions were not always  handled well.

We learnt to empathize  better than before in an  effective manner. We learnt  how important it is to know  the compatibility of the  market and our product. We  learnt how important it is to  collect data and statistics to  understand how our product  may perform.

Meta Level  What does design thinking mean  in context of your work?

Use cases in your own environment

In context of our product, design  thinking means how innovative and  unique our product is when  compared to others in the market. It  is all about how different the ideas/  designs implemented on the product.

 Modeling   Parties   Socializing   Concerts

Challenge  The challenge at hand was to come up with marketing ideas for our family business in the gemstone  industry. Our family was doing business in the gemstone industry since 1995, mainly in the B2B  segment and was now looking to take on a larger client base and expand both its influence and  revenues.

Selection  We decided to procced with Mind Mapping for achieving our target. As this would allow most all the  stakeholders to give their inputs. The mind map would give us a fuller picture of the scenario at hand  and the possible points of improvement and maybe even new approaches.

Application  So, first of all each of us decided to contact one of the end consumers we were in contact with  (some of our key accounts) and enquire them about how were they doing, how was their business  doing, what was their experience buying from us, what were the problems (if any) they faced during  the whole process, the points were we could improve, would they recommend us to any of their  friends or relative(calculating NPS), etc, etc.

After gathering all the data and some preliminary insights, we all sat together and wrote all the  important points on a whiteboard (in order to have a visual which helped us to keep things relevant  and real), and then started to connect the points. In order to understand if one of the points  affected the other and if yes then how? We were also looking for some unarticulated messages that  might be there, which would arise when we looked at the whole picture.

Insight  The insights we got were really astounding, we got to know that most of the customers were looking  for better credit terms, from a period of 30 days to a period of 45 days. text:
Challenge:

As an enthusiast to e-commerce and to understand the dynamics of it, I had to research what is needed  to boost sales using a factor that is not well exploited.

Selection:

I have selected a mind mapping tool which will narrow down the possibilities, and offer a well- established option to pursue that will increase sales as intended.

Application:

A research has been done using reviews and surveys. The outcome revealed that a high percentage of  consumers are very much interested in delivery time. To further investigate this outcome, a specific  geographical area was selected to identify the resources needed to answer the question of the time  factor in the delivery process. A brainstorming sessions were initiated to review this issue, and the  results of those sessions concluded that consumers’ satisfaction will be at its peak if the concept of same  day delivery is applied. The process, workflow, and cost of implementing this concept is under way to  test the feasibility of implementation.

Insight:

The tool has helped identifying a great concept that will be initiated on a small geographical area, and  the outcome will be evaluated based on the incremental sales increase and customers’ satisfaction.

Approach:

It would have been also adequate to use learning launch, since the concept of online business has been  out there for a while, and the drawback and incentives can be detected in less time consuming  approach.

text:
Challenge:

I practice cognitive psychology and many people sufferings are based on fear. During my work with  them, I follow three main steps and in each of them I use storytelling. The first step is to examine in  what state person is, what are his thoughts and hopes. During this stage I find that very many people  don’t have real contact with themselves, so they struggle with giving me the information what is  needed for successful therapy. In cases when traditional question approach doesn’t work, I use  storytelling, describing similar cases to direct people to understanding of their emotions and then we  work with it. The second step is specifying what people want to get as the result of our work and  what they need it for. Here storytelling is necessary to give them examples of outcomes of similar  cases, of changes in metal and sometimes physical state of the person. This is done to motivate and  direct. In this assignment I am going to focus on those cases when people had phobia, they wanted  to get free of. After the condition of the person, his hopes, motivation, and fears are clarified we  move to the third step: exposure therapy. This is, as I believe, is the brightest example of  storytelling as an efficient tool of working with human mind.

Storytelling is used to create the image as real as its possible, so that person could face it and learn  how to deal with his emotions. Many phobias and fears I worked with are not material (such as fear  of spiders, for example) but instead are abstract, or based on the occasion that already happened.  So, here storytelling, based on the previous experience of the person or on imagination, is the only  way of how to get his mind “into” this scene. To conclude this paragraph: I use storytelling to give  people similar cases so they can understand their emotions better and to motivate them to try the  methods I suggest, after which storytelling is used to make them face their fears.

Tool Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I am a student enrolled in a marketing and entrepreneurship course in which I have a final

project that asks me to create a business idea that is sustainable and generates a great value  impact on society. Since the main objective of the project is to create something that actually  helps society, two of the steps of design thinking must comply, empathize with the people and  define the true problem. In order to do so, me and my team are applying the tool of storytelling.  It is very common that people won’t share to you as a researcher their main life problems or  issues, and in the strange case that some of them actually start talking about them, they won’t get  too deep into their problems unless you motivate them to do so, this is where the tool of  storytelling comes in pretty useful. If you empathize with a person by sharing some personal  story about some specific aspect then it is way more plausible that the client, which is hearing to  that story can remember some of his own experience and understand what type of information  you are looking for, after that another challenge is presented, which is focusing on their feedback  and understand their story.

Application

My final project team decided to work with the topic of pollution and the major problems

and causes that are presented with the pollution of the planet, more specifically we wanted to do  something related to recycling in Mexico, which is currently an underdeveloped field in the  country. REFLECTION- STORYTELLING  AS A TOOL FOR POTENTIAL DISCOVERING AND DEVELOPMENT

Bankole Ismail

Challenge and Selection

As a teacher and coach, storytelling has been one of the indispensable tools and techniques I use al the  time to help my students discover and develop their potential in such a way that they are able to pattern  their profession in line with their potential and passion.  Coaching students and adults who came out from  inner city schools were they never had the privilege of having a school guidance or career counsellors  could be very challenging. Many of these people came out from schools doing things they don’t like or  have passion for. The most pathetic part is the fact that they become a victim of workplace by getting  demoralized and demotivated as a result of the fact that they work with their own weakens instead of  using their strength to work. I saw the need to help them discover their strength and how they can direct  same to for optimal opportunity that could single them out in career path and job placement using  storytelling as a tool to inspire them and inform them on how they can use their natural empowerment  and talent to turn their lives around in job search and in workplace.  When I work with students, I share  stories of different stores to help them discover themselves and identify inherent potentials and talent  that can be channeled into a career or hobbies.  Often they think those skills are just what is different  from what they need to become in life. Example Reflection: A new town square, where people feel good

Challenge

I live in Prague, the capital city of Czechia. The district is made up mainly by housing estates that were  built in 1970s. The district is ideal for families, because of extensive greenery, transport accessibility  and civic amenities. However, as much as the district tries to be modern in its ideas and approaches,  there is still a lot of unused areas that developers are trying to gain. Stakeholders’ interests in the  district are the main friction area. Now, there should be a new square in front of the town hall. The  square will serve the citizens – kids, young adults, senior citizens, mothers, fathers, but also the local  representatives or visitors. What should such a place contain so that people feel good there?

Selection

For the purpose of finding out where, when and why people feel good in certain public places, we  selected the mind mapping tool. Mind mapping provides a segway from what is to what if. We need to  gain quite a lot of data and seek patterns in “what is”. Customers (=citizens) make observations –  where do they feel good? From these observations, we can gain insights – what are the factors that  cause them to feel good?

Application

We held a forum, where were approximately 80 citizens and 20 local representatives. By digital voting,  they chose 10 most favourite places in the district. These places were written on pieces of paper and  placed all around the room. People could place sticky notes with what exactly they like in the place,  but also something they don´t like. After that we formed teams in front of each paper and the teams  discussed together. We, the facilitators, helped the teams to form insight statements from their  observations. Presentations

I work with vulnerable populations, people with  developmental disabilities, senior citizens, and people in economic hardship. Many of these people face  oppression and dysfunction in all aspects of their lives and need to be empowered, and inspiration is one  way to do so. I spend a lot of time "opening people's hearts" and finding ways to inspire them to improve  their situations. When I work with older adults, we share stories for different reasons. Often they are  lonely and very happy to share their life stories with me in order to make connections, and they find  meaning in sharing these experiences, in a sense, as a form of teaching and/or legacy. For my  developmentally disabled clients, I share my life story to help them imagine a state of independence, I use  their feedback with the context of my story to identify their goals, and sometimes we use the story to  better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this information to develop different  strategies to try to find a way that works for them to gain more independence in areas of their lives that  they feel are lacking. Reflection – Visual Thinking

Challenge & Selection

I choose Visualization or Visual Thinking; it is a way to understand and organize my thoughts and  a way to improve the way I think and communicate. It is a great way to understand confusing and  complex information especially when we are fed by too much information and we become  overwhelmed that we tend to shut down.

As an engineering student, visualization is useful especially with solving word problems, and  thinking of new ideas to present and to make it into reality. As engineers transforms raw materials  into a more valuable product and design thinking tools, especially visual thinking, is really helpful  in building up ideas, organizing thoughts, improve thinking, and deeper understanding about  something that you want to innovate. In solving word problems, it is hard to understand when you  just read it, so it is helpful if you visualize the problem and start organizing your ideas to solve it.  As engineers, I think the most important tool in Design Thinking is Visualization.

Application

In Visual Thinking, one does not need to be an artist to do visualization. Ideas cannot be done, if  you cannot visualize it. You just need to externalize your internal thoughts and making them more  understandable and explicit. Will apply visual thinking in a form of roadmaps, drafts, and sketches.

In engineering, sketching, and visualizing something is really helpful if you want to innovate  something. We are taught computer aided designs, and how to draw with right measurements so it  is not very new for us engineering students is the visual thinking. Same as with planning something  you want to create or innovate, you first visualize how it works, what is it, how do you want it to  look like. You visualize first, organize your ideas and then make it into reality.

text:
Biblio-motional Experience Mapping

The Use of Visualization to Understand the Library Studying  Experience

Challenge

I’ve studied in class, on busses, in coffee shops, in bed. I’ve studied at the gym on the  treadmill. I’ve even studied at a bar during happy. I’ve studied in a lot of place, but I can  never get myself to study at the university library. When friends and colleagues ask why I  never study at the library, I couldn't really articulate a persuasive answer. All I’d say is that I  didn’t like to go there much. Truth is, I didn’t know why.    After taking this Design Thinking course, I decided to further investigate this personal  challenge. I felt I was missing out on a seminal graduate school experience and wanted to  better understand why. To do so, I decided to use two approaches:  the visualization design  thinking tool and creating emotional maps of the experience.

Selection

The process of visualization “allows us to think in a nonverbal way” (Lesson 1, ​Visualization  Tool​ video). It helps us communicate complex ideas by activating the, “[right side] of our  brain, parts of our creativity, that we might not normally be using in the course of  conversation” (Lesson 1, ​Visualization Tool​ video). I decided to recall a time I went to the  library to study and to visualize on post-it notes the different parts of the experience. I  wanted to create a storyboard of the experience.    I also decided to create an emotional map of my experience of going to the library. An  emotional map is a representational tool that would allow me to recognize the different  emotions at different parts of an experience. I wanted to immerse myself in the experience  and surface the pain points that were inhibiting me from normally going to the library to  study.

text:
Create new services in banking branches

Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

Retail banking is an especially heavily regulated activity worldwide, and in France it is mostly  run by former civil servants. Major decisions are made by the ministry of finance and apply to  all banks nationwide. In this environment innovation is viewed with suspicion at best, and kept  under tight control by the regulator. However, banks are under increasing strain, with rock  bottom interest rates that undercut their economic model and an aggressive competition by  “fintech” start-ups. They have little choice but to innovate themselves out of their predicament  to survive.

My client is a French regional bank, a subsidiary of a major agricultural banking group. Apart  from its traditional commercial objectives, it is especially dedicated to financing farmers (who  are heavily represented at the board), and to improve the local economy as a whole. It is a major  employer in the region, and it owns by far the biggest number of local branches among all retail  banks. Traffic in these branches goes down every year, making it difficult to justify such an  extensive physical presence. Yet the branches are viewed as an essential strategic and financial  asset: closing them in great numbers would trigger big market share losses, contradict the  mandate to sustain the local economy and be politically suicidal for most deciders.

Example Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

I am an intern on the Structural Analysis Department on a company in my town. Currently,  my department is facing a problem with the software we buy to do our job (this software  belongs to an external company). For matters of confidentiality, let´s call this software  “Namsys”. Since the external company charges Namsys by its time of use, a problem that  has emerged is that the workers of my company sometimes forget to close Namsys when  they are not using it (when they go to eat, for example) and, because of this, on these  situations, the costs of the use of Namsys raise even if it is not being used, since it is still  opened. My team calls this extra costs “idle costs” since they are being produced when  Namsys is idle, or not being used. Because of this, the challenge I was given was to reduce  the idle time of Namsys to reduce the extra costs this provoked.

Selection

When I was called for this project, the initial steps of the process were already taken: they  already had the data that was needed and a brainstorming process took place after that.  After this, we decided to test one of the solutions: to create an internal software that detects  when Namsys is idle and that closes it automatically when this happens. For this, we used  the learning launching tool. To make it short, a learning launch is a fast and cheap  experiment to test an idea and to prove a hypothesis. Our goal with this idea was to see if it  was the right solution and, if not, to learn from it to deliver something better.
