text:
Mind mapping

Luis Leon

1. Challenge.

I was working with a big transportation enterprise, and they wanted to  redesign a core process related to the vehicles’ maintenance. They had a lot  of problems with the data, the flow of the vehicles in the process, and the  close of the process.

2. Selection.

I suggested using the design thinking frame because I was in the first weeks  of the course. We used the classic five steps: empathize, define, ideate,  prototype, and test. I used before in other exercises, the triz grid in the second  step but in this exercise, I didn’t consider it appropriate due to the audience  and the redundant ideas of improvement leaving the problem and its effects  aside. So, I preferred to use mind mapping.

3. Application.

I knew that they have a lot of information and histories around the process  development and performance. I needed a strong insight to continue with a  focus on the ideation step.

We started in an individual 10-minute session, in which the people organize all  the information about the complaints, misfunctions, pains, problems, and  knowledge lessons in his role in the process we were working about.

Then, I drew in a whiteboard my mind map, initially with three branches or  arms: pains, complaints, and misfunction. The people began to tell stories and  I painted the situation with a representative icon or sketch, when the map had  some graphics ideas, the magic occurred, we had in only shot of sight, years  of history.

4. Insight

The group realized as a whole shared comprehension not the cause of the  problem (we didn’t look for it), but the main insight related to the process and  his design. We found that people knew very good his functions at the routine,  that they communicate outputs to the next process in an appropriate way but  they didn’t work as a team, they didn’t know the goals and procedures of the  rest of the group, and the company as a whole. Reflection – Storytelling

CHALLENGE

I was working on a retail company within the Talent, Culture and Communication Directorate (TCCD). One  of the main objectives of my position, was to engage people with the new culture – where a key element  was being customer-centered. The main challenges in this task were three:

-  We had to define what does a “new culture customer-centered” meant, so that employees can  relate with and live it day by day.

-  The scope of this project intended to reach 12,000 employees, with very different profiles from  each other: people with few months or a lifetime working in the company, different education  backgrounds, different locations within the country and different ethnographic profiles.

-  We had limited resources: the TCCD was a team of 10 people divided in 4 different areas and I  was the only person in the Organizational Culture area; the budget was limited by the CEO and  Human Resources Director; and we were time framed.

SELECTION

After a couple of months of brainstorming, workshops, and meetings, we came with a Culture Model that  visually looked like a compass, which pointed to a Pillar in each direction: The North, South, East and West.  Each Pillar was based on the values of the company and comprised two Organizational Competencies,  which described the kind of behavior people were expected to show.

Challenge

For three years now I have been part of the customer service sector of a company that  provides cable and internet service, in which I have slowly been acquiring more  supervisory responsibilities. Due to the pandemic, we have seen the need to have more  employees. However, due to the large numbers of attention and the dislike of customers  for the current circumstances, these new employees have been demotivated with their  performance. They do not believe we are meeting the expectations that our bosses  believe we should meet. That is why we, as supervisors, have made the decision to try to  improve the motivation of these new colleagues, which we hope will later impact their  work behavior.

Selection

As a team, it is the ﬁrst time that we apply Design Thinking in problem solving, we have  decided to use Storytelling as a tool in this oportunity and the selection is not arbitrary.  This type of approach is the most important to focus on the human factor of our new  employees.

Application

The idea is to ﬁnd the common ground between their current concerns and those that we  had at the beginning of our work journey. We realized that our bosses were losing sight of  the need to think of our colleagues not only as factors within a production chain, but also  that it was essential to foster a two-way relationship where something could be learned  from both sides.

These new employees need to know that there is someone who cares not only about the  performance of their work, but that there is someone who cares about how they feel  about the Way they are performing this task. Perla Luna

Benefits of Mind Mapping

In the course we learned that mind mapping is an effective creative  thinking tool

In its simplest form, a mind map is a collection of ideas that have been  put into the format of a visual diagram. Starting with a central idea or  topic in the middle of the map, branches radiate from the center  containing further themes and concepts to be explored – typically in the  form of words, short phrases, and images. This gives mind maps a  natural organizational structure.

In a mind map, information is structured in a way that mirrors exactly how  the brain functions – in a radiant rather than linear manner. It literally  ‘maps’ out your thoughts, using associations, connections, and triggers  to stimulate further ideas. They make it easier to extract your ideas from  your head into something visible and structured.

Research shows that the brain likes to work on the basis of association,  and it will connect every idea, memory or piece of information to tens,  hundreds and even thousands of other ideas and concepts. This is why  mind maps are beneficial for countless tasks.

Below, we will critically discuss how you can use mind maps to aid in  various processes, such as memorizing information, conducting  presentations and solving problems.

Mind maps involve a unique combination of imagery, color and visual- spatial arrangement which is proven to significantly improve recall  when compared to conventional methods of note-taking and learning  by rote. Ayoa’s mind mapping tool is faithful to these beneficial

features, giving you the option to create quick box-style or highly  creative maps with adjustable curvilinear branches, as well as add  images and emojis, and change the color of your branches and text.

Sometimes because of this, there has been observations that the person working  on a particular job is using potentially harmful method of work. In order to lessen the frequency of  this and make the workplace safer, the safety team has to come up with an idea.

Selection:

The safety team went through various brainstorming sessions in order to come up with a pilot  project that can be effective in this issue. They came up with a learning launch tool in which they will  roll out this new idea in only one plant of the manufacturing unit and see how it goes for a couple of  months.

REFLECTION

Challenge and Reflection

One of the challenges in organizations is the need to constantly stay competitive and be at least at par  or ahead of competition to stay in the game. I come from the financial services industry that is currently  is very traditional and undergoing massive digital transformation and I would say whoever provides the  best solution can win the market. Given this marketing condition, you can imagine the work involved  internally. The key challenge is getting products and updates to our platforms quickly to market or  sometimes, it is staying on project delivery schedule to catch up with competitors.

Application

One of the most striking tools for me is the learning launch. Most often than not, due to time or  resource constraints, we tend to think of solutions on our own, or try to force fit a process/ solution and  digitalize things as it is. We assumed this is the way to do things and let users accept it as it is.

Sometime ago, we had a project to develop an app, where we were trying to meet a timeline and were  already in the process of documentation and development requirements gathering. Due to the rush to  meet deadlines, we went ahead and developed screens and flows on how the app interfaces would look  like according to logical order and placement. We also used product names and labels on the UIs and  grouped the icons logically. Normal process is that we also have some usability study before  implementing a UI design for an app – a process where we do an FGD (focus group discussion) to gain  some insights on consumer behaviour but that takes time to do.  We decided to do it later due to time  constraints. For me, upon hearing about learning launch in this course, I was reminded about FGDs.

text:
Storytelling

Working as a tattooer, I need to communicate with people a lot. Most of the time I need to talk

with my clients. For that I am not a social person, I do not know how to communicate people, for

example how to make them understand my design ideas and the aftercare process that should be

complied with. Storytelling is a tool I ﬁnd useful in my work.

Storytelling can connect to the emotions and the values of the us. It can be part of my business

and a product I can give to my clients in our communication. It’s about the connection that we

give to people about a piece of informant that we are trying to share. The story is its essence,

which I should spend more time on conveying a message that has logic.

Application

Take aftercare process for an example. Usually I will need to tell the clients like ABC what you

should do and what you should not. Sometimes they just can not remember and understand.

Even though I give them a card printed with the whole process they still just throw away the card

and do not take care of the tattoos properly. Then I am thinking of the storytelling tool. I tell the

clients about the tattoo aftercare process as a story. After three hours, with the second skin cover

what will happen to the skin and the tattoos. Then during the process, in your daily, what kind of

actions will be harmful to the healing process. And during that several days, that is the part of

tattooed skin doing and your immunity system. After three days, what you should do to take care

of the tattoo. What will happen if these are not done. I use a story to connect all the healing

process then the clients can understand.

Insight & Approach

I ﬁnd it quite useful and the story is quite acceptable. It inspired me that in our life, we should use

this storytelling tool more. When people give me their requirements, it will be easy for me if they

tell me a story of their thoughts. How come the ideas and what makes them want what kind of

tattoo. Then

text:
LEARNING LAUNCH

CHALLENGE    Covid19.     The world around us is changing in real time. In all likelihood, careers will change by the time we  come out of this, scathed. During the #StayHome period, many will also take this opportunity to  introspect. I have too. For over 16+ years, I have had the privilege of living and working in the US,  Singapore, Vietnam, Indonesia, South Africa and now, Germany. Prior to Covid19, I was on the cusp  of moving back to Singapore to start a new role professionally, and on the personal front, a new  beginning. But that has all changed, and its back to the drawing board, back to basics. But as the  story goes, many successful ventures were formed after the financial crisis of 2008-2009.    SELECTION AND APPLICATION    During Covid19, I enrolled in various courses, including Design Thinking. My introspection has led to  some critical positive outcomes. I finally managed to put pen on paper and prepare a list of business  ideas envisioned during my exposure and experience in diverse parts of the world - engaging with  clients and consumers, boards and bartenders, preachers and politicians and many with a rag to  riches story. This further allowed me to reach within my network of business leaders and the  investment community.     To put these ideas through the litmus test and go beyond just the imaginary and imagery, the  Learning Launch was an ideal tool.     It was important to bring a skeptic on board at the onset to whet the process of continued  development, pivot or look for the nearest trash can. I completely align with the theory of  confirmation bias (and guilty of applying it on a few occasions myself). Along with a small team and a  small savings kitty, we ventured into searching for those needle-movers.     We created a shortlist from an initial plethora of ideas and verticals as per below:

1. Sport   2. E-Marketplace   3. Contactless  4. Food Delivery  5. Social Tech  6. …

We earmarked the first 3 to pursue.     INSIGH

to hospitals and clinics. These solutions comprise hardware such as servers, work stations,

medical grade monitors, direct radiology and computer radiology digitizers among others.

that works together with a Radiology Information System, in charge of managing the imaging

department workflow.  You probably got losted or bored halfway the previous paragraph or, if you read it all, are

need such solution. This is not any different to what many of our potential customers felt

every time we approached them to start a conversation. In other cases, the customer had an

idea of the solution but did not know exactly why he needed it, the scope of it and the many

advantages they could derive from it. There was and still is some confusion in our market

regarding the best way to implement these solutions, in part due to companies that focus on

solutions.    Selection    We thought it was necessary to do something to educate our potential customers on the

Learning Launch for Annual Review Process

Challenge

Every year my team completes a months-long review process of international trade data. In the five  years I have been working on it, this process has remained unchanged. This year, not only are we short a  team member due to a vacancy, but we also have a brand new project that will be competing for time  and resources during the annual review. Our challenge is to try to make our annual review process more  efficient both with time and resources.

Selection

Because we have been aware of and preparing for this issue, our team has already come up with  multiple ideas for getting all of the work done with less resources. These range from ideas like tightening  the schedule, having team members work concurrently on different projects and even pulling resources  from other teams.  Because we have a lot of ideas to sort through and not a lot of time until the review  starts, we will try learning launches in order to test solutions quickly. In our case, our “customers” are  not traditional customers,  but other employees of the organization who compile or otherwise use our  data.

Application

For our first learning launch we focused on the project’s schedule.  We created process flows, including  durations and dependencies, based on past reviews. By mapping out the entire process, and inviting  feedback from the other areas of the organization that use our data, we were able to identify tasks that  could be processed more quickly or concurrently. Because all of our stakeholders were involved, any  problematic schedule changes (like unrealistic durations, unavailability of inputs) were identified and  avoided right away.

Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a powerful tool that are applicable in various situation of our  daily life because it is the tool that I applied all the times. As a founder of the pesto pizza an online agency that propose a large band of choices concerning  Hostels, I always faced the challenges of how to attract more website’s visitors  to try and fall in love with our Hostels’ selection. Besides, I also faced  challenges of how to ensure the phenomena of finding new Hostels’ partner to  convince them to be part of our website. I choose to apply storytelling as it is  able to get insight into users, build empathy and reach them emotionally. I often  create personal activities that would make our website agency more attractable.  Special offers always captivate the attention of our website’s visitors, they are  mainly activities that people could enjoy during their vacation.

Application

Storytelling indirectly involves emotional branding. Emotional branding in fact  is the practice of building brands that directly appeal to consumers’ self,  emotional state, needs and aspirations. The purpose of emotional branding is to  establish a connection between consumers and products by stimulating  consumer emotions. Human needs such as love, power, emotional security, and  self-satisfaction are based on emotions in the subconscious, as the basis of  emotional brands, and allow marketers to create self-fulfilling prophecies in  consumer demand. People want to meet demand, and advertisers need to  implement these needs in a permanent cycle. In our case, the brand consists on  the Hostel we propose in our website, to make it more interactive we reserve a  section for reviews that would give the user the impression of safety. Challenge:

That happened during my previous job and it was in the power generation sector and the CEO  decided to assigned me to a construction project based only on the trust not the qualification, and  the challenge for me was I did not have any information about the construction technicalities, plus  that the project was delayed by 7 months and need to be delivered as soon as possible.

Selection:

The selection was complicated not only one selection of the methods will be enough I need to use  more than one method mixed together because the situation was very complicated, so the closest  used methods was the visualization and the mind mapping mixed together, learning launch.

Application:

First of all I did a mind mapping to come with a plan to get to know how I will deal with this strange  situation, and the result was that I do not have the knowledge to lead that project by myself so I will  need a group of professional team members to handle the technical issues and I will be able to  handle the management issues, plus that type of accountability will need a certain type of friendship  and a high level of communication.

Second I used the learning launch, I met all the team members and I request a meeting with all the  team and the CEO to primary study the project and set the roles and come up with solutions for the  tie line that already got a problem.

3rd step using the visualisation with the client, I setup a meeting and got all the information from the  client and his issues with the project and his problems with the previous project manager, to use all  that information to set the statistics

Insight:

It really started working with the team with the new policy that every specialized person will be  responsible on his part of the job and he will attend the technical meetings with me to replay on the  technical requirements, and I will not get the success of the project for myself but we all will get the  success, and everyone felt the ownership of the

DESIGN THINKING APPLICATION  This paper aims to show how I applied a Design Thinking tool to a current challenge I am working on in  my professional work.

I.  CHALLENGE

I am currently doing projects for the ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY (WWF) in the Philippines that  advocates a new concept of Corporate Social Responsibility, but brought down to the level of an  individual, and in particular for the youth. We call this Personal Social Responsibility or Personal CSR  (CSR 3.0) which is anchored on 3 values:

a. Citizenship – where the individual is aware of his or her responsibility in the community, and

society

b. Sustainability – Where each person tries to live in a sustainable way that respects the

environment.

c. Responsiveness—Where each person responds to those in need, and uses his or her talents to

contribute to social good.

The reason why our Foundation believes in this concept of Personal CSR for the youth is because of the  following reasons:

1. The youth in our region (Asia) comprise majority of our population. Therefore they are a force

who can contribute a lot of positive impact for socio-economic development (UNFPA, 2014).

2. Young people are always asking themselves – “How do I create meaning in my life?” “How do I

make a difference?” Hence they are constantly looking for avenues to discover what they want  to do in life, while finding that sweet spot where they use their talents and passions to serve a  specific need in the world (Wong, 2012).

3. Because corporations are always looking for innovative ways to contribute to society, it is

recommended that they engage more young people in their CSR efforts because the youth have  these innovative ideas, and have the passion and ability to execute them (Klein, 2012).

In highly technology and global competitive world, person needs to develop and use various  sets of skills for being successful. One of these types of skills is design thinking. Design is  considered as key activity of engineering. Design thinking is crucial to design effective  solutions for meeting social needs. Similar as problem solving, design is also a natural  human activity. In the business process, design thinking is essential to design the products  and services for achieving business competitive.

This design thinking essay includes reflection and self-analysis which I have experienced  overall design thinking activities in the class. By this reflective report, I will demonstrate my  knowledge of design thinking in the overall unit. In addition to this, design thinking essay  will also include the action plan of key activities which I require to gain knowledge and skills  in next six months. This design thinking essay is the demonstration of my learning and  understanding in the class lectures. In addition to this, this design thinking essay would be  prepared on the basis of blog entries which are recorded previously.

In the blog entries, there are total 9 blogs including week 1 to 9 which are recorded as my  learning process. This design thinking essay will include time-stamped meaningful blog  entries of overall unit. The report will also include critical self-analysis for the personal  development which will be directly connected to identify strengths and weaknesses.

In the blogs, I have recorded all the activities done in the classes related to the concepts of  design thinking. The recorded blogs are very helpful for to analyze my performance and  understanding during the overall class activities. Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge & Selection

I am an intern in my organization (an IT services company) in the consulting area. I am a member  of a Design Thinking team created to improve our ways of working and create value to our clients.  We are not Design Thinking experts, so we are taking courses and trying to learn more about this  interesting subject.

This is a big company, therefore there are a lot of employees and we don’t know each other in  many times, so what If I need something related to another department? or the opposite side,  what if a salesman, for example, needs a consultant to ask them something? I think this is the  main problem of these huge companies. Therefore, I started to think a solution for this problem  and asked myself how I could fix it. After days of research and benchmarking other companies I  found a solution. WHAT IF I create an online platform, divided by departments, where I’m able to  find each of my colleagues, to post anything in forums. We would only have to put our credentials  to enter the platform.

I introduced this idea to my boss, and he was delighted! We thought that the best option was to  launch a prototype and see how it worked.

Application

For our first Learning Launch, my team and I created a web application but in beta version. We  thought in our needs as employees, If I had this application what would I add? We made a list of  everything we need: employees chat, members of each departments, people hired, holidays  calendar, forums…

After a month of hard working and with the help of the coding team, we made the beta version  and we launched it. It was completely a success! Our colleagues were delighted too, we knew each  other more, we found things about our colleagues that we didn’t know, for example, one member  of the marketing department had his own business of heating jackets. Everybody was very happy  with this platform, so the board accepted to make the final version with some added details.

Challenge

I am part of a sand mining business. We mine and supply natural building material.  Our organisation is divided into three components, namely: Mining, Transportation and  Stock piling depot. We supply material to variety of clients ranging from big  construction companies to individuals who may want to renovate or build a new home.  Our challenge is to improve our operations in order to make them more efficient. By  resolving this challenge, we will be able to serve our clients better and improve the  organisation’s profitability. Our main focus will be on the usage of machinery and plant  equipment during mining and transportation activities. We aim to discover what the  team members regard as challenges that hinder efficient and effective production  practices in the mining and transportation activities.

Selection

Our chosen design thinking tool in addressing the challenge that we are facing is the  learning launch tool. In basic terms, the learning launch tool is an experiment that  seeks to examine ones new idea, to test its fitness in a real market place. The reason  for choosing this tool is that it is customer centric, hence it requires one to get out there  and talk to the customer. The fundamental element in this tool is to formulate a  hypothesis. In the video by Norbert Pohl, it is highlighted that the purpose of a learning  launch is to get the truth. This truth will either confirm or disconfirm the assumptions  made.

Application

In applying this tool, we followed the learning launch process. We put our idea into a  hypothesis. We then established our key assumptions. For our first learning launch,  we focused on the usage of the plant and equipment during the production processes. text:
Reflection - Storytelling

I decided to tackle a problem related to education: How do we engage our

students into reading literary texts or books? The key word of this question, for

me, is “engage”. As a literature teacher, I don’t want my students to just go

through the pages mindlessly, I want them to include the habit of reading in their

lives and to develop a meaningful connection with the stories.

For that, me and other teachers decided to use the Storytelling tool, since this

exercise emphasizes the human experience in contact with a challenge or cause.

According to Corey Perez, in his lecture, Storytelling transforms a problem, which

should be tackled from a rational and linear perspective, into a cause, which

unites people’s interests and abilities. More than that, as he asserts, Storytelling

creates an emotional connection between the participants and this challenge.

These were exactly the features that we were looking for in our discussions. With

this tool, we could spark the interest of our students in the act of reading and

position them as active agents in these stories, which are the stories of their lives,

in the end.

We started the activity by asking one class of each grade (since we many) to

individually describe their daily lives. We offered a big weekly chart divided by

days of the week and hours of the day, in which they could map their days, from

when they wake up to their sleep hour. We asked them to include any relevant

information, be it extra courses, part-time jobs, commitments, study schedules,

favourite hobbies.

As a complement for this concrete representation of their routines, we invited

them to a group conversation on their impressions, feelings and opinions about

their lives. Their likes, dislikes, opinions on school, education, and work. We,

teachers, listened for more than one hour and we took notes of words and

aspects that called our attention.

Reflection on a learning launch

Challenge    I am head of software development and member of the product management team at a  small to medium sized business in Switzerland. The company sells standard software in a  specific niche of the financial industry. From time to time we have to implement new modules  for our software.  Our challenge is to improve the effectiveness of the software  enhancements we implemented. Why effectiveness ? Because in the past, it was considered  that as a standard software supplier we certainly know what customers needs & pains are.  We then implemented new modules or functions. While offering the newly realized modules,  we experienced regularly that it was nice that we have built something ­ it just was the wrong  thing. No effective solution, because it did not really fit to the customer's needs, so obviously  there was no satisfaction or wow effect at all.      Selection    I have selected the learning launch tool ­ why ? Simply because the learning launch tool  offers the idea/execution of testing a MVP under real market conditions, therefore following a  fail fast (...and with this probably a fail cheap(er)) process. Software development is an  insane expensive process ­ especially in the country I live in. Margins are generally  decreasing, competition is global: if someone has to expect a minimal chance for a fail with a  piece of software ­ then the earlier this happens, the better it is.    The video lesson from Professor Ed Hess in week 4 provided me an additional hint:  One could think to invite some sceptic customers too ­ if the hypothesis “survives” them ­ the  rest will be a piece of cake.     Application    We wanted to provide a new investment management module to our customers. Based on  the experiences in our company, we have taken some advices based on internal experience.  Additionally we did some research on competitors and the market of investment  management software solutions. But the most important part of t

text:
Topic: Mind mapping through ideation

1. Challenge:

To discover a new innovative way to use solar energy. Solar energy can replace non-renewable  energy, but there are some barriers that it has to cross. The acceptance by the people, and the  logistics of delivery of solar power has confused marketers. Hence a product that can overcome  these barriers and create a need for solar energy, and achieve acceptance in the society.

2. Selection:

I have chosen the tool of mind mapping for my analysis. As it can help to build a storyboard with key  words, and their association can lead to ideas.

3. Application:

We can map out the various terms around solar energy first, which gives us the

  benefits of solar energy,

  the delivery logistics,

  cost of installing solar energy,

  consumer, and

  other barriers.

We can now further divide each of these subtopics into key words, so consumer can get divided into,

  consumer expectations,

  consumer knowledge,

  consumer acceptance, and

  the demographic information.

Each of these keywords can further be divided, for example consumer acceptance can be further  divided into:

  Welcomes the change and

  Rejects the change.

4. Insight:

This gives us insight on the fact that all places might not be open to accepting solar energy, hence  based on the demographic research we should target only those cities which have high level of  educational qualification, welcomes the change and technology of solar power, and can afford to  make an investment in the planet.

5 Approach:

I would make a diagram or an actual creative art sheet to present my mind map, for better ideas and  higher clarity.

Reflection - visualisation Unlocking community facilities

Challenge I work for a local government (council) in Melbourne, Australia. Management and  elected members  were concerned that council managed community facilities were difficult to access by community  organisations and members of the public. My team is not responsible for the management/booking  of any facilities, however, is responsible for planning for the demand for additional facilities. The  scoping stage of the challenge indicated that: • Council hired 56 facilities • Facilities were managed by 5 different departments (8 different work units) • There were 32 different customer categories • More than 140 different fee options • Seven different booking systems • Eight different booking forms and hire agreements

The project scope was to: • Improve the experience for the customer, while not centralising the management internally • Optimise community access and use of council managed community facilities

The project was considered a wicked problem to solve because:  • The problem was human-centered - we had no information about how intricacies of the

management system, nor customer experiences/expectations

• There were too many moving parts to clearly understand/document the problem as such we

relied on gut-feeling

• There was a large amount of uncertainty around what the current practices were • Whilst there was a corporate booking system, the data was unusable for analysis

Due to lack of data, storytelling was a powerful tool to keep the project’s momentum and to trial a  number of ideas.

Selection One of the biggest challenges was for the different officers in charge of bookings to accept current  practices were inefficient and bad customer service. text:
Challenge and Selection

I am an officer of our School Organization named Junior Chamber  International – National  University Student Chapter. I am elected there as a Secretary, so it is very important for me to be  able to use the visualization tool to let the other officers understand the plans of the organization  more and for us to easily identify the possible solutions to the existing problems of the  organization. I have once managed a whole event and I always use visualization tool to share my  insights to the committees that I assigned to a work, they also make visualizations for their  suggestions that will improve the event that we are planning to execute.

Application

I started the planning of the event by gathering the committees and other officers of the  organization. Then, I started to make a visualization of what I want for the event to look like. I  started drawing the set-up of the stage and other booths that will be functioning throughout the  event. I explained everything that I want to happen for the event from start to finish so that we  can identify the possible problems that the event may have and immediately make a solution,  and then I let them interact with me with the use of visualization tool. They can edit what I draw  on a whiteboard whenever they have a good suggestion. We always care for the welfare of the  attendees; we want them to experience a well-planned event. We continued making progress  until we came up with the final plan.

Insight and Approach

The final plan is listed on a paper, we printed copies for the people that will be involved on the  execution of that event for them to follow that throughout the event. Whenever we are having  a problem during the event, we can act on it immediately because we also listed possible  problems that we may encounter and the solutions for that problem.

I can say that through that visualizations that we shared to each other, we managed to achieve  the goal of that event and we succeed

The instructor, the  author, and the performer experience a comparable goal: to acquaint, employ  and inspire their audience.  We all attempt to convey the information in the  most compelling and intriguing way possible.  Telling a story captivates the  audience in a novel way. Storytelling, then, is yet another tool for my  collection. text:
Example Reflection – Storytelling

Storytelling is a magical tool that I use most of the time in my class.As a teacher ,I

works as a mentor of few students. I have the responsibility to manage student

expectations and to communicate their own expectations about how they will interact with others.Finally, I have to evaluate men-tee's level of knowledge, skill, and

ability . But every time I am concerned about their mental health.I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to motivate them to improve their states.

I can humanize themselves through sharing stories about my own academic and professional journey. I also share my mistakes and failures too, as these are often where our biggest lessons are learned. It will also help them to be aware that challenges will arise, and the way I dealt with the situation might also help them gain insight about how to build resilience.

I have a story about using storytelling. One of the mentee has very much attention disorder problem.His personal life was not healthy too. So one day I told him about

my past experience. I told him that when I graduated form college I don’t have any future goal. My graduation number was not very satisfactory.But I want to ahead my future with higher studies.. Suddenly I got a call from a reputed university to

pursue my higher studies. Somehow I manage to qualify in the entrance examination. Though my result was not very good but still I have a faith on myself and I love the subject very much.

This worked really well. He really needed individual attention for that brief time, and it ended up with that and a true support. He understand the true value of education and calmed down, her mother, who had become worried about him, calmed down, and everyone around them calmed down. Peace reigned again in there little family.

text: The tool I chose was Storytelling, because after all, we always tell stories, don't we? For  example, in the following I will tell my own story.    Storytelling in my UX Design area is very important from understanding how stories happen  and describing them to discovering problems, when to tell the story of a solution and how it  applies there in that given context.    I applied this tool to the work I did for an NGO that helps animals in Ceará. It was essential  to solve this problem that was to obtain donations for the shelter. Through a website that  contained a virtual puppy in which those who visited the site should take care of it, and  through this interaction the animals themselves counted the expenses they had with each  category such as food, hygiene, etc. And after this care and counting of the context there in  the shelter, the animal asked for help as you could contribute so that they continue to have  the care that you had with him virtually.    The experience was very nice, it was used as a mascot the representation of the advertising  dog itself there, called Ralf, and it attracted interest from local newspapers and gave some  visibility to the shelter, it was very gratifying.    After the completion of this project, I identified some improvements as in the graphic part,  perhaps to see better the language issue of this storytelling and to implant more accessible  resources such as, besides the text balloons, the sound resource of speech.    In addition to this differentiated interaction, the website itself could bring testimonials, animal  and volunteer stories to raise awareness through real stories. It always helps!    It is a really incredible resource to work with, storytelling. I try whenever possible to apply it  in my area. And it was really cool to understand him better during this course.

Challenge in Projects, by Antonio Hanson    Page 1

Challenge in Projects - Identify Root cause and enable department to work on improvements.

1. Challenge

Not aligned working process and understanding of responsibilities in projects.  Project stakeholders have no common understanding of the working process and  responsibilities of the assigned role. This is causing massive delay and unwanted discussions /  confusion in projects.

2. Selection

I selected the tool VISUALIZATION (Module 1) to easily enable the workshop participants to  draft, draw / sketch their view of the process.

In week 1, the 7 minute video “Visualization Tool”, shows that it is great to enable thinking in  a nonverbal way.  Quote:” The visualization is a really core component of the way that we communicate,  whether we're aware of it or not. When we're dealing with very complex problems, we're  actually enacting a different kind of problem solving that has to bring in more than just logic.”

3. Scope

Identify Root cause and enable the department to work on improvements.

4. Application

My approach is conducting workshops with all project stakeholders to gather their  understanding of the process, including the good sides and the pain points.  To be efficient I invite all stakeholders in groups owning the same role in projects. Each group  size should be limited to 4-6 participants.  Each stakeholder shall provide the understanding of their role in project and which  challenges they face.  The best tool to do this is using visualization.  Each participants uses a white board and later on colored sticky notes “POSTIT”. The  participant results and working process will be documented by taking photos of the white  boards and the group.

After we make a serious of ethnographic interviews we make and amazing discovery of how students  perceive the library. You see, one of the main reasons for the lack of attendance in those months was  precisely because there were no classes and the students did not really have a strong emotional  connection with the library so nothing called them to have to attend at that time and mostly preferred  to go to the national library.

That was the key of our beginning to decide to create a storytelling with the students through the social  networks, by using a novel format known as canvas for facebook, that allows the user to interact with  images, photos, videos and sounds from a smartphone, we created a story taking advantage of the  context of Halloween to tell the events that would happen to a student if it was locked overnight in the  Ain  Shams University this night of fear.

text:
Visualization

Challenge :

As a software engineer freelancer,my biggest challenge was to describe how my

program works and what are the steps that I would be taking in order to solve the problems  to my clients through a video meeting or even worse through chat.

Selection:

After completing the course I started implementing visualization, which is a tool that

consists of  easing the consumption of data to ordinary people in order to facilitate  detecting  patterns and drawing  actionable conclusions.   Application:

First,I started incorporating  visualization techniques over video meetings. I started

to show only the part of the code that was interesting without diving into all the functions  which worked great when my client were a little proficient in programming but didn’t yield  much difference otherwise, it also wasn’t possible to do this over chat which was frustrating.  I moved to another method, which was UML, UML is a modeling language in the field of  software engineering that is intended to provide a standard way to visualize the design of a  system. It made a huge impact in my communication with my clients as it simplicity and  graphics made the ideas flow better and the conversations more fruitful.

Insight  & approach :

I learned a lot from visualization, the most important point was that not all people

understand what I say  even when they say so, implementing UML with my clients not only  made them understand my approach to creating their desired programs  but also invited  them to engage more and add suggestions which helped creating more sophisticated  programs that met their needs.

Since I’m transitioning  towards the analytics field, I made sure that I don’t only learn

the theories but also create useful visualization and graphics to improve the collaboration  experience.

The activity will be carried out at the beginning of the working day, so that the workers are  more willing to collaborate, since by experience, if the activity was carried out later, the  workers would be thinking only of leaving and the information collected could be wrong.

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information. I have founded State Bank of Pakistan, a design studio with a colleague I have meet during my master in London. Our  background in urban design and social strategy has pushed ourselves to trigger new more socially oriented  approaches in the urban development dynamics. This appears really difﬁcult to be implemented in the Italian  reality due to a lack in the ﬁeld of urban planning and design. The approaches we wanted to promote  consists in local economic development and social innovation, social participatory design processes, human  centered design, citizens engagement and co-creation within the ﬁeld of the urban regeneration and  development.

2. Selection: In your own words, brieﬂy describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you  selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references). We have decided to explore the learning launch as tool to rapidly test our idea to then ﬁnd the best format  usable to actually implement State Bank of Pakistan approach and business. We picked this tool becuase the case is really  complex and it requires an amount of a depth and rich understanding of how shaping the business idea  properly. Through the use of learning launch, we have been able to shape, reshape and shufﬂe again our  initial hyphotesis.

3. Application: Describe how you applied the tool you selected to your challenge (e.g., what you did  and how the tool was applied effectively or ineffectively). Greg Parker  Coursera: Design Thinking for Innovation  Reflection – Storytelling  November 9, 2019

Selection

Storytelling is the design tool I selected for my reflection.  My challenge is associated with a small Coffee  Shop and Café at the Business School of my local University.  The Coffee Shop and Café is located on the  2nd floor of the Business School and has limited hours; including closing by 2:00PM.  Often times, students  are either unaware of the food offerings provided at the Coffee Shop and Café or do not have classes on  the second floor and as a result do not purchase food or beverages.  It initially appears to be an out of  sight out of mind scenario.  The Café is one of several food locations on the campus and unfortunately this  location is not profitable.  The Coffee Shop and Café is located in a historical building that was remodeled  by merging the new features with old features.

The challenge is to increase the number of patrons to the Coffee Shop and Café as well as enhance the  communication and marketing of the food and beverage offering.  Classes are offered every day of the  week; however, no classes are offered on weekends.  Employing a barista every day with limited sales  results in a unprofitable situation.  It was very important to understand the variety of potential customers  for the Coffee Shop and Café at my local university.  Hence, the storytelling tool assisted in gaining an  understanding of the potential customer.

Application

I believed that if we were able to get a heartfelt and deeper understanding of the potential customer, we  would be able to better understand their needs as well as their pain points. Reflection: Improving a critical HR process using Visualisation tool

Challenge and Selection

My company is a terminal plant specialist and hence we engaged and relied heavily on foreign workers for construction  and performed maintenance work of terminal plants for our clients. From time to time, our workers would take an  extended period of home leave (vacation) when they fulfilled certain length of contracture employment, 2 years and  after project completion.

1. the administrative support for the sheer numbers of workers involved;   2. the collaboration with all the internal and external stakeholders (e.g. management, accounts, work permit,

and prototype some ideas to save time and financial investment, so we use the Learning

Launch tool.    Application    We conducted Learning Launch twice during the project, at first we prepared a questionnaire

with questions about food, exercise, medical monitoring, illnesses and medicines in use to

our clients. The questionnaire was anonymous because our goal was to gather information

to create our customer profiles, to know if we are going the right way.    In the second Learning Launch, we prioritized identifying and understanding what the most

important information we should provide to our clients. We created a low-fidelity prototype for

doctors and nurses to evaluate. We have learned a lot more than we thought, and with the

feedback from healthcare professionals we can better understand how to inform our clients

an organization who had a shared interest over popular culture: Korean dramas, K- Pop, and the entertainment industry. Because none of our office board is Korean or has a deep  enough understanding of certain aspects of Korean culture we would like to have  someone who has a better understanding to assist us in creating better quality  meetings for our members.

called the Korean Students Association (KSA) whom we would like to seek help  from; however, whenever we try to approach them with an idea we are shut down.  We have failed to understand why and want to approach them again with a different  method.

​Reﬂection — Learning Launch

​I am member of design team in my current company and we faced interesting task that made a lot

of discussions. Our client provides solution for people who have problems with pelvic ﬂoor. Recently

they produced new version of their product and won RedDot award. Because of that they decided to

change web-site of the product in order to increase sales in the online channel. We created two

diﬀerent solutions. The ﬁrst one is social prooﬁng concept, that provides a lot of information about

users, their feedback, testimonials, success stories, publication in press, etc. The second one is

product oriented concept, that provides information about product and the solution for customers.

So, opinions are diﬀerent. Which of the concepts will acts best?

​Our team has already done several design thinking activities, like journey mapping, creating

personas, etc. So we are ready to try the learning launch tool. We want to test our ideas with

potential target audience.

​For our ﬁrst learning launch, we focused on the information structure and how properly users

eKYC (electronic know your customer) solution for Bank

1. Challenge

We provide banking and financial services in Vietnam. In the context that customers are less likely to  come to the bank counter because Covid-19's issue is very complicated; the customer is difficult to find a  parking space, then waiting to be served; This resulted in a sharp drop in transaction volume, making us  need to find solutions to solve this problem for both customers and banks. We think that it is necessary  to have an eKYC (electronic know your customer) solution to identify customers via mobile devices,  though customers do not need to go to the bank counter to be identified and they can make  transactions remotely. This needs to be in place for a maximum of 3 months to ensure attracting new  customers and serving existing ones.

2. Selection

We think that these are just our analysis and assumptions, not sure whether eKYC implementation can  solve the above problems? While the cost of hiring vendors, building solutions, and integrating with  existing mobile apps can take a lot of resources including time and money. So we choose the Learning  Lunch tool to verify our assumptions to be correct, based on our testing with customers, if our  hypothesis is correct and valid, the bank will step up from and develop the eKYC experience more  widely.

3. Application

We begin with an analysis based on the bank's existing data on customer transactions. Then we define  the customer base and build a customer persona who wants the eKYC solution. We meet and interview  the client in the set of customer base to test and refine it. We then proceed to build the customer  journey mapping based on the interview data we have collected. Designing a common history to win the challenge of the future

I work as a management consultant and my job is, most of the times, to help client companies  review their current strategy and organization and decide how to change and adapt both, in order  to remain competitive in a rapidly evolving environment. I was recently engaged by a large  multinational enterprise that works in the area of consumer goods with the following request: the  management team of the Italian subsidiary (around 25 people) has been recently profoundly  changed with young new mangers joining the firm in several key roles. This change has created a  tension in the team between the new-comers, strong of their professional skills and updated  knowledge, and the “old guard”, composed by seasoned managers with lot of experience and  power in the organization. This split is not helping the company in moving ahead with the speed  and efficacy it needs. Moreover, now it is time to develop a new strategic plan and it is mandatory  for all the managers composing the team to offer their contribution while avoiding interpersonal  conflict or power fights. A hard confrontation is expected but should be limited to the different  views about the future of the company and should find a synthesis in a strategy shared and  supported by the whole team. How can we create the conditions for all this to happen in a one  and a half day of residential workshop?    I was working on this project together with a colleague of mine. She is a psychologist and her  knowledge was very helpful in finding the right solution to this problem. text:
Example Reflection – Visualization

Challenge

One of my company’s subsidiary has planned an organization which aims to be shared ideas about  common topics between my company and them. Only 10 minutes has been allocated for our  team to tell how we manage our business, so we had a strong challenge with time restriction.

Selection

Vast amount of number have been obliged to tell, since our profession is revenue management. In  order to transfer our knowledge to others, being coherent and persuasive was our main focus, and  visualization method fitted well for that focus

Application

As I mentioned in “Selection” part, a great KPI pool will have been told. We have planned our  presentation flow before and decided to tell our subject in 5 slides: main KPI’s, history of them, what  we did before, what we are planning to do, and KPI projection.

Pie chart was the best way to show all KPI’s and their share in one scheme, so first slide included a  pie chart. In order to tell the history of any KPI, bar chart was suitable. Nevertheless, template graphs  in MS applications like pie chart and bar chart was insufficient to express the action history and new  plans. There are some free presentation templates on web, and 24slides.com is one of them. That  website has helped us to prepare our 3rd and 4th slides with aesthetic visuals. Finally, KPI projection  was similar with KPI history, so bar chart was used for the last slide.

Insight & Approach

In case vast amount of numbers are obliged to tell and time limit is a challenge, visualization tool is  useful for a clear presentation. Even if you tell missing parts about your presentation, visualization  prevents that possibility and help you to leave a perfect perception to the audience.

text:
MIND MAP

Challenge & Selection

My challenge was to plan my career path and being promoted to higher position in

my current organisation in 2 years. I’ve diagnosed areas of my expertise, skills and

gaps that I need to complete.

I’ve chosen to use mind map as a visualisation to my challenges. I’ve grouped in 4

different areas which could have an impact on achieving my goal – being promoted

to the higher positions. In my opinion mind map is a great tool to organize a large

quantity of data, establish criteria and plan the suitable actions. In order to prepare

a mind map I have used mobile applications which gave me possibility to quickly

modify my plan/strategy based on the feedback I’ve collected.

Application

I’ve prepared first chart with the main goal I wanted to achieve. I’ve put there also

all the ideas and tasks.

Based on job description, collected feedback what skills I need to have on this

position and my idea of it I defined four core areas of actions that will bring me

closer to have opportunity to being promoted. I analysed which of them will be

useful even without my promotion and I focused only on  two of them as leverages

of my success.

Insight & Approach

At the beginning of my challenge I was afraid that there are too many actions and

challenges that are ahead of me and I won’t be able to achieve my goal. After

putting all of the information in the chart I’ve realised that it is possible to classify

actions I need to plan in main categories. What is more I don’t need to realize all

the tasks but it is crucial to focus on one or two of them with the most added value.

What is more mind map helps me to coordinate my activities and also plan them on

the time line so I feel that I have a control over this project and I can modyfia it.

text:
Reflection - Storytelling    Challenge     We are a group of school friends who have got together ‘virtually’ almost twenty-five years  after leaving school. One of the friends posted about an unfortunate case of a young boy  (studying in our school), who had leukemia and needed urgent funds for treatment. The  amount had to be remitted in the shortest possible time to save his life.      The challenges were as follows

-  We needed to reach out to as many donors as possible in a short time

-  We had to be able to communicate with the target audience in a language that they  would find interesting and appealing

-  The people who would contribute were busy folks and I had only a few seconds to  grab their attention

-  Because it was a medical emergency, there were medical terms associated with the  illness and the remedial processes – they were not understood by the audience.

-  There are many skeptics around crowd-funding appeals of this nature. So our appeal  had to stand out in terms of authenticity.

-  The process of remittance also had to be very simple and convenient

Selection     We decided to use the tool of Storytelling to make my case. We wanted to create an  impression in the shortest possible time to allow the donor to make up his mind and  contribute to my cause.     I remembered the lecture by Ricky George from Mars and how a human being needed to be  at the centre of the conversation and used a real story in my appeal.    Application     My story centred around the young boy’s love for cricket – a game that is very popular in my  country. To gently nudge the memories of our own school days we used the tag line ‘help  him go back to playing cricket again.’    By bringing in an everyday real-life slice of life, the audience immediately connected with  the story and donated for the cause.     This is how the appeal went -     Two months back, 10 year old Vincenzo Mondal was only worried about how many runs he  would score at the next cricket match.

Learning Launch

Challenge

I am working for a software editor, member of the gaming department and my challenge with my team is  to design new mobile games that we hope that large public will like and adopt them.

For our last mobile game application, we decided to adopt the design thinking process in order to design  innovative games and we will focus on trying to uncover during a first launch what our colleagues from  other departments consider to be enhanced and improved with regard the first testable prototype that  we developed.

Selection

As we progressed in the Design thinking process and we have a working prototype of our application, we  decided to try the learning launch tool in order to test our assumptions and prototype. The learning  launch will allow us to think fast and cheap by having a quick and inexpensive feedback and market-driven  data. We hope that the learning launch step will allow us to quickly identify the strengths and weaknesses  of our new mobile application and to prompt new ideas.

This is very important step as it will make our application resonate with live users and make the first  contact with reality. Learning launch should help us to improve our first prototype by being more agile,  responding quickly and doing incremental changes.

We selected 25 colleagues, equal percentage of males and females, from an age range corresponding to  our target audience (between 20 to 40 years old) and we are going to ask them to test the first prototype  for one week and submit their feedback.

Application     Two main assumptions were in the scope of our first learning launch process and we were ready to test  them.     The first assumption we tried to test is that our new application is easy to install, and the new player can  be on board quickly and easily. We asked our colleagues from other departments to download the  application on their mobile phones, install it and start to play. We have asked them also to send us their

text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection  The challenge faced was exploring a complex and uncertain issue for which there are no good analogues  and we were unable to go directly to the customer to gather data. Because of this several methods  needed to explore the “What is.”     The team I led through this process used this approach to seek to understand the world of a physician  who is now having to treat patients via telemedicine in response to COVID-19, determine pain points in  this process and position us to generate potential solutions.     The tool selected was Mind Mapping which,  from the course , we know is a process to generate insights  from exploration and use those insights to created design criteria.     Mind Mapping was selected because it allowed for data collected through several design thinking  approaches to be combined in a way that would detect patterns to inform our next steps. Additionally, it  allowed us to leverage input from both a small agile team and a broader team in this process. This   allowed for both refinement of the data as well as the creation of organizational alignment around the  output.       Application   To execute this process, I enlisted a small group of stakeholders and leveraged the Mural platform so  that we could simulate being in a room together and utilize divergent and convergent thinking  techniques. The team executed several design thinking approaches to generate a robust data set. These  included persona generation, empathy mapping and journey mapping.     Once the small team had generated all this data, it was time to share with a broader team who also  serves this customer. For this, I applied the Mind Mapping process outlined in the course and in  “Designing for Growth, “ by Liedtka and Olgivie.     This was done by inviting the broader team to take a curated tour of the small team's work and walk  through each area of the gallery/Mural first as individuals and then in collective synthesis. Reflection- MIND MAPPING Challenge & Selection:- A mind map is a graphical way to represent ideas and concepts. It is a visual thinking tool that helps structuring  information, helping you to better analyze, comprehend, synthesise, recall and generate new concepts. In a mind  map information is presented in a way that resembles much more closely what idea you had in mind.  Since it is an activity that is both analytical and artistic, it engages your brain in a much, much richer way, helping  in all its cognitive functions. And, best of all, it is fun! Its fun part may help all the person present in the room to  be attentive and understand better. It presents, in a visual way, the core elements of what a person might be  thinking or want to explain or give the idea of its concepts.  Mind mapping tool can be used to organise large amounts of information, combining spatial organisation,  dynamic hierarchical structuring and node folding. In my personal life i use mind mapping in every way possible  eg.- making my timetables as i am in college it helps a lot & taking notes of what has been taught in class. It has  also been suggested that mind-mapping can improve learning/study efficiency up to 15% over conventional note  taking.

Be as visual as you can. Keep the topic labels as short as  possible. Reflection on the Visualization Tool

Challenge

Coming from an engineering background, I have noted while sharing new ideas and concepts  among the various stakeholders, there is a less usage of Visual Imagery. Though the times are  changing and new tools are available, still considering that the stakeholders are from different  backgrounds, there is always a strong emphasis on the need of the Visualization tool during the  design thinking process.

Selection

In this reflection, I have selected the Visualization tool to highlight its emphasis in the industrial  environment. To explain the need of this tool I will give an example of the word ‘force'. This word  has many different ‘sub-meanings' when used in different fields. These fields may include English,  Physics, Chemistry, Design, the entire diverse world of engineering etc. Thus to emphasis on the  right ‘sub-meaning’ of ‘force', we employ the use of Visualization design tool, so that the  stakeholders get an exact insight and understanding of what the presenter is trying to convey.

Application

After explaining the need for this design tool, the next question is how do we apply it? In this  diverse world, the applications of employing this design tool are many. I will give my example of  how I had employed this design tool. As I have mentioned earlier that I am from am engineering  background, my job is to generate as many ideas as possible. With that done, the next question  is how to share these ideas with my stakeholders in an impactful way? How can they understand  what I am trying to say or how will the concept work?

The answer is to simply convey my ideas through pen and pencil. Of course you need some Da  Vinci magic to make it more impactful, but a simple sketch will do a better job than many pages  of engineering gibberish. Keep your stakeholders and their background in mind during a  presentation or a proposal. Canva is another tool that I use to make the presentation more  ‘stakeholder friendly

text: As a display artist, I certainly use visualization or visual thinking the  most. Visualization is very important as it allows us to think in a non- verbal, creative way. Since I am an artist, I express absolutely  everything through visualization.  Now, working with a client or those who evaluate my product, first of  all, I present to them a presentation in which everything is clearly  shown in diagrams and pictures. What inspired me, how I came to this  or that idea, what result I wanted to get – all of this is shown visually.     In my project, which is related to the creation of a font, for example, I  clearly showed where I took the elements to create a font, in what  order I connected them and what result I was striving for (references).  Taken together, this formed a large, but understandable scheme. It  helped a lot to convey information to people. Made my thoughts  available to others. Visualization is especially helpful when I need to  quickly present a product (in this case, a font), show the history of its  creation and how it can be used. In fact, it seems to me that  visualization is the only way to do it quickly and correctly. It is a  powerful tool for presenting complex information in an interesting and  easy to understand way. The human brain synthesizes and stores visual  information much faster and better than any other. However, if the  visualization is done incorrectly, the effect may be the opposite.  Incorrect presentation of information can not only partially distort the  message, but also lead to a completely misunderstanding. Data  visualization allows you to analyze large amounts of information and  see trends and relationships that were previously hidden.

Challenge

After long years of working as an employee, I’ve decided to take and leap of faith and start my own  business. Now, bear in mind that I have long diverse track record in different industries and diverse set of  roles/functions. My primary passion and skill was always about talking possibilities and wonders of  technology. Once I get to talking about a subject that I’m passionate about, the crowd will buy into my  narrative and my gift was always in persuading people in things that are important to me.

With that as a context to the challenge my initial Hypothesis was based on idea of introducing “Innovation  as-a-Service” model for SME’s across Scandinavia. This would be a type of a mix between Management  Buy-In and/or Consulting for Equity. Would that Idea work?  Or would be forced to pivot our core service  offering towards more traditional Management Consulting practice or probably even launching Venture  Capital fund.

After carefully assembling a team of partners with diverse sets of backgrounds, skills and personality types  we began testing our Hypothesis whether or not it could be confirmed.

Selection

After rigorous selection process to assemble a team we landed on testing the Learning Launch and called  the process for “Rapid Fire testing” to get assessment about our service offerings for matured Scandinavian  business environment, dominated by legacy technology and slow passed innovation.

We started our “Rapid Fire test” by gathering piles of data from public registrars. Mind MAPPING

Challenge & selection: As I was working for a large FMCG company, I was asked to establish our main  brand as a leading player in the digital world, in my country. The mission looked challenging and I  was just starting with the new role. I had to find a way to define the strategy together with some key  company leader. Therefore, I used the Mind Mapping method to start shaping the strategy and the  action plan. I choose the mind mapping tool, because I wanted to connect participant ideas to a  central challenge we had. I wanted to favour creativity, find a method that allow people to work  together et get the best of the participant experience and mix all sort of enterprise background.

Application: First of all I have displayed on the wall in front of all managers the central question /  challenge we had to solve and I have phrased it the following way: How can we make our brand the  most accessible and profitable online luxury brand for everyday enjoyment and indulgence, within 5  years? I gathered about 12 of the best managers in a room and I have asked them to write on sticky  notes, all possible answers to the question in a very concrete manner, when possible with a verb,  action and very solution oriented. Then, we have reviewed all proposed notes together to make sure  we understood them correctly, sometimes we have rephrased them to make them clear.

Then we started the mind mapping exercise. Silently every participant was connecting all sticky notes  within each other starting from the central question, and we were grouping ideas based on affinity  and logic. At the end of the exercise we had a couple of grouped solutions emerging from the mind  map. Finally, we asked each participant to vote for their preferred grouped solution and suggest who  was the most appropriate person to lead the task. After adding up all marks, we had our solutions  prioritized in front of us.

text:
Design Thinking Innovation on Learning Launch

Challenge

I am heading one of the Product Lines in the Packaging Materials company and lead a team of  Product Managers. We work a lot with the new product development, but very often base ideas on  how new products shall look and perform based on our own assumptions and technical capabilities,  rather than on customer insights and needs. In this assignment, I would like to reflect how we utilized  learning launch on one of the new products. Specific of our business is that it is very capital heavy  and launching new product requires many investments into development work, some production  asset adjustments, promotion, etc. Therefore, if the product does not fly – risk of losing substantial  money is high.

Selection

Learning Launch is a great tool to test if idea or product can meet customers’ needs and create value  for them before decisions with big financial impact are done. It can be used to test the entire concept  or specific assumption and from my perspective represents the quintessence of the agile approach.  The aim of using this instrument is not to prove that idea is right, but to test if it fails or not – so  failure is similarly welcomed result as success, important that it happens quick and cheap.

Application

Starting with the product development – something that has been already done in the past. We had  a need to fill production capacity and decided to develop a product that would fit to the “sweet spot”  (optimal production parameters that gives the highest efficiency) of production. Our assumption was  that this product could be used for customer segment that is new for us and our assumptions for the  product concept were based on the subjective judgment of that business and product requirements.  Since we were targeting a production sweet spot, it was not difficult to create recipe and produce  material, but we decided to first test that our assumptions were correct before launching new  product.

Storytelling

Background & Selection-

Storytelling is really an effective and we all are listening stories since childhood. We connect  to characters, to emotions, to learnings, the values in the stories. We often convey  messages in broader way and with logic. We always should consider about the audience, to  whom we want to connect. The relevant topic will connect them and they will listen to it  from heart, no matter about circumstances.

I work in a manufacturing unit as section manager. There are workman on shopfloor, who  come from a small villages near by and comparatively have less educational qualification. It  is often cases that housekeeping and delayed production in particular area was below par  and every time I have to aware about it and after some words to them they could carry it  out. But it was not a practice and each time we get few downgrades in the area. To make a  considerable difference, I used tool of storytelling and started it more often to up keep the  area.

Application-

I told them a story of making tea. We make tea in kitchen and what if we keep the required  things all over our home? What if we switch on the gas and went to market looking for  lighter? What if tea is ready and we are looking for cup and finding it after 15 minute? What  will happen when guests visit  your home and you are taking longer time to make a cup of  tea? Thus I was able to make them realise the importance of keeping all tools at right place,  a place of each toll, periodic cleaning of machines, prepare well before start of machine. I  also arranged small video from Mercedes Class production line. The things were tidy, ease  of work and fresh look to area.  By telling the importance of up keeping and asking many  questions, I was able to make them realise the importance of house keeping, tools at right  place, energy saving and the increased output and productivity.

Reflection – Visualization

Challenge – Being a solution architect, my role involves providing solutions to achieve the operational  excellence by improving the business processes and user experience to our customers using the  innovative technologies.    Many times, the business process spans across the multiple business units or  departments across the organizations. The organization silos provide structure that allows expertise in  different area, but creates a barrier for information flow and lack of coordinated decision-making process.   My recent challenge was to improve the account receivable process for a mobility transportation  organization who operates in 100+ locations providing on demand service. This required breaking the silos  barrier, have a shared understanding of complete end-to-end business process and information flow and  then identify the process improvements opportunities before providing the possible solution.

Selection – I use the tool of visualization with our customers for scenario visualization. Visualization plays  a role throughout the design and development process. Visualization can materialize the concepts and  make their characteristics more explicit. It makes them clearer and more understandable. It allows to  communicate the ideas and sequence of thoughts. Many times, it helps to identify the hidden entity which  was overlooked by silos between the units.  I always start the process by specifying objective and creating  the drawing of business process flow from stakeholders’ input.  This allows to create a document to work  collaboratively and brainstorm to find the many alternative solutions.
