Challenge

As a designer, I was always relied upon to create visualization or diverse levels of fidelity design  to visually illustrate a shared idea in most leadership roles I occupied back in the university. The  key significance of visualization is its ability to stimulate thinking and enhance dialogue. As a  new hall of residence executives back in the university, we were faced with the challenge of  salvaging an ailing student-run restaurant. Most of the newly admitted students were not  eating in the restaurant but were ordering food from outside the hall. This posed a slight  challenged to us since the administration had invested a lot in relocating it to a more  convenient spot in the hall.

Selection

During the discussion stage between hall administration, we the executives and some selected  students we in cooperated the stick figure sketches to give a seamless visual understanding to  almost everyone in the room. Four out of the five administrators were quite old and the  visualization was purposed for them to share in our views visually.

Application

At this stage I made sketches to illustrate the students journey from going out to buy till they  finally ate their food. In a form of journey mapping, I made sketches whiles we discuss what  could the possible challenge the students had and how we could solve it with very little  investment. After each sketch, I explained the possibilities and the changes that could be made.  As we Iterated at every stage of the students journey we understood what could be the  problem. There had been an influx of delivery services in the school and most restaurants  outside the halls also had their own delivery mechanism. Most of delivery services were timely  and had added value like picking up drinks from stores which was more affordable the  restaurant the student was ordering from. And most of these services were for free. Through  the visualization which more of infographic we all could vivid understand the students

My Reflection – Visualization

Challenge & Selection:- There is an overwhelming problem of refunds  to customers in my company, first thing that came to my mind during  the course. I see how pictorial approach will help in resolving the  problem, now I have diagram putting the issue at the center, and  different stakeholders we need to bring on board in my head. I have  written down questions we need to ask base on what is, what if, what  wow and what works.

We will also do sketching and prototyping, brain storming and a lot of  practice, just like the story of The Good Kitchen in Denmark, we will  use pictorial label in trying to serve our clients better in the aspect of  the refunds. I prefer we have an open mind like Geoff, instead of  George with the fear of falling that actually affected his new  assignment in spite of his past success stories.

Application:- I prefer to group the stakeholders in small cluster of 3-4  teams, this will make participation easy and interactive. Each team will  focus on one area of the problem and represent them with notes then  we come together at the end and deliberate every team’s idea. To me  this was the magic that change the case of senior citizens in Denmark  case.

Insight:-  “The most fundamental natural law of innovation is that the  only certainty is uncertainty” so innovation is not a cast a stone, in fact  we should not be afraid of failing in the process of creating new things,  instead we should be more focus on the journey . George in the course

was afraid of getting into new things and that greatly affected  negatively.

Approach:- In the process of innovation, it is always good to show  customer’s empathy(that’s putting the clients problem at the center  and ahead of your company’s solution), this will make us create new  value for them, and that will eventually make us different to the clients.

text:
Design Thinking in Performance Marketing

Challenge – To calculate accurately the value of lead prospecting in higher education. Traditionally higher education  digital marketing has been all about leads and follow ups to convert them. The old school thinking goes that cheaper  leads mean more leads and more conversions. This is not a sustainable approach and eventually is a wastage of  monies.

Application - Looking at this wastage of time, effort and monies, I decided to clean up the process and take top  down approach and focus on the main goal which is deposits.

Taking each deposit value into consideration and the amount spent on leads and each stage of the life cycle of the  lead I had to calculate a cost of acquisition (COA). Taking this COA in mind, I then took out data for last 4 years to see  the amount spent on each channel/source and the conversion from them.

Apart from the monies spent on each channel, there are slight deviations in lead follow up in each channel by tele  sales team. While some high converting lead channels take longer to convert and the number of calls and longevity  are also factors that account for operational costs.

So taking in last 4 years average both in terms of spends and operational vs revenue from deposits, I could create a  right mix of sources for the coming session while looking at other factors like geographical resonance, demographic  conversions.

This application of historical data helped me get better conversions, lesser spends and overall better productivity  from the tele sales team.

Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge & Selection

Two years ago I worked as a lecturer at the Pesto Pizza of my city. Our class goal  was to match student's knowledge with non-profit organization necessities. We would make teams  of 5, with people from different careers (economics, accountancy, business administration, actuary),  and then guide them in the process of designing and executing innovations that could help a  selected NGO (non government organization) in their business.

In this case I will talk about ​our work with Cupe, a NGO that aims to improve life conditions of  low income individuals using educational and support tools. ​Their main function is about giving  workshops and training to help people get a job​.

The challenge was to create something that could boost investors willing to give financial  assistance ​to Cupe. With that goal in mind and after being working on the “what is?” stage, we  started to connect the dots using mind mapping.

Mind mapping, as seen in the third week video, is about looking for patterns in the collected data.  The use of this tool would help in the quest for a design criteria just before entering the “what if?”  idea generation fase.

Application

We knew that it would be easier to open investors pockets if they get solid prospects about the  return of their investments​.  Taking that into account and after spending some weeks getting data  from the different stakeholders, we started to draw a mind map.

At the center of the map we placed the beneficiaries of Cupe work. Then around it, we draw the  different topics (and subtopics): Who are they/How they live (cluster in main groups); Cupe  (functions) ; Investors (cluster main groups) ; Government (relevant policies linked to this  population).

With the map on the table we began feeding it with data. We conducted extensive surveys to all the  actors in play. Some patterns started to emerge. It was clear that the effectiveness of the different  services given by Cupe

1. Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

Ans. The project is for an online shopping portal for cameras and accessories. The users will be able  to buy as well as rent accessories as per their needs. The portal will have online delivery mechanism,  a community forum for discussions and a dedicated helpdesk support. For tech savvy photography  enthusiasts, who wish to buy or rent cameras and accessories online and save the effort to go outside  their homes, the camera accessories is a photography device that will help photographers to buy or  rent accessories as per their needs at reasonable price. Unlike simply buying accessories, the portal  will also support home delivery and a community forum to ensure better customer experience.

The challenge is to increase the number of views, page hits and transactions on the website and  increase the usage.

2. Selection: In your own words, briefly describe the tool you selected (e.g., what it is and why you

selected it for your challenge -- including any appropriate video lecture references).

The tools used are persona identification, storyboarding and problem scenario identification

text: Challenge  Reflection – Learning Launch  Being the member of advertising department,our challenge is to improve the workflow within the  department in order to increase sales and to spend advertising budgets on the right campaigns. The  project scope includes 15 employees, as well as the marketing department and IT department, with  whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal resources (i.e., budget and employee time).  The project should not exceed 30 business days and the solution should include an even distribution  of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover what our team  members and our key stakeholders within the marketing department and IT department, consider to  be ineffective or problematic with regard to the workflow.    Selection  Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities/tools, so we are ready to  experiment  with the learning launch tool. Broadly speaking, the learning launch is an experiment  meant to quickly test an idea and prototype.    Application  For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of our online tasks. In particular,  we wanted to see if we could structure our tasks, projects, and processes to adapt the methods of  Scrum project management for our work (e.g., time boxed, daily, specific meetings, reviews, etc.) in  an effort to become more agile. This tested our assumption that the structure and execution were  the main causes of our workflow challenge. Our team went through a two-day training. Next, we  went through five workshops to structure our tasks and processes in a more agile way. These two  sessions occurred within in a three-week timeframe. We expected to produce a document with a  clear description of our new, more agile processes/workflow.  For our second learning launch, we focused on gaining clarity about our tasks and priorities. This  tested our assumption that our prioritization of tasks was the main cause of our workflow

VISUALIZATION

Challange and selection

The tool I would like to select would be the visualisation tool. Visualization basically means imagining things and then bring those ideas in front of the customers in a way that they get the clear idea about it. I believe, visualization is one of the most important tools for design thinking. Visualization not necessarily mean we all need to be artists. Everyody can imagine things in a very creative way. We can imagine the things that are not yet the reality but we can make them the reality by visualizing the things properly and bringing the right ideas to the customers or the stakeholders. I can use different things to deliver my visualized idea to the customers/stake holders. For example i can be using photographs, power point presentations with different symbols, colors, etc. Or i can be using sketches too. Visualisation is a powerful tool since there is no limitation as to what we are capable of imagining and visualizing and we can use many creative ways to deliver those ideas to people. Today, as we are all aware that the world is facing one of the biggest challanges of all the decades, the "covid 19 pandemic". I would like to use the visualization tool to try and find a solution to fight the pandemic.

Application

I would like to start the process by firstly visualising the ways or ideas through which I can help people fighting this pandemic. One of the solutions could be to create certain drones that are specifically designed to carry some basic medications, grocery items and so on to deliver them to the people to their homes without any human intervention. Since that we all are aware that the whole nation is in the lockdown and many of the poor people are finding it very hard to get their basic things needed for everyday living. And also it is highly necessary that people maintain social distancing for this pandemic to get away as soon as possible. So one can use these drones to deliver the basic necessary items door

I was appointed the brands and communication Team lead of my organization, a non- governmental organization where I was saddled with the responsibility of Making the local  organization programs and projects visible to the global world in due time.

Selection

Myself and my team got expose to some design thinking tools, the learning lunch tool happened  to the best fit for what needs to be achieved as it speaks to quick test of an idea and prototype

Application

This to check our arrangement to see if  that is the main cause of the challenge. We engage in a performance and project management  profession for three days training for better understanding, Then we go through one  week of  workshops to structure  out given tasks and processes to conform in a more agile way. All this  was done with few weeks and the outcoming gave us a clearer part of what needs to be done  that wasn’t done

text:
Reflection

Challenge

I am a student of 3rd year UX Design Class. My/our challenge is to improve the working of our  college bus transportation system in order to attract more users. The project scope includes the  entire bus ecosystem composed of stakeholders like the ticket-giver to the driver, bus  coordinator and the college authorities who outsource the buses and lastly the bus agencies.  The project is limited to internal resources like the budget and college timings. The solution  should not cut any jobs and should evenly distribute work.

Selection

Since the buses were already plying, we had to first research on the secondary data and then  connect various aspects of the situation in order to study the ecosystem better.  Also we  collected primary data to study this ecosystem in an idealistic manner. So we chose to create a  Mind Map. Broadly speaking, a mind-map is a diagram in which information is represented  visually, usually with a central idea placed in the middle and associated ideas arranged around  it. This helped us to create theme and patterns across the data.

Application

We finished our literature review and collected Visual Data and conducted ethnographic  interviews. Initially we focused on the roles of different people, so that we have a clear idea of  a missing link if any. We divided the roles into three categories of Management, Operators and  Commuters. Then we drilled down into each of their tasks. This helped us link all of them  together. Mind Map was done for a time period of a week which helped us gather and  segregate data properly. We then added various visuals and links to it so that we could present  it effectively to the stakeholders.

text:
Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is a tool I use to normalize the experiences of new parents. I coach and provide therapy to women experiencing postpartum anxiety and depression and am a parent myself. Oftentimes, in the early stages of parenting, individuals struggle to feel like their thoughts, emotions and decisions are normal. So much so, that they have difficulty with making even basic decisions. For example, should I take the baby to the park or just stay home? What if my baby cries when I have to go to the supermarket. On a more extreme level, parents will attach value statements about themselves or about their child. For example, “I can’t go to the park because I don’t know how to get my child to come home. I’m a terrible parent and can’t set boundaries.” Storytelling provides great support and normalization and because I’ve worked with parents for so long, I’m able to share some of the struggles other parents are experiencing and help other parents recognize that they are not alone in their struggles and that their children are not uniquely challenging. Further, storytelling helps alleviate anxiety because it creates a common space for thoughts that feel too difficult to share with others.

Application

I also use storytelling to improve my agency's level of care and to help my colleagues decrease their anxiety around note taking. I developed the internship program at my current agency to improve access to care and to improve student learning opportunities. I provided examples and stories of how interns have helped agencies in the past and how this may apply to our environment. For my colleagues, when they are struggling with notes, I provide not only storytelling but some visualization tools for them to rely on when they are feeling stuck. I created a list of typical clips and phrases used in mental health notes to guide anyone struggling to develop the proper language and I discussed my experience in higher level of care environments to reduce anxiety

Challenge:

I am working for a Pharma Company as a part of the Marketing division. My role is of designing  visual-aids and other marketing materials for Marketing Reps working on the field. The marketing  reps were currently briefing the doctors through physical media like thick books which were  cumbersome and little outdated to match with today’s digital era.

The challenge was to convert this system into digital media which becomes easier for the marketing  people to brief and handle.

The  structure was designed first as to how the data will be collected and routed to different stake- holders and sent to the development team for production for Beta-testing before making it live on  the iPads of the Marketing Reps for actual briefing of the products to the doctors at their clinics and  hospitals.

I had created the designs already and had to convert them into the format required by the IT Team.  The artworks and product sequencing was handed over to the production team and after lot of  coordination and some iterations the Visual-Aids were digitalized into iPad and send for testing.

The Doctors found it quite intriguing and engaging to be briefed in an interactive manner.

Challenge

I am working as an Industrial Designer in construction Equipment company.  We work mainly for enhancing aesthetics and visual aspects of machine. But 3  Years ago We got this challenge of making modular Display HMI for Various  Construction Equipments for our company. Using same LCD display module for  different machines was challenging since every machine has different sort of  information and bring one solution which caters to all machines was tough.

Selection

We thought of using white boarding (Now I will call mind mapping) technique  to put all necessary information from different machines in the table format to  see if we can find some connections between the information.

Application

We made one big white board dedicated to dump all the information related  to different machines in the tabular format. We used to update the white  board as requirements used to change from different machine departments.

So we used to look board from the distance and marked some common  attributes for display. So far everything was going right but we completely  forgot about the manufacturing constraints of LCD + analog dial display.  Because our tabular white boarding method was capable of putting machine  information and not manufacturing constraints.

Insights

Putting information of different machines out there in the board helped us to  see common attributes emerging from the table. But we completely forgot  how to connect the dots with manufacturing parameters. Visualization is analysing the current situation and find out  possible ways to shorten the processing time through drawing.    Application and Insight

We spent an afternoon, using simple diagrams and arrows, outlying (1) the  connections of each task, (2) parties involved, (3) time spent and (4) data flow for the  process on the whiteboard.  By visualizing the whole process and the connection,

Challenge Description –

•  I In today’s world people have been very keen at using the technology. For

every basic need, people have involved the use of Softwares and  Apps. In the

last few years, Machine Learning has been used for most of the tasks. When it

comes to knowing people, you cannot just do it by knowing people. There

should be a proper application, that’d help in knowing people’s interests, likes

and dislikes. A platform where we can adequately know people activity is

Twitter. We can know a person, by his timeline of activities. By applying the

concept of Sentiment Analysis which is a finite part of Machine Learning, we

have created an interface, where people’s interest or opinions about a particular

issue can be judged. This would help a lot for Analysis or Grouping people into

a category.

•  We have created this with a vision of as it would reach all age groups. As we

know of today, everyone on this planet is aware about the use of social media

on a large scale. Hence, getting the profiles of people and getting proper

categorized format of their likes and dislikes on particular topics would be vastly

helpful for sure.

Selection-  I have selected tool visualization

•  Visualization or visualisation is technique for creating images, diagrams, or  animations to communicate a message. Visualization through visual imagery  has been an effective way to communicate both abstract and concrete ideas  since the dawn of humanity.

•  I strongly believe in the power of visualization. We must “see that image” in our  mind before we ever venture forth to manifest it.

text:
Mind Mapping

Challenge/Selection

I'm a full-time student, however I also indulge in personal training sessions where I train people

with regards to their respective fitness goals. I`ve observed that many gym members who work

under a trainer, although might achieved all their goals, however still lack any interest in the

workout that they do. Most of the time their workout consists of unnecessary long hours of

cardio where they are sweating like a pig and hating every bit of what they are forced to do.

Before I started taking personal clients, I used to look at such members and felt really bad for

them. So, I decided to work with a few clients free of cost to not only gain experience but to

also help them. I offered my services to a few members who wanted to shed a few pounds and

started I used the tool of mind mapping.

Application

First of all, before deciding by myself what I wanted for them to achieve, I asked them what

their goals were, I let them be in charge of their Goals and bodies instead of acting like an

authority over them. I kept asking them questions and told them to picture and map all of their

answers in their mind. After a series of question all the members came to the conclusion that

their goals had nothing to do with what they had been doing for years. I asked them to then

draw whatever they thought about during that time. I instructed them that although they want

to lose weight, they could still achieve it by different methods.

I gave them different option to mention on their maps for a single goal, this included different

things, strength training, resistance training, powerlifting, cross-fit and even cardio. I informed

them of each and every possible option and asked them to think about what would be more fun

to do. Some highlighted powerlifting some strength training, but none mentioned cardio.

Design Thinking for Innovation Assignment

Learning Launch Tool

Challenge

A medium sized organization that has been in existence since the last 9 years. The  organization’s learning and development (L&D) program was the least to say cliché with only  classroom training provided. The basic notion in the organization was that the L&D function  is not very impactful, and trainees attend it only because it is mandatory. The major challenge  here was to reinstate the importance of L&D in an organization, building a training module that  is relevant to business processes and leverage it to achieve organizational goals. The scope of  L&D is however currently limited to 20 employees in the organization, highly unstructured  approach being followed and a limited budget available to spend.

Selection

To resolve the above challenge, learning launch was the most appropriate tool of design  thinking as with the limited number of employees in the organization, a prototype is easy to  execute and gain insights on whether the assumption is a viable solution to the problem.  Learning from those experiences and implement solutions differently and inactively to  understand what went wrong and what could be done in a better way.

To identify the proving and disproving variables, a  questionnaire was rolled out to understand what was right about the assumption and what was  not. My Storytelling Experience

Challenge and Selection

Market success sparks a clear engaging story. Storytelling creates authenticity. Authenticity connects to  the behavioral design principle. It is the art of communicating eloquently and creating emotional  connections with people. My dad is a talented artist and struggles to create a market for his paintings. I  was inspired by the storytelling tool. My first question is; How will I use storytelling to successfully  connect my dad’s paintings with potential customers? According to the video reference; ‘Storytelling  says it's not about the list of things we have to do, it's about the connection that we give to people  about a piece of information that we're trying to share.

The first consideration I have is the paintings themselves--if they are abstract or otherwise  interpretative, it would be prudent not to impose too much of a narrative upon them. If they are more  representational, then it also depends upon the potential customers one is trying to seek (for example,  domestic or international) I say this because appealing content will differ between cultural bases.

Another consideration is story content in relation to the artist--whether abstract or representational, a  narrative created by the artist becomes something altogether different and doesn't necessarily  compromise the work in any manner--instead, it can augment the appeal of the work when the  customer is provided with an understanding of the artist's thought processes, daily travails, experiences,  and so forth.

Challenge

I am one of three Program Analysts in my organization’s Public Works Business department. Our  challenge is to perform supporting financial actions in various systems to ultimately spend the Public  Works department $XM budget. We need to be able to answer any questions that come in with regard  to the status of budget vs actuals, to answer/advise on various options to modify execution plans as  emergent requirements pop up and to accurately project/inform if there will be sufficient funds to  execute their plan and stay under budget.

There are at least 15 different product-line and program managers in our department that we support  and additional data calls from our internal command and other commands that all ask us for different  data analysis. Questions and data calls come in at a rapid pace and with short turn around due dates.  Ideally, we would know what all the questions are in advance so we could prepare/setup to be able to  answer but since the financial systems and business rules have been changing for the past two+ years,  no one seems to know what they need or want. Our organization has been modifying financial structure  and organizational structure for the past couple of years with no end in sight. There is another  impending financial system and organizational transition planned in about nine months.

With only three of us performing this time critical work there is always the need for us to cover for each  other when we go on leave or go to training. I am currently finishing this class while I’m supposed to be  on leave because a critical data call came in when I planned to take this training. Assignment - Learning Launch;

1. Challenge:

As a Recruitment agency, we’re overwhelmed with various job order received  comprises of all sorts of job specializations. At time such orders lead us to out of focus  & out of track. Some of the job orders, we were not able to fulfil because of our team’s  knowledge & experienced in those fields are limited. As a result, we lost more revenue  & upset many clients. And at the same time our team are under tremendous pressure  to perform for result & eventually we lost some of our employee too.

2. Selection:

Knowing of the above challenges, we need to launch a new workflow/solution that  enable us to accept job orders that works with our forte. This launch will eventually  convert to more sales, maintained more happier clients & allow us to retain our  employee.

3. Application:

For launching of new workflow, we assemble a working committee of 3 members as  to test on our assumption as to specialize in between 5 to 7 job specializations. We  collected past 3 years internal sales record as to analyse what are the job specialization  that we’ve achieved. Also, research on the open job market as what are the highly  demand of up to 5 job specializations offered by the employer. Follow by a survey with  our 10 clients on their projection of up to 5 job specializations, that they will hire for  the next 12 months. Concurrently a survey will be conducted internally with our 8  team members on the job specialization that they faced challenges with, as compared  to those that are more confident to deliver. These 4 initiatives will be completed  within 3 weeks timeframe. With such finding & clarity that we gathered, we were able  to propose a new workflow.

Reflection- Mind Mapping

Challenge    I am currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration. As a part of our  curriculum and to supplement our education and learning we are regularly tasked with  projects and assignments.  These are in various formats; some are research driven reports,  some questionnaire-based analysis of a certain market trend and some in the form of  presentations. The one factor common in these tasks is that a central topic is assigned around  which further research is required. There is a requirement to visualise thoughts and  communicate. While traditional note taking is always an option, there are more effective  processes to streamline and put in order the thoughts and ideas that arise during research.     Selection    I am enrolled in an internship at a digital marketing firm. As one of the interesting tasks, our  team had to revamp and rejuvenate a client’s marketing strategy for their online platform.  The project naturally required conducting extensive research of the competition to gain a  complete understanding of the market. This would enable us to better place our own client  in the market in relation to its competitors. To make sense out of the wide array of  information and to chart all of it into a constructive flow, I used mind mapping as a tool. The  specific application was MindMeister.  As opposed to just a pen and paper, MindMeister is a  wonderful tool plan a course of action. It provides a clear central idea and links all resultant  ideas to ensure coherency and a clear train of thought.       Application     When given any task, I start by gaining a clear understanding of the main topic or what the  crux of the matter revolves around. text: Storytelling is the difference between solving a problem and creating a cause. A cause is something that  ignites and unites people.     So, the challenge is we are currently in the rainy season. Here in Nigeria, it’s between the period of April to  September. My dad was driving my sisters and I on a morning afternoon sometime last year. It was about  7:30am and a great proportion of road users as at that time were on their way to work/ places of business.  The point is majority of the people had no umbrellas, raincoats, or rain boots. Some sought refuge under  shades and houses/shops with covered spaces, others kept running under the rain. I had been in those  shoes before. It was cloudy that morning, and I had an appointment to catch up with. I had an umbrella I  could have left the house with, but I was reluctant because holding umbrellas can be very stressful when  they are in use and when they are not. I left the house without my umbrella and I was beaten by the rain  (it started shortly after I embarked on my journey). Not only was I late to my destination, I was drenched  and stressed.    Over 50% of Nigeria’s population thinks like this. Umbrellas can be really stressful to carry about. Same with  rain boots (which is even worse).     My research has shown that Nigerians will be more than willing to get a product that will suffice as an  umbrella while eliminating the stress part of it.  Introducing a small portable umbrella (with no handle but  a head band instead) that can be folded into the size of a small handy purse when not in use and worn  around the head when it is in use, will serve as a  solution to this challenge.     Although, we are working on creating a sample and observing how the target market embraces this  potential product.

Storytelling is a tool that I use when working with my clients on the consumer goods sector. Many of  whom have access to great amount of information and little time to rationalize it. Reflection – Learning Launch for Data Product Design Thinking

Challenge:

I am a member of a team that provides business intelligence and analytical solutions to the advisory  services team of a financial services firm. The advisory team published a list of recommended preferred  securities every week that is accessible to almost 4,000 financial advisors.

The challenges faced by the advisory team was that their members had to spend considerable amount  of time every week in collating, sorting and formatting data from Bloomberg before publishing the  recommended preferred securities list. Also, it was cumbersome for financial advisors to view and filter  preferred securities from the basic published Excel file as per particular criteria such as coupon rate,  yield to worst, tax considerations, ratings and outlook categories.

Selection:

Learning launch tool enables engaging potential customers in the creation, design and testing of new  ideas as soon as possible; and learning as you go, iterating constantly for improvement.

Our team used the learning launch tool as it is the ideal technique to ideate, create prototypes and test  various solutions in several cycles that will be created for the advisory team as well as the financial  advisors. This seems to be the best approach in applying design thinking for data products.

For the first learning launch, we underwent two rounds of discussions with the advisory team. This  helped our team to be aware of the weekly updating process in detail. Design Thinking for Innovation Final Assignment:  Hector Rodriguez

In 2015 I attended the TEDxMileHigh conference. Interacting with the other attendees I heard the  same story from multiple people. “I am inspired by these talks but then Monday I’m gonna go to

work. Tuesday I’ll go to work. Wednesday I’ll hear from my well meaning but risk averse friends and  family. By then, I’ll be right back where I started.” This story was consistent with my own story and  the story of countless people I know. We end up stuck living a life that is less than what we desire,

what we hope for and what we are capable of.

This may sound like a very major challenge. There are many reasons people are dissatisfied with life  and work. However, this is the beauty of design thinking. Problems like these are what motivated me  to learn about the discipline as the problems addressed by design thinking are often more interesting  than the ones addressed with linear thinking and analytics. Through my process, I was able to  determine what smaller piece of this issue I was able to impact.

I chose storytelling as my tool primarily because it is the tool that appeared the most clearly  connected with my initial motivation. Storytelling allows me to envision the very people I want to help  in order to discover the root of their problem. This video lecture describes how storytelling is  compatible with “having a cause”, and describes the power of selling a challenge through telling a  compelling story.

Reflection assignment – Storytelling

Challenge

One of our clients wants to perform an upgrade for their IT systems. This system culminates both IT  and Business-related topics and as such impacts the business processes when updated. Within the  company, there was a severe disconnect between the business and IT side. There is no communication,  needs and wants are not expressed properly, and everyone works within their own silo. For a successful  upgrade plan, there is a severe need for alignment, communication, and cooperation between  Business and IT and within them as well. The business side has many time-consuming projects planned  in the next few years. The IT side will require resources of business to successfully upgrade and  implement. Our biggest hurdle is convincing all sides of the company that they are part of the same  team and share the same mission. This may not seem like it fits in innovation, but the IT system is  what’s called a PLM system chich also aids and improves the processes set in place for innovation and  development of new ideas.

Selection

The obvious tool for this is of course storytelling. We must create a common ground between all facets  of the company and thus by including them in the same story we hoped to connect them and facilitate  collaboration. Storytelling allows the stakeholders to express their concerns and discuss where and  most importantly when the upgrade can take place. By creating this cultivated upgrade goal, we hoped  to forego all immediate rejection and move toward possible options/

Application

To create the right story, we first had to gather information on the clients and their current projects.  We found out, as said above, that the business side has little time in the upcoming years. They blatantly  rejected any resource requests that we made at the start. This meant we had to dig deeper and by  including IT stakeholders we managed to explain the necessity of the upgrade. Challenge

My team and I were included to a completely new project at work. It was

very challenging because it was a new important supplier for us. The thing about  of our team, was that many of our members team were multidisciplinary team  and some of them were inexperienced at the way the supplier works. It was  important for all of us to be on the same way and to have the correct  comprehension of supplier’s work for the better understanding of the project. Selection

So, we (the team leaders) decided to put more effort on the explanation

for al the members. We decide that if we create something to visualize better  how is the flow of the supplier, it will be easier for everyone to see it. In order  to this, the tool I use was Visualization. We wanted to clarify all the doubts about  how they operate an, the way we would be involved with the running project.

Application

We started drawing in different post-it all the elements involved in the

flow of the operations of our supplier. We look for different colors to symbolize  persons, machines, areas, connections, etc. Then we tried to structure it as a  diagram and matching different things with lines and arrows to symbolize the  direction ad collaboration among different elements. We ask someone from the  new supplier team to supervise and check that our flow diagram was correct  and easy to understand it in the correct way.

MY Journey®: Company General Use

Soft Startup - Visualization

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding of a problem  space to my management before proceeding to the solutions. I use this approach with my management in my  workspace because it allows me to visualize the issue in order for them to better understand and calculate the  magnitude of the issue for swift and efficient resolution. During my field deployment, l have used power point  technique with live streaming animations and infographic with an existing options that will visualize the issue to the  team, including management and counterpart project management team (PMT), grabbing their tension with all  possible challenges in the near future. The team, management and PMT, has diver’s specialty from mechanical, civil  and electrical engineering which will be hard in the first place to understand a process issue in a facility. The visual  presentation define the issue as part of the commissioning of new facility and how can we identify the best option  from integrity, cost and time.

Application

I start the process by creating infographic equipment’s and animated process flow. To develop these infographic  equipment’s, I used Visio simulation tools to enrich my slides with a detailed pictures and tools of all type of  equipment and process configuration. The Microsoft Visio is a drawing software with variety of diagrams including  flowcharts, org charts, building plans, floor plans, data flow diagrams, process flow diagrams, business process  modeling, 3D maps, and many more. If infographics are not available, then I search in public domain for visualize  equipment and configure processes to deliver highlighted efficient resolution.

text:
Reflection - Visualisation

Challenge and selection

On a recent project, I was asked to work with a community who lived in a significantly biodiverse area  in South Africa. It was assumed that the community would be happy to take on the mantle of custodian  of the environment, and take measures to protect and conserve it. However, it soon became apparent  that this was not the approach being taken by the community, and the area was under severe  environmental threat. The local municipality sought to engage with community members, in such a  way that members would see the benefit of becoming agents of natural resource management, and  conservation.

Although an anthropologist by profession, it is my background as a graphic designer that has enabled  me to help communities visualise their way into a new way of living. Using various visualisation  techniques has helped me on many occasions to breach the language barrier that is so prevalent in  South Africa, which has 11 official languages. By using visualisation techniques, such as Photovoice,  we are able to better understand the current context of participants, their thoughts and opinions, as  well as their hopes for the future, in a way that pure dialogue would never enable.  Due to the  education system in rural South Africa, many people are not encouraged to think critically, and are  certainly not encouraged to be creative. Visualisation helps them to access creativity, and use parts of  the brain that have grown dormant.

Application

Two visualisation tools were chosen for this project. The first was Photovoice. Volunteers were  selected from the community, and attended an orientation, which described the purpose and  intention of the project. Reflection-Visualization

Challenge.

I am an entrepreneur, and I am starting a project to sell sportswear online together

with my brother, our challenge is to make our business grow and be well known, but

to be known for having a page that attracts a lot of attention. only for the quality of

our clothes that if we evaluate and we already have, we want our clients to be

attracted to our page and when they open it they realize that they are going to find

what they are looking for and need. A page that stands out and is not so common

and basic.

Selection

We opted for a very important and necessary design tool for our challenge which is

the visualization tool, because with this important tool we can reinvent our page,

looking for an innovative idea to do something new.

Application

We started by analyzing and asking our clients what they liked the most and what

attracted them the least about our page? After 2 days of questions we realized that

what matched the most was that the photos were striking, but would you like to see

them in someone to know how the clothes fit on a body, we thought of solutions and

one of these is the most common on the pages which were photos of the model

wearing our clothes, but thanks to the design thinking we wanted to delve into the

solution because that was very basic, so we decided to take the photos but with

more common people with whom it is easier to identify ourselves than with a model,

so when customers saw how they fit they really knew how clothes looked on people.

Insight

At the beginning I thought that people were going to reject the idea, because it was

not something that customers are used to, but thanks to design thinking we took a

-  Challenge

I am a student of the Administration career, I studied Advertising in which my  teacher asked us to carry out an advertising campaign. My team consisted of 10  members and we had to come up with a creative idea for the Aurecon brand  campaign. We conducted an investigation of the history of the brand, as well as the  market it was aimed at and the advertising it handled at that time. We had to  choose between the tools and options to generate an advertising campaign that we  were taught on the subject and apply them creatively, it was at that moment that  we were challenged since we could not find the creative idea on which to base our  campaign.

-  Selection

We needed creativity for our work so we decided to use the visualization tool  because it would allow the team members to speak non-verbally, creatively and  express our thoughts through drawings, colors, symbols and images that could  clarify the others the ideas that each one had for the project and each one had a  different idea for the realization of the campaign that also included posters, TV  commercials, radio commercials, etc.

-  Application

Each member was asked for a sketch of her campaign idea and presented the next  day. Some presented videos, other posters, also photographs and drawings, each  member let their imagination explode, and by visualizing all the ideas we were able  to have a clearer idea of what others were thinking, in this way we began to  complement each idea and created a campaign creative.

-  Insight

At the beginning the team met and we used the usual technique to generalize an  idea, which is to speak and enter into debate, but it did not work since no point was  reached because we did not understand the ideas that others had regarding the  campaign. so we opted for the visualization tool so that we could see those  creative ideas that each of us had. Our product has  been in the market for a long time, but we realized that we are quickly losing our market share  due to better quality product coming up in the market.  For years we have been working on this  product but we realised that it will not be possible to improve the product further with traditional  technology. Our challenge is to enable our team with advanced data science based technique  so that we can improve our product to meet the customer satisfaction. Learning launch was a perfect suit for us because we had an idea to train our team for data  science but it was something very new for us. We had assumptions that data science will solve  our problems but we were not sure. So as mentioned in the last module of the course, we  cannot rely on our own assumptions and we needed to test whether our idea will work or not. However, even though there  is a lot of people doing some good work in these areas, there is no good DevOps conference. Even  world-wide the best is the DevOps Enterprise Summit. The franchise is originally from Brazil and this  is the first branch in Mexico, and all the collaborators were new and we did not have a good work system,  there were no fixed hours, we did not know how to handle correct customer service, the workspaces were  not correctly defined among other things.

Selection

Problems began to arise because there was no order and Schedule for each collaborator, there were many  partners and each one set their own rules, nobody knew who the should pay attention to and between us we  had many difficulties in the first months, it was a new business and we had no information on what we shoul  do to improve the work environment. The development of a mind map is a big help to align an organization,  since each one of the collaborator have participation and ideas, it could be better to identify and solve the  problem.

Application

text:
STORY TELLING

CHALLENGE AND SELECTION

I am super passionate about what I do in the world which is selling of banks products to Corporate

organizations and convincing them we are the institution of choice in service delivery and ultimately

superior returns. Telling business and marketing stories is a thing of pride for me as it helps me in

convincing and driving new business developments. Many times I recite how best to deliver my stories

to convince a prospect and in turn convert them into full fledged customers of my bank,

APPLICATIONS

In delivering my stories, I consider a lot of factors that guarantees an almost successful outcome in   my several years of experience. Some of these factors includes:

a. Solving a Problem: This usually could range from the basic needs to the more personal

issues and complicated corporate needs of the customers. Having ready made answers to  their needs and questions instills a level of desire.

b. Being Personal: In storytelling, getting personal when delivering your lines helps

communicate trust and confidence which translates to successful marketing.

c. Be Authentic: This simply means communicating the truth in the most effective manner.

Being caught in a lie never ends well and is a terrible way to start a relationship.

d. Have a Desired Outcome: This means knowing what the endgame of your conversation is.

Might even realize you do not have to complete your story most especially when the desired  outcome has been achieved.

INSIGHT AND APPROACH

With several years of experience in using this tool (Story Telling). I can say with certainty that it is  very effective in the Business development field as it communicates effectively and also requires  direct feedback.

This feedback in turn determines the effectiveness of the tool and also helps in reflecting on how  best to improve on the skill.

Story telling can always be improved upon but is a guaranteed a high probability of success once  mastered.

WATER-A PART OF OUR LIFE

Summer vacations had started and Stella was very excited. She was going to her Grandmother's house in liyue by

train, One day he and her cousin, Junaid decided to go to the village pond. On reaching there, they were shocked to see  the awful condition of the pond. There was garbage thrown all over and the water was dirty and stinking. The last time  she had come to this pond as a child, it was so clean. Radha asked her cousin what had happened to the pond. Junaid did

not know. But, suddenly both of them heard someone say, "But I know".

"Now we understand. Mr.Water. Please tell us what we can do to change this?", they asked. He said, "Please spread  awareness in the village that if waste thrown the pond will cause harm to all aquatic life and also harm the health of

other animals and humans in this village." "Yes for sure we will do this. We promise you that in a few months this pond

would be clean again". they promised.

Stella and Junaid took the help of their grandmother to talk about this problem in the next Village Panchayat meeting.  They explained to everyone how garbage in the village pond was leading to water pollution, harming aquatic plants and

animals. This was harming animals who drank from the pond and ultimately the villagers and the entire village

ecosystem. The villagers realised that this was one of the reasons, domestic animals were frequently falling sick and so

were small children, the weak and elderly.

Stella and Junaid made posters, and with help of the Panchayat members spread the message in the village. The

Panchayat also put up Do not Litter' signs near the pond. And in some months, the pond was clean again and a lot of

aquatic animals started living there. The village. air was cleaner and people and animals were falling sick, less

frequently. Soon it was time for Stella to leave as her holidays were coming to an end. She visited the pond one last  time with Junaid to bid good-bye to Mr. Water. And this

Challenge

This challenge tries to approach the adolescent female population with the aim of acquiring a

greater understanding of the influence of the new "premature sexuality" and corroborating the fact

that the majority of the sample deals independently the topic. Considering issues such as the early

development of women and the premature start of their sexual activity, including men's reaction to

this type of event.

Selection

Visualization is an insightful tool when it comes to direct evaluations of the adolescent female

population, which is what this challenge will address, because it is a key component in the way of

communicating what is thought or felt, in this way we are able to see more beyond just an induction,

we can conclude with the content that is provided to us.

Application

Every day, my group and I (all are women) use the visual approach to assess how teens approach

problems "independently" because they don't feel safe to comment on what happens to them most

of the time. The organization has broken the use of this tool countless times to take advantage of

direct approaches, managing to define parameters and identify the weak points and opportunities

of the population to be studied.

Initially we brainstormed to evaluate the best resource, we planned a series of meetings, informal

interviews, with adolescents known to the organization because they had related problems. Such

interviews would be given with psychological mediators who would help in the analyzes to

determine the best conclusion about premature sexuality in girls. We group ourselves in pairs to

give comfort to our "sample" and make them free to express through a drawing and, of course, its

words any fact.

An organization that is dedicated to solve problems of environmental  impact and social problems is in a small problem which prevents their  progress is increasing, that problem is that they do not have enough  monetary resources to continue developing their activities as they do  daily.

In order to solve this they decided to hire a person who is capable  enough to be able to use some of the four tools that are visualization,  storytelling, mind mapping and launching learning to be able to get  them to have enough income to not end their project.

This person came to the conclusion that he would have to use all his  qualities to make his mission to save this project successful. He  decided to use each of the tools for the realization of what would be a  commercial to raise funds, in reference to the storytelling tool he came  up with the idea of making this commercial and expose to the general  public the situation in which our planet is and the conditions in which  certain vulnerable groups are.

Finally, he will use mind maps to get a clear idea of the important  points he wants people to observe and that is practically the challenge.

After a few months he finished his challenge in a pretty epic way, not  only did he raise enough money to continue with the operations of that  organization, but he also reached the hearts of the viewers because  the approach he gave to the commercial was human and made the  people who saw it not only donate a little money, but also join the  cause by taking action to change the world in which we find ourselves.

Storytelling and visuals are two of the most powerful tools content marketers have. Both of these  attributes can help get ideas across more effectively and increase engagement. Combining these two  elements—well, that’s a recipe for success.

How can marketers go about creating a successful visual story? Luckily, there are plenty of tools  available to help you take a marketing yarn and weave it into a beautiful visual. Here are 11 of the  top software programs, websites, and more for creating your visual content marketing stories.

1. Ceros

Ceros is a design platform that makes it easy for marketers—or anyone, really—to create  infographics, e-books, and websites without the need for coding knowledge. It enables you to create  aesthetically pleasing designs easily, animate them, and input features like social media plug-ins and  pop-ups. It also includes access to a catalog of fonts and icons.

Here’s an example of an animated infographic created by Fitbit using Ceros. Infographics are popular  these days, and they’re very effective pieces of content. The animation in this one, though, helps it  stand out from the crowd and makes it more engaging.

2. Infogr.am

Infographics are a fantastic way to organize information visually. They make text easy to digest and  tend to get shared a lot on social media. Infogr.am is a tool that makes designing your own  infographics a simple process. You can also make cool charts and maps by using one of Infogr.am’s  themes.

National Geographic is great at creating interactive maps that make information easy and fun to look  at. Here’s an example of a map of U.S. states and their ecological footprints. You could easily create  something similar with Infogr.am.

LeARning LAunch

A learning launch is an experiment conducted in the marketplace quickly and inexpensively. It forms a bridge  between customer co-creation and commercial rollout.

1. Set tight boundaries.  Since this is a learning launch and  not a pilot, it is important to plan  for it to end. Set concrete limits  on key variables, such as time,  geography, number of customers,  features, and partner firms.

2.  Design with a sharp focus   on key assumptions.    Review the key assumptions that  you identified. For those that you  indicated will be tested in the  market, keep in mind the following  when planning your in-market  experiment:

a.  See to it that the prototype  reflects the key assumptions  you need   to test.

b.  Translate the assumptions  you plan to test into  specific metrics.

c.  Be explicit about how you  will generate the data   you need, especially  behavioral data.

d.  Be explicit about the search  for disconfirming data.

e.  Match the budget to an  affordable loss calculation.

3.  Build a team that is both  disciplined and adaptive.   The composition of the team  makes a difference. Yes, you  want the passionate supporters  of growth and innovation on  the squad. But having a few  skeptics around will ensure that  you are not designing a test to  give you the answers you want.  Also, someone with a financial  perspective is valuable—and  project management skills are  essential.

Challenge:    The leadership team of the firm I work for had agreed on the priorities and strategy for leveraging  technology to realise business goals. As the strategy was a multi-year journey and involved  orchestrating multiple levers simultaneously, they wanted to (1) put in place a scorecard to ensure we  are closely monitor and demonstrate the execution of strategy as intended and (2) facilitate a  consistent understanding of success (up to 4 levels from the top). Some examples include – high level synthesis vs. ability to  drill down; snapshot of current performance vs. forward looking predictions; One metric at a time vs.  evaluate the interaction of multiple metrics at the same time. It was clear that refreshing previous  dashboard templates with data for new metrics was not an option.    I knew a dashboard was required but not sure about the form and interface necessary to strike the  right balance between the interpretation and expectation of user groups regarding the strategy. This  involved first making their mental models as explicit as possible (see week 1 interview)and using them  as building blocks to develop a common mental model that everyone can use to manage the execution  of strategy. Hence, I chose visualisation/visual thinking as a tool. VISUALIZATION    Challenge & Selection:   I am a marketing profession and work in an organization where our team members are  based in different offices and different time zones (Asia & US).  We do a lot of conference  calls to update each other about on-going project. These are all voice calls so there is no  way to know if they are paying attention or understand the contents through facial  expression. We usually talk either early in morning means night for the other team  members who are tired from the working day.  Calls are usually 60 minutes long so we  need to manage the amount of information presented and discussion between the  members.    To ensure that the other team members that are on the conference calls have an  accurate understanding of my contents quickly, I present information using visualization.     Application:   Following are the guidelines I apply when I prepare presentation:

•  Use of images, videos, charts, infographics, tables, etc.  They capture the team’s  attention and simplified complicated information.

•  Slides in bullet points instead of long paragraphs so that they will listen to me,  instead of reading the slides.

•  Keep the number of slides to minimum.

They have been effective for me to communicate my thoughts and bring everyone onto  the same level of understanding effectively.  By using such tools, they also stimulate the  right brain thinking and set the stage for creative thinking.

Insight & Approach  The appropriate selection of images and videos is important. Since there is culture  diversity within the team, an image that’s very popular in Asia may not means the same  in US.   Also, I have to be mindful about the amount of information that I want in a chart  or infographic. Sometimes, I put too much in one and questions that were asked are  more than I could handle.  I feel that I didn’t manage to go deeper into some questions  and uncover those unarticulated needs.     Moving forward, I would also prepare open ended

Challenge

I am a member of India’s fastest growing consumer startup, Emirates Airlines. I am currently a part of the  corporate strategy team where in my role is working on projects of strategic importance that will  accrue benefits to the organization in the medium and the long term.

One such project I worked on was creation of a new distribution channel wherein Emirates Airlines will  enable its Key Opinion Consumers (most convinced and loyal consumers) to become resellers for the  products of the brand. We faced enormous channel in establishing such a distribution channel,  motivating the Key Opinions Consumers to resell on behalf of the company and overall keeping the  brand image positive and controlling the whole channel.

Selection

Our team had already brainstormed the problem statements and realized that the company is  excessively dependent on one type for channel for consumer order fulfilment. Being a D2C brand,  the channel was online marketplace (like Amazon, Flipakrt). We had identified that given the Indian  Business economy context, a word-of-mouth solution to such a problem is viable. More so it  increases the reach of the brand into economically poorer regions of India where online shopping  has not yet been adopted. Hence, we had a set of experiments figured out and need to choose the  one yielding the optimal results. Given the fact that the startup space is quickly evolving, with new  competitors budding up spontaneously we had extremely quick turnaround deadlines and hence the  choice of a learning launch, because definition learning launch is meant to test (and table) ideas  quickly and evolve at a faster pace.

Challenge: - I got the software system contract from a leading casino in Sri Lanka.  My duty is to analyze  the whole process which is totally manual and design fully automated software system to cover all the  tasks which are carried out by the whole staff members of the casino. The casino was operating at the  time I got the contract so, I needed to work with the running business and I had only myself to do the  whole parts of system designing process.  Only the networking part has been done properly and  computers were installed in the required main places but server and storage was not purchased at  that time. The casino is running 24 * 7, so no system shut down or restart is allowed.  All the functions  of the Casino were carried out manually by the staff before introducing an automated system. All  reports were generated by using excel sheets, all customer details have been maintained in a paper  based files, all payments were issued on a paper based voucher system and so many chits were  circulating among people in the casino for different purposes. To overcome those manual processes,  new automated system is needed to be installed in the facility. As I initially identified, there were 8  sub-systems in the system and all sub systems should be interconnected to from a complete ERP  system. I was given 6 months to complete the whole system.

I selected key functionalities in  initial phase to implement and then gradually designed the system step by step.

Challenge:  Working at a media agency, there is nothing more important than understanding targets. As a part  of the Knowledge and Research department, it was important to supply employees/planners with  relevant information. The company always relied on quantitative data to propose media plans for  big brands. But employees were usually afraid of data or they got lost in the inﬁnite pdfs and excel  tables, not knowing how to read vertical and horizontal percentages or how to link one information  to the other, losing the greater meaning of the data itself. The company had already designed a  study to cover most of the information need of clients, but this data was really hard to work with, as  it came in a non-friendly format for employees, resulting in a wasting of time and efforts of our  employees/planners. Employees received raw data on a monthly basis, having to search for their  own insights in order to complete their work every month.

Application: To understand the ﬂow of data, our team got together with two planners to understand the process  of media planning and how the information ﬂowed inside the company and got to the clients. We  identiﬁed all the touch-points and drew a map + timeline which clearly showed how much time was  being spent on each task, and what were the ﬁnal results for the clients. We then brainstormed a  whole new process, which took into consideration all of the details that came in touch with our main  challenge. One important fact was time, as in the original process every employee had to go  through the data too look for the same. As we visualized this, it was easier to understand that we  could centralize this process into an automatic report. Seeing every step and touchpoint versus  times was really eye-opening. text:
Challenge – story telling

Storytelling in the design process can be implemented using various  techniques and methods such as the following: The design thinking  process ensures the user evolvement in every stage to build a user- centred solution. Therefore, the storytelling is used throughout the  design process, yet there is a different usage goal in each phase.

Selection

During the design process, storytelling is used to understand the  underlying problems that consumers face when using a product or a  service, and then use this knowledge in reflective practice to  formulate the solution which is tested by the consumers. Hence,  storytelling contributes to the different stages in the design process  for different purposes in each step.

Application

Storytelling in the design process can be implemented using various  techniques and methods such as the following:

1. Digital and Visual storytelling;

2. Scenario generation;

3. Storyboarding;

4. Plays;

5. Animation;

6. Talk and images; and

7. Text and images

Insight

In the solution definition and prototyping stages, the design team  would number of potential solutions that need to be tested and  evaluated to understand which is the best solution from the user

perspective. In this stage, the storytelling can be used again in this  stage but with a different purpose. In this case, the team tries to  understand which solution is the most appropriate for the consumer.

Approach

the storytelling is a powerful communication tool that enables us as  a human being to understand more about our emotional  experiences. This makes it an effective method to use during the  design process. It can be used during the design thinking process  phases with a different goal in each stage. Storytelling can help us to  gather personalised emotional data about our consumer’s  experience which can be hard to collect using other research  methods such as the survey and consumer journey mapping.

Learning Launch in the emerging battery toothbrush segment

Challenge

I am working as a regional marketing manager in a personal care company in APAC area. I am  responsible to the oral care category (Toothpaste, Toothbrush & Mouthwash products). For our  toothbrush business, we are specialized in manual toothbrush with distinct market leadership and used  to have a lot of innovation to build the category.

While in recent years, we found some changes in the toothbrush category across APAC markets. There  are quite a few new entry brands that focusing on battery toothbrush (pricing index 1000 vs manual  toothbrush). With such a high price products, surprisingly retailers and consumers are showing interest  on these and we see a trend switching from manual to battery (volume growth in battery toothbrush >  volume growth in manual toothbrush). As a result, the company designed to invest in developing our  own battery toothbrush portfolio, while it comes to my team for qualifying the new product innovation  and launch activation ideas.

We were facing some challenges on launching our first battery toothbrush such as,

1) As a brand with strong consumer perception on manual toothbrush, we worry our brand cannot

carry battery toothbrush which has a pricing index 1000 vs manual

2) As a relatively late comer, we need to build our own distinctiveness in order to compete with

brands that already entered the category

Selection

In the early stage, the team has already used Storytelling and Prototype to engage our potential  consumers. The design of our battery toothbrush was influenced by observation of the households’  usage frequency, moment, duration; as well as the buyers’ (usually the Mum/Wife) purchase decision  making process, shopping journey. After understanding the targets, we then develop a prototype and  test it out with competitive products, which enable further optimization on the design and product  usage experience.

text: Mind Mapping , Design thinking              Mind map is a graphical presentation of an idea or a concept .All of us have 100 and 1000 of ideas poping up in  our mind and this technique will help us represent our ideas and thoughts through a Map or graphical representation        Mind map is prepared with the combination of IDEA , TREE STRUCTURE TABLE , COLOUR COMBINATION S ,  which help the viewers to find different kind of relationship between ideas . Mind map is created by subdivision  of a main topic into various subtopics covering the overall circumstances and thoughts that are made up in the creato rs mind       Mind map help us to create a logical view of note taking or making references and develops our mind to grasp the id eas and thoughts in system and a structural manner and also increases our creativity and the way of planning a desig n . This technique will make a creator go deeper in his idea and makes problem solving much easier       This is the technique to explore our mind and organizing this on simple peice of paper and can be done while thinkin g about something on real time.This helps to connect ideas together and put a plain and simple idea on a paper for de signers. Speaking of students, mind mapping is the best way to take notes upto date and nothing changes that.      The thought process has many benefits adding up to itself. It's going to be easier for us to understand out own ideas  and also find our wrongs from rights, then solve the problem. Afterall, this is what the modern design and problem s olving follows in everyday life to find their mistakes to correct them. Hence I conclude Mind mapping can really ma ke a difference in design thinking and help us to generate an idea.

Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge     I’m part of the PMO of my organization’s and currently our challenge is to define the value  proposition of the reconciliation module. This module is in production since long time ago,  however during the last year we have found that the customer doesn’t understand very well  how to use it and the value of use it. We need to find the way to redefine and/or redesign the  module and show the customer that they need this module to control the whole flow of their  sales.     Selection     After our research and self-verification, the outcome was to select the mind mapping tool. In a  nutshell we consider that it can help us to define the value proposition and redesign the module  at all taking in consideration all the information gather from the customers.     Application     We started with a brainstorming meeting to organize all the information collected by each team  member in a visually brain-friendly method as mind mapping suggested. Afterwards we draw in  the blackboard a single idea that was represented with text “Reconciliation”, then more  subsidiary ideas were added around the main idea and related to it by lines. It is important to  mention that we ensure the use of a unified hierarchy to represent all the ideas, and in parallel  we use different visual elements to organize ideas such as customer logos, icons, etc.

Insight     The outcome of the process of apply the mind mapping was a diagram that represent  the idea of the reconciliation module needed from the customers point of view, it was  slightly different from what we were thinking in the past. The next step is that our team will  review this insight and incorporate it into the roadmap, so new releases with the new design are  coming.     Approach

Thanks to the mind mapping tool, we were able to unblock a redesign required from long time,  based on that, we have decided to implement this technique as priority for reviewing any  discrepancy between our product

text:
The Challenge

This challenge was not much of a challenge for me. I am a Social Work student, helping

people is always my passion. I am that friend that is always there to listen and give advice or encouragement. My friend had a problem with her fiance and she didn't know who to talk to about her problem.

She recently found out that she had a huge temporary (1 year) job offer out of the country

but her fiance is already settled in the country they were living in at the moment. She did not know when she would get there given that she had to wait for her visa and travelling was a mystery. They were already planning their wedding. She was overwhelmed.

The Selection and Application

When she called me crying and was explaining the problem to me, the first thing that came

to my mind was my similar experience. I had a huge opportunity to leave the country and it posed problems in my relationship. However, I studied, we both visited whenever we could and I came back for good after four years, just like we planned. So I told my story, I selected storytelling because it was the best option at that time, it helped me to express how I relate to her feelings. I applied it well but not well enough.

The Insight and Approach Gained

She took my story as hope which was good but she also used my solution which wasn't the

best idea for her situation. I didn't think that my solution would work for her and I didn't expect her to use mine. This experience made me learn to be careful with storytelling, in that not just telling the story but also emphasizing exceptions.

On a next occasion if I'm using storytelling I must emphasize why I'm sharing the story, in

this case it was hope and emphasize that everyone is different and my solutions may not work for another. However if advice is needed give it well, but allow the person to make their decision.

text:
Visualization

What is a Visualization?

One of the most required and important thing for design thinking . It helps us to  think in a different and a better way. It helps us to visualise in a non-verbal way  and helps us to improve our creative skills.

What is done in Visualization?

In visualization we have equal importance for listening, thinking and even  drawing.

Steps of Visualization:

a) Input :  Here listening is input   b) Processing: Here thinking is the process  c) Output: Here drawing is the output.

All these steps together helps us to get new possibilities to solutions.

The main part is that you must be able to communicate with people. The  requirements for mastering it are imagining people, spaces, situations and  actions or movements.

The more you start drawing pictures, the more people understand of how  and what you are talking in visual image form.  It's anything but difficult to  make a basic outline – and most anybody can draw a stick figure, a circle, a  square, or a bolt. Those are the essential structure squares of making a  Visualization. We can open the ability to think contrastingly by doodling.  Representation has a task to carry out all through the Design Thinking. It's a  fantastic device, in that sense, in that we're utilizing those instruments and  that piece of our cerebrum at each stage in the plan cycle. It's not simply  something that has an application in one piece of the Design Thinking. It  has numerous methods of being helpful at various pieces of the Design  Thinking measure.
