REFLECTION- VISUALIZATION

1. CHALLENGE

In my case, I can clearly imagine something, think of a solution in my mind, think of different  ways to achieve a goal, to solve a problem or improve a product, I can even imagine a new  world, but when the time comes to transform my thoughts so that they are understandable to  different people, the fact that everything I imagine must stop being abstract and become  something concrete becomes hard work for me; because I must initiate a process in which  my purpose is to visualize the whole scenario, I must begin to discern and codify the  information, begin to separate relevant information from that which is not, this means a  challenge for me, since in my opinion every single detail is important, I am a perfectionist  person, therefore, I focus too much on the small details, although I recognize that what for  me can be decisive is not really very practical.

My personal challenge is more than discerning, it is to express the information in a coherent  and understandable way for all types of public, my challenge is to express my idea in a clear  way so as not to give room for ambiguities. It is to take into account 100% the user, to foresee  that what I project in a visual way meets their expectations, fulfills their needs, and becomes  really useful when looking for a practical and useful solution to the problem posed.

2. SELECTION

text:
Understanding through Visualization

Challenge:-

We follow Agile and we have 2 weeks of iterations for our intermediate deadlines, but after few  iterations we had heated issues pouring in between the multiple shareholders (Dev, Test, Devops and  Management) as we missed the timelines. Each had their own reasons and were not able to convince  others of their limitation or issues even after multiple discussions and meetings. This has been  happening across projects and this time I wanted it to find a long lasting generic solution independent of  the development platform.

Selection:-

We tried story telling (meetings actually) but it didn’t fit our requirements as it was getting impossible  for one stakeholder to convince the other and we finally moved to visualization were we made each  group (stakeholders) present their process visually (simple drawing) so as to bring in a shared  understanding of each of the diverse groups problems and limitations in a more meaningful and easy to  comprehend way.

Approach:-

We began by asking each stakeholder to present the complete flow in a visual manner. More of a mind  map (a simple hand drawing) presenting their steps with an image in mind. The moment we brought  these to discussions, very clearly you could see the different stakeholders realizing the other side  problems, from their perspective. It didn’t solve the issue, as everyone brought the strawman fallacy,  but it was our starting point.

Next we started digging deep with questions and counter questions between each stakeholder. Once  ready, I made a one on one discussion with each group, discussed with them, interviewed them and  based on their inputs created another rough data set. Made a complete list of all different partners  involved, their first set of inputs based on their mind map presentation. Then the points derived from  the one on one and the counter questions. Using this I created the flowchart map having inputs of all  stake holders involved in his.

text:
The tool that I selected is: "mind map".

My challenge is to be able to win the marketing contest with my

marketing plan that I will carry out together with my team of six people.

I am studying the fifth semester of my undergraduate degree, so I cannot

apply this method in my work, but in my studies.

As a form of evaluation in this matter, we were asked to compete for the

entire university with a marketing plan that included the market study,

our objectives, goals, policies, budgets, plans, interviews, in short,

everything that a plan of marketing requires.

I chose the mind map because the brainstorming it generates is

extraordinary, plus it captures it in a place where everyone can perceive

it and create great things with it. As we could see in the video, it is

something in which everyone can participate and it shows us more than

one perspective.

My team and I created a file on google drive, since it was not possible to

see each other in person, so that each of us could edit it whenever we

wanted, comment on it and tweak it when necessary. The mind map

helped us a lot, since each one could express their thinking in their own

way, it was easier to understand each other and very dynamic, it was

very useful for the development of the project.

As I said before, the mind map generates a great brainstorm, in addition

to providing you with more than one perspective of the situation, you can

perceive things that you would not have been able to if someone else

had not contributed their ideas to the mind map, it allows you to expand

your panorama, there are more options, possibilities, paths.

For some other project that I have to do I could do my learning launch, I

would like to experience the impact it could have on people and the

knowledge and experience that I have of this, I feel that once I start doing

it, the other times will be more easy.

Design Thinking Reflection - Visualization

Challenge

Visualization is a tool that I use all the time. I work at an accounting firm and evaluate the design and  operating effectiveness of our clients’ financial controls over various financial processes. My client is a  big public company, and has multiple controls for each financial process, such as the process around  payroll, inventory, revenue, and expense. Effectively designed controls mitigate the risk of material  misstatement related to financial account balances.

In order to evaluate the design effectiveness of their financial controls, we need to first obtain a  preliminary understanding of the process through reviewing any available documents, such as process  narrative or flowcharts, and we identify all the potential risks. Then we meet with the process owners to  obtain clarification and confirmation. After that, we determine if the risks are being mitigated by the  existing control, and if not, what attributes should be added to the new or modified control in order for  it to be effective by design.

The challenge is that some financial processes could be quite complicated, and we may miss to identify  all the significant risks, and in turns misjudge the effectiveness of the design of the controls.  Furthermore, there could be misinterpretation of the processes and controls because the processes are  complicated and new to us. I needed to cover the process around the “capitalized expense” account and  this process did not have a flowchart and the narrative was a little bit confusing.

Selection

In order to ensure that we identify all the significant risks, what could go wrong, and that we obtain a  thorough and accurate understanding of the processes we used visualization extensively as a team to  communicate our thoughts.

LPG GAS CYLINDER ONLINE METERING EXPERIMENTATION - LEARNING LAUNCH

I currently reside in Nigeria, and the most common energy means for cooking in the country is using  either wood/coal, kerosene stove and Liquefied Petroleum Gas- LPG. The CHALLENGE with the people using LPG is the high cost  involved in buying the LPG when compared to how much the fossil fuel are gotten. So, my team and I  came up with idea of introducing a pay as you use system of consumption in these communities; the  members of these community live on daily wages when compared to the cities. We realized this  technology are already in use in Kenya and Tanzania, but we were not so sure how it will be embraced  in Nigeria. We decided to get a prototype of about 10 (ten) units, and we decided to deploy for some  handful of community dwellers for few weeks.

SELECTION:

As a team, we decided to use the learning launch tool. We believe this will help us fine tun the design,  make it simple, yet effective technology that our target customers can easily navigate through and  use. Working with some few community dwellers and mind you we have already gone through several  redesign thinking activities to come up with a customized go-to-market prototype for Nigeria.  These  pre activity knowledge has helped us to select the learning launch tool for our challenge and working  with these prototypes will help us experiment the idea with a small group of community residents.

Example Reflection – Learning Launch

1. Challenge

I am a member of the admissions team in my Institute and the challenge encountered  by us is to improve the interest of prospective students and convert them into paid  registrations and then on to making them the students of the course offered by us. For  this we need to run the right digital marketing campaigns as well as conduct offline  events to generate interest. The admissions team comprise of 5 employees. This project  from the start of the campaign to the outcome ie conversion as students should not  exceed 90 days. The workflow of this process would be analysed to uncover the  problems and to carry out improvements on the same.

2. Selection

The team has discussed different design thinking tools to be used for this purpose.  Finally the learning launch was zeroed in as the tool to work with.  This tool enables  to test an idea and its prototype on a smaller scale before a full scale launch.

3. Application

The initial focus on the learning launch was the efficient start to the digital marketing  campaign.  To effectively focus on this task, a 1 day training program was conducted.  Based on this program, a workflow document with clear cut measurables and  responsibilities was drawn. A Quiz was administered to the team members to test the  understanding of the new workflow processes along with the prioritization of the tasks  at hand.

4. Insight

The learning from this activity was that the whole approach was outcome focused rather  than process improvement of any kind which could automatically improve the  outcomes. The other insight that was gained was that the admission team was slow to  respond to queries from the prospects and that an agile approach was required. This  approach called for a redesign of tasks and a relook at the priorities. These insights  would be incorporated into future design launch and also before a full scale launch for  student admission process.

However, different partners have  different views about projects, how plans are made, who should be involved as well as what  should be included and how they should look. Hence involving all relevant stakeholders and  keeping them interested in planning is sometimes an obstacle.

Visualization: this is a tool useful in everyday tasks in which graphics can be used to get the  message across as well as for further clarity and understanding. It helps in explaining further  what one is putting across as at times people may perceive words differently and make own  conclusions which may not necessarily be the presents (Jana Zeller, Module 1). It is a tool most  suitable in all kinds of tasks and can be easily adapted and combined even with other tools to  make an emphasis or statement a little clearer. text:
Data visualization is the graphic representation of data. It involves  producing images that communicate relationships among the  represented data to viewers of the images. This communication is  achieved through the use of a systematic mapping between graphic  marks and data values in the creation of the visualization. This  mapping establishes how data values will be represented visually,  determining how and to what extent a property of a graphic mark,  such as size or color, will change to reflect changes in the value of a  datum.

To  communicate  information  clearly  and  efficiently,  data

visualization uses statistical graphics, plots, information graphics and  other tools. Numerical data may be encoded using dots, lines, or  bars, to visually communicate a quantitative message.[1] Effective  visualization helps users analyze and reason about data and  evidence. It makes complex data more accessible, understandable  and usable. Users may have particular analytical tasks, such as  making comparisons or understanding causality, and the design  principle of the graphic (i.e. showing comparisons or showing  causality) follows the task. Tables are generally used where users will  look up a specific measurement, while charts of various types are  used to show patterns or relationships in the data for one or more  variables.

Data visualization is both an art and a science. It is viewed as a  branch of descriptive statistics by some, but also as a grounded  theory development tool by others. Increased amounts of data  created by Internet activity and an expanding number of sensors in  the environment are referred to as "big data" or Internet of things.  Processing, analyzing and communicating this data present ethical  and analytical challenges for data visualization. Startup Idea Verification - Learning Launch

Challenge & Selection:

Me and a couple of friends have had an idea for a startup that aims to source exotic chocolates  & edibles sourced from all over the globe and create a market for them in India. The challenge  is to find out if there is scope for such a market and to find out if it is a sustainable one or not.  The project scope includes a small team working on sales & marketing in parallel to face the  challenge. After going through all the tools, a learning launch seems the best idea for the  specific challenges as it will give a better picture in this scenario.

Application:

For our first learning launch, we focused on the structure/execution of our online marketing  tasks. In particular, peer to peer marketing using various social media. Given the fact that we  were a group of college students, we could generate a small momentum inside a controlled  environment. We set up a small learning launch in one of the Cultural festivals by setting up a  stall. We primarily focused on chocolates sourced from Europe and South America sourced  from known people travelling from these places.

Insight:

By applying the learning launch tool, our team identified a few assumptions and cleared a path  for future learning launches. This learning launch is considered as a controlled one as the  customer base comprised of more than 95 percent students. In our approach, the results were  slightly different from the ones anticipated by our team. Even though people were enthusiastic  about this concept, willingness to buy the products was less amongst people. Our assumptions  about enthusiasm offsetting the price factor was wrong and people were considering the  budget allowance as a primary factor. The second most important factor which came up is the  quality/authenticity of the items.

text:
New Investments Flow – Analysis and Approvals for Innovation

Challenge

In this case, challenge is the opportunity to improve the flow analysis for new investments, to achieve faster introductions of technologies, improve efficiency and cost reductions. Currently, the steps related of analysis and staff approval requires a lot of time, being a bottleneck in the whole process – causing employee stress, project schedule delays and benefits postponed.

Currently, the process takes between 5 to 8 months – analysis and decision-making. In this period, many conditions could change and benefits are lost. It represents 50 to 60% of total flow, even considered these investments development and installation.

Selection

Tool selected was Visualization, to show for all stakeholders what is the current analysis flow and the main relationship between steps. How important is the tasks, what is the earned value in each step and how we can reduce the flow and optimize the staff jobs – improving communication, avoiding reworks, losses and stress. In fact, is not clear for the team members how much time it takes and if all steps are really needed, because the flow was designed a long time ago.

The main goal using this tool is to develop a unique understanding of the flow and find the opportunities to improve efficiency, achieving a sense of agreement.

The third challenge that  I face is to encourage timid students to share while balancing the domination of some outspoken  students in group discussions. This makes me wonder how I can actually do something to help the  students so that they have the right structure to think effectively and share their thoughts efficiently.       Selection  In one occasion I was introduced to a technique called Issue Trees, which is similar (or rather the same)  with Mindmapping. Design Thinking for Innovation – Reflection on the Mind Mapping Tool

1.) Challenge  At my work on a manufacturing site of a consumer electronics company, I am asked to improve the  quality and output quantity of a production line. Design Thinking techniques are rarely known in the  factory, and if people heard about it, they usually associate it with the creative and a bit unrealistic  people from the product design department. A culture of small continuous improvements exists, for  which everyone, from manager to engineer to operator, is responsible. Larger improvements where my  project is aiming for, are more challenging as production reliability might be a affected and multiple  teams are involved. Besides that, when a pre-selected solution has to deal with automation (i.e.  robotics), the sensitive association with cutting jobs is present.

2.) Selection  I started my project with identifying the current state (‘What is’-phase). The people who work directly  with the production line, usually have the best realistic and pragmatic knowledge. But most of all, I  wanted to have them being engaged with the project; they would have a major influence in the concept  selection (as they needed to work with it), and it would improve their work without having to fear for  losing their jobs.   Based on this challenge, I selected the Mind Mapping tool, in order to achieve insights in the current  state of the production line. Getting the involved people engaged is something I want to achieve with  the Tool as well. As described in Module 3 of the Design Thinking course (and within the book Designing  for Growth by Beatriz Tsotetsi & Tommy Hall), with Mind Mapping all relevant aspects of a topic are  visualized and clusters and interdependencies are made. Eventually, the problem description is  sharpened, and the design criteria for developing concepts are established, on which all the relevant  stakeholders have commonly agreed.

text:
Reflection – using Mind Mapping to write essays

Challenge

My son absolutely hates homework.  He especially dislikes writing assignments that require

multiple paragraphs, including an introduction, a stated claim, an attention grabbing sentence  and finally a conclusion.  These are daunting assignments that can sometimes be so  overwhelming that he simply can’t get started.  I cringed when he came to me as I was working  from home in the middle of the afternoon.  I was deep into my most productive hour, but he was  in tears because he had five paragraphs to write by the end of the night. He was clearly freaking  out. He had to write an essay on a book he had read.  My son is a great reader and can devour  hundreds of pages in a single sitting, especially if they are interesting to him.  However, at the  end of the day, he has no idea what to write about and needed some help getting started on the  first sentence.

Selection

The tool I used to solve this problem was mind mapping to identify patterns and insights. As I

reflect on this technique, I shared with my son that this is something I was lucky enough to learn  in high school by a very good teacher.  I had also hated essays too when I was his age and felt  overwhelmed throughout my early teenage years whenever I had to write one.  This very good  high school English teacher of mine, perhaps unknowingly, taught me the mind mapping  technique and probably changed my life as far as writing is concerned.

Application

This is how I used the tool:  With every book there are basic details that are usually common,

so I asked my son about the book he had read.  I asked about the setting, the time period, the  main characters et cetera.  I asked lots of questions and he answered. For each answer he  gave, I helped him summarize it into one sentence, and I wrote what he said verbatim on an  index card. text:
Learning Launch

Challenge  I am working as a design engineer in a Scandinavian company. The tasks are mainly design and  development of mathematically and algorithmic software for our products. Acting in a global market it is  important that we are able to develop our products efficiently and providing a high quality as demanded by  our customers. Development of such specialized software as we do involves several engineering disciplines:  people with skills within mathematic and dynamic behavior of mechanical systems, and software engineers  with skills in how to implement the algorithms into microcomputers. A challenge we face in our daily work  is the efficient flow of information between people spread among the various disciplines. Historically we  have used one set of tools for development of the mathematic and algorithms and another set of tools for  the final implementation into a microcomputer. (In this sense the ‘tools’ are special programs running on a  PC). This involved a manual translation process from the development domain and into the implementation  domain; a translation which is both time consuming and error prone.

New tools has emerged which is able to combine the development domain with the implementation  domain in automating the translation process. The idea we were going to test was if we could make this  new tool operational in our organization; a task which involved both technical skills and personal skills in  joining the multi engineering disciplines closer together.

Selection  The task I am describing here was carried out a couple of years ago, - before I took the Design Thinking  class. By reflecting back I now realize what we did at that time was close to the concept of the Learning  Launch tool as Luz Marina described so good. Therefore, I will address the sequence of test we went through  from a Learning Launch point of view.

Challenge & Selection    During this crisis, many small shops that sell Non-essential products closed their doors and  they are unable to continue because people are afraid to go outside their homes.    Application    My story today is about a merchant selling household utensils. Sajjad said that he is going  through an economic hardship that people do not come to buy things from him as it was in  the first. He even cut the prices of his products in half, but also only a few of them come to  the store. He also wishes that he could offer his products on The Internet so that people can  search for what they want and buy and even he can deliver products to them in their homes  without the need to come to the store and it will also ensure that these products are   purge    Insight & Approach     From the story of John, we see that he needs to display his products on a larger scale, not  only through a store, and also needs a way to deliver these products to users.  So, since I have a software background, I can program a platform that enables John and  anyone who sells products to set up there own online store to display products to people and  also enable them to deliver these products to users.

text: CHALLENGE: Each year, The Traction Avant Nederland Hotel Company conducts a S.W.O.T process  (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) across our global portfolio of 92 hotels and  over 33,000 Ladies and Gentlemen.  Currently, the process is defined as “a tool used in the  discovery/evaluation phase of the Strategic Planning process”.  Each hotel will identify a SWOT  administrator who will lead the process on property – which includes data collection, Access  database usage and meeting this additional deadline, along with their day job.   As the brands  S.W.O.T. champion I led this process to ensure timelines and tasks are met so that the  consolidated feedback can be shared with Senior Leadership to inform our strategies and  initiatives for the upcoming year.  The current process for S.W.O.T. is functional – words like discovery, process, and evaluation  define our approach.      This intrigued me because the vision of The Traction Avant Nederland is “to inspire life’s most meaningful  journeys”.  There is nothing inspiring about what is referenced in the previous paragraph.  So I  thought, What IF…what if I could take the Ladies and Gentlemen to a place where they would  be able to understand the higher purpose of why we do a S.W.O.T.?  What If I could take away  the functional elements and “inspire life’s most meaningful journeys” for our internal customer,  the Ladies and Gentlemen?  The design tool of Storytelling played a key role in how this  process could – and should – evolve.  I wanted to connect to the emotions and values of our  employees.  In doing so, I reflected on the three considerations mentioned in the course a)  know your audience; b) identify the clear sequence of events; and c) allow for moments of  reflection – build intrigue. I will craft  stories to aware people of different age groups. Therefore distinct stories will be required so that we  can reach out to every individual. The challenge I have applied the design thinking tool Visualization to is social equity issues in  my hometown of Chicago. Recently, I was given the task of identifying the root issues of the  inequity in the city and subsequently, conjuring a technology-driven solution. There is a plethora  of studies on the root causes of inequity available, so interpreting it all seemed to be a Herculean  task. I decided it would be easier to draw conclusions from the data if I were able to see it  visually. I grouped out several different categories of data related to inequity, such as the  unemployment rate, graduation rate, and life expectancy in the respective communities.     What particularly stood out to me were the reports of the lower graduation rates, in some

instances there were gaps as large as 15% between Black and White communities. It had seemed  that using Visualization had helped me find my culprit. Further research led me to find that those  without a GED have much lower chances at employment and higher rates of poverty than those  with one. I deduced that this higher rate of poverty consequently led to the lack of health care  and lower life expectancy. After using simple graphing programs with the data, I saw that the  funding for schools in majority Black and Brown communities was significantly lower than  funding in majority white neighborhoods. This gap in funding could possibly be the reason for  the gap in graduation rates.     This led me take a different approach in the Visualization tool, and look at anecdotal data

Storytelling tool

the tool I used was the storytelling tool. He had to solve the problem that arose when

attracting more customers to a family restaurant.

The restaurant was not receiving enough customers, so it had to close, so it was

decided to apply the Storytelling tool and tell the story of the restaurant.Telling the

story was essential for the owners of the restaurant. the goal was to connect with

the emotions of future customers.

the key is to know how to tell the story of the founding of the restaurant well. a good

story had to be told to clients, to keep their attention and deliver good content. the

idea was to convey relevant information and content.

First, you chose what you wanted to say and when to say it. once this analysis was

done, what followed was to communicate it effectively, casually and emotionally

The restaurant is focused on families, so telling its story was an advantage, given

that the restaurant was founded in 1980 by a Jewish family of emigrants, a series of

1-minute videos was published on the restaurant's social networks, where Different

family members told the story of the restaurant and how the menu was chosen.

The publication of the videos aroused great interest among clients, so the narrative

tool was effective.

The visualization tool will be applied soon. Our goal will be that through images,

customers imagine the history of the restaurant and feel part of the story.

Reflection on Visualization as a Design tool

Challenges

It is my observation that many a times during the initial project planning phase with the Client, we  miss out on a few pointers during discussions. Even though there is proper documentation of the  SOW, SLAs and timelines, this oversight of exact requirements is often missed; which snowballs into  a bigger milestone lapse during the implementation stages which finally require rectifications at a  much-advanced stage.

Proper representation of the company goals and services and extrapolation of exact requirements is  the need of the hour.

Selection

Presentations and explanations provided in the meetings can be interpreted by the clients in a  different way. It is essential that both our company and the client are on the same page. To remedy  this concern, I have selected the “Visualization” Design tool.

Visual imagery of the project progress and outcomes when presented to the clients, helps us  understand any underlying concerns, align their ideas with ours and get consent on the final plan.

Application

I`ve noticed that pictorial representation is more understandable than a monologue presentation. By  using Visualization, I make the discussions an interactive session with the client and probe more to  find minute specifications that aren`t mentioned in the initial project plan. I follow the Visualization  process of:

Exploration → Pattern finding → Ideation → Prototyping →Pilot + Scaling

My Brain starts visualizing the requirements as puzzle pieces and the final outcome as the completed  puzzle picture. If I miss out a piece, the bigger picture will not be complete; enabling both the client  and us to be more attentive.

Challenge

I work in a pan-national company with all country marketing positions. As a part of the job I was  assigned a specific area with distributorships to be managed for sales and marketing of our  product(s). Instructions, data collection, information, support and feedback is required on regular  basis. Most of them were not comfortable with English or national Language, but only with regional  language (my limitation). One-to-one interaction was the most effective but least efficient. All other  tasks were delayed due to more time being dedicated to communicate with all distributors. It is an  old business and partners have become comfortable in the traditional way of doing business. So my  challenge was to communicate effectively with all channel partners.

Selection

All of the partners require internet connectivity, working email, computers and mobiles. My  assumption was that all of them checked their e-mails and messages regularly. I selected the  ‘Learning Launch Tool’. Because the learning and adaptation was from both sides, I chose this  method as it would help me understand the behaviour as well communicate with the partners.

Application

I started with communicating via mail and in English only. The second step was to get individual  feedback – if they were attentive to the communications and if yes what was their level of  understanding. Next step was to draft emails bilingual (English and national-Language) and again get  individual feedback.

In next step I started with mobile sms messages, followed by whatsapp messages and whatsapp  groups (territory wise). The initial phase was to communicate only to partners only. Next was to  include the managers employed by partners in all communications. Feedback was taken regularly at  different levels to understand the effectiveness of communications.

My father is a shop owner and I occasionally help him in running it whenever I get the time  from my studies. To overcome this problematic situation, I made various case reports on  how I can help in increasing the sales by finding out the reasons behind why customers were not  coming to shop and what approaches to use to get back on track after hard times.

DESIGN THINKING COURSE  FINAL ASSIGNMENT - Sara Robinson  STORYTELLING

Challenge

Coursera’s Design Thinking course made me acknowledge a useful and proven process for

the creation of innovative ideas. I will try to apply learned concepts and tools in my presales

role at work. Some of the tools such as visualization and storytelling were already in use in

my role, although I now have a better background to apply them more efficiently within the

design thinking process, defining the “What is”, “What if”, “What wows” and “What Works”.

Storytelling for technical presales

In LATAM (Latin America), customers with IT (Information Technology) requirements are

usually overwhelmed with many solutions to be analyzed for their needs. Comparing those

solutions may become a very big effort for customers and vendors. Features may not be

standardized, and business processes may require customization or a combination of two

or more technologies to cover a specific need.

Storytelling is very useful for technical presales in IT. As a presales engineer, this tool allows

me to:

● Share stories of other experiences or other success cases with customers.

● Discover many issues and opportunities in customer’s organizations (corporations,

government agencies, etc).

● Show that the project I sell can comply with customer’s needs.

Insight - Applying Storytelling for presales engineering

While customers listen to the stories I share, I also ask them to share their own problems

and opportunities for their business. I use that feedback to design a preliminary solution

that will then evolve into a successful project. The way to evolve is through an agile

methodology. So, we iterate in the definition of the solution as many times as we need, in

order to define an efficient solution that complies with each other's interests and goals.

The solution becomes our solution (not only mine or the customer’s).

Challenge & Selection    Storytelling is a great tool that I use all the time. I work with vulnerable populations, developmentally  disabled individuals, senior citizens, and economically disadvantaged people. Many of these people deal  with oppression and dysfunction in every aspect of their lives, they need to be empowered and  inspiration is a path to empowerment. I spend a lot of time “opening people up” and finding ways to  inspire them to improve their circumstances. When I work with seniors, we share stories for different  reasons. Often they're lonely and are so happy to share stories of their lives with me to connect and  they find meaning in sharing these experiences as a form of teaching and/or legacy, in a sense. With my  developmentally disabled clients I share stories of my life in order to help them visualize a state of  independence, I use their feedback against the context of my story to ascertain their goals, and  sometimes we use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this  information to develop different strategies to try and find a way that works for them to gain more  independence in the areas they find lacking in their lives. The agency was in the grip of a “compliance culture” and its clients were failing in this  non-empathetic, rigid structure. text:
Mind Mapping Tool

Challenge & Selection

I have worked in IT department of the company to develop and maintain in-house application.  My work focus on enhancing new feature to support the business needs. In the past, we found   gap of solution because we have many skills blended both business and technical area;  Business analyst, System analyst, Developer, UX/UI designer, but no one is in the same page.

I choose Mind Mapping Tool for my team because it represents idea in visualize and structural  that make easier understanding among team member to gain more ideas.

Application

The requirement from business user is like an opened end question that we do not know the  exact answer and the possibility is endless so design thinking process is suit to my work, to  gather ideas, to make them more clear and analyze for more options. In this stage, we try to  move from “What Is” to “What If” and discover as much as possible ways to get there - refer to  “The transition from what is to what if, is design criteria, not a design.” video in week3

I select Mind Mapping Tool by using it with sticky notes on whiteboard. When requirement  come from business user, I start the process by conducting a meeting with my working team  give them sticky notes and brief them the requirement with some questions such as what is the  impact to existing application?, what is the impact to legacies?, and what we have to  implement? And let team write down the idea on each question about 10 to 15 minutes. Then I  take the notes, group the in similar topic and ask team to review. In this moment, we can move  the notes, draw line and arrow to link the items to realize how everything related. After main  topic is ﬁlled, we drill down to the next level to get the clearest answer for each. And most of  the time we come up with new interested topic. Sometime, after discussing we change our  mind so we can move the note around. Flexibility and expandable are the advantage of this  selection.

Storytelling the Admissions Process

Challenge

I handle digital marketing for a university in Pakistan. This semester we were planning our  marketing campaign when the pandemic hit and forced us to shut down our campus. Initially, we  had made several plans of holding open houses and asking students to visit our campus to see  our facilities. We even decided to make a nice welcome oﬃce to provide information to any  student or parent coming to visit. These plans were put on hold and we had to design our entire  admissions campaign online. In general we struggled to attract students to our newer programs  and felt that by opening up the campus and showing the facilities we had we could attract better  candidates and grow our brand. In short we wanted our prospective students to experience our  culture and campus, which could have helped them make a decision to apply to our programs.

Selection

When we decided to take our entire admissions campaign online, we had to ﬁgure out a way to  still allow our prospective students to experience our campus and culture. We pondered what  would be the best way we could do that, so we chose to take the Storytelling approach.  Storytelling allows brands to connect with the emotions of the audience and show characters that  the audience can relate to. As the Storytelling Tool video from Week 2 of the course says that  storytelling doesn’t solve a problem but creates a cause “A cause is something that ignites  people, and unites people.”

Application

We realised that the best storytellers for this situation would be the Alumni. If prospective  students saw Alumni established in good companies, and they tell the story of their experience on  our campus, then that could attract those students to apply. Learning Launch Tool

1. CHALLENGE:  I work for a global organization in the Learning Culture function and am

responsible for enhancing employee’s knowledge in both compliant and awareness topics.  I am  currently leading a project to help our Leaders understand/practice a foundational internal  business concept, execute on its components and spread awareness of the concept to their  employees.  Currently, out of 10,000 managers, 5500 have never been trained on the model.   The specific challenges to address are: (1) prioritizing the audience that needs trained with our  limited amount of time and budget, (2) gaining commitment from the audience to participate  given strict time constraints/schedules, and (3) ensuring the learning is effective.

2. SELECTION:  I selected the Learning Launch tool since the process is ‘fast and cheap’

(according to Marcel Nguyen, Week 4 video).  The Learning Launch tool involves conducting a small  experiment to test an idea or in this case ideas.  First, I had to identify/confirm the customer  needs and test the assumptions collected.  It’s also important to work with facts.  The facts are:

•  I have identified the customer needs to have 4500 managers trained on our business  system by the end of 2019

•  The 4500 managers who need trained are all over the world and speak English

•  There is not budget for ‘face to face’ training

•  Schedules are tight, and our time allotted to capture their attention is limited

3. APPLICATION:   First, using Secondary Research (Session 4), I met with several key

stakeholders, Subject Matter Experts (SME’s) and managers who have already been trained on  the business system.  Their feedback coupled with the SME’s and sponsors of the project, we  have 3 potential assumptions to solve our challenge.  I completed the Learning Launch design  for each of the assumptions.

text: Challenge and selection:   In the city of Monte Quemado, province of Santiago del Estero (Arg), with a deeply  rooted gastronomic culture, we decided to sell healthy meats due to a prima facie  concern.     Selection and Application:   The tool to use is visualization or visual thinking that led to a quick understanding of an  important health problem, the number of people with obesity is disturbing in the  community and we take for granted that there is something else behind this disease. A  sample of the population was taken to work and we discovered that the ethnographic  study tells us: foods rich in carbohydrates almost entirely, too much protein, abuse of  sugars and total ignorance about vegetables. To continue investigating, blood samples,  body mass index (BMI) and blood pressure were taken. All thanks to the participation  of the government of the Province and the Regional Hospital. These results were  disturbing, the values for diabetes were too high.     Vision and Application:  This motivated us to work more and co-work with many people: nutritionists specialized  in diabetes and morbid obesity, professional chefs, regional producers and with graphic  designers for the launch of the brand. Meats are fully balanced individual servings  accompanied by detox juices with mixtures of vegetables and fruits without added  sugar. This motivated people, even healthy people, to embrace life and for the new  generations to completely modify their diet.

If you want to meet those expectations, your online ordering experience needs to be top-notch.One way both retailers, manufacturers, and distributors of customization products can stand out and create a memorable online customer experience is through product visualization.

For example, our  suite of CPQ tools  offers a set of robust visual product configurators to ensure order accuracy and improve the customer experience. This includes depicting your products in 2D, 3D, or even  virtual reality.And if you’re wondering how product visualization software knows what your product looks like, the software uses images and artist renderings that you upload to the system. The software also uses the dimensions you input into the system so that customers can get a better feel for the scale of your products as well.

We are facing a chronic problem of Humidity & Temperature Variation in Spinning plant. Humidity & Temp plays a vital roll to control the yarn strength, breakage & its all quality parameter. I took this opportunity to resolve this problem by visualization tool. So I called all stakeholders associated with this problem in one room & explained what I have learn from the visualization tool. Then I shared the visual video for better understanding of all the team members.

Application

text:
Example Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

In literature, storytelling technique comlies an immense part of culture, customs, technology, and

ideology transformations. This tool is very prominent since it reacts with the people and gives

them the sense of familiarity and complete understanding this opens the door to the simplicity of

engagement.  To do so, I usually give the person an environment of full of choices for instance,

when I want to persuade this person I should never act like I am deliberately want him to do this

for me or for my company instead I show them as a perfect choice that they can take to develop

their lifestyle or whatever.

Application

My story was about environmental protection and sustainability. As I advocated more on the

credibility and the emergency of the issue, a guy shouted out that this is nonsense at all. The

developed countries use these slogans just to stop us from producing more and they want us to

just be their consumers, he added. I was happy that my method of storytelling wasn’t infertile.

Though I gave some answers to the crowd as a whole I preferred to get a time with this tempered

man. He told me that his timber industry has collapsed because of these movements and no sign

of protection and reservation in the most developed countries but ongoing mass production.

Insight & Approach

From that point I assured him a total comprehension of his position. I talked to him about my

purpose about the speech was to narrow the importance of sustainability in other words the need

for production of furniture with the growing more trees was in demand. I also do your business

in the same industry yet I balance my profits and the greater good, I followed.

While I was doing this course, I got storytelling technique as powerful and compatible method at

almost all times and conditions.

Visualization Project

Challenge and Selection    Visualization is a tool that as an elementary teacher I depend on a

significant amount. Helping students be able to visualize the story they are  reading, or the project they are about to create will help them with the process  and their comprehension. Visualization helps bring certain concepts to life for  third grade children.  To help students engage in innovation through a mathematical  and social study approach, the children will work in teams to create a tower with  toothpicks and playdoh that has a specific range of surface area, while taking into  consideration the type of building. This helps the students understand the idea of  area, size, and measurement in a more visual way.     Application    We begin discussing what area actually means? Why is area important? I

start sharing with my class how we are thinking about building a house but we need  to think about the size and area. I ask them to turn and talk about why does the  size or area matter? Children have a hard time taking measurement and putting it  into perspective. Though this miniature town, the children will be able to relate  their town to this one and understand measurement and sizing.     I now share with the students that they are going to be building a

community town as a class, similar to the town they live in. They are in charge of  designing a variety of different buildings for our town proposal, to share with the  Town Board Zoning Director. They will work in teams of three to create their  building. But together as a class they must think of the logistics and sizing of the  buildings. As teams decide what type of building they are going to construct they  meet as a class to make sure they have the different buildings that are necessary  in a town. Learning Launch to test a new idea

Challenge

I have recently joined a global corporation to help them to become a knowledge sharing organization.  Prior to my arrival, there were number of ideation sessions held to generate ideas to improve  knowledge sharing and peer learning. Stakeholders were engaged to prioritize these ideas to  implementation.

I was asked to develop a detail business case to start the implementation of a high priority idea –  Deliver of Knowledge Sharing Sessions. These sessions are 30min-long weekly sessions presented by  Subject Matter Expert covering exciting technologies they work on, partnerships with internal and  external parties, and techniques they use at work. These sessions would help knowledge sharing with  other teams and make new connections with experts.

Selection

Instead of spending a lot of time on developing the business case, I consulted all stakeholders with my  approach to start the implementation with a pilot. I convinced all stakeholders that this pilot would  quickly help us to measure benefits, gather user feedback and test the process from start to end. Also,  I promised stakeholders that they would receive weekly reports on progress. We all agreed to try out  this pilot approach for first 4 weeks.

Application

In first 4 weeks, I delivered 4 knowledge sharing sessions with different teams. I closely monitored  progress, measured benefits/KPIs, and gathered user feedback on these sessions. There was good  acceptance from users, and teams started collaborating on new projects. However, we observed  number of challenges with our delivery process. They required number of changes to our process.

Mind Mapping - Insurance innovation

That is why some insurance companies started to target cyclists as consumers, but the  consumer experience is still far from ideal, so I wanted to understand, and ultimately create  a better insurance experience for road cyclists.    For that, I chose the mind mapping tool during the exploration phase, in order to look for  insights based on what insurances are in the market, as well as what kind of cyclists are  purchasing it. Road cyclists, mountain cyclists, and commuters all have different goals, gear, and  risk-levels. For instance, commuters use the bike for brief moments of the day, generally  have cheaper gear, and don’t have performance in mind. On the other hand, mountain and  road cyclists have quite expensive bikes and equipment, can be out for many hours a week  and because of the nature of the sport, are exposed to more injuries and accidents.    I also added to my mind map the insurance companies that are offering cyclist coverage,  dividing it by price, and coverage and general user experience. STORYTELLING IS A MUST-HAVE TOOL

Challenge & Selection

I work as a presale consultant at an IT company. My job is to consult our customers on software  solutions needed to improve their business and to sell our products. Our software is a high value  investment, very often the decision maker is CXO level. How can I convince them to buy our  solutions instead of competitors’? There are tons of software out there with minor difference  between them. Talking about all the system’s functions will not work. The CXO level does not  understand and don’t bother much about the technical stuffs, rather they want to know which  value the solution brings to their business, how it helps to smooth operation, increase efficiency  and revenue. Over time, I found out that story telling is a great and must-have tool to win the  customer.

Application

Regardless of who my audiences are or which product I am selling, using storytelling during my  presentations allows me to easily share message and got my audience engaged and interested.  As shared in the “Storytelling tool” video of Week 2, it's about the connection that I give to people  about a piece of information that I’m trying to share. An engaging story helps to increase my  prospect’s trust in me, my company and the pitched product or service. The customer wants to  hear a story about others who have the same challenges as they face and how my solution has  helped them to overcome those. Storytelling is not only relevant but easy to follow, engage and  therefore more convincing.

Storytelling had helped me to win a big first deal for one large customer to use Workplace by  Facebook. Workplace is a social network like Facebook but restricted in the company’s border. text:
Mind Mapping for Career Pathing

Challenge

The company I work for currently employs nearly 11,000 people in this region.  There are many different  divisions and numerous departments within those divisions.  A great challenge within the company is  career pathing for employees.  It is hard to define a specific career journey because there are so many  possible paths.  Employees may not only want to move up within their department; they could also want  to move to a different department or even division.  There is not enough communication to relay to  employees about the necessary steps to change job roles within the company.  To tackle this challenge, I  became a member of the “Career Squad.”  The ultimate goal of the squad is to empower the employees  in their career journey through clarification, transparency, and education.

Selection

We have selected to use the mind mapping tool to further understand employee concerns and  brainstorm ideas to achieve small goals.  As stated in Guadalupe Gutierrez’s video, “Mind Mapping Tool,” a  mind map allows us to look for themes and patterns within our data to establish criteria for the “What  If” phase.  In order to effectively clarify a career path, we must be able to identify the patterns and  interests of our employees.

Application

We first collected our data by sending company-wide surveys to understand “what is.”  The surveys  included questions about the overall environment within the company and improvements that could be  made.  Open-ended questions were also included so that we could get verbatim from the employees.   We took a deep-dive into the employee feedback and survey results to understand that there is  employee dissatisfaction surrounding career pathing, or rather, a lack of information and  communication.  There is no clear alignment on what career paths could potentially be available.

text:
Reflection Storytelling

Challenge

I work in a market research agency. We recently developed a new approach to analyse  consumer behavior and opinions from web sources. After testing the approach in a small scale,  we find the results very promising as they provide rich and valuable insights. However, at this  point our approach requires a lot of manual work and thus is rather inefficient – especially on a  larger scale. We would like to develop a fully automated process of our approach that provides  the same valuable insights as found in our tests – but much more efficient. This means,  however, that our company has to make an investment in our approach. This again, means we  will have to convince a number of stakeholders of our approach, make them believe in us and  eventually release a budget for the investment.

Selection

I think the key to success, to convince the budget managers of our idea, is to wrap it into an  inspiring, emotionally involving story. Preet Luna’s contribution about the storytelling tool in  week 2 of this fantastic course really was an eye opener here. After watching the rather short  video it became very clear to me that in order to make this idea successful we would have to go  beyond presenting a solid plan. We would have to share our excitement about the idea, make  the stakeholders see our vision. Even though until now I have never been a great storyteller – I  decided to make a start with this challenge.

Application

To create a stage for our story, we initiated a meeting with budget managers and other  stakeholders of the company. As usual, we created a PowerPoint presentation as a means for  sharing our ideas. This time, however, we made sure the presentation wasn’t just about  projecting figures on the wall. Challenge

*What is?

I work as an Interior Designer in a team of 5, for a huge global company specialized in home  furnishing. The work is mostly about planning and implementing solutions based on the data  we collect and the goals that we want to achieve on the market, doing it in the store without  any real communication with the actual customers. So basically, visualizing solutions for the  virtual problems without meeting the individual. There is even a “Life at home” document  based on a wide research of the local market trying to help us in understanding the many needs  in the ultimate goal to make life better for the many.

Recently we got a new project due to high demand on the market to create a brand new service  in giving Home Furnishing Consulting services to our customers, which is quite new to the team  giving that there is no experience in meeting and communicating with the client ‘one on one’.  **(Perhaps we were actually missing this piece of the puzzle?)

Challenge:

I was very interested in the ﬁrst block of our training - visualization. As a person who works in 3D and visualizes space, I am always interested in the topic of visual thinking. Visualization is a core component of our way of communicating, whether we think about it or not. When we deal with very complex problems, we actually play out different situations that give us more knowledge than just logic. We actually make predictions. It's an incredible tool, in the sense that we use it as part of our brain at every stage of the design process.

Selection:

Visualization is the application of images. It is not about drawing in any way, but about visual thinking. It allows us to go beyond the application of texts or language. It is a method of opening up another part of our brain that allows us to think non-verbally, which managers usually do not use in any way.

When you clarify a thought with words, others form their own personal mental images as a principle, inﬂuenced by our training. When you say, "We need a new platform for growth," the IT expert sees servers and code, and the marketing guru sees an advertising campaign. If you instead present us with your idea by drawing it, you reduce the likelihood of incompatible mental models.

I always had a problem of misunderstanding between me and my teacher, when I showed him my work on the project and told him in words the concept, we did not understand each other from the word go. Neither I did not understand his advice, nor he my ideas. I did not draw sketches on principle, because I thought I was bad at drawing. Now I understand how important and useful it is. In Tim Brown's  book Change by Design, he states that drawing for designers is a way to express their ideas and only drawing “can simultaneously reveal both the functional characteristics of an idea and its emotional content.” It is not necessary to poses good drawing skills –

Mind Mapping,      Challenge:     For several years I have been working for an Asset manager in the Netherlands. During this period I have been involved in many  projects. Certainly in the world of asset management, much has changed in recent years in the area of Law and Regulations.  What I mainly experience in these projects is that all departments have a different interest in starting a new project. This  certainly does not benefit the project. How do you get everyone to complete a project in the common interest and how do you  motivate everyone who participate in the project?    Selection:    An improvement project can be approached in different ways. The most common way is the scrum approach. We work in  multidisciplinary teams that work in short sprints, with a fixed length of 1 to 4 weeks. Cooperation is very important and  everyone must be able to respond quickly to changing circumstances. Scrum is based on the theory of empirical process  control, or empiricism. Empiricism assumes that knowledge arises from experience and making decisions based on what is  known.     I chose mind mapping because I am looking for a way to show the creativity colleagues always have at the start of a project,  to  keep this up to date and very important to keep it visible.   But also with the thoughts to keep colleagues motivated and to show how their creativity contributes to the project.    So I want to see if scrum can be combined with Design Thinking and especially with Mind mapping.    Application:    When starting a new project at work, I checked whether it is workable to combine the scrum approach with Mind Mapping. The  central theme was to increase the STP (Straight through processing) rate for a specific product that we trade with an x  percentage.    As a scrum team, we have tried to provide insight into the various topics related to the 'increase STP rate'

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation – Final Assignment   Antonio Juarez

Challenge:

I work for a large consulting firm in the IT services space. Specifically, I advise large corporations  (primarily marketing departments) how to better engage customers and prospects to realize more value  from these relationships. Recently, a global auto rental company with whom our firm has a deep  relationship posed the question to me and my team of how to increase adoption of the firm’s new  mobile application. They had spent a bunch of money building and launching a new mobile application  and were far behind in meeting the Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) with which they had justified the  original investment. Senior management was unhappy.

To start, my team and I took initial issue with the premise of the initial ask and coordinated a workshop  to reframe the question. Rather than solving the “increase adoption of the mobile app” question, we  drilled to the root issue or key business problem being “how do we leverage the mobile channel to  better engage with our renters.” This was an important step in framing the challenge – it removed a  specific solutioning bias pertaining to application adoption as well as limited the scope of our inquiry to  renters versus prospects.

Once we aligned on a business problem, we completed a research phase that included analytical data  from the current app, segment & behavioral data from the relevant renter segment, constructed  journey maps to show the current state, did competitive research, etc. Additionally, we interviewed 20  users of the app, several customer service reps, etc. We presented these “as-is” findings back to the  business and scheduled a workshop as our next step with a focus being on engaging cross domain  stakeholders (business, IT, marketing, product) to collaborate on creating prioritized design guidelines as  a framework for our innovation process.

text:
Challenge and Selection

Storytelling is of vital importance to consulting in that it is one of the main deliverables  that clients are seeking when they look to hire a partner. People don’t just want to be  told what to do; they want the story behind why the status quo is not working and how  your proposition will make a difference. When I work with different firms, oftentimes  marketing teams are tasked with the impossible and stretched very thin. That means it's  my job to dig into what’s broken, ask questions, create efficiency, and ultimately —  deliver a story to my clients about how we can transform their day to day work from the  way things are to the way things can be. This requires getting to know my clients and  understanding how they will best receive news, both the good and the bad.

Application

Delivering results to a client is about more than just handing them the plan of  execution. For people to feel that they are partners in an engagement, the art of  storytelling is key. In concluding an engagement and delivering results, I use  storytelling to remind clients about the journey we’ve taken together throughout the  last few months. I begin with the problem that we worked closely together to refine.  This is a helpful refresher on how our goals were established and what our KPIs will  measure in the results. I then talk about how our hypotheses informed the experiments  that we conducted, and the reasoning behind what worked, what didn’t, what we  learned, and why I feel the final results are the best path forward. Walking clients  through the whole story of the engagement helps them feel included in the journey  and invested in the new beginnings.

MIND MAPPING:

Mind mapping is a creative and logical means of note-taking that "maps out" your ideas in free-form.  They are non-linear representations of how you connect ideas and concepts. They are useful for  creative thinking and brainstorming.

All mind maps have some things in common. They have a natural organizational structure that

radiates from the centre and use lines, symbols, words, colour and images according to

simple, brain-friendly concepts. Mind mapping converts a long list of information into

a colorful, memorable and highly organized diagram that works in line with your

brain's natural way of doing things.

Why to use it?

Mind mapping assignments can increase student’s achievement and knowledge

retention because students are constructing knowledge. Mind maps help students

learn information by forcing them to organize information and allow them creativity

by the addition of color and images. These types of maps have been shown to lower

extrinsic cognitive load because students are creating a two-dimensional space to tie

ideas and concepts together. They allow students to create visual images to make

information more meaningful and allow for deep learning to occur.

Common uses:

Mind maps can be used for a variety of purposes including:

✓ Note taking  ✓ Brainstorming (individually or in groups)  ✓ Problem solving  ✓ Studying and memorization  ✓ Planning  ✓ Researching and consolidating information from multiple sources  ✓ Presenting information  ✓ Gaining insight on complex subjects  ✓ Jogging your creativity

How to develop the habit of Mind Mapping?

✓ Start in the middle of a blank page, writing or drawing the idea you intend to develop. I

would suggest that you use the page in landscape orientation.

✓ Develop the related subtopics around this central topic, connecting each of them to the

center with a line.

text:
Reflection

Storytelling

Storytelling describes the social and cultural activity of sharing stories, sometimes with improvisation, theatrics or

embellishment. Every culture has its own stories or narratives, which are shared as a means of entertainment,

education, cultural preservation or instilling moral values.

Storytelling predates writing. The earliest forms of storytelling were usually oral combined with gestures and

expressions. In addition to being part of religious rituals, some archaeologists believe rock art may have served as a

form of storytelling for many ancient cultures.[2] The Australian aboriginal people painted symbols from stories on cave

walls as a means of helping the storyteller remember the story. The story was then told using a combination of oral

narrative, music, rock art and dance, which bring understanding and meaning of human existence through

remembrance and enactment of stories.[3] People have used the carved trunks of living trees and ephemeral media  (such as sand and leaves) to record stories in pictures or with writing. Complex forms of tattooing may also represent

stories, with information about genealogy, affiliation and social status.[4]

With the advent of writing and the use of stable, portable media, stories were recorded, transcribed and shared over  wide regions of the world. Stories have been carved, scratched, painted, printed or inked onto wood or bamboo, ivory  and other bones, pottery, clay tablets, stone, palm-leaf books, skins (parchment), bark cloth, paper, silk, canvas and

other textiles, recorded on film and stored electronically in digital form. Oral stories continue to be created,

improvisationally by impromptu storytellers, as well as committed to memory and passed from generation to generation,

despite the increasing popularity of written and televised media in much of the world.

The challenge is to make the programs more profitable while at the same time  keeping up the general quality of teaching and research of the university in order to  stay competitive and meet the national assessment criteria. The student numbers  are growing and more growth is expected. However, in the last two years, with new  investments the costs have exceeded the revenues. Thus, a new structure by  reducing the current resources has to be created by the next winter term, which is  starting in about 8 months. Besides economic and quality aspects (accreditation) to  be considered, the main challenge is to integrate all stakeholders: teaching staff as  well as students evaluations, who are the end-consumers and the most important  focus group. Moreover, the curricula are supposed to be more flexible adaptable to  the different campuses in order to meet their own regional needs.       Selection  The academic program leaders in the past have already undergone steady, but  minor optimizations of the curricula. Although being mostly designers and used to  creative work environment themselves, time pressure often prevented to come up  with new innovations.   As the scrum master, I developed a plan together with the product owners defining  sprints and the delivery team while using a kanban board. As tools, I decided to stick  to use various mind-mapping tools to re-think the curricula in a free and creative way  in order to avoid sticking on the already known and be able to come up with new  ideas. Reflections: Learning Launch for a Well-Being Programme

Challenge  Physicians burnout is a prevalent issue worldwide and there are increasing studies/articles on  physicians leaving service due to excessive workloads, display of disruptive behaviours due to higher  stress, display of greater dissatisfaction and increased no. of physicians seeking help etc. This is an  important issue as burnout not only affects the individual’s health and well-being, it also affects their  relationship with colleagues and family members, as well as the quality of clinical care, patient safety  and satisfaction etc.     However, we hypothesized that the number of physicians seeking help from the official institutional  support offered (e.g. helpline to offer employee assistance, “SPEAK UP” initiative) is only tip of an  iceberg, as burnout is commonly viewed as a weakness and there is fear of being stigmatized. We also  hypothesized that physicians are more likely to seek help when the situation has become more severe,  and this can be alleviated if there are physicians themselves within the work environment to recognize  the signs and symptoms and intervene at an earlier stage, in comparison to a passive approach.

Selection  A learning launch, or smaller-scale experimentation is selected for the well-being programme due to  the lack of complete data on the level of burnout across the institutions and data on the usefulness of  the existing interventions that we had hypothesized to be under-utilized. Also, burnout is a sensitive  topic to physicians that needs to be carefully managed. Many of our ideas are actually “smart guesses”  that we think may work and are not suitable for a massive implementation yet. We would likely need  to refine the programme based on participants’ feedback, and there can have deeper conversations  when the group size is smaller. Post-Covid Schooling - Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection

Covid-19 situation brings a new world to us. We usually conducted physical school but

this time the idea of online class is presented to us as obligation. Nowadays classes

and exams are mostly conducted virtually. Recently a school managing committee

requested us to conduct this assignment to see how an effective online schooling

mechanism we can propose. The first tool we used was the tool of Visualization, or

Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a

diverse group of students, parents, teachers, IT professionals and other relevant

stakeholders. Before going to make action plans we use Mind Mapping tool to facilitate

brainstorming among relevant stakeholders and contributors. We use this approach

often with our customers to solve a problem efficiently.

Application

Usually at the event of mind mapping sessions, to start with we present meaningful data

with visual presentation to our participants to be aligned with the problem we will be

trying to solve. After the briefing session we invite participants to be distributed among

predefined groups where already set of questions there to discuss and a moderator of

each group fascilitae the group to come up with their inputs. Participants then place

sticky notes to each group poster board. Usually 30 minutes the session goes and after

that each moderator presents one after another with their ideas and proposals.

But during this pandemic situation we conducted the whole workshop online in zoom

platform and were able to run an effective mind mapping session. At first we had a

Challenge and Selection

The very first weakness that I discovered to myself is that I am not good in communicating towards people  regarding my ideas with a problem or topic. Instead of discussing to the group the problem I use to do it on  my own sometimes which leads me to be an outcast when it comes to presentation. There are times when  one of the group’s member is one of my friends and when it comes to problems that I didn’t understand I’ll  just ask him/her which help me to visualize the current problem that leads also to visualization with possible  solution. To make it simple I am interested in applying visualization tool not only for my own self but also for  me to be able to share the ideas that I have been framed.

Application

During school presentation I always rely on thing that I found in books, internet and journals without my prior  knowledge regarding the problems or topics that have been assigned to me or to the group that I’m in. It’s a  shame when you have least knowledge to the said topic because you can’t help the audience to visualize  the topic that you are nurturing them, that’s why I want to have my own visualization regarding the topic in  order for me to relay the message completely to audience.

DESIGN THINKING FOR INNOVATION ASSIGNMENT

COURSERA

Miguel Fernandes

THE CHALLENGE1

I am a systems thinker, learning to think-design. In the last six months I have been involved  in a multidisciplinary design project led by design teachers and students from Alliance University. The project has to do with Concord, an amusement park under construction in  Costa Rica.  Concorde is going to be a park able to offer its Costa Rican’s (CR) visitors a  space-time shell for both a ludic reunion with their culture and with ancestral mother earth.  And for non-Costa Ricans an opportunity to know more about this rich culture-nature.  As a  matter of fact, the originators and financial supporters of this undertaking aim at building a  thematic park able to offer visitors a variety of ludic interactive experiences to recover both  the meanings that historically have shaped CR’s cultural identity and the respect for their  natural legacies.

In preliminary meetings with management to define the design challenge, they pointed out  that they had paid much attention to the “reunion with the culture” aspect of the project but  that they needed to think more thoroughly the “reconnecting with mother earth” aspect.   Accordingly, management posed the following challenge: design experiences that could  open the senses of the visitors to the surrounding nature and to the particular disruptive ways  we relate to her.

We began our design-thinking process with the what is stage. Accordingly, we launched a  series of activities such as interviews to management, gathering of relevant written and video  materials and visits to the park under construction. Using tools like mind mapping, several  issues began to emerge from the data thus collected. text: Challenge: Get approval to create an innovative development experience for  new managers    I was tasked with coming up with a learning solution for new managers in our organization. Our current  approach to management development was to send managers out of the office to a workshop for several  days of full-day academic learning about how to lead and manage people. Our senior leadership believed this  approach was necessary so that managers weren’t distracted during training and they could receive a “brain  dump” of HR-related information all at one time. In my initial conversations with new managers, however, it  became clear that this approach was ineffective. Although they needed the HR information, they were  stressed out by the idea of being away from their jobs for the week and they couldn’t absorb so much  information at once – particularly when they had no chance to apply it in the moment. We were so focused  on the dissemination of processes and policies, we had lost sight of managers’ emotional needs, which our  training programs weren’t addressing at all. I had a vision for approaching the learning solution in a  completely different way but, before I could move forward with the idea, my immediate challenge was to  get several groups of senior leader stakeholders to embrace the concept. Without their support, I would  never be able to make such a large scale change.      Selection: Storytelling    I work for a very large financial services institution. The connotation is that there are lot of “stuffed shirt”  banker types…which isn’t too far off the mark! As I went through the Design Thinking for Innovation program,  I thought to myself that the technique I would use the least would be storytelling. I just couldn’t quite  envision a positive reaction from the stakeholders I work with, thinking they would find the technique too  “fluffy” and not sufficiently data-driven. After all, we are in the business of making money, not making  emotional connections!
