Challenge & Selection

In a context of rapidly evolving technologies, business models, demographics, and  constant changing needs and expectations, the way training institutions understand  their mission and perform their work has profoundly changed. As a result, the  management board of our university has decided to set up an appropriate  intelligence and prospective system to increase the institutional watch-keeping  capability, share knowledge, anticipate trends and improve the quality of our  services. However the expressed need was very vague and required clarification. So  I have been asked to address this challenge and help the board to clarify their need  as a baseline for a future project.

Amongst the four design thinking tools presented in the course, I have selected the  visualization tool (Module 1) that seemed in my view to be the most appropriate for  starting the reflection process, highlight the range of different representations  associated with the challenge of institutional intelligence and achieve a shared  understanding of the need. I use this approach often now with project team members  or stakeholders groups with various background and expertise to help them get to  know each other better, foster collaboration and demonstrate the value of diversity in  the design process of any new projects. text:
Reflection on using learning launch To check product usability

Challenge

I’m a software engineer and I work in a company that develops financial and operational data  visualization tool. We noticed a decline in the usage of our product and we made it a goal to find  out why and also come up with a solution in due time. My team and I used other design thinking tools such as ethnography to understand the  environment and tasks most of our clients use our product for and we’ve found out that even  though the product does what the client wants, they feel overwhelmed with the interface  because there is a lot of buttons and options to click or select to accomplish a task.

Selection

We chose to use the learning launch tool to prototype and test the newly redesigned interface to  understand how it affected their work and whether they easily use it to accomplish their daily  tasks.

Application We launched the prototype of the new interface version alongside the production version and  routed 20% percent of our users to the new interface. We collected feed-backs and iterated on  the interface designs.

We also organized workshops to witness how they used the new design and collected more data/ feed-backs and made relevant changes to the new interface.

Insight

By using the learning launch tool we identified many pain points of our users and corrected most of our wrong assumptions about how we thought the clients use our product.

We found out that our users used the interface easily when the buttons and options were  organized according to a particular business process they usually undertake daily.

Approach

Using the learning launch tool was the best option for solving this problem because we got the  chance to test our assumption and then iterated very quickly based on user feed-backs till the  product was at an acceptable level. This made most of our client happy because their needs  where put into consideration while designing the new interface.

Marketing a B-School

Challenge   I work in a Private B- school as Head of Marketing and Admissions team. As a background the B-School  offers Management programs for people with prior work experience of minimum two years. We believe  that we operate in a very niche space as we are a private B- school that offers one year full time  management program (Most B- schools in India offer a management program that is full time and is of 2  year duration. In addition, these 2 year programs open for fresh graduates and have no minimum work  experience criterion)

The B – School is now planning to enter into the space of 2 year MBA program. The target group will now  include graduates who are fresh out of undergraduate colleges. The new program, (MBA 2.0 for our  discussion) presented a real “Wicked Problem” for the school in more than one ways. The areas up for  discussions ranged from what courses should be offered in order position ourselves differently to how we  make ourselves heard in a very noisy, busy and competitive marketplace.

To me as head of marketing, the biggest problem was the human problem. The target group of fresh  graduates was completely alien to us. We had no idea of their aspirations, what they are looking for, what  are their compelling reasons to do a management education. The entire team was looking at us to provide  inputs on the audience so as to help in decision making. Above everything else, I was very aware that we  are not selling a product, it about a young person’s career and we have to do a good job in representing  the aspirations and dreams of the young people to our management team.

text:
Design Thinking-Visualization

Challenge & Selection

The very first thing I always do is, I think. I am a visual thinker because when I visually think I  learn about complex mechanisms. Visual thinking covey a better answer than a verbal one in  maximum cases. Now a days the ugliest side of an urban city is traffic jam. And increasing of  ride sharing platforms in many cities the number of cars is also increasing day by day which  causing more jam, and the fares are also increasing. I want to reduce the use of cars and also the  fare, by connecting 4 people in one ride heading in the same direction. The tool I used is visual  thinking or simply visualization.

Application

This is going to be a service where an individual will share a ride and splits cost, fare with  another traveler who happens to be going in the same direction. I will make it affordable to  everyone reducing congestion, pollution, ease traffic, reduce CO2 emissions. We have done a  survey with people using ride sharing platforms on a regular basis and also with them who use it  occasionally. Most of them were students and corporate people. Around 60 percent of the people  said they do not use ride sharing platform that much till they get a discount although they have  ride sharing applications installed. And the rest 40 percent use it more often but would be glad if  the fares were less.

Insight & Approach

People now do not have to break their bank for a ride, meeting new people every day, less cars  less congestion on road. A service where the "60 percent of people" can get a ride and splits cost  with another traveler so they do not need discount as the fares will be divided. And for the rest  "40 percent" our service will make it more affordable for them.

The tool I used for a case study of a prototype manufactured for a rural community was Visualization, which  allowed us to create a shared understanding of the real problem to be addressed before proposing  solutions. This technique was used in an interdisciplinary group (a diverse group) to define key elements, the scope,  the limits and the elements to consider the points of pain and opportunities for improvement with respect  to the prototype to be manufactured.

Application

I start the process by drawing on the board the production process of the cusi oil, in which the bottleneck is  detailed. A punctuation of that process is made to analyze how the milling phase could be automated, taking  into account that the population where that product is manufactured does not have electric power. This is  the challenge to define the mechanism that will follow the machinery to be manufactured.

For this purpose, in the concept process, we used the in/out tool that allowed us to define the limits of the  machine and the type of mechanism that would be used for its operation. Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

Storytelling is the first tool I have officially used this time. But I don't think it's the first time we've

ever thought about a situation because we have a lot of understanding around it. I'm working on

building an artificial intelligence legal system. Laws are always difficult areas where ordinary people

are not easily accessible, but the goal is to make it easier for ordinary people to use them through

the establishment of this system. So I talk about it with the general public who use the law. Instead

of using difficult legal terms as a legal slogan, it uses easy sentences and uses artificial intelligence

to make use of the law more convenient. In particular, the goal is to make it easier for many real

estate dealers to take advantage of relevant laws and enhance their social value.

Application

Let's separate the buyer case and rental case. In case of a trade deal, not only houses but also land

should be traded together, which requires a full understanding of the legal situation in Korea. In

the case of a lease transaction, if there is a problem with the owner, the effect could be, so you

should know how to secure sufficient rights first. The legal system should be designed to take into

account the user's situation, which allows the user to acquire only the information that is currently

needed.

Insight & Approach

The legal system using artificial intelligence has finally been opened. The system has begun to

automate and provide what previously had to be explained by real estate experts or legal experts.

This is the first system we have developed in Korea and has been recognized for its innovation in

the market. We were able to win various awards in recognition of our efforts within the company

and at the same time enhance our social value. Years of work have paid off, and above all, the

satisfaction is beyond description, having developed a system that many people like.

Example Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge

My organization is in software development industry, specialized in enterprise content management.

Our projects consist of implementing document management systems according to business needs

and rules of our customers. For that, we use our document management platform, which is capable

of defining different workflows for specific types of documents.

We had a following challenge -

•  The client was not having internal resources (key users) capable of defining

workflows for the documentation.

•  There were no clearly defined business rules for the documentation management at

the beginning of the project.

•  The documentation handling was manual or through e-mails with lots of back-and-

forth between employees.

•  In addition, it was important to have a quick win in order to boost the confidence of

the client's employees involved in the project.

Selection

Client's business processes were unclear but it was not the matter of defining them but rather

discovering them. Processes were somewhat in effect as there were defined business needs and

employees' responsibilities.

One of the options was visualization that would help stakeholders to see the workflows and the

effects they have on the documentation being handled (lifecycle states, approvals/rejections,

attachments, electronic vs hardcopies etc.).

However, as the stakeholders were previously involved in similar activities with other consultants

and with unsatisfying results, we concluded that the risk of saturation is too high and we should skip

as soon as possible to the phase where we can show actual system, even with flaws.

Furthermore, as we already had a document management platform which was in itself a minimum

viable product it was was economical to go directly to learning launch.

Application

For a learning lunch, we set up the system where users could send documents between each other

without any business rules as if they were using e-

text: Challenge   My wife and I have been focusing on not to buy industrialized food. The side effect was that  we started preparing our on food and every day we see ourselves going less and less in the  supermarket, but more and more to farmers market. We have been getting a lot of  appreciation from our friends related with our sourdough loaf and getting a advise to open  a small bakery.      Selection   We really appreciate the positive feedback from friend and relatives, but we know their  feedback could be influenced by our friendship.  We decided to go with the Learning Launch approach so we can test our product and see if  there is really a market for it.    Application & Insight   We were thinking to open a small booth in a place that host farmer market in the weekend.  The idea was to have some product to sell, but most important to have free trials and ask  the feedback about the public.  Within some more thought we found that being the producers and ask the feedback in front  of the customer could maybe intimidate them to give just positive criticism.  We decided to place small learning launches conducts by friends and relatives. The idea is to  give them the sourdough loaf and they could take it to their work, share it and get some  feedback about the acceptance. We are expecting to get real feedback and really know  what is good about our product and most important what can be improved and what they  would expect from a bakery selling it.  In the meantime we will have a Facebook page done with some professional looking photos  and nutritional information about sourdough loafs.  If things go well, it will make look that we already have a business running and they can  place orders.

Challenge

Health Periodic Exam

My first challenge with Design Thinking was rethinking the service Health Periodic Exam offered by the Federal Public  Ministry of Brazil. This is a periodic health examination that, through legislation, should be offered to all active public  servants in Brazil. The service is offered unequally to all units of the Federal Public Ministry, not reaching all required  public today. It is also important to note that the number of examinations and consultations offered to the civil servants  varies according to a categorization of profiles about risks to health.

The objective was to expand access service to all civil servants of the institution, and rethinking the entire customer  journey.

Selection

To conduct the work, we selected the visualization tool so that we could see together all the steps, information and  agents involved in the Health Periodic Exam. The idea was to create a great visual map that could compose a whole  vision of service, so that participants could gain a global understanding to conduct a holistic analysis.

Application

I started the work creating a panel with two well-defined spaces: "what I know" and "what I do not know". I questioned all  participants what they knew about the Health Periodic Exam, how the service was provided, which was related, etc. Who had an idea, had to wrote it in a post-it and put it on the dashboard.

When I stepped out to explore my petty  entrepreneurial callings, and thrown with challenges, I realized that our innate strengths can help us in  ways we never foresaw. Gaining a better understanding and insight into this labyrinth was crucial to moving the  start-up forward with better conviction and taking needle-moving decisions. I was once working with the  data when I accidentally realized that I was making patterns out of the mess, and in turn, the patterns  easily emerged into flowcharts. The concepts of bubble diagram models in Architecture was not very  different. It could describe complex directional movements of information, in loops or otherwise,  branching out and merging in countless times, and still make sense to the persons working with the  diagram model. text:
Reflection - Learning Launch

Challenge & Selection

I am a member of a small mobile app entrepreneur venture team.  We are developing a mobile app for  personal use.   Our challenge is to increase the sales of the app and to expose the app to wider  audiences. The team resources were limited. It included three sw engineers for the app development  while the marketing aspect of was relying on the mobile phone company’s infrastructure for app  deployment and advertisement which was basically the search engine of the App Store.  The feature and  requirement of the app was based on developers’ personal needs and use cases.  Although there were  many similar mobile apps in the App Store, our app presented some uniqueness such as the special way  for user password entry, data backup to personal computer via Wi-Fi connection and a “closed” app  with no back channel connection to external websites for security reasons.

Early the development cycle, we had decided to provide the basic features so that we could shorten the  time to marketing/sales duration, and experiment the features that we provided.

The mobile app had gone through three month testing within the team members and friends who  volunteered to be real users.  The features of the app were based on what we knew best for the users.   As it turned out, our app introductions were aligned with the learning launch methodology described in  this class.

Application

The primary focus of the first Learning Launch was to gather the results for the app deployment, basic  functionalities and software bugs.  We wanted to use this launch to ensure that we comply with all  stringent requirements and Infrastructure of the App Store, collected software bug reports, and ensured  all the functions worked as designed. text:
Challenge & Selection

With So Many Insurance companies available & So many multiple Options to choose from – Buying  Insurance is a cumbersome & confusing process. Specifically, being employed – with the Employer giving  out options – handling multiple documents of Papers to read from , Whole process is a time consuming  & worst process that I have been through Once myself .

Everyone goes through the same cycle -experiencing It in the same way most of times. Sometimes its  way where the person selling the Insurance doesn’t know what the benefits are / Insurance premiums  are & Just goes forward & say this is the Best Insurance that I have to Offer

So let’s think of Situation for those people –  Specifically Small Business who can’t afford Insurance, This  is the Challenge that I went ahead with analyzing if there exists such people & Started with the  Customer discovery process as part of participating in Lean Startup Conference . So to gather this Data  /Insights & get answers to Question <What is >– we used the process called : Visual Thinking

Application

Using Visual Thinking, Tool – we went to achieve a shared understanding of a problem space among a  diverse group of stakeholders like Small Business / Unemployed before attempting to identify and  define possible solutions to the problem – Who had no insights / ideas to the Insurance buying process. I  used this approach & Stepped out into the Market to gather Statistics & Insights to answer the Question  to gather data for this Problem: What is the process generally this people (Small Business) would have  with their Health Insurance buying Options

Based on the Interview /Insights in studying this potential Customer – I came to know & understand that  the People that sold them Insurance – did not know much details of the potential benefits their  Insurance had to offer , Leave alone that – One /two persons that I spoke with – didn’t know if their  insurance would cover critical conditions like : Diabetes

Challenge and Selection

I choose Storytelling as a tool to solve various  problems. I meet several people of different age  groups, even disabled people. I meet them and discuss  their problems and try to solve by using storytelling  tool. Explain them benefits of having positive mindset  through storytelling. I use stories to make them  understand how to be an optimist in life.

Application

There are many applications of using storytelling, I try  to explain them their needs also by using storytelling  tool. I try to find out where I lag while solving their  issues and try to improve them. I also say them to  control the stress as having more stress and tension  will have a impact on productivity. So be tension and  stress free.

Insight & Approach

I think it is the best approach according to me to find  solution of any problem. I even faced many problems  in work but I solve using Storytelling approach. It  insights me to have enthusiasm and energy to work

and I say various stories to solve their problems and it  really has impact on them.

text:
Design Thinking for Innovation – Final Assignment

by Claudia Perez

Challenge and Selection:      As a Venezuelan, wanting to help my country overcome all the difficult situations led me

to one of the most beautiful and fulfilling experiences: Community Service. My desire to help  others who I knew were not capable of helping themselves made me commit to a cause that  made me the woman I am today. For the past three years I have been involved in an non-profit  organization that dedicates all their resources to helping these affected communities around  certain cities in Venezuela, by giving them food and medical resources, playing with the kids in  their schools or parks near the zone, and helping families with their situation by offering jobs to  the parents and education for their children.

This has been an incredible challenge for me and for the rest of the members of the

organization, and with time, we have achieved wonderful goals that at the beginning seemed  almost impossible. Mind Mapping was one of the most useful tools that helped us accomplish  great things, and without it, I think we would have taken another course of action that would  have not been as successful as the one we followed. This design tool made us look for patterns  and themes in the data we collected inside the communities we were working with, and made it  easier to move from the “What is?” to the “What if?”. As said in the lectures, mind mapping  involves studying and analyzing the minds of our customers, not only ours individually, and  thanks to this, we were available to translate the collected insights to concrete ideas.     Application:      The organization started in 2014, and after a long process of identifying the opportunity

and necessities in several communities, we started scoping our project. We applied the Mind  Mapping tool to get a more thorough and concrete insight of what was happening in these  communities, along with what the members of them thought and worried

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

I was working in the salmon industry in the south of Chile, one of my main tasks was to manage de  innovation system of the company, analyzing statistics, following up on ideas and motivating workers to  innovate.  The first two task were easy, but the third one wasn´t, because the workers didn´t know how  to innovate, didn´t want to, and for them was something only genius people could do. I´m talking about  people who most didn´t finish school, barely could read or/and write, and we were asking them to  innovate on a computer, where they have to go to a special link and fulfill a form that didn´t use the  simplest words, so to speak. In this scenario, the rate of new ideas was about one or two per month, and  the amount of ideas that were fulfilled was nearly to zero.

When I first get involved in the innovation system, I was told how a worker innovate by using an old tire  to increase the resistance of the cages and saved 15 USD million annually. I was shocked by the simplicity  of the idea, and also was shocked how it didn´t inspired others. So, I must confess that I didn´t know this  tool at that time, I used storytelling, I star traveling among all the farming centers telling this story, but I  didn´t get to motivated them, it was frustrating because I was facing uncertainty. Until I meet the worker  who created this idea.

Application and Insight

When I talk with this worker, I realized that the 15 USD millions that he make the company save with his  idea, means nothing to him, because he get nothing from that and second was a number he could not  even imagine. For him, there was three important things: the first one was that by using the old tire he  could do better his work and saved him from various day to day problems, the second one was that the  idea was real, because he can see it, show to people, and used it. Urban Organic Farming – Visualization tool

Challenge:     I live in one of the most polluted cities and the scarcity of both pure air and  organic chemical free food are at its peak. The rooftop Garden (or any other  available place for that reason) can be one the possible solution of having  access to hazardous chemical free option of eatables. Application:

The exercise began by going through all the places in the house and nearby  where the spaces that wanted to be used for the gardens were located, after  this, the visualization exercise was done in each of the places, drawing one by  one the spaces and how they would be distributed based on the idea that my  dad had.   Then, in each drawing we began to describe what type of plants would go in  each space such as flowers, vegetables, aromatic, herbs among others. The purpose of creating a video was to create consistency for all line managers by ensuring that every line manager  delivered the same story when engaging with their staff.    This powerful video was used as a story-telling tool to initiate monthly engagement / café conversation sessions with  their respective teams in order to collectively rebuild/transform the company’s DNA. 1)  Concern(s)/theme

2)  Agreed action

3)  Execution

CHALLENGE

Ten months back in my organization, we had a challenge of very low turnout to the staff  restaurant. The organization was very concerned about this as they could not ensure the quality  of food eaten by the staff outside the office and also concerned about the staff well-being.  Based on these reasons, the organization decided to find a solution. A team was selected for  this purpose and I was the head of the team.

SELECTION

The mind mapping tool was selected as the design thinking tool to help resolve the challenge.  The tool was selected because it helps to identify patterns and insights that can lead to more  creative solutions to challenges.    APPLICATION

We selected few staff to gather data on reasons why they don’t eat in the staff restaurant. We  met with each of them to confirm their available date for a one-one-one session as we could  not get all of them at the same time. We had sessions with 10 staff members and we gathered  lots of reasons why they don’t show up at the restaurant. Based on the feedback we drew a  mind map to identify a pattern and we realized similarities in their reasons for not eating at the  restaurant. The reasons that were most common were quality of food, cleanliness and early  arrival of caterer. The process took over a month because we had to schedule individual  meetings with staff.

We then met with 3 different caterers, presented our top requirements to them and put them  one week rotation. We had informed staff of the rotation earlier. We sent online  questionnaires to the 10 staff selected earlier after each week and we got positive feedbacks.  We then selected 2 of the 3 caterers and the turnout to lunch increase by 80% within 2 weeks.    INSIGHT

text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection:

The Story telling is in the DNA of Indian People, because every cultural aspect of the Indian  tradition has been transferred or cascaded to people generation over generation thru story  telling. Turning point for the Great leader Mahatma Gandhi had come from the story of  Harichandra  told by his mother, from that time he has decided speak only truth. Many of the  saints like  Ramakrishna Paramahamsar was teaching or preaching thru story. Steve Covey the  Management Guru extensively uses the story telling , example in his book “The 7 habits of  Highly effective people. A story where in a railway station two children were making lot of  nuisance to the co passenger, who were in the Platform , every one was annoyed and they  were upset not only with the children but also with the father who was there and not at all  bothered what is going on.

When people started bullying him to control the Kid and they were questioning , why you are  not controlling the kids. He told the co passengers that they are coming straight away from the  funeral of the kids mother, who died because severe illness. He was so sad and not able to feels  what is going around, on the other hand the children were very small to understand the loss of  their mother. Then people started taking care of children them self. This has changed the co  passenger’s perception. Thru this story he was trying to convey that don’t judge and have  empathy on the person who is opposite to you. I can never forget, that is the impact of story  telling.

Application:

Currently working in an American MNC in India and working in leadership level. One of the main  requirement is “Leader as Teacher” need to take some management classes, also do regular  mentoring. I use the story telling approach these occasions.

One of the training session about challenges faced while moving from a role as working  individual to role of a supervisor where one has to get the job done thru the team.

text:
Challenge-

I am heading marketing in ABC and my groups challenge is to improve on branding and establish  brand architecture for ABC .A well-defined brand architecture helps drive effectiveness in a brand  portfolio. When brands and their roles within a portfolio are clearly defined, there is internal and external clarity on  what the brands stand for a how a brand relates to other brands. A defined architecture helps present the brand  consistently across geographies and touch points. Clarity and consistency drive efficiencies – in marketing spends, in  synergizing efforts consistency and efficiency enhances the effectiveness of the brand in stronger brands.

We are, for the first time, defining a brand architecture strategy for the ABC. This will help us  leverage our most precious asset other brands in our portfolio to the fullest extent. Put simply, we are developing a  framework to help us decide on how we use the ABC brand, how we relate other brands to  ABC and finally, how we best present the ABC brand to the internal and external  world.

Selection-

My team has gone through several design thinking activities/tools, therefore we decided to start with learning  launch tool followed by Visualization, or Visual thinking. By using Learning launch we can experiment to quickly test  an idea and prototype for Visualization. Visualization, or Visual Thinking, was used to achieve a shared  understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders (Manufacturing /Sales /After Market etc.)  before attempting to identify and define possible solutions to the problem.

From Week 4 –We can quickly learn to develop prototype of designs /logos and from Week 1 we can put prototype  to get stake holders to add value by feedback through visualization.

Application -

By using Learning launch 1st , we use the term “wordmark” we are referring to the “ABC” mark. The  millennium logo is the symbol that currently goes with the wordmark.

text:
Connecting with your audience through Storytelling

Challenge:

In a world were information flows unrestrained in every direction and readers are invaded with  articles, tweets, news, jokes, etc… creating relevant content is key. I work in the internal  communications team, and even though we have a “captive audience” (our employees),  engaging them is not assured just by sending the regular newsletter. So the challenge is how  to engage associates (or your captive audience) and not just bombard them with information:  speaking to them about what they want to hear and doing so the way they want to hear it,  connecting with their emotions.

As Elisa Cool, VP of Brand development at Contently; says in her webinar The art of  Storytelling – “Content is what you offer your audience in exchange of their trust”.

Selection:

I selected the storytelling tool which consists on reaching out to your audience with content that  is engaging in the way of a story. Stories are inherent to the human being; we have been  hearing them since we are kids. So, if we can manage to tell a story that relates to the people  we are talking to, then is much easier that they pay attention to what we are saying. If the story  has an emotional component, it could even start a conversation among your audience, but first  of all, it will give your content or your message a chance to be heard.

text:
Storytelling

Challenge & Selection

The tool I chose was storytelling because it is a key element in the design thinking  process. If the story is not well told or does grab the public’s attention, it is very  difficult to sell an new idea. I´m head of financial planning in a retail company,  and I use this tool when I have to propose initiatives for cost reductions or sales  increase. People from different areas participate in these meetings where  initiatives are proposed: Country Manager, Operations, Finance, Marketing,  Human Resources, Real Estate, etc. The major challenge is to tell a single story  to people from such diverse areas, and manage to convince all of them.

Application

First of all, I have to know the audience: understand who each person is, what  are their motivations and what could hinder progress for them.. Understanding  the public is key, and based on this I will create a story using a language and  register that everyone can understand. At this point I ask myself questions like:  Are they marketing people? Are they finance people? Are long meetings boring?  Do you prefer to be clearer and more direct?

After I have understood who I am going to speak to, I begin to put together the  sequence of events that I want to communicate to them. At this point I try to be  more specific with the events that I think the audience will want me to go deeper  into.

Finally, I create some moments of reflection, with the aim of increasing and  decreasing the suspense of the story I am telling. By generating suspenseful  moments, the audience becomes more interested in the story. To generate these  moments, I ask a question, there is a silent pause and finally I give an answer.

It is very important to sell the idea as a great necessary challenge, and for that I  always try to relate it to some long-term strategic objective. If I get the idea aligned  with some of the company’s strategic objectives, surely all disciplines want to get  involved and I will be

text:
Example Reflection -Learning Launch tool

Challenge

I am a member of my organization’s software development department and my  challenge is to improve the capacity of quality department in order to increase  overtimes for quality engineers and do not delay the software deliveries for  customer. The main duties of quality department are to compare existent developed software  with requirements from customer, report defects and be sure that defect is fixed and  users can use software functionality according to their goals without any problems. The quality department has 5 engineers and 30 developers for software  development. Development works according to Scrum the sprint for 30 calendar  days and delivery to customer each 30 day. Instead of planned scope at the begging  of sprint the quality department has lots of customer request and tasks that  impossible to estimate and predict. Scope of each release can be very different, so it  led to lots of overtimes and stress for the engineers. While the engineers switching to  urgent tasks deadlines for planned activities begin to start.  We will focus on trying to avoid delay in software delivery with no losses in software  quality.

Selection

The team is try to using the learning launch to test their assumptions on a real  project in one sprint and see what assumptions of the team can be the potential  working to achieve their goal.

Application

For the first learning launch team we focused on varied tasks that do each test  engineer every day. In particular we want to see all the tasks that each engineer has  in one sprint. Reflection- Story Telling

Challenge and Selection

I have always used story telling as a tool to convey my thoughts and to get my point  across the mind of my audience. It has always been an asset for me and has helped me  to make good connections with people I come across in my life. I have travelled to and  lived at quite a few places and have had lots of experiences engaging with the people I  meet. I always have some story to tell them and gauge their attention towards the  conversation.

While preparing for the interview rounds during my B-school admission preparation, I  was always concerned about my ability to explain my education and experience in the  merchant navy to the interview panel. Here the tool of story telling came to my rescue.

Application

Using the tool of story telling for this challenge, I’d always start off with how my  experiences in life pulled me towards a career which required me to travel as I work and  my affinity towards machines made me choose marine engineering. This helped the  interview panel to understand my personality as a professional and as a person.

The story telling tool helped me explain to them why I had not been working for some  time and also form a positive impression about my attitude. I was even able to include  interesting events I experienced during my short stint in the merchant navy.

Insight and Approach

I realized that this tool not only helped me successfully answer the questions asked but  also made my interview experiences very pleasant and memorable.

The interviewers seemed to be interested in what was to come in my story and even  used to share their own experiences in life. We’d often discuss about the improvements  that could be made in the shipping industry and they even asked me about things that  they were unaware of about the life onboard ship.

Challenge and Selection

I recently visited a government school in my neighbourhood in order to learn about the situations  faced by the students there and the circumstances in which they study and live. Most of the  students in the school came from economically disadvantaged households where they faced  difﬁculties involving a lack of money and facilities necessary for daily needs such as food, and  healthcare. Like all other parents, the parents of these children want them to receive a good  education which is all rounded in nature to develop their personalities, mental abilities, talents and  physical abilities. However, it was observed that the students were unable to successfully develop  in most of these ﬁelds, which was a disappointment for the parents and students alike.

By using the storytelling tool, my aim was to interact with the students of the school in order to  discover what the essential problem was, that is, why they were unable to learn what was taught in  school effectively. By doing so, I intended to not only arrive at a solution for the issue at hand, but  to make the children aware that they must talk about their struggles and difﬁculties in order to  improve the situation. The usage of the tool involves talking as well as listening. By listening to the  children and by narrating to them some of my own educational experiences, I hoped to be able to  make them feel as though they could relate to my experiences as well. Also, by listening to the way  the students at my school tackle with various types of issues, they may feel inspired to do the  same for their welfare. Hence, I intended to show them the path they needed to take, for which  guidance through storytelling was ideal.

Visualization

Challenge & Selection    The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared understanding  of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to identify and define  possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers, who are government  agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission or the delivery of their  services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non-citizens. I have used the  technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set of questions or prompts for  discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each other in the process of defining  the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between elements to consider when identifying  pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.    Application    I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw man  graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The existing  material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing materials, GAO or  other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal interviews with one-three  of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the initiative.    If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from previous  research, and discussed in David Gray’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front-stage/back-stage  approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service – has customers  with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the organization to provide  the service. 1. Challenge and selection: Describe your challenge, including all relevant

information.

I work for a municipality in the Netherlands. Like many cities in the world, the  municipality is trying to develop to a smart city (we prefer to call it smart  society because it is all about the people and businesses and not about  techniques)). A few years ago, I was working on a project called “smart  lighting”. Basically, this project was about upgrading our public lighting system  to a smart and interconnected lighting grid which serves as a carrier for  innovative services. At a certain stage of the project we came across questions  on ownership of data processed by the sensors of the public smart light grid.  Should we treat it as open data that belongs to the public or as proprietary data  that only belongs to the private company? The private company we talked with  experienced a lot of uncertainty when data should be treated as open data. They  thought that this would have a negative impact on their business model, which  was based on selling of data. At some stage of the project we had endless  discussions on legal aspects of ownership of data. This led to a serious deadlock  of the project. We decided to take a step back and look at the vision on open  data and open innovation. We decided to “re-scope” (test) this vision: which  beliefs did we have to be tested? Where are our blind spots? I choose the method  of storytelling for this re-scoping of the project.

Challenge Selection

Storytelling is a best tool that I use most of the time. I worked with different people with different  professions. Many of these people deal with many problems in a society and on their work place. I used  to speak my story to them on how I am dealing those problems and managing the stressed given of  these, appreciating individuals is good to know them well. Storytelling is a wide avenue to inspired  people to do his/her best in a job.

Selection

I used the storytelling as a tool to inspire my students by relating my story to their lives.

Application

I have a story about using storytelling. Now that I am a teacher and a school head as will. I used to  narrate my story to my students that all the pains, sacrifices, hard work and fame in achieving my  dreams, I told them that your are just about to start your life journey as students many same problem  would be experience too. What I did to become strong? I hold my faith in God that all things are possible  with him. Those advises came from also to my parents now that I am sharing to my students my story I  hope that they will add in on their strength as young individuals.

Insight

By sharing my story I realized that being a teacher is not easy why? it is because aside from that the  teaching is a noble profession it seems like a harder and harder job, before you can share and inspire  others you should be able to inspire yourself to make a difference to others.

Approach

using storytelling it quite difficult thinking of the situation of the people whom to listened  up to your  story, some might not believe on you and some may give doubt but despite of it storytelling is a good  way to show the story of others.

I have worked with underprivileged children a lot. Many of these kids have faced difficulties to get good  schooling. I have taught them some concepts of science, chemistry and math too in the forms of stories.  Sometimes I have made and played out stories by them being a part of it. Placing them in the lens can  teach them how they would apply something they have learnt when they are faced with such a  situation. It is fun for them because we start off with music or singing, something that catches their  attention.

Reflection – Visualisation and optimisation – not just finding ‘the common ground’

Challenge

Exponential growth in data, the proliferation of information sources and repositories, the ever- intensifying cyber threat and more stringent legal and regulatory requirements have intensified the  criticality of robust information security across both the private and public sectors.

I am working with teams of specialist information security architects and accreditors to design new  ways of working that will allow them to satisfy this ever-increasing demand.  The teams come from  several government departments. The primary objective is to create collaborative teams working in  innovative ways to support the information security requirements of multiple government customer  groups.

The immediate challenge was not to take the ‘best elements’ of the individual teams’ current ways  of working or to coalesce around existing best practice, but to find new and innovative ways to  deliver the increasing and diversifying workload. The challenge was also to address the ‘not invented  here’ risk that could undermine innovation, progress and future implementation. [See:  Design  Thinking for Innovation > Week 4 > Strategic Opportunities > Strategic Contribution #2 (Satisficing  versus optimising).]

Selection

We had carried out a knowledge sharing exercise in which we had compared the current ways of  working of the individual teams (‘What is?’).  We had completed a short ‘what would great look and  feel like’ exercise and identified a set of high-level design criteria.  We now wanted to develop  concepts and candidate ideas that could then be assessed and tested (‘What wows?’).

Visualisation was chosen to break away from the previous mechanistic and process led discussions  and to drive a more creative way of generating new thinking and ideas. [See: Design Thinking for  Innovation > Week 1 > Visualization Tool.]

text: Balance work-free time – Storytelling     Challenge & Selection   During the course of Design Thinking I have discovered that I am already using Storytelling. I am  Storyteller and I can confirm that this is such a great tool.  The last years have demonstrated me that  there is a imbalance between the career and the free time. The most affected persons are the one  between 28-42 years old. I am interacting and working with this category of employees.  Many of these  people deal with an imbalance life and with all the inconveniences that are arising from this. This  imbalance is also affecting their careers, their personality and their interactions with their colleagues.   Every organization has this type of employees. The general solutions are not so efficient like the ones  who are answering to the employee’s needs. I spend a lot of time finding a solution for having a good  work environment, interacting directly with employees in imbalance periods of their lives. Storytelling  seems to me very efficient because in the moment you share real life stories, solutions and  achievements the peoples get more connected ant they find their optimism and their goal to balance  their own lives. Happy people means happy work environment and the best results.  That is why it was  necessary to find out the reasons that lead to this imbalance, how to correct it, to find the correct  approach in order to stabile this employees attitude towards their life and their career.   The organization management requested for solutions in order to help this category of employees,  most of them very valuable employees.   Application   The projects are based on real stories, persons and real advices. Persons who had gone through  imbalance periods of their lives shared their stories and the solutions that helped them to find the  balance. Application

We have been carried  out a new project focused on re-designing the current experience of our customers living  abroad and are using our instant messaging mobile application. Since the problem has been addressed that some of new users  do not sign-up after downloading the app.     In order to generate the best design solution, we give importance to crowd sourcing in our  project. So, the project team consists of 10 team members who are working at different  departments of the company, from technical and non-technical sides.    Selection    As most of the team members have not been involved in this kind of project carried out  through design thinking methodology before; I prefer to use tools of visualization in order to  build a good understanding of problem that we are trying to solve.     I created a research wall to display insights and all relevant research outputs in one place.  The visual aspect of the wall triggered idea generation and enabled project members to  better understand research insights. I usually use mind mapping tool in order to generate an  idea and represent concepts. It helps us to better analyze, comprehend, synthesize, recall  and generate new ideas. text:
Visualization

Challenge & Selection

Recently I happened to be at a ‘formal’ meeting seated around a table trying to  verbalize a problem and develop a concept. 30 minutes into the meeting  someone had the courage to break the formality and started to draw on a  piece of paper. What happened next didn’t surprise me. It’s not the art that  mattered, but the surfacing of the problem, conceptualizing ideas and gaining  the engagement to shape it better .Visualization is a core component of the  way that we communicate, whether we're aware of it or not. When we’re  dealing with very complex problems, we’re enacting a different kind of  problem solving that has to bring in more than just logic. Visualization is  really important for the process of Design Thinking because it's actually a way  of unlocking a different part of our brain. It allows me to think in a non-verbal  way and access parts of our brain, our creativity. Most design thinkers call  visualization as “the mother of all design tools”, because they are used in  every stage of the design thinking process.

Application

Visualization is equal parts listening, thinking and drawing. Listening is the input,  thinking is the processing and drawing is the output. These three skills work  together equally in understanding complexity, visualizing outcomes to create new  possibilities.

It's really  important to be able to understand the way that you communicate  with people. The primary tools for thinking visually are really just mastering  some basic elements of imagining people, spaces, situations and actions or  movements. It's very easy to create a simple diagram and most anyone can  draw a stick figure, a circle, a square, or an arrow. Those are the basic building  blocks of creating a  Visualization. We can unlock the power to think  differently by doodling. Alicia Diane Durand’s Discovery Doodles - The  complete series is a good starting point if you are in search of confidence and

Reflection- Visualization Tool

Challenge

The challenge is to think of a design of a cellphone charger that is easy to use, easy to carry, can charge  safely and can be use anywhere you wanted even if there is no outlet for charging. Nowadays, the production  of mobile phones has extremely increasing day-by-day, as well as different kinds of portable charger like  power banks that is easy to use, handy and can charge safely. But before we can use the power banks, we  need to first full charge it to an AC source, it is actually a back-up power device when you are traveling. In  line with this, the use of renewable energy is starting to be a big trend linked in the world of technology.  Renewable energy like solar energy, wind energy, hydropower etc. Therefore, our team wanted to design a  portable charger that is based on renewable energy source. It is an energy harvester using an  electromagnetic induction as a renewable source and will be applicable for mobile phone charging. No need  for AC source charging, to produce an energy, you only need to shake it.

Selection

Visualization tool, as our team selected for the challenge, is a way that we can visualize what will be the  future actual image of the design project. We can imagine how it works and who will use it regularly.  Visualization tool as a process of exercising your mind to more complex and more challenging design thinking  application.

If you want to visualize more what we will be doing and why we chose this visualization tool as the means to  our challenge, you can watch a video related to our shake charger which is the shake flashlight. It is when  Michael Faraday discovered that by passing a magnet through a coil of wire, a small electrical current is  created. And for that, it is the same thing that when the person shake flashlight.

text:
Storytelling for illustrating my idea to my partners    Challenge:

I was trying to implement an idea for implementing digital receipts in the shops. I had  considered the workflow of how the idea will work and how the user will perform different  tasks while shopping. I had a team for this process. So, I had to explain my idea to them in  order to make sure that everyone involved in the process has a clear cut knowledge about  our plan and there is no ambiguity and misunderstanding between the different members of  the team.

Selection:

Storytelling is a great tool for representing an idea in a more practical way. The events  connected through imagination provides a great intuition how the idea works and how the  work flows. ​ The storytelling process is very much suitable for sharing the idea accurately  with fellow members to make sure that everyone is on the same page. This is the reason  why I used this tool for my case.    Application:

I told my colleagues about a story representing our own situation while shopping. I explained  the disadvantages of paper receipt and made everyone realise that digitization is important. I  told a series of incidents and made it easier for others to understand the idea better and also  they could add up some interesting facts that will make our idea work. I could also make  everyone imagine how digitization will benefit the general public too.    Insight:

By using the process of storytelling, I could map out all my processes involved in my idea  and explain to my fellow partners about the disadvantages of paper receipt and provide  intuition of digital receipt. Also, I can easily explain the actual workflow that the idea delivers  in a clear and concise way and made sure that there was no ambiguity between us and we  were talking about the same thing.

I am a member of my organization’s online marketing department and our challenge is to improve the  workflow or a product within the company in order to increase sales in the online channel and to spend  marketing budgets on the right campaigns.

The project/ product scope online application and interactive website for the insurance company  includes the online marketing department composed of 4 employees, hat needs to deal with larger  department and IT department, with whom we work closely. The project is limited to internal resources  (i.e., budget and employee time). The project should not exceed 15 days and the solution should include  an even distribution of working hours amongst the team members. We will focus on trying to uncover  what our team members, as well as key stakeholders within the larger marketing department and IT  department, consider to be ineffective or problematic about the workflow.

Our team has already gone through several design thinking activities and sessions, so we are ready to  try the launch of the website and application.  the application launch is an experiment meant to test an  idea and service of a new feature integration.

Challenge & Selection:

I find myself exploring the problem of people who currently must sign up for various job  portals to feel like they are doing a successful search.

My development team must empathize with the consumer to be able to propose product  features that match to her customs and tastes. For that reason, I am going to use the  storytelling tool, which creates an emotional connection with the character being described, as  mentioned by Ruben Pabon in the video “Storytelling Tool” in week 2 of the course.

Application:

I make a story developed about Georgia:

Georgia is a mom and she works as an accounting assistant in the city center. She has been  working in a company for 6 years and has been a mom for 6 years. She stays in her work, but  she is not happy with her salary, she works already there because of her schedule that allows  her to spend more time with her family. Every day she spends 3 hours on a bus

Thinks: She wishes she could work closer to spend more time home with her little daughter  Bethany. She believes that for his time in the company and her good performance, he deserves  a raise.

Sees: Georgia sees her daughter is growing up as she spends more time at work and loses  family moments.

Feels: She feels sad for not spending time at home and disappointed at the little understanding  that she receives from his boss, who does not consider the awarding of prizes and promotions  due to the reduced work schedule.

Does: Georgia spends 2 hours every Sunday night looking for job opportunities on web portals,  however the short time does not allow her to do a productive search.

In addition, it was accompanied by a storyboard that reflected the current situation of Georgia,  a general description of the solution that is proposed, and the new reality of the character  (Georgia) after solving her problem.

The development team participated in further feeding the story, in addition to listing the  features that the application should have for it

Mind Mapping

Challenge

I was assigned to a group within my organization to increase the well-being of my fellow  employees. My organization routinely sends out generic surveys to all of the employees in order  to measure the level of satisfaction in the organization. The results of these surveys always reveal  that the employees are unhappy. The survey did not provide any open ended questions or any  opportunities to provide individualized feedback. The majority of the responses indicated that the  main reasons for the dissatisfaction was due to the long hours and stressful nature of the work.  Managers decided that there was not enough personnel to change the work schedule so there was  nothing they could do about the long hours. In an attempt to mitigate the stress, a relaxation  room was created where the employees could utilize new massage chairs, or a mini putt-putt  course. However, follow up surveys indicated that employee happiness had not improved.

Selection

My group knew that we needed to gain a deeper understanding into why the employees were  unhappy. Another generic survey was not going to provide us with the information we needed.  We needed to have genuine conversations that would reveal the sources of dissatisfaction and  discover personalized ways to create happiness. We decided to get more personal with the  surveys and use Mind Mapping to identify common themes that could feasibly be addressed.  Mind mapping was an ideal application to use because it allowed us to organize a large volume  of information into more manageable themes. There was no way we could personally satisfy  hundreds of employees. However, Mind Mapping narrowed those hundreds of ‘wants’ into a  smaller, workable amount of concepts.

Challenge

I develop software for a measurement device (the “Device”) which is installed on large, complex  semiconductor processing equipment (the “Tool”).  The device requires hardware “tuning” by installers  who turn calibration screws until the Device signals are maximized.  Currently, the installation team uses  a vendor app running on a laptop to view the Device signals.  The laptop must be abandoned at  customer sites, as customers wish to ensure that none of their Intellectual Property can be stolen.  The  install team wants to make similar software available through the Tool software/GUI.  However, the  Device produces a substantial volume of data, at a high data rate, and must be transferred through  three to four servers before it can be plotted on the GUI.  The data is likely to have a time lag or be a  drag on the local network.

Selection

I chose the Learning Launch tool.  In particular, I wanted to apply the Assumption Worksheet, as there  were considerable assumptions on the part of the installers requesting the software and on my part in  being wary of the complexity of the data.

Application

Hypothesis: we need a new utility on the Tool software to replace the Vendor software running on the  discardable laptop.

Key assumption 1:  Data volume for the transferring all of the data from the Device to the Tool’s GUI is  not feasible.

Test: Calculate the data volume and find out who is the network expert for the Tool’s software,  and ask if the data transfer is doable.

Results of test: Data transfer would be acceptable.

Key assumption 2:  The computer can pre-do some of the analysis that the installers do by eyeball, and  present the data to the installers in a superior way to the Vendor software.

Test: I interviewed the installers to determine exactly how they use their eyeballs to evaluate  the continuous stream of data.

Challenge & Selection:

I am a mechanical engineering student and I use to work in a different  projects and design and simulation  with SOLIDWORKS , a lot of designs for  a lot of projects without studding the need of it .

In my country we usually go to a gas station waiting for hours just to have a  small tank of cooking gas which cannot last for a month. Also we have a  problem with garbage dumps. Visualization was a great tool to help us to find that  solution and knowing the pain points  of the people need our help.

Application:

I realize that problem because I suffer it myself in my home, also our  neighbors. In our habits we take more care about organic waste. We don’t  like just put in a garbage dump, specially the bread without feeling guilty. I  asked many neighbors what do they do with their organic waste ? some of  them feed it to their animals and they through it when it becomes spoiled,  and others just threw it away. Searching for the best solution for as much  as possible of problems we found Recycling garbage but it wasn’t the best  solution for the organic waste. So we found Biogas. So using visualization we solved the problem of organic waste and  the lack  of cooking gas in the same time.

Knowing the real problems that people suffer from and knowing their pain  allowed us to find the best solution for them. Without using the tool of  Visualization we would not realize their daily habits, their problems and  needs. We had a better understanding of the problem we were working on.

Reflection on Visualisation

Sk Rana

Challenge    I work in a Fintech company and provide specialised services to the financial institutions. My stakeholders  are increasing facing challenges from their customers and increasing competition from their competitors.  On top, the increasing regulatory requirements are adding to their woes. The complexity of their problems  are overwhelming for me many times and bringing them together for a consensus is very challenging. I  work to provide an innovative solution to their complex problems. Many times I meet a diverse group of  stakeholders with a complex problem and a variety of wish lists and it becomes difficult to arrive at a  shared understanding of their problem and the possible solution. In my current problem I was challenged  to select only the functionalities which will enhance the user experience in using the financial tool while  increasing the operational efficiencies and meeting the key performance indicators.     Selection    In the kick-off meeting I user PowerPoint presentation and did not have a good experience in engaging  the participants. Many participants seemed to be un-interested with the bullet points. Incidentally I was  attending the course of Lobina and found the usage of the tool visualisation suitable for my kind of  problem to engage a large number of stakeholders. I followed the presentation of Angela Myer and came  to know the benefits of using the tool. As I use big room planning sessions with many stakeholders, I  selected visualisation tools to help my stakeholders define the scope and boundaries, the key elements  and their inter-relations and finally agree on the list of problems to solve. Visualisation is important in my  problem area to unlock the creative side of the brain of the stakeholders and to think in a nonverbal way  to visually understand the problems. text:
Reflection- Mind Mapping

Challenge and Selection

First of all, I use Mind Mapping as a method to find steps for solving any problems and find the  target  in my life. I often use this method while doing group project at my campus. In my  opinion, this is the best method because I can know what I should do by reading from the line   that I have drawn before.

In campus, I join robotic extracurricular at Rajarambapu Institute of Technology. For specific, I am a  researcher in the extracurricular. The challenge for me is finding a research topic for being  shared to the members of the extracurricular. I use mind mapping method to find what I should  do and the target while finding a research topic.

Application

I use this method for finding the best way to solve that problem. First, I draw a box which  written “Research Topic”. Then, I write two branches in the left and the right box. The left  branch is written “The steps” and the right branch is written “The target”. Not only two  branches, but I also added more branches in “The steps” and “The target” for make the steps  and the target become more specific.

When I try to find the research topic, the steps are search my interest and find a journal which  is suitable for me . For the target , I hope that I can finish reading the journal within one week.

This method I very effective for me because I can know the way to reach my target effectively.  Why did not I use table instead of mind mapping? Because I think that table is boring, I prefer  seeing mind map to the table.

Insight and Approach

To be honest, before joining this course I did not know about the method for organizing the steps to a  project. Now, I know the step how to organize the step to finish a project. By using mind map, I can use  the branches to see the steps and the target that I want to reach in the future.

I will use this method again for doing another project at campus or my extracurricular.

text:
Storytelling

Challenge  In the financial services sector, due to regulatory needs all incidents need to be registered and its  consequences measured. An incident in this context is every occurrence where a process fail, such as a  payment not being processed correctly or a system being unavailable for a customer. The collection of  these, along with the assessment of consequences (e.g. extra hours, fees, penalties, loss of market  share), is paramount to predict the amount of capital that needs to be reserved for risks and to avoid  systemic instabilities in the market.

The problem is that, although extremely relevant, this process is cumbersome and time-consuming, as  people have to individually analyse each occurrence and liaise with multiple departments to estimate  correctly the impacts. This leads to subpar notification on most banks and an underestimation of the  required capital to sustain these risks. The challenge then is how to simplify the identification and  quantification of these events in order to provide a realistic picture of the institution exposure.

Selection  The tool selected to help tackle this challenge is storytelling.  The purpose of this tool is to ensure that  the design process capture the users’ needs and the value we want to deliver. A good story makes it  possible for all the participants to empathize with the users and ensure that their work is well  represented.

According to Aristotles, there are seven elements of good storytelling:

1- Plot – What are the character(s) doing and what are they trying to accomplish?  2- Character – Who are the people, their traits, backgrounds, aspirations?  3- Theme – What is the end goal or obstacle that needs to be crossed?  4- Dialogue – How do people interact, are they angry, sad, happy?  5- Melody – What are the emotions that set the tone to this?  6- Décor – What is the physical environment and limitations in which the users perform their acts?  7- Spectacle – How the audience remembers that

Reflection – Learning Launch

Challenge and selection

We are a team of researchers working on innovative didactic (both normo- and disabilities) at

Google at the department of Electronics Information and Bioengineering. During the  last year, when Italy was locked down due to the COVID-19 pandemic, our lab challenge consisted  of offering an effective way to pursue the DAD ("didattica a distanza", i.e. distance teaching and  learning). The solution should have included an easy-to-use tool that helped professors and students  to feel and work together, though not being at school in the same physical class. The developed  tool, using the flipped classroom approach, makes the students watch a video before the  explanation made by the professor and provide this latter with a chart that shows students’  reactions (i.e. which parts of a video are clear and which, on the contrary, are not, along with the  overall acceptance, in terms of clarity and appreciation, of the videos).

Thus, our challenge was human-centered and there were many people involved in the problem;

anyway, especially at the beginning, the statement of the issue was not clear since never faced  before; similar (didactic) situation had never been experienced, then there were not analogous data  available, and many unknows and past indicators were useless. We then firstly needed to explore  and get agreement on the problem. For all these reasons, the Design Thinking approach seemed  very appropriate to the process of developing of our tool. Our team has never gone through Design  Thinking activities, but it was immediately unambiguous that it could have been very useful to solve  our problem: especially the learning launch tool, which is meant to quickly test ideas and  prototypes, was a perfect fit. Example Reflection – Story telling

Challenge & Selection

I work for a humanitarian organization for children. We work intensively through focused welfare  projects to help guarentee education for poor children in India.

There are many underprivileged children who are under difficult circumstances, such as child labour,  children from poor families, married children (especially girls) ...  and in order to help these children ,  it is mandatory to go first through their families and help inspire them. To do this, I always tend to  use Storytelling which is a great tool to get insight into families, build empathy and reach them  emotionally to help enlighten them about the necessity of education

I also use stories to better understand their interests and thought processes. I use this information to  develop different strategies to try and find a way to convince them about the advantages of child  education

Application

Here’s a story about using storytelling in my work for the humanitarian organization. At its debuts,  the organization built classes in underpriviliged villages of the country and expected high attendency  rates. I was trying to explain to them the benefits of taking a more client focused approach, and in  particular, of recognizing each person as a unique being, and addressing their individual needs first  and foremost.

I told a story about a family I had met composed of a mother and her daughter. When I first saw  them, they were lying in the street next to their highly damaged house while the daughter , aged 10  to 11 was crying, her sobs muffled as she leaned forward against her school bag. I approached them  kindly and asked about their issue. It turned out that she was planning on marrying off her daughter  to an overly aged man to help them with the daily expenses. The child will therefore be stopping  school and focusing on house chores and taking care of her husband.

Insight & Approach

Reflection – Storytelling

Challenge:

I’m a final year undergraduate student in an Indian College. The college administration

invited final years for discussions to develop measures to make our campus more friendly for

women. On discussing about this issue with our female friends in college, we arrived at our

problem statement: “Promoting Gender Equity in Campus”. Our campus is very

conservative. While men are given enough freedom to do as they wish throughout the day,

women are confined within their hostels post a 9 PM curfew. The issue of Promoting Gender

Equity in Campus could be considered a “wicked problem”.

Tool Selection:

To tackle this wicked problem, we made use of the tool: Storytelling. Storytelling engages

people and allows us to understand their unarticulated needs as they share their experiences

and values (Ref. Week 2 Lecture4 https://www.coursera.org/learn/uva-darden-design-

thinking-innovation/lecture/PAXCd/storytelling-tool). It explains the interconnections among

people in situations and settings, and teaches broad lessons that engage real human beings.

Stories generate questions, questions expand the breadth and depth of stories and this leads to

lots of innovative thoughts and ideas.

Tool Application:

We invited both male and female friends to talk about their routines. As they shared their

routines, the female friends observed the striking differences between their routines and the

routines of our male friends. We made use of journals maintained by our friends to

understand their needs better. We also asked our friends to imagine a situation where they

would be free to do as they wish and then asked them to narrate what they imagined.

Mind Mapping to Improve Digital Product Design and Development

1.Challenge: Describe your challenge, including all relevant information.

I was working with a small organization to develop a digital design repository and knowledge  sharing solution. This solution was intended to support the development of digital products  through the sharing of design and related information across staff involved with designing and  building such products. The end-users of this solution would comprise the product  development team and key stakeholders. The solution itself was intended to integrate, replace  or enhance current information systems. In trying to understand customer needs and priorities  across a wide range of end-users with different backgrounds, I designed and conducted a  series of custom workshops to obtain source information from end users. The findings from  these workshops were used to develop appropriate customer journey maps. The workshops  spanned over three months, involved more than thirty staff from across the organization and  resulted in the development of over thirteen journey maps for the same number of distinct  personas. Data and information gathered in these workshops resulted in a summarized report  that spanned over a hundred pages. In order for the development of the solution to move  forward, end users, key stakeholders and sponsors needed to have a good understanding of  the current situation to inform design goals.  However, I found it challenging to analyze the  information, develop a design hypothesis and present key findings and recommendations in a  cohesive and understandable manner. This became even more of a challenge when I found  that I was given 20 minutes to present my findings and another 40 mins for discussion. text:
Reflection : Storytelling

Challenge

Want students to use these aspects of storytelling to better understand their experiences and  actions therefore through the use of story, students engage in an active learning process  whereby they actively read and reflect on their stories. At the same time the professor is  offered a window into the student’s understanding of the clinical incident. Through reflection,  we focus on the context of the story and, through the use of guiding questions, students begin  to understand any implicit meanings. This helps then to intentionally connect their classroom  learning with real-life practice. Stories are shared between students in a small seminar class.  Our role as faculty is to guide a critically reflective dialogue within the small student discussion  group. Stories provide the mechanism for understanding as they can be reflected on,  reanalyzed and understood.

In addition to guiding students to use their critical thinking skills in a clinical story context, we  also want them to begin to understand something about their thinking process. So we talk  with them a bit about critical thinking and problemsolving, and help them make connections  between these terms. In this way they begin to more closely focus on their own thinking  processes. Our learning objective reflects both of these considerations

Selection

Following presentation, discussion and assigned learning activities, the students will be able  to:

1. Use elements of storytelling to help them analyze and learn from their clinical practice  experiences.

2. Improve critical thinking skills (analysis, inference, explanation and evaluate) through  stories that they tell about their clinical practice experiences.

3. Analyze and discuss the knowledge that they have gained from actual clinical experiences
