Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge    We are making major revisions to our top-selling professional education course, which  historically has involved textbooks, some video lectures, and an online or in-person exam to  complete. Studying takes 2 to 6 weeks to take an exam and the full course, for a professional  designation, is 8 exams on different topics. Feedback from students indicates we need to  change the format to adapt to new learning needs.     Selection    A lot of work had been done prior to my joining the project.  Surveys, interviews with students  and with their employers, review of product feedback, competitive analysis, plus much more. In  addition, those involved in designing the new course and its content are very seasoned  professionals with a lot of experience in what works and what doesn't. In fact, most of them had  taken at least some of our courses as students, so were very familiar with the student  experience.     For example, we think students want more online courses, fewer printed textbooks, shorter  course segments, recorded live instructor segments, audio books. We think they want more  real-life examples, but does that look like case studies, or like industry-specific topics?    The key was to specify all the assumptions, data points, and hypotheses that were driving  decisions and be sure we agreed on what was important and how to proceed. As a market  researcher, my goal was to collect all the hypotheses and outstanding questions in a systematic  way so I could validate and/or understand them better through additional research. I decided  mind mapping was the technique to use.    Application    I started with a small group of key leaders and invited them to two meetings. Stephen White: Regional volunteering challenges  CHALLENGE  The challenge is to develop a region wide approach to volunteer development within a specific area  of South Australia.   The area contains a number of smaller size towns < 6000 people and several different local  government authorities (LGA) all operate relatively independently. The region is a predominantly  crop farming with the usual challenges of the same people, averaging 60+ years old, volunteering in  multiple organisations because ‘no one else will do it’.  There are common issues across the entire  region but no one has previously suggested a region wide approach to consolidating these issues an  develop an approach to encouraging volunteering diversity in the region.   What does regional volunteer development look like? Good question. This is the challenge we need  to explore. An outsider would suggest things like training, health and safety in the workplace, risk  management, governance and so on. But no one has asked the key stakeholders in the region. Their  understanding may look very different. This would suit a design thinking approach to circumnavigate  traditional thinking and develop new models of operating. It was selected because some stakeholders may have had  exposure to it previously, but this could not be guaranteed (both comfort and non-comfort zones).   The key focus would be the question posed ‘What could a regional volunteer development plan look  like?’  We felt the tool would respect the diverse nature of the stakeholders and it was felt this might  achieve a number of things: unlock latent ideas; challenge resistance from some individuals; quieten  down or disempowering a number of individuals who always took over any group discussion because  their ideas were right; empower individuals who were very quiet and rarely said anything yet we felt  they had g

Mind Mapping

Challenge & Selection  The first tool I used was the Mind Mapping tool when I initially joined my current company where  I was brought on to chart the current onboarding process for new customers and identify areas  of opportunity for process improvements.  I decided to use this approach because I could begin  by mapping out my own onboarding experience as a customer (because I had my own data  points) which could easily be described as dreadful and I had tons of feedback. I then extended  the invitation for other associates to map out their experiences as well, giving us a broad sense  of what was happening across the process since no documentation for this existed at the time.     Application  I started the process by designating a huge whiteboard (conveniently located to senior  leadership) as the space where myself and other associates could place visuals of their  onboarding process – application information, messaging screenshots, printouts of emails  received during the onboarding time-frame, copies of welcome materials, call recordings with  service agents and relevant information about product usage/ease, etc. I also asked everyone  to write sound bites of their experience – what went well, what did not, what was devastatingly  awful, would they recommend to friends and family.  I then added actual customer complaint  verbatims to this board that we received through website surveys, social media, call listening  sessions and regulatory organizations. This whiteboard turned into a very powerful visual of an  undocumented process that was ripe with opportunity to make it better for our customers.      As more and more associates contributed their information on the board themes started to  emerge. The  problem at hand was to create a sugar free offering for juices and communicate it in such a way that  people select it over sugary drinks. Storytellings sticks in the mind of consumers and links their thinking with the brand. I decided to link  the experience of eating a fresh fruit to the process of drinking a natural drink. Taste is the major  factor when selecting a juice and I had to convey the health benefits of drinking natural juice which  compensates for the lost additional sweetness. I selected this approach as an emotional element of  storytelling will persuade buyers.

Application

I created a storyboard which showed how we gather various ingredients- apple, beetroot, carrot and  honey from pure and organic sources and don’t add any preservatives to it. The bottles were given a  resemblance to apple fruit to provide physicality to the story and remind users of the natural fruits.  Better grown fruits without preservatives will be better for you and your families health. Overall, it  will be an enriching juice without added sugary preservatives that often have negative effects on the  health of consumers.

The brand’s story- ABC juice- focuses on health benefits and how the healthy ingredients have a  story from farm to the bottle. I have many interviews with local street commerce, big comMerce, young customers and old  customer and then I did an interview with all them using jamboard (free google app to burn the  creativity) to cluster new ideas and discuss it. It was awesome!

I had many insights for example, people want to create an order using their voice and not the  keyboarding. Old and young customers want to pick recipes and the app calculate automating  what kind of food and size must to buy and where.

Commerce wants to get a small ERP who makes easy its managing. Product most selling, top  customer and what the competence sell!

Approach

Definitely making a session in a room like an art gallery would be the best, but for covid19 at this  moment that was impossible. However the next time I will do it!

Linda Mthethwa               19 November 2018

thinking that maybe there is a market for renting out this kind of equipment. I live in Windhoek, the

capital city of Namibia. Namibia is a very popular tourist destination because of the beautiful and

unspoilt nature and wildlife. I made the assumption that tourists that visit Namibia do not necessarily

want to buy and travel with equipment like binoculars, spotting scopes, satellite navigation devices,

e.g. the kind of equipment and gear a tourist will require for a trip to Namibia, and that there would

be a business opportunity for providing a service for renting out this kind of gear.

2. Selection

My “what is” was a desk study on the number and type of tourists that generally visited Namibia. My

“what if” was the idea that there will be a market for renting out certain gear to tourists to Namibia.

Thus, for my “what wows and what works” I needed to test my assumption that tourists will be willing

to rent gear when travelling to Namibia, as opposed to buying and travelling with their own gear.

I did not want to invest too much capital into buying a lot of equipment that I could rent out to tourists

before I knew that my assumptions were actually valid. Thus, I had to do an experiment that was fast

and cheap and I therefore opted for the learning launch – which is in essence the prescribed design

thinking method to test the key underlying value-generating assumptions of a potential new-growth

initiative quickly and inexpensively before going into a detailed investigation with the commitment of

text:
The young achievers

• Challenge and Selection:

I have been associated with a volunteer-based global organization named Aviva  for the last one year. Teaching and mentoring is a passion of mine, which I pursue by teaching  unfortunate and needy young children (up to 6th grade) every Sundays with this organization.  I still remember the initial days when I found it difficult to build rapport with the children. This  was really important as it made imparting education easier (by getting their undivided attention)  while also made for a cause for them to come on a regular basis. With time, I found that some  of these children did seek inspiration and had dreams that they wanted to realize. For me, it  was about helping them to visualize what their dream looks like while also making it  entertaining for them so as to keep them interested and because of their tender yet  impressionable age (approx. 6-10 years) and a sparkling nature, using their creative  imagination via storytelling seemed like the most suitable way to meet this objective.

• Application:

Time was of the essence, we met for four hours every week in a public park which was followed  by a break of 6 days. The stories needed to be short, captivating, fun, inspiring but most  importantly relatable (even to a 6 year old). After interacting with them for a few weeks, I got  an insight into their family backgrounds, their daily routine and their likes and dislikes. For  genuine inspiration, the stories needed to be real and presented in such a way that meets all of  the above criteria. For a few children who wished to be a doctor, I recited stories of my aunt  who is a doctor. I told them about her practice and the respect she gets in the society. A few of  them wanted to be engineers, I told them about my experience in engineering college and of  the various practicals we did on “big machines” and of the “biscuit factory” that we had visited. Reflection – Mind Mapping

Challenge

I am a member of the project department of my organization and my / our challenge is to  improve the quality of life for truckers who are our customers. The project is following the agile  methodology, SCRUM, and I am the scrum master of a team composed of 10 people, 8 of whom  are managers from different departments.

The project is limited to internal resources (that is, the employee's budget and time) and  employees are not dedicated, with no uniform distribution of working hours among team  members. We will focus on trying to discover and build a tool that can improve the quality of  life for truck drivers, taking advantage of the strength of our brand in this field and leveraging  the number of clients of our company insurance broker.

Selection

Our team has never worked with agile methodology or design thinking before this project,  however, we have already been able to apply some tools, such as: CSD matrix, attributes matrix,  desk research and interviews. Now, we need to consolidate all the information we have obtained  so far and, for that, we will use the mind map and subsequent definition of personas, in order  to advance in our delivery of value to the client and sponsors.

Application

Our first challenge was to structure our tasks, schedule and agile people. That done and using  some of the design thinking tools in the empathy stage of the project, we moved on to a second  moment, which was when we used the mind map to put ourselves in our client's shoes, based  on all the information obtained so far with the surveys, interviews and benchmark. Challenge:

I’m the design engineer for Go-Live. And it’s very important for our team to understand

each other’s proposal or thinking. And I explain my design concept for other department like

production and quality without any misunderstanding.

Selection:

Visualization is very useful to have same understandings with other members who work at other

countries. Because I work in Japan, but the production plants or other members are in the other

countries like USA, Mexico or Argentina.

Application:

I have to explain my design concepts with them. It’s very easy to get misunderstandings with other

team members to explain my design concepts by only wordings or verbally talking. And I use visual

tools like CAD or Power point to explain my design concepts.

Insight:

CAD is very useful to get same understandings in the visually. And other members who understood

can send their concern points specifically. Thus I can improve my design concepts based on their

feedbacks.

Approach:

I’m trying to improve my communication tools not only visual tools but also support documents

to explain my messages. Just CAD data is not enough to bring my messages to other members and

I have to prepare supports documents for it. Because we are working other time zone, and I have to

bring my messages by just sending a mail rather than verbally talking.

Visualization

Challenge & Selection

The first tool I used was the tool of Visualization, or Visual Thinking, to achieve a shared  understanding of a problem space among a diverse group of stakeholders before attempting to  identify and define possible solutions to the problem. I use this approach often with our customers,  who are government agencies working to apply technology innovations to modernize their mission  or the delivery of their services to their customer, which may be U.S. citizens, businesses, and non- citizens. I have used the technique of using a straw man visualization of a problem domain with a set  of questions or prompts for discussion to allow a diverse group of stakeholders to learn from each  other in the process of defining the scope, boundaries, key elements, and relationships between  elements to consider when identifying pain points and opportunities for improvements or solutions.

Application

I start the process by creating a straw man graphic of the problem domain. To develop the straw  man graphic, I will draw from any existing material available to understand the environment. The  existing material may be operational or procedural documents, training materials, marketing  materials, GAO or other auditing reports. If materials are not available, then I conduct informal  interviews with one-three of the stakeholders who serve as my main points of contact on the  initiative. If appropriate to the situation, I will borrow the concept to “front-stage/back-stage” from  previous research, and discussed in David Gray’s book, “The Connected Company”. The front- stage/back-stage approach helps to reinforce the notion that every service – even an internal service  – has customers with whom the service provider interacts and internal processes that enable the  organization to provide the service. Visualisation mixed with storytelling techniques

Challenge

While helping out a customer with their Agile Adoption we arrived at a team structure where it was  unclear ‘why’ certain things were on their todo list form a end-user perspective. There was no link  to their real customers and a true vision was missing for upcoming releases. The team was  building applications for internal customers (customer support, sales, infrastructure…) that would  reduce paper consumption as a whole but were unsure about the effects and effectiveness of their  deliverables. This uncertainty manifested itself in lack of motivation within the team and a lack of  adoption of the applications at the end-user side. A disconnect!

Selection

There was a long list of todo’s for the team to build available and an overall purpose was ‘assigned’  to reduce paper consumption. Facts we could not disregard as a whole as there were expectations  created within the organisation related to those facts. We could convince the team and their end- users to engage in a 1-day conversation on future releases with as purpose to align expectations  and generate a common purpose amongst them.

One part of the problem was known: paper consumption but there were lots of other, not yet  discovered, terrain that we chose to facilitate a collaborative session where diverse groups of  people would generate a visual representation of their expectations related to how new  applications should behave and affect the way they did their work. We were going to go for video  prototyping as a way to visualise the different perspectives.

Application

In order to guide the attendees we designed the 1-day in such a way that people would open up  their minds to other needs, wishes and insights. A true learning experience for all. Technocreative Solution

Challenge

I am leading a creative team which supports Pre-Sales department. My team’s responsibilities  include creating digital and multimedia assets production for Pre-Sales department. Our work  includes all kind of creative stuffs needed to boost sales of our company products; it includes some  technically challenging solutions. One of the project on which we were working was technically and  creatively challenging, it’s an interactive 3d models of our company’s product. Team was divided  into different geographical areas such as India and USA. We were developing 3D models in India and  need to show (cross check) it to our manager and product technical managers, to know whether 3d  model is technically fine or not? But problem was, uploading this complete 3d model on internet  which was rendered with lights, animation and other settings due to heavy output (in terms of file  size). This complete process just to show one model needs 2 days of time. And it’s just a single  model, we had lots of models in our project. And in case of feedbacks, again same 2 days(approx..).  My major concern is how do I reduce this time frame and speedup/overcome this process.

Selection:

First, we need to find out that it’s a problem. Second, we should know that it needs to be solved. So,  I focussed on problem, started searching and brainstorming about ideas to solve this issue and speed  up my work. I than zeroed on a unique plugin which we could use inside 3ds MAX software (3d  model making software). Flare3d is a platform for creating interactive 3D content for web and  mobile devices. With a powerful Stage3D rendering engine and an intuitive IDE. They also provide a  plug-in, which one can install into 3ds MAX (3d software) and directly generate SWF (file one can  play on browser) as output.

Challenge  My organisation’s IT function had recently been restructured into a set of smaller individual businesses  within IT (value streams) and an associated set of group that provide support and governance over these  value streams.

The value streams run independently like their own businesses so they can deliver value to their specific  customers groups within the organisation that they serve as fast as possible. However they also need to  align to the common IT strategy of the organisation, maintain visibility of all the work occurring within IT  and work together across value streams to deliver a complete service that meets the customer needs.

The existing way that IT funding requests and solutions were reviewed, assessed and governed by a single  team and single IT executive would not work in this new matrix structure. The current method of detailed  review of documents and series of meetings to discuss them would be too time-consuming to ensure  alignment and enable visibility.

Selection  It was important to be able to determine what would be feasible (“what Works”) very rapidly without a  large investment of time and cost as the process would be used weekly by a large number of people,  including all of the IT executives whose time is extremely valuable.

In the future we will automate the final governance process, but don’t want to develop software to do this  until we know the process will achieve the desired outcome.

This is why I selected the learning launch approach, outlined by Matthias Walther in the Learning Launch Tool  video in the Experimentation Module, to be able to test my hypothesis by doing an experiment that was  fast and cheap.

Image source -> Matthias Walther - https://www.coursera.org/learn/design-thinking- innovation/lecture/F04r6/learning-launch-tool

Reflection – Mind mapping

Challenge

We are a functional food production company, and our company was trying to implement a digital  marketing campaign through mobile app relating personalized nutrition and healthy eating. The  challenge was that in the amid of covid, we decided to do it online that we needed to create digital tools  for the campaign. And also we wanted aspects from stakeholders, employees and customers, and the  information we got was quite large. Therefore, we needed to apply some tools to get our campaign  launched successfully.

Selection

We used mind mapping tool to initialize our campaign idea. First of all, we invited some of our  customers to give feedback and be participated in the process. As said in the lecture, mind mapping tool  looks for patterns and insights in large quantity of data we collected and point out the reality of the  situation. Therefore, we decided to use mind mapping tool to achieve our mission. It was not easy to get  to the common ground, but mind mapping tool helped us get launched our campaign in time.

Application

We started with the mission of our campaign, and we first talked with our stakeholders. After that, we  developed a framework, and we wrote down all theme ideas got from our employees. At this step, we  added every detail of each theme and we even invited some customers to know what and how they  would like to be involved and what the impact would be for them by participating in the campaign. Then  we created mockup app, sent them out to our customers and got feedback from them. We needed to  make major changes along the way but it saved us a lot of time and money as we saw the weakness of  our campaign before we launched.

Reflection Assignment - Visualisation

Challenge & Selection

In the following, I will describe how I was able to overcome a challenge by using the power of  visualisation. The tool of visualisation gives a great opportunity for making an idea that you have more  tangible and more concrete. This can be done by either drawing the audience a picture, sketching out  concepts by using workflows and maps, drawing a low fidelity prototype (such as a sketch or  wireframes) on a whiteboard or even by building a small prototype out of simple material such as  Lego® stones, Play-Doh® and straws. There are many different ways of visualising an idea that help  turn your thoughts into something that the audience can look at in order to understand the thoughts  that you had better.

I used the power of visualisation in an introductory design thinking workshop course at my company  where the challenge set was to create a “pharmacy of the future” within 2 hours. I chose the tool of  visualisation in order to be able to draw my team colleagues a sketch of the app that I was thinking  about in order to be able to better explain my team colleagues my idea on how to solve the  interviewee’s problem statement. This was especially important in this group as I did not know any  other my team colleagues yet and therefore decided it was easier to explain them my idea by drawing  it out rather than trying to explain it in words in English to a group of non-native people from different  departments. In this way, we could check whether our ideas for solving the problem statement  matched up and we could see where we complement each other to come up with an ever better  solution for the problem statement. In my case drawing my idea as a low fidelity sketch on the  whiteboard was the best way of drawing out my idea as I had a mobile app in mind and in this way I  could show my idea on what the app would look like and what the user journey would be.
